# cpd 2: command reference

Status: **normative for every cpd 2 implementation Job**, under [contract.md](contract.md): where the two disagree, contract.md wins and this file is fixed. Vocabulary: [CONTEXT.md](../CONTEXT.md). This file uses the contract's names, states, tables and Event kinds exactly; "§n" without a prefix means §n of this file, "contract §n" means contract.md §n and "cpd 1 §n" means `docs/archive/cpd1/cli-contract.md` §n.

It specifies every command of the design outline §3 (`~/.cpd/plans/cpd-rust/`) (synopsis, flags, preconditions with their error and exit codes, effects, JSON output, idempotence), the pi adapter's protocol, the Worker contract, what the TUI reads and `doctor`.

Evidence labels as in contract.md: **verified** (run on the homeserver on 2026-10-14), **docs** (read in the named tool's documentation or source), **unverified** (a design assumption the implementation Job must check).

The commands serve the **CPD flow** (hs-n31): three stages, **Context** (Grounding, Grilling), **Plan** (Clarifying, Scoping, Splitting, Orchestrating) and **Dispatch** (Documenting, Red testing, Implementing, Verifying, Deploying). contract §3.9 maps each step to its phase and commands.

## 1. Conventions

### 1.1 How each command is written

Every command section has the same parts:

- **Synopsis**, then a table of every flag. `<x>` is required, `[x]` optional, `a | b` exclusive. A repeated flag says so.
- **Preconditions**, checked in the order listed; the first that fails is the result. Each row gives the error `code` and the exit code (§1.2). The common refusals of §1.3 apply to every command and are not repeated.
- **Effects**: **rows** written (table and columns), **Events** appended (kinds of §5.2), **tmux** and **git** actions and files under `$CPD_HOME` (§1.4). "One transaction" means one write transaction with its `txns` row, its `history` rows and its Events (§4.2). External work (git, tmux, hooks, `gh`, pi) is never inside it.
- **Output**: one JSON example of success. Every failure is the envelope of §1.2, `{"ok": false, "error": {"code", "message", "details"}}`; `details` is listed where it carries something the caller acts on.
- **Idempotent**: what a rerun does. The default of §1.3 is `"already": true`; a command that differs says so.

A command is **internal** when cpd runs it by itself and neither an agent nor the User types it: a program cpd starts in a pane or detached, or a command only cpd's own parts (the engine, the pi adapter) run. Internal commands are hidden in clap (`hide = true`; a command under a hidden one is internal too), so they are absent from `--help` text but listed, marked, in the `tree` (§1.2). Today: `session run`, `attempt run`, `tui view` and its views, `plan decide` and `session state`. They are documented so their implementation Jobs have a contract.

### 1.2 Output and exit codes

Kept from §1.2 (D1). Every command prints exactly one JSON value on stdout. Six kinds of command print something other than one JSON value and are the only exceptions (amendment 10, §19):

| Command | What it prints | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `cpd events follow` | one Event per line (§5.4) | a streaming command (§1.2) |
| `cpd cockpit serve` (§11a) | one frame per line, NDJSON, on stdout (§5.5) | a streaming command (§1.2); it reads requests on stdin |
| `cpd session tail` (§10.19) | one line per completed transcript message, the grammar of contract §6.20 (§10.19) | a read-only tail of a durable Session's host socket: it streams live frames as they complete, as the socket tail of Q33 is |
| `cpd gate finish` (§26) | the run's report on stderr and its exit status | it prints no JSON of its own; the status is the command's, or 64 when the run left something behind |
| `cpd session run`, `cpd tui view` (internal) | they run pi or draw a ratatui view in their pane | they are the programs inside cockpit panes (§6.2), not commands an agent calls. If they fail before taking the terminal, they print the failure envelope and exit with its code |
| `cpd tui action` (internal) | nothing, ever | the StatusBar's click binding and the `merge` popup's confirm (`cpd tui action merge <owner>/<repo>#<n> --client <client>`, hs-d473) run it with `run-shell -b`, which puts the active pane into view mode on a failure or any output (§13.2); it reports a failure with `display-message -c <client>` and a failed merge with the cockpit's one failure dialog, a `text` dialog (§13.2, §17 "No notes") |
| `cpd` (no arguments), `cpd tui --attach` | nothing on success: it replaces itself with `tmux attach` | the design outline says `tui` "builds and attaches the cockpit"; without `--attach`, `cpd tui` prints JSON like every command. Bare `cpd` is §13.3 (hs-d259) |

`cpd --version` (like `--help`) prints one JSON value too: `{"ok": true, "version": "0.22.45-070ddee", "protocol": 22, "store": {"opens": true, "refusal": null, "unknown": [], "pending": []}}`. The `version` field is `<semantic version>-<commit>` where the semantic version is `0.<protocol>.<migrations>`: the commit is the short hash the build was given in `CPD_COMMIT` (set by `scripts/install-cpd.sh` and the Gate, so an installed binary reports the commit it was built from) and `dev` when the build was given none, e.g. `0.19.45-dev` (docs/implementing.md "The version string"; docs/versioning.md). `store` is the **verdict** of contract §4.5 ("The window") on `$CPD_HOME`'s database opened read-only, computed by the one function every guard uses (`store::verdict`): `null` when the database file does not exist; otherwise `opens` (`true` when this binary can open the store, migrating or converting it if needed), `refusal` (`null`, or `{"code", "message"}` with `code` one of `store_too_new`, `store_failed`, `migration_changed`, `migration_order`, §1.3) when `opens` is `false`, `unknown` (the migration names the store has applied that this binary lacks, in name order: inside the window they are all additive) and `pending` (the names of this binary's migrations the store has not applied, in the order they would be applied; for an unconverted store the legacy names it lacks, then every named one). `unknown` and `pending` are `[]` for a store that is not named yet and filled whenever the store is a named store, whether or not it opens. `protocol` is an integer, **23** today (1 until Plan manager added `session-message`, 2 until Plan inbox added the four `inbox-*` kinds, 3 until `session state idle --reply`, hs-d278, 4 until `session-titled`, hs-d257, 5 until `workflow-base-changed`, hs-d324, 6 until `session state waiting`, hs-d303, 7 until `review-opened`/`review-closed`, hs-d496, 8 until `session-retiered`, hs-d506, 9 until `plan-outlined`, hs-d502, 10 until `job-merged`'s `data.turn` and `session-message`'s `data.unblocks`, hs-d514, 11 until `session-resumed`, hs-d552, 12 until `session report`, hs-d573, 13 until `incident-started` and `incident-ended`, hs-d634, 14 until `mcp-attached`, pro-d8, 15 until the adapter runs `session switch-failed` and `session switched` and the `error` Event carries the reporting Session, 16 until `workflow-described`, pro-d94, 17 until `session-model-changed`: the tier-preset switch, the adapter acts on it at the Session's next idle, §14.6, 18 until `context pending`'s plan-level `jobs` field (Plan `explore-view`): the adapter's Manager `Pending work:` digest reads it, §15.7, 21 until the agent key on every display surface: `session show` and `session list` carry `key` and `board take` and `board list` carry `from_name`, both read by the adapter, which also restores a fixed name and handles `key_fixed`, §10.1, §10a, §15.4), raised whenever an Event kind, an Event `data` field the pi adapter reads, or the output of a command the adapter runs changes in a way the adapter depends on (contract §5.2 "The protocol number"); the adapter checks it (§15.2). `--version` never creates, migrates or writes the database and runs neither the schema check nor the conversion. **The guards read `store`:** a driver or a Lead's wrapper reloads into a binary only when `store` is `null` or `store.opens` is `true` (contract §3.4, §6.7) and `scripts/install-cpd.sh` refuses a build whose `store.opens` is `false` and a Lead Branch build that carries a migration file that is not on `origin/main` (contract §3.7).

Every `--help` prints `{"ok": true, "help": "<clap's text>"}`. The root help (`cpd --help`, `cpd -h`, `cpd help`) adds `tree`: the whole command tree, every command whatever its depth, in clap's order, clap's own `help` subcommand left out. `cpd <group> --help` and `cpd help <group>` print `help` only. Each node is `{"name", "about", ...}`: `name` the command's word, `about` its one-line description (clap's, which ends with its § here). A runnable node (no subcommand, or subcommands that are optional, as `tui`) also has `callers`, `cockpit` and `internal` (§2). A node with subcommands has `commands`, its children. Example (trimmed with `...`):

```json
{"ok": true, "help": "...", "tree": [
  {"name": "context", "about": "Contexts and their records (commands.md §3)", "commands": [
    {"name": "new", "about": "Create a Context (§3.1)", "callers": ["Lead"], "cockpit": true, "internal": false}
  ]},
  {"name": "ask", "about": "Ask the Lead a question and wait for the answer (Worker) (commands.md §8.1)", "callers": ["Worker"], "cockpit": false, "internal": false},
  {"name": "tui", "about": "Build the cockpit and start the engine (commands.md §13)", "callers": [], "cockpit": false, "internal": false, "commands": [
    {"name": "view", "about": "A view in a cockpit pane (internal; owns its terminal) (§13.2)", "commands": [
      {"name": "tree", "about": "The session tree (left)", "callers": [], "cockpit": false, "internal": true}
    ]}
  ]}
]}
```

### 1.3 Selection and common refusals

- **Plan:** `--plan <id>`, else `CPD_PLAN`, else `plan_required` (exit 2) (§1.3).
- **Context:** `--context <id>`, else the Context of the selected Plan when a Plan is selected (by `--plan` or `CPD_PLAN`), else `context_required` (exit 2). New: a Lead's pane has `CPD_PLAN` set (§6.5), so it never needs to name its Context.
- **Session:** `--session <id>`, else `CPD_SESSION`, else `session_required` (exit 2). `CPD_SESSION` is set in every pane cpd starts (§6.5).
- **Session references** (hs-a3, hs-q3; agent keys, pro-d345, pro-d346): wherever a command takes a Session (`--session`, `CPD_SESSION`, or a Session argument), the value is parsed once, at the boundary, into a `SessionRef`, and resolved once into a `SessionId` (`core/src/session/resolve.rs`, `docs/implementing.md`). Every command section that takes a Session says it accepts **any form of §1.3**, which is this list. The forms are tried in this order; the first step that matches decides, and a step that matches nothing falls through to the next:

  1. **Exact Session id.** `sessions.id` equals the value (a UUID in practice). That Session.
  2. **Exact name.** `sessions.name` equals the value: an agent key (contract §2.2 "Agent key") or any other name. Several rows can share a name (every Attempt of a Job is named by the Worker key; a fork is named `<source name> (fork)`), so the candidates are ordered: live (`archived_at IS NULL`) first; then non-fork (`forked_from IS NULL`); then the highest Attempt number (`attempts.number` of the row's Attempt; a Worker row's `attempt` is `<job>-a<n>`); then the newest `created_at`; then `id`. The first candidate is the Session.
  3. **Legacy alias `<context>-manager`.** When form 2 matched nothing and a Context `<context>` exists: that Context's Manager Session, live first, then the newest `created_at`, then `id`.
  4. **Relative Plan.** The value has no `:`, the caller Session has a Context, and the value is a Plan id of that Context (`plans.context` = the caller's Context). The key `<caller context>:<value>`, resolved as form 2.
  5. **Relative Job.** The value has no `:`, the caller Session has a Plan, and the value is a Job key of that Plan. The key `<caller context>:<caller plan>:<value>`, resolved as form 2; a Job with no Worker Session yet falls through.
  6. **Legacy forms, unchanged.** A **Plan id** (any Plan) is that Plan's Lead Session, `plans.lead_session`. **`<plan>·<prefix>`** or **`<plan>.<prefix>`** (split at the first `·` or `.`; `.` because `·` is hard to type and Plan ids never contain either) is the Session of that Plan whose id starts with `<prefix>` (at least 1 character). A **bare id prefix of at least 4 characters** is the Session, of any Plan or none, whose id starts with it.

  **The caller** is the Session in `CPD_SESSION` (`session::sender()`). With none (the User at a terminal) or an unknown one, forms 4 and 5 are skipped.

  **Key syntax.** A value containing `:` is a key of 2 or 3 `:`-separated segments, valid as a Context id, then a Plan id, then a Job key (§2.1): two segments name a Lead (`<context>:<plan>`), three a Worker (`<context>:<plan>:<job>`). Any other value containing `:` is `invalid_session_id` (exit 2). No other form matches a value with `:`. A value without `:` must match the Session id pattern of §2.1, which accepts `cpd` and `cpd-manager`; else `invalid_session_id`.

  Matching is exact and case-sensitive. **Archived Sessions count** at every form; where a form has both, a live one beats an archived one. **Nothing matches:** `session_not_found` (exit 4). **Several Sessions match** a prefix form (6): `session_ambiguous` (exit 3) with `details.candidates`, never resolved by guessing. Output always carries the full id.
- **Workflow** (R34, §1.3): `--workflow <key>`, within the selected Plan, used by `job add`, `pr open`, `pr rebase`, `pr push`, `pr view`, `pr reply`, `pr rerun` and `pr post`. It may be omitted when the Plan has exactly one Workflow that is not `cancelled`, which is then selected; with two or more, `workflow_required` (exit 2); with none, `workflow_required` too, its message naming `cpd workflow add`. A key that is not one of the Plan's Workflows is `workflow_not_found` (exit 4). Exceptions, stated at each command: `pr poll` has no `--workflow`, it polls every open pull request of the User (§9.2, hs-d96) and `job edit --workflow` changes the Job's Workflow, so omitting it changes nothing (§5.2). `workflow add`, `workflow edit`, `workflow cancel` and `workflow start` take the key as their positional argument.
- **The Lead's Workflow** (contract §3.6, pro-d219, pro-d259): the Workflow of the Plan that the working Lead's current turn concerns, stored as `sessions.working_pr` and drawn as the Lead's dot (§13.2). Its definition is contract §3.6's. Only these commands name it, and only when the Plan's working Lead runs them: `job add`, `job edit`, `job cancel`, `job retry`, `job urgent`, `job approve-tests`, `answer`, `workflow add`, `workflow edit`, `workflow describe` and `workflow cancel`.
- **Job, Attempt, Escalation, Plan review:** a positional id, within the selected Plan (§2.1).

Common refusals, which apply to every command and are not repeated in the sections below:

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | 2 | unknown flag, missing argument, flag value of the wrong shape, exclusive flags together |
| `plan_required`, `context_required`, `session_required` | 2 | the command needs one and none was selected |
| `workflow_required` | 2 | the command needs a Workflow, `--workflow` is omitted and the Plan does not have exactly one Workflow that is not `cancelled` (R34) |
| `supersedes_invalid` | 3 | `context decide` or `context note` named, in `--supersedes`, a record whose kind it may not supersede, or a record twice (§3.5); `details: {record, kind, allowed}` |
| `supersedes_unlinked` | 3 | `context decide` or `context note` whose text names, after `supersedes`, `overrules` or `replaces`, a record in force of the Context that `--supersedes` does not list (§3.5, the prose check); `details: {ids}`, the unlisted ids in text order; nothing is written |
| `curation_not_pending` | 3 | `context retire` (§3.17) named a record that has no `pending` retirement: none, already decided, or not curated; `details: {record}`; nothing is written (hs-d551) |
| `explore_pending` | 3 | `plan phase plan` (§4.4) while a scout or research Job of the Plan is `queued`, `running` or `failed`; `details` `{plan, jobs}`, `jobs` the sorted keys of those Jobs; nothing is written (pro-d374) |
| `shaping_manager_only` | 2 | `plan new --shaping` (§4.1) run by anyone but the Context's live Manager (a Lead, a Worker or the User's cockpit): only a Manager creates a Lead-less shaping Plan (air-d19, air-d22); `details.caller` is the caller's role, or `null` when the caller is the User at a terminal; nothing is written |
| `plan_has_lead` | 3 | a Manager ran a shaping-Plan command (`job add`, `job list`, `job show`, `job cancel`, `job retry`, `attempt list`, `attempt show`, `attempt read`, `attempt abort` or `answer`; §4.1, §5.1 to §5.4, §6.2, §6.3, §6.5, §8.2) on a Plan that has a Lead (`lead_session` not null): a Manager never runs a Lead's command on it; `details.plan`; nothing is written (air-d19, air-d22) |
| `plan_other_context` | 2 | a Manager ran one of those commands on a shaping Plan of another Context; `details` `{plan, plan_context, context}`, `plan_context` the Plan's Context and `context` the Manager's; nothing is written (air-d19, air-d22) |
| `shaping_explore_only` | 2 | `job add` (§5.1) on a shaping Plan (`lead_session` null, phase `shaping` or `done`) with `--kind` other than `scout` or `research`, or with `--workflow`: a shaping Plan holds only explore Jobs; `details` `{plan, kind}` or `{plan, workflow}`; nothing is written (air-d19, air-d22) |
| `agent_forbidden` | 3 | `context archive`, `context unarchive`, `plan archive`, `plan unarchive`, `session archive`, `session unarchive` or `session resume` (§3.9, §3.10, §4.10, §4.11, §10.10, §10.11, §10.17) ran with `CPD_SESSION` or `CPD_ATTEMPT` set and non-empty in its environment: these commands are the User's and the engine's, not an agent's; refused before the Ledger is opened; message `cpd <command> is for the User and the engine, not an agent: Plans and Sessions archive on the engine's asleep -> archive schedule.`; `details` `{command, session, attempt}`, `session` and `attempt` the values of `CPD_SESSION` and `CPD_ATTEMPT`, or `null` when unset or empty |
| `user_only` | 3 | `context curation` or `context retire` (§3.16 to §3.17) ran with `CPD_SESSION` or `CPD_ATTEMPT` set in its environment: only the User decides what leaves the Context, so no agent's Session runs them (hs-d551); the cockpit's popups and views run without those variables (§3.15) |
| `args_invalid` | 2 | `context retire` (§3.17) named one id in both of its lists |
| `session_ambiguous` | 3 | a short Session id (§1.3) matches more than one Session; `details.candidates` lists their ids |
| `push_rejected` | 3 | `pr push` found the remote branch moved (§9.9); `details.stderr` is git's |
| `base_not_found` | 4 | `workflow add`, `workflow edit` (§9.4): the base branch does not exist; `pr open` (§9.1): the base branch of a stacked Workflow, its base Workflow's Lead Branch, is not on the remote (never for a `merged` base Workflow: that Workflow is unstacked first, hs-d301); `details` `{workflow, base, base_workflow}` (hs-d324). Not returned by an `open` or `update` Job's submit: the merge of that Job finds it (contract §7.4 step 6) and ends the Attempt `failed` / `gate_error` with it as the detail |
| `base_conflict` | 3 | `pr open` (§9.1, contract §7.6 step 1) found that the gated commit conflicts with `origin/<base>`, freshly fetched (`git merge-tree`); `details` is `{workflow, base, base_sha, sha, files, next}`, `files` the conflicted paths, `next` the commands the Lead runs, as written (hs-d490; it replaces hs-d329's `base_behind`, retired: a base that merely moved ahead refuses nothing). The merge of an `open` or `update` Job finds the same conflict at its step 6 (contract §7.4), not at submit: the Attempt ends `failed` / `merge_conflict` with the files in its detail |
| `workflow_not_open` | 3 | `pr reply` (§9.8a) and `pr rerun` (§9.8c) found the Workflow not `open`; `details` is `{workflow, status}` (pro-d68, pro-d155) |
| `approval_required` | 3 | `pr reply` (§9.8a), `pr post` (§9.8b) or `pr repost` (§9.8b2) ran with `CPD_SESSION` set and non-empty, the policy requires the User's approval (`pr.feedback.reply = bots_only` and the item is not a bot review thread, or `pr.post.require_approval` true) and the Session holds no live approval for that action (§9.8d, pro-d451); `details` `{workflow, to, kind: "reply"}` for a reply, `{workflow, kind: "post"}` for a post or repost; nothing is posted, sent or written |
| `feedback_not_found` | 3 | `pr reply` (§9.8a): `--to` is the `id` of no item in the Workflow's stored list; `details` is `{workflow, to, open: [ids]}`; nothing is posted (pro-d68) |
| `no_failed_run` | 3 | `pr rerun` (§9.8c) found no GitHub Actions workflow run of the Workflow's head commit failed; `details` is `{workflow, head_sha, runs: [{id, name, status, conclusion}]}`; nothing is re-run (pro-d155) |
| `pr_not_closed` | 3 | `workflow cancel` (§9.6) found the `open` Workflow's pull request not stored `closed`; `details` is `{workflow, number, url, state}`, the stored row's `state` (`open` or `merged`) (hs-d329) |
| `already_posted` | 3 | `pr post` (§9.8b) found a `pr_posts` row for the Workflow; `details` is `{workflow, channel, ts, link, posted_at}` (pro-d65) |
| `post_disabled` | 3 | `pr post` (§9.8b) found `policy.pr.post.enabled` is false; `details` is `{workflow, key: "pr.post.enabled"}` |
| `not_authored` | 3 | `pr post` (§9.8b) found the stored pull request is not `authored`; `details` is `{workflow, number}` |
| `post_unconfigured` | 3 | `pr post` (§9.8b) found no channel configured; `details` is `{keys: ["pr.post.channel", "inbox.team_channel"]}` |
| `pr_not_ready` | 3 | `pr post` (§9.8b) found `postable::unready(&row)` is not empty; `details` is `{workflow, number, url, reasons: [<as_str of each>, …]}`, the Unready reasons being `not_open`, `draft`, `conflicting`, `changes_requested`, `checks_failed`, `checks_pending`, `comments_unread`, `bot_comments` (pro-d64, contract §2.2, §8.3) |
| `base_workflow_unknown`, `base_workflow_unavailable`, `base_workflow_other_repo`, `workflow_other_plan` | 3 | `workflow add` or `workflow edit` (§9.4, §9.5) found a bad Workflow reference in `--base` or `--needs`: no such Workflow (`base_workflow_unknown`, the long form `--base <plan>/<key>` only); a base Workflow that is `cancelled` or `merged`; a base Workflow of another repo (`base_workflow_other_repo`, the long form only: a bare `--base <key>` of another repo is a branch, `base_not_found`); a Workflow of another Plan (`workflow_other_plan`, the long form or `--needs`) (contract §2.2 "A Workflow reference" and "Validation of a reference", hs-d522); `details` as at §9.4 |
| `stacked_rebase` | 3 | `pr rebase` (§9.3) found the Workflow stacked on a base Workflow; `details` is `{workflow, base, base_workflow, next}` (contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows" step 4, hs-d325) |
| `attempt_running` | 3 | `pr rebase` (§9.3) or `pr rebase --continue` found an Attempt of the Workflow of any kind (work, open, update) running (pro-d103, pro-d105); `details` is `{workflow, jobs: [keys], attempts: [ids]}`; nothing is changed, checked before the fetch; the message tells the Lead to steer the Worker to do the rebase instead |
| `needs_unavailable` | 3 | `job add` (A4, pro-d89): a named Job is `cancelled`, `failed`, a draft in a phase after plan, or an `open` or `update` Job; or in phase `dispatch` a failed Job has no fix appended yet (A4): that failed leaf refuses to queue a new Job that needs it; `details.jobs` lists them; may include `fix_job` with the Job key for the failed leaf |
| `invalid_context_id`, `invalid_plan_id`, `invalid_workflow_id`, `invalid_job_id`, `invalid_attempt_id`, `invalid_escalation_id`, `invalid_review_id`, `invalid_record_id` | 2 | an id does not match §2.1 |
| `invalid_session_id` | 2 | a Session reference (§1.3) matches neither the Session id pattern of §2.1 nor a key: a value with `:` that is not a key of 2 or 3 `:`-separated segments, valid as a Context id, then a Plan id, then a Job key (§2.1), or a value without `:` outside the Session id pattern |

### 1.4 Files written by commands

The `$CPD_HOME` layout is §1.4. Commands in this file write files the contract's layout does not list (amendment 4, §19); each is beside its peers and named so it cannot collide:

| File | Written by | Read by |
|---|---|---|
| `run/<plan>/lead-message.md` | `plan new` | the Plan's Lead `session run` and durable host startup (their first message, hs-d812) |
| `run/<context>/manager-message.md` | `context manager` (B3-A2) | the Manager's `session run` (its first message) |
| `run/<plan>/summary.md` | `plan render` (§4.5, hs-d502): the Plan summary of the Plan as it is, without a review | the User, the Lead |
| `run/<plan>/summary-<review>.md` | `plan review` (§4.6, hs-d502): a copy of the summary that a later render cannot change | the pi adapter, which shows it in the Lead's chat (§15.5) |
| `run/<plan>/feedback-<review>.md` | the pi adapter: the User's note from the chat dialog's Change, overwritten on a retry | `plan decide --feedback-file` |
| `run/<plan>/messages/<session>.md` | `session fork --message-file` copies the file here | that Session's `session run` |
| `vectors.db` (`$CPD_HOME`, with its `-wal` and `-shm`) | `context embed` (§3.19) and `context curate` (Experimental Feature `write_curation`; contract §4.6): the derived vector cache, safe to delete | `context curate`, `context search` (§3.4), `context embed` (§3.19) |
| `run/titles/<session>.log` | engine E10: the output of the `session retitle` runs it starts (hs-d257, contract §1.4); `locks/title-<session>.lock` is the run's own lock (§10.14) | the User |

### 1.5 Text arguments

Free text (Job `--title`, `--reason`, Context record text, Escalation questions and answers) is one argument, 1 to 20 000 characters, with no NUL; else `usage`. Context and Plan titles (`--title` of `context new`, `context rename`, `plan new`, `plan rename`) are 1–200 characters with no control characters, else `usage` (exit 2). Names (`--name`, `session rename`) are 1–80 characters with no control characters, else `invalid_name` (exit 2) (cpd 1 §11 `session rename`, kept). Files given by path (`--spec`, `--brief-file`, `--feedback-file`, `--message-file`) must be readable UTF-8, else `file_unreadable` (exit 2). A Workflow's title (`--title` of `workflow add` and `workflow edit`, hs-d285) is 1–72 characters on one line, with no control character; else `usage`. A Workflow's Jira ticket (`--jira` of `workflow add` and `workflow edit`) is a Jira key matching `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$`, else `usage`.

## 2. Command index

The index is generated: [docs/interface.md](interface.md), rendered from the `tree` of `cpd --help` (§1.2) by the test `cli/tests/interface.rs`, which fails when the page and the binary differ, either way; `CPD_BLESS=1 scripts/cargo.sh test -p cpd --test interface` rewrites the page; never edit it by hand.

**Definitions:**
- **callers** = the agents meant to run the command, any of `Lead`, `Manager`, `Worker`.
- **cockpit** = an action of the User's cockpit runs it (the cockpit is the User's interface over the same commands, §17 Actions).
- **internal** = §1.1.

Anyone may run any command; a command with no callers that is neither cockpit nor internal is the User's, at a shell (for example `doctor`). The callers and the cockpit flag are kept in the binary (`cli/src/interface.rs`), next to the clap tree. The table's Writes column (each command's Effects says what it writes) and Contract column (each description ends with its §) are not carried over (hs-d251).

## 3. `context`

A Context and its records (§2.2, §4.6). The records live only in the database and Contexts are machine-local (hs-a1). Every record write follows §4.6 exactly: one transaction that validates, inserts the `context_records` row and appends `context-record` `{record, kind, machine, seq}`. No lock file, no git, no file.

**Record ids.** `<machine>-<letter><n>` with `n` = 1 + the highest `n` already in this Context's records for this machine and letter (§2.1). The write transaction makes it race-free; only this machine writes its letter sequence.

**Retries.** A record write is recognised as a retry and returns the existing record with `"already": true`, when this machine's latest record in the Context has the same `kind`, `text`, `supersedes` and `by.session`. Also, a `decide` or `note` whose trimmed text and `supersedes` list equal an in-force record of the same kind (any machine or session) returns that record with `"already": true`; a different kind, list or text, or a record out of force does not dedupe. Any other write appends a new record; records are never edited.

### 3.1 `context new`

```
cpd context new <id> --title <text> --owner <login> [--jira <key>]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | Context id (§2.1) |
| `--title <text>` | required; 1–200 characters, no control characters, else `usage` (§1.5) |
| `--owner <login>` | required: the GitHub owner (user or organisation) of every repo the Context's Plans work on, its policy key (contract §8.3, hs-d288); a login of contract §2.1, else `usage`; stored lowercased |
| `--confirm-fallback` | optional: if the owner is unknown, create `policy/<login>/owner.toml` as a relative symlink to `../clayton-duarte/owner.toml` and proceed; if the owner is already known, the flag changes nothing (idempotent); if `policy/clayton-duarte/owner.toml` does not exist, fail `fallback_missing`. Without the flag, an unknown owner fails `owner_unconfirmed` |
| `--jira <key>` | Jira Epic key, stored only (`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$`, else `usage`) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| no Context row with this id, unless it has the same title, Jira key and owner | `context_exists` | 3 |
| no Plan row with this id, deleted ones included, unless a Context row with this id exists (then the rows above decide, so a rerun is `already`) | `id_taken` | 3 |
| the owner has a policy file, `$CPD_HOME/policy/<owner>/owner.toml` (contract §8.3; an empty file is the default policy), else with `--confirm-fallback` create it as a relative symlink to `../clayton-duarte/owner.toml`; without the flag, `owner_unconfirmed` if the owner is unknown (details: `owner`, `file`, `fallback`, `flag`); `fallback_missing` if the fallback owner's file does not exist; `details.owner` and `details.file` | `owner_unconfirmed` (1), `fallback_missing` (1) |
| that file, read as every resolve reads it, is valid; `details.file`, `details.key` | `policy_invalid` | 1 |

Effects:
- **Rows**, one transaction: `contexts` (`created_on` = `machine`, `owner`). **Event** `context-created` `{title, jira, created_on}`. Nothing else is written: no directory, no git.
- **tmux:** none.

```json
{"ok": true, "context": {"id": "building-cpd", "title": "Building cpd", "jira": null, "owner": "clayton-duarte", "created_at": "2026-10-14T21:10:00.000Z", "created_on": "hs"}}
```

Idempotent: yes. The same id, title, Jira key and owner return `"already": true`, also for a Context whose id a Plan holds: the two archived pairs `bifrost` and `gatemac` predate `id_taken` and are left as they are.

### 3.2 `context list`

```
cpd context list
```

No flags, no preconditions, no effects (one read transaction).

```json
{"ok": true, "contexts": [
  {"id": "building-cpd", "title": "Building cpd", "jira": null, "owner": "clayton-duarte", "archived_at": null,
   "records": 57,
   "plans": [{"id": "cpd2", "title": "cpd in Rust", "phase": "dispatch", "lead_session": "596d007f-…", "archived_at": null}]}],
 "events_cursor": 48213}
```

`owner` is the GitHub login of the Context's owner (contract §2.2), or null for a Context created before the migration. `archived_at` (here and on each Plan) is null, or the time the object was archived (contract §2.2 "Archived"). Archived Contexts and Plans are listed too. `events_cursor` is the highest Event id visible in the same read transaction (§17). Idempotent: read-only.

### 3.3 `context show`

```
cpd context show [<record>] [--context <id>] [--since <seq>] [--record <id>] [--topic <t>] [--all]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<record>` | positional, an alias of `--record <record>`: the same output and the same `record_not_found` (exit 3). Exclusive with `--record`, `--since` and `--topic` (`usage`, exit 2) |
| `--since <seq>` | only records whose index position `seq` is greater (exclusive, like `events --since`); what a Manager's turn-start update holds (§15.7); a Lead passes the `seq` it last read |
| `--record <id>` | print that one record in full (B3-A4): `records` has only it, `markdown` renders only it with its whole `text`. Exclusive with `--since` (`usage`). A record not in the Context: `record_not_found` (exit 3, §4.6). When `<id>`'s machine prefix is another machine's, the refusal adds `details.record_machine` and `details.local_machine` and its message is the cross-machine one below; a missing record of this machine keeps its error unchanged, with no machine details |
| `--topic <t>` | print every curated record in force of that topic, one per line `- [<id>] <short>` (contract §4.6, hs-d549, hs-d551), below. Exclusive with `--since` and `--record` (`usage`) |
| `--all` | a boolean: print the full history, the output bare `context show` had before the bounded view (Output, below; pro-d1, pro-d3): every section and every record, no `omitted`. Exclusive with `--since`, `--record` and `--topic` (`usage`, exit 2) |
| `--pushed` | with `--since <seq>` (`usage` without it): the call of pi's turn-start update (§15.7). It logs channel `pushed` for the records the output holds (Effects) |

**Callers** (Plan `explore-roles`, R10): the Lead and the Manager, as before and the **Worker**. An explore Worker (`scout` or `research`, §5.1) may run `context show` read-only, as its Spec's Deliverable section says; nothing enforces it (§2: anyone may run any command). Every other Worker's rule stays the Spec-only rule of the skill.

Effects: no Context record changes. Read log (best-effort): with a Session in `CPD_SESSION`, else `PI_SESSION_ID`, that parses as a SessionId and is a row of `sessions` (otherwise nothing is logged and nothing is an error; this is **the Session rule**, which §3.4, §3.5, §4.1, §5.1 and §10.13 refer to), it appends `context_reads` rows (contract §4.4, §4.6 "Reads"): channel `show` for `--record <id>` and for `--topic <t>`, one row per record shown; channel `pushed` for `--since <seq> --pushed`, one row per record the output holds; a bare `--since` without `--pushed` logs nothing. A failed log never fails the command and never changes its output or exit status. Output: the Context, its `records` and `markdown`, the rendering of §2.2 "Context record". Bare `context show` (no `--since`, `--record`, `--topic` or `--all`; `--context` and `--plan` only choose the Context) is the **bounded view**, decided by the User (Context records pro-d1 and pro-d3; assumptions A1 to A5 accepted with them). Its `markdown` renders these sections, in this order:

1. `# <title>` with the Jira key, as before.
2. `## Decisions`: every decision in force (not superseded, not retired), never capped. A superseded or retired decision is not shown here; it is counted in History.
3. `## Topics`: one line `topic (n), topic (n), ...`, the curated topics of the records in force with the number `n` of those records, in alphabetical order of topic (A5). It counts curated records only: a provisional topic (§3.3a) is not counted here, and `show --topic` is curated-only too. The section is absent when no curated record is in force.
4. `## Notes`: the notes in force (not superseded, not retired), capped to the newest 40 by `seq` (A1) and shown in `seq` order. When more exist, a footer line follows: `... <k> older notes omitted: cpd context show --topic <t> | cpd context search <query> | cpd context show --all`, `<k>` being the number left out.
5. `## Plans`: only the **active** Plans (A2). A Plan is done when this machine's `plans.done_at` is set for it; a done Plan is not listed (it is counted in History). A Plan of another machine, or one with no row in this machine's database, stays listed. Each listed Plan has its repos and its brief nested short, as the Plans and Briefs paragraphs below describe.
6. `## History (omitted; cpd context show --all renders it)`: one line per non-zero count, in this order: `- <n> superseded decisions`, `- <n> superseded notes`, `- <n> done plans`. A record is counted exactly where `--all` lists it: a superseded or retired decision under Superseded decisions, a superseded or retired note under Notes, a done Plan under Plans. The section is absent when all three counts are zero.

Each item shows its id and date, as in `--all`. Bare JSON (A3): `records` holds only the records the markdown shows, in `seq` order (the decisions in force, the notes in force within the cap, the listed Plans and their briefs); done Plans and their briefs, superseded or retired decisions, superseded or retired notes and the notes beyond the cap are absent. It also carries `omitted`, an object whose keys are always all present: `{"superseded_decisions": n, "superseded_notes": n, "older_notes": n, "done_plans": n}`, the number of records left out of each kind, `older_notes` being the notes in force beyond the cap.

`--all` is the full history: `markdown` renders every record under the sections Plans, Decisions, Superseded decisions and Notes (each superseded or retired record labelled and naming its successor, as before), `records` holds every record in `seq` order, and there is no `omitted`. `--all` is exclusive with `--since`, `--record` and `--topic` (`usage`, exit 2). `--since`, `--record` and `--topic` are unchanged: with `--since`, `markdown` renders only the records after the cursor, in the same order of sections as `--all`. The Briefs and Plans paragraphs below describe the Plans listed; in the bare view a done Plan and its brief are not listed.

**Briefs** (B3-A4): a record of kind `brief` is listed **short**, in `markdown` and in `records`: its id and the first line of its `text`, under its Plan (the Plan's section), never in full. In `records` its `text` is that first line and the entry has `"short": true`; its `plan` is `{id, machine}`. The full text is `cpd context show --record <id>`. `--record` is the only way to get a brief whole.

**Plans** (R34, A12): each `plan` record is listed with the repos of its Plan's Workflows that are not `cancelled`, read from this machine's database (`workflows.repo`) in the same read transaction, each repo once, in Workflow key order; a Plan of another machine, or one with no Workflow yet, shows none. The record itself carries no repo (§2.2; a `repo` in a record written before R34 was dropped by migration 0007's import, contract §4.5). In `records`, a `plan` record's `plan` is `{id, machine, jira}` and the entry has `repos`, the list just described.

```json
{"ok": true, "context": {"id": "building-cpd", "title": "Building cpd", "jira": null},
 "records": [{"seq": 42, "id": "hs-d7", "kind": "decision", "at": "2026-10-14T21:12:00.000Z", "machine": "hs",
              "by": {"session": "596d007f-…", "plan": "cpd2"}, "text": "One engine per machine.", "supersedes": ["hs-d2"]}],
 "markdown": "# Building cpd\n\n## Plans\n…"}
```

Idempotent: read-only.



**`--topic <t>`** (FX5 of hs-d549, hs-d551): prints every curated record in force of the topic `<t>` (the exact topic string of `record_curations`), oldest first, one per line `- [<id>] <short>`; the way to read what the digest leaves out. `markdown` is those lines and `records` the list `{id, short}`. FX5: an unknown topic (no curated record in force has that topic) is refused `topic_not_found` (exit 4, `details: {context, topic, topics}`, the topics in use). Read-only.

```json
{"ok": true, "context": {"id": "building-cpd", "title": "Building cpd", "jira": null}, "topic": "engine",
 "records": [{"id": "hs-d7", "short": "one engine per machine"}],
 "markdown": "- [hs-d7] one engine per machine"}
```

**`--record` of another machine's record** (decision pro-d2, User, 2026-11-03): Contexts are machine-local (contract §4.6), so a record exists only on the machine that wrote it. When `<id>`'s machine prefix (the part before `-<letter><n>`, §2.1) differs from this machine's `config.machine`, `context show --record <id>` is `record_not_found` (exit 3) with `details` `{context, record, record_machine, local_machine}`: `record_machine` the id's machine prefix, `local_machine` this machine's configured name. Its message is exactly `Context <context> has no record <id>. <id> belongs to machine <record_machine>; this machine is <local_machine>, and Contexts are machine-local, so another machine's records cannot be read here. The authoritative contract is in CONTEXT.md and docs/contract.md.`, with the placeholders filled. A missing record of **this** machine is unchanged: `record_not_found` (exit 3) with `details` `{context, record}` only and the message `Context <context> has no record <id>.`. Only `show --record` carries the machine details; the `--supersedes` refusals of §3.5 are unchanged.

```json
{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "record_not_found", "message": "Context building-cpd has no record pro-d7. pro-d7 belongs to machine pro; this machine is hs, and Contexts are machine-local, so another machine's records cannot be read here. The authoritative contract is in CONTEXT.md and docs/contract.md.", "details": {"context": "building-cpd", "record": "pro-d7", "record_machine": "pro", "local_machine": "hs"}}}
```

### 3.3a `context topics`

```
cpd context topics [--context <c>] [--plan <id>]
```

Lists the **topics in force** of the Context (contract §4.6): each topic that a record in force carries, with the count of those records. A record is counted **once**, under its curated topic (`record_curations`, §3.13a) if it has one, else under its provisional topic (`record_topics`, §3.13a). So the counts can exceed what `context show --topic` lists: `show --topic` is curated-only (§3.3), so a topic listed here can be one it refuses as `topic_not_found` (C5 of Plan `ctx-topics-surface`). The Context is `--context`, else the Context of the selected Plan (`--plan`, or `CPD_PLAN`, §1.3).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| a Context was selected (§1.3) | `context_required` | 2 |
| the Context exists | `context_not_found` | 4 |

No new error code. **Callers** (as `context show`, §3.3): the Lead, the Manager and the **Worker**.

Effects: none. Output: `topics` sorted by topic (the topic string, ascending), each `{topic, count}`, `count` the number of records in force with that topic, each record counted once under its topic (C5, above). `markdown` is one line, the topics comma-separated, each as `<topic> (<count>)` with no `- ` prefix, for example `engine (3), store (1)`; the same line is the `Topics:` line of the first messages (§3.11, §4.1). A Context with no record in force that has a topic gives `topics: []` and `markdown: ""`; that is not an error.

```json
{"ok": true, "context": {"id": "building-cpd", "title": "Building cpd", "jira": null},
 "topics": [{"topic": "engine", "count": 3}, {"topic": "store", "count": 1}],
 "markdown": "engine (3), store (1)"}
```

Idempotent: read-only.

### 3.4 `context search`

```
cpd context search <query> [--context <id>] [--limit <n>] [--kind <k,k>] [--all]
```

Searches the Context's records by their id, topic, short form and text, ranked by an in-memory FTS5 index that is built on each call and never stored (contract §4.6 "The search rail"; hs-d655: on-demand retrieval; pro-d9). The Context is `--context`, else the selected Plan's (§1.3).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| a Context was selected (§1.3) | `context_required` | 2 |
| the selected Plan exists (when the Context comes from `--plan` or `CPD_PLAN`) | `plan_not_found` | 4 |
| the Context exists | `context_not_found` | 4 |
| the query is empty after trimming | `usage` (`details.query`) | 2 |
| the query is malformed FTS5, such as an unbalanced parenthesis or `NEAR(` among the kept operators: SQLite refuses it | `usage` (`details.query`, `details.message`, SQLite's message) | 2 |
| a `--kind` value is not a record kind | `usage` (`details.kind`) | 2 |

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<query>` | the search text. Words are text: an id such as `hs-d655`, a dotted or slashed token or an apostrophe is quoted for you, never FTS5 syntax. `"a phrase"`, `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, `NEAR(..)`, parentheses and a trailing `*` (prefix match) are kept. The operators and the rewrite are in docs/research/context-holographic.md `## Search contract` |
| `--limit <n>` | at most `n` records, default `20`; `0` is every match. Applied after rule (b) below |
| `--kind <k,k>` | only these record kinds, comma-separated; default `decision,note,question,answer` |
| `--all` | include the records that the selection below would hide (rule (a): out of force, or a pending duplicate or superseded retirement), each labelled as `context show` labels it. Without it they are hidden |

**Ranking.** The index is one FTS5 table over the Context's records, columns `id`, `topic`, `short` and `text` (tokenizer `porter unicode61`). `topic` and `short` are the record's curation (`record_curations`, §4.6 "The distiller curates"); an uncurated record has empty ones. Hits are ordered by `bm25` with the weights 10 for `id`, 2 for `topic`, 2 for `short` and 1 for `text`, lower first; the score shown is `-bm25`, higher is better. A record whose id equals the trimmed query, compared case-insensitively, is always first, with a score at least the top score (so `search pro-d300` returns `pro-d300` first, though other records quote it). Equal scores put the newer record (higher `seq`) first. In `hybrid` mode (below) the order and the scores are the Reciprocal Rank Fusion of the lexical and the semantic lists (contract §4.6 "The vector leg").

**Selection**, two rules (contract §4.6 "The search rail"):
- **(a) Before ranking, without `--all`:** a record is hidden when it is out of force (a superseded record, or one with an approved retirement) or when it has a `pending` `record_retirements` row whose reason is `duplicate` or `superseded`. Its target stays visible. A `pending` `documented` row hides nothing. A record whose id is the typed query is exempt from the pending rule.
- **(b) After ranking:** a hit whose score is below `0.35` times the top hit's score is dropped (no hit is dropped when the top score is 0 or less). The record named by the query id is exempt. Zero hits is a valid answer, not an error. In `hybrid` mode this rule floors the lexical list before the fusion, and `--limit` is applied after the fusion.

**Callers** (Plan `explore-roles`, R10): as `context show` (§3.3): the Lead, the Manager and the **Worker**. An explore Worker (`scout` or `research`) may run it read-only, as its Spec's Deliverable section says; nothing enforces it (§2).

**Output** (`ok` true, the data):

```json
{"context": {"id": "host", "title": "…", "jira": null}, "query": "decision", "mode": "fts", "records": [{"id": "hs-d7", "topic": null, "short": "one engine per machine", "kind": "decision", "at": "…", "seq": 7, "score": 1.8, "in_force": true}], "markdown": "- [hs-d7] one engine per machine"}
```

`records` holds the hits in rank order, with `topic` the record's topic as a string, or `null` when it has none (its curated topic, else its provisional topic, §3.13a; C7 of Plan `ctx-topics-surface`); `short` the curated short form, else the record's first line at most 120 bytes; `in_force` is false only with `--all`. `markdown` is one `- [<id>] <short>` line per hit, or `- [<id>] [<topic>] <short>` when the hit has a topic (curated or provisional), with ` (superseded by <id>)` after a superseded record and ` [retired (<reason> <target>)]` after one with an approved retirement, as `context show` labels them. Both are empty on no hits.

**Mode** (contract §4.6 "The vector leg"): `mode` is `fts` when the Context has no vectors for the embedder's model (the embedder is never called); `hybrid` when it has them and the query was embedded: the lexical and the semantic lists are fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion, k = 60, and each `score` is then an RRF score, about 0.01 to 0.03, which must not be compared with a bm25 score; `fts-only` when it has them but the query could not be embedded: the result is the lexical list alone and `semantic_error` is the embedder's code (`embedding_unreachable`, `embedding_refused` or `embedding_bad_reply`, contract §4.6). `semantic_error` is present only with `fts-only`. The embedder never fails the search.

Effects: no Context record changes. Read log (best-effort, the Session rule of §3.3): with a Session, one `context_reads` row per returned hit, channel `search`, `rank` its 1-based position in the returned list and `score` the hit's score (contract §4.6 "Reads"). The index is built in memory for each search and no record is stored. A `hybrid` search starts one embedder call; search never embeds records and never writes a record vector (contract §4.6 "The vector leg").

**Search log** (Plan `ctx-observability`, pro-d13). Every search, with or without a Session, appends one `search_log` row to `$CPD_HOME/vectors.db` (contract §4.6 "The search log"), best-effort like the read log: a failed write never fails or changes the search, its output or its exit status, and the file is created by the first search if it is absent. The row holds the query, the `mode` (`fts` or `hybrid`; a `fts-only` search is logged as `fts`), the counts `candidates`, `floor_dropped`, `pending_hidden` and `hits` (defined in contract §4.6 "The search log"), `fts_ms`, and, when the query was embedded, `embed_ms` and `embed_tokens`. The output of `search` does not change. `cpd context stats` (§3.20) reads the log.

Output: `context` is `{id, title, jira}`; `query` is the query as trimmed; `records` is a list of `{id, topic, short, kind, at, seq, score, in_force}`: `topic` is the record's topic as a string, or `null` when it has none (its curated topic, else its provisional topic, else `null`; C7 of Plan `ctx-topics-surface`); `short` is the record's curated short form, else the first line of its text cut at 120 bytes, `at` its time, `seq` its index position, `score` the engine's score (an RRF score in `hybrid` mode, below); `in_force` is whether the record is in force. `markdown` is one line per record, `- [<id>] [<topic>] <short>` when the record has a topic (curated, else provisional) and `- [<id>] <short>` when it has none, with the out-of-force labels of `context show` (§3.3) after the line, joined by newlines.

```json
{"ok": true, "context": {"id": "building-cpd", "title": "Building cpd", "jira": null}, "query": "engine", "mode": "fts",
 "records": [{"id": "hs-d7", "topic": null, "short": "one engine per machine", "kind": "decision", "at": "2026-10-14T21:12:00.000Z", "seq": 42, "score": 1.5, "in_force": true}],
 "markdown": "- [hs-d7] one engine per machine"}
```

Idempotent: yes; a rerun with nothing new to index returns the same records.

### 3.5 `context decide`, `context note`

```
cpd context decide <text> [--supersedes <record>]... [--no-supersedes] [--context <id>]
cpd context note <text> [--supersedes <record>]... [--no-supersedes] [--context <id>]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<text>` | the record's `text` (§1.5) |
| `--supersedes <record>` | `decide` and `note`: the id of an earlier record this one replaces (recency wins, contract §2.2). Repeatable: `--supersedes hs-d2 --supersedes hs-d5`, or the comma form `--supersedes hs-d2,hs-d5` (ids hold no comma), or both. A decision may replace a decision or a note of the Context; a note may replace a note only |
| `--no-supersedes` | `decide` and `note`: a bool flag that confirms the text names no record this one replaces, so the prose check below is skipped. Conflicts with `--supersedes` (`usage`) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| each `--supersedes` record is a record of this Context | `record_not_found` | 3 |
| `--supersedes` names one record twice, by repeating it or in the comma form | `supersedes_invalid` | 3 |
| `--supersedes` on a `note` names a record that is not a `note`, or on a `decide` names a record that is neither a `decision` nor a `note` | `supersedes_invalid` | 3 |
| the text names, after `supersedes`, `overrules` or `replaces`, an unlinked record (below) and `--no-supersedes` is not given | `supersedes_unlinked` | 3 |

`supersedes_invalid` has `details: {record, kind, allowed}`: the id named, its kind and the kinds the writing record may supersede (`["decision", "note"]` for `decide`, `["note"]` for `note`). Every target is validated on its own, in `--supersedes` order. Nothing is written. A record superseded by a decision or note leaves force and every digest, stays readable and `context show` labels it superseded, naming its successor (§3.3).

**Prose supersession** (D4). A text that says it replaces a record without listing it is refused, so that every supersession is linked. The check runs after the retry check (below) and before the write:

- A **phrase** is one of the verbs `supersedes`, `overrules` or `replaces` (case-insensitive), followed by one or more record ids (§2.1) joined by `,`, `and` or `&`, for example `supersedes pro-d344 and pro-d341`. The ids of a phrase are those directly after its verb, up to the first word that is neither an id nor a joiner.
- A named id is **unlinked** when it is an in-force record of this Context whose kind the new record may supersede (for `decide`, a decision or a note; for `note`, a note) and `--supersedes` does not list it. An id of another Context, a record out of force (superseded or retired), or a record of a kind the new record may not supersede is not unlinked, and no refusal follows from it.
- Any unlinked id makes the write fail `supersedes_unlinked` (exit 3), `details.ids` the unlinked ids in text order. Nothing is written.
- A partial amendment is not a phrase: in `supersedes A1 of pro-d342` no record id follows the verb, so nothing is matched.
- `--no-supersedes` skips the check, whatever the text says.
- The retry is decided first: an identical latest record is returned as `already` even when its text would fail the check.


Effects: the record write above (one transaction), with kind `decision` (letter `d`) or `note` (`n`); `by` = `{session: CPD_SESSION or PI_SESSION_ID or null, plan: the selected Plan or null}`; `supersedes` = the ids named, in order, stored as one comma list (contract §4.4). **Event** `context-record`. No tmux. Then, best-effort, the citation marking (the Session rule of §3.3): for the writing Session, `used` = 1 on its `context_reads` rows of each record it read whose id the new record's text cites (`RecordId::scan`, contract §2.1), except the new record's own id and its `--supersedes` targets. The User (no Session) marks nothing. A failed marking never fails the command or changes its output or exit status.

```json
{"ok": true, "record": {"id": "hs-d8", "kind": "decision", "at": "2026-10-14T21:30:00.000Z", "machine": "hs", "by": {"session": "596d007f-…", "plan": "cpd2"}, "text": "…", "supersedes": ["hs-d2", "hs-d5"]}, "seq": 58}
```

`supersedes` is an array of id strings, absent when the record replaces none. It was a single string before `context-supersedes-list` (contract §4.5): a reader that expects a string breaks on it.

Idempotent: a retry is recognised (above); otherwise each call inserts a record, by design (records are never edited).

### 3.6 `context answer`

```
cpd context answer <question> <text> [--context <id>]
```

`<question>` is the record id of the question.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `<question>` is a record of this Context of kind `question` | `record_not_found` | 3 |
| no answer in this Context's records names it yet | `question_answered` | 3 |

Effects: the record write with kind `answer` (letter `a`) and `question` = `<question>`; **Event** `context-record`. Then the citation marking of §3.5 (best-effort, the same rule; there is no `--supersedes`).

```json
{"ok": true, "record": {"id": "hs-a2", "kind": "answer", "at": "…", "machine": "hs", "by": {"session": "596d007f-…", "plan": "cpd2"}, "text": "Yes, per machine.", "question": "hs-q3"}, "seq": 59}
```

Idempotent: a retry is recognised; a second, different answer is refused. Contexts are machine-local, so only this machine answers.

### 3.7 `context sync`

Removed by Plan manager B1 (hs-a1): Contexts are machine-local; records live in the database. The command is now unknown (`usage`, exit 2); engine E6 is removed with it (contract §3.7).

### 3.8 `context rename`

```
cpd context rename <id> --title <text>
```

Changes the Context's visible label (contract §2.2: ids are immutable, titles editable). `--title` is required, as `context new`'s: 1–200 characters, no control characters, else `usage` (§1.5).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Context is not a Permanent Context (`cpd`, `host`, `codereview`), checked first; `details.context` | `context_permanent` | 3 |
| the Context exists | `context_not_found` | 4 |

Effects: an unchanged title: `"already": true`, nothing written. Otherwise **rows**, one transaction: `contexts.title`; **Event** `context-renamed` `{title}`. Only the database changes.

```json
{"ok": true, "context": {"id": "building-cpd", "title": "Building cpd 2"}}
```

Idempotent: yes.

### 3.9 `context archive`

```
cpd context archive <id>
```

Archives the Context with its Plans, all their Sessions and its Manager (contract §2.2 "Archived").

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the caller is not an agent: neither `CPD_SESSION` nor `CPD_ATTEMPT` is set and non-empty (checked first, before the Ledger is opened); `details` `{command, session, attempt}`, `session` and `attempt` the values of those variables or `null` | `agent_forbidden` | 3 |
| the Context is not a Permanent Context (`cpd`, `host`, `codereview`), checked after the agent check above; `details.context` | `context_permanent` | 3 |
| the Context exists | `context_not_found` | 4 |
| the archive rule holds for the whole cascade, all or nothing (contract §2.2 "Archived"): (a) no Session of the cascade (the Manager, and each Plan's Lead and side forks) is `working`, `waiting` or `blocked`; (b) every Workflow of those Plans is `merged` or `cancelled`, and no `cancelled` one has an `open` pull request; (c) no Job of those Plans is `queued`, `running` or `failed`, and none is `draft` (hs-d731: `plan cancel` abandons a Plan, `job cancel` one draft); (d) no Escalation of those Plans is `open` and no Plan review is `pending`. An open Inbox item does not block it, and neither does a Plan not in phase `done` (pro-d421; E8 closes the Inbox items of an archived Session). The automatic sleep and archive of E13 and E14 (`LEAD_FINISHED`, §3.7) still require phase `done` and no open undismissed Inbox item. A Workflow of one of those Plans that a Workflow of a Plan outside the Context names as base Workflow or need blocks too (hs-d324); the Context's Plans archive together, so they never block each other. `details.blockers` lists each as `{kind, id, plan?, reason}`: kind `session` (`Session <name> is <state>.`), `workflow` (`id` the Workflow key, `plan` the Plan id, `Workflow <key> of Plan <plan> is <status>.`, or `Workflow <key> of Plan <plan> is cancelled with an open pull request.`), `job` (`id` the Job key, `plan` the Plan id, `Job <key> of Plan <plan> is <status>.` for `queued`, `running` and `failed`; a `draft` one is `{kind: "job", id: "<plan>/<key>", reason: "draft"}`), and `escalation` and `review` (as before) | `archive_blocked` | 3 |
| no Lead of the cascade is in the chat slot; `details.next` = `cpd session park` | `in_chat_slot` | 3 |

The engine archives on its own (E12 Worker archive, E14 Plan archive after sleep, contract §3.7); the User archives from the cockpit or the CLI.

Effects, in this order (all or nothing):
1. **Check** every object of the cascade. If any blocks, nothing is written and nothing is closed.
2. **tmux:** close every live Lead pane exactly as `session close` does (§10.9): `kill-pane`, `state = stopped`, `tmux_pane = NULL`, with its `session-state` and `session-moved` Events. pi stops; the session files stay.
3. **Rows**, one transaction that re-checks the rule first (`archive_blocked` if something became live meanwhile): `archived_at` = now on the Context, on each of its Plans and on each Session of the cascade, that is not archived yet. One **Event** per object changed: `context-archived` `{archived: true}`, `plan-archived`, `session-archived`. A durable Session of the cascade (its Manager included) has its host stopped within one engine tick of this step (contract §6.19).

```json
{"ok": true, "archived": [{"kind": "context", "id": "building-cpd"}, {"kind": "plan", "id": "cpd2"}, {"kind": "session", "id": "596d007f-…"}], "closed": ["%41"]}
```

`closed` lists the panes closed in step 2. Idempotent: yes; a Context that is archived already (and whose cascade has nothing to archive) returns `"already": true`, writes nothing and closes nothing.

### 3.10 `context unarchive`

```
cpd context unarchive <id>
```

Clears `archived_at` on the Context and, with the same cascade as `context archive`, on its Plans and Sessions. Unchanged for a Permanent Context: `context_permanent` (§3.8) is not checked here.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the caller is not an agent: neither `CPD_SESSION` nor `CPD_ATTEMPT` is set and non-empty (checked first, before the Ledger is opened); `details` `{command, session, attempt}`, `session` and `attempt` the values of those variables or `null` | `agent_forbidden` | 3 |
| the Context exists | `context_not_found` | 4 |

The engine archives on its own (E12 Worker archive, E14 Plan archive after sleep, contract §3.7); the User archives from the cockpit or the CLI.

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: `archived_at = NULL` on the Context and every archived Plan and Session of the cascade; one **Event** per object changed (`context-archived`, `plan-archived`, `session-archived`, each with `{archived: false}`). No tmux: no pane is touched and `session open` resumes a Lead later (§10.4). No archive rule applies.

```json
{"ok": true, "archived": [{"kind": "context", "id": "building-cpd"}, {"kind": "plan", "id": "cpd2"}, {"kind": "session", "id": "596d007f-…"}], "closed": []}
```

`archived` lists the objects changed (their `archived_at` is now null); `closed` is always empty. Idempotent: yes; nothing archived: `"already": true`, nothing written.

### 3.11 `context manager`

```
cpd context manager [--context <c>] [--by-user] [--runner <pi|durable>]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--by-user` | (hs-d542 A2) when registering a new Manager, stores the flag on the Session and writes no first message (§1.4); `plan new` and `context manager` use it (§4.1); omit it and the Manager starts with its first message, as today |
| `--runner <pi|durable>` | the new Manager's runner; default the config key `manager_runner`, default `pi` (contract §6.19). `experimental.durable_leads` does not apply to a Manager (contract §6.19 "The config keys"). Only on registration: a resume keeps the stored `sessions.runner` and a `--runner` that differs from it is refused (`usage`, exit 2) |

Gets the Context's **Manager** (B3-A1, B3-A2; CONTEXT.md "Manager"): registers and starts it when the Context has none, starts it again when it is stopped. The Context is `--context`, else the selected Plan's (§1.3).

**A Permanent Context** (`cpd`, `host`, `codereview`; contract §2.2 "Permanent Contexts") first runs **ensure** (contract §3.7 E22, the function the engine runs every tick): it creates the Context's row when missing, clears its `archived_at` (the row only, never its Plans' or Sessions'), and registers a `stopped` Manager, with no pane, when the Context has no live one (`by_user` 0, so its first message is written; tier `manager_tier`; runner `manager_runner`). A live Manager in any state is left alone. Then the rules below apply to the Manager as to any Context's: a Manager that is stopped with no pane gets its pane. So a Permanent Context that was never created, or whose row is archived, starts here.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Context exists (a Permanent Context is ensured first, so it exists) | `context_not_found` | 4 |
| the Context is not archived (a Permanent Context's row is unarchived by ensure); `details.next` = `cpd context unarchive <c>` | `archived` | 3 |
| a Permanent Context's row is deleted (`deleted_at` set): ensure refuses, an id is never reused | `context_exists` | 3 |
| a Manager is registered and `HOME` is not known: its `cwd`, the User's home directory, cannot be read | `usage` | 2 |
| the cockpit's tmux session exists when a pane must be started; `details.next` = `cpd tui` | `no_cockpit` | 3 |
| `--runner` is neither `pi` nor `durable`, or a `--runner` on an existing Manager differs from the stored `sessions.runner` (the message names the stored runner) | `usage` | 2 |

Effects, by the state of the Context's live (not archived) Manager Session:
- **None:** **rows**, one transaction: `sessions` (new UUID v4; `role = manager`; `context`; `plan` null; `name` = `<context>` (the Manager's agent key, contract §2.2 "Agent key"); `cwd` = the User's home directory (`$HOME`, canonicalized when that works; contract §2.2, pro-d343), never the caller's directory or `$CPD_HOME`; `tier` = config `manager_tier`, default `O5`; `runner` = the `--runner` flag, else config `manager_runner`, default `pi` (contract §6.19); `forked_from` null; `by_user` = 1 when `--by-user`, else 0; `stopped`); **Event** `session-registered` `{role, name, forked_from, tier}`. Then **tmux**, as `plan new` starts a Lead (§4.1 step 4): `new-window -d -t =cpd: -n ctx-<context> -c <cwd> -e CPD_HOME=… -e CPD_SESSION=<session> -P -F '#{window_id} #{pane_id}' -- cpd session run <session>`, `@cpd_session` on the pane (no `CPD_PLAN`); one transaction: `sessions.tmux_pane`, **Event** `session-moved` `{pane, window, place: "parked"}`. When `by_user` is 1, no first message is written; when it is 0, its first message is written to `run/<context>/manager-message.md` (§1.4): `You are the Manager of Context <c> "<title>". Follow the cpd-manager skill.`, then, when `context topics` (§3.3a) has at least one topic, the `Topics:` line between the header and the pointer line (`Topics: engine (3), store (1)`, the same line as `plan new` gives it, §4.1 step 3 and §3.3a; a snapshot at write time, no cap; its counts follow C5 of §3.3a), then the on-demand pointer (hs-d655) `Context on demand: cpd context search <query> --context <c> · cpd context show --context <c> --since <seq> · cpd context show --context <c> --record <id>` (contract §4.6 "Consumers"). No digest and no records are written: the Manager reads the Context on demand. **For a durable Manager** (`runner` `durable`, contract §6.19) the tmux step and its `session-moved` are skipped: the new Session is left live and `stopped` and the engine's hosts step starts its host at the next tick, with a null `pane`/`window` in the output.
- **`stopped` with no pane:** the tmux step alone, in the stored `cwd`: `session run` resumes pi on its session file (`pi --session <file>`, §6.5), with no first message. A durable Manager is started by the engine's hosts step instead, not here; a resume keeps the stored `sessions.runner` (it never changes after creation, contract §6.19).
- **Otherwise** (it has a pane): nothing.

The command never moves the chat slot (hs-d103); `session open <manager>` does (§10.4).

```json
{"ok": true, "manager": {"session": "3c9a…", "name": "building-cpd", "state": "stopped", "pane": "%47", "window": "@21"}, "started": true}
```

`started` is true when this call registered the Manager or started its pane. Idempotent: yes; a Manager with a pane returns `"started": false` and writes nothing.

### 3.12 `context pending`

```
cpd context pending [--context <c>] [--markdown]
```

The in-flight work of a Context (hs-d159, P1; CONTEXT.md "Pending work"): what its active Plans have started and not yet landed on the base. The Manager runs it before starting or routing work for an issue, to see whether something already fixes or changes it. The Context is `--context`, else the selected Plan's (§1.3).

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--markdown` | also print the result as markdown, instead of JSON |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| a Context was selected (§1.3) | `context_required` | 2 |
| the Context exists | `context_not_found` | 4 |

An archived Context is not refused: it has no active Plan to list unless one was left active.

Effects: none. One read transaction, no write, no subprocess (no `git`, no `gh`): everything comes from the database, so the GitHub state is the last one `pr poll` stored.

Output: `plans`, every Plan of the Context that is not `done` and not archived, in creation order, each with `id`, `title`, `phase`, `lead_session` and `workflows`: its Workflows that are not `merged` (cancelled ones included), in key order, each with `key`, `repo`, `base`, `status`, `lead_branch`, `pull_request` (`{number, url, state}` as stored by `pr poll`, or null before its pull request is opened), `waiting_on` (hs-d521: blockers of this Workflow, absent when none) and `jobs`: the Workflow's Jobs that are not `cancelled` and not yet on the base, in `seq` order, with status `draft`, `queued`, `running`, `failed`, `merged` or `waiting` (hs-d523: display only, waiting on a Dependency or Workflow that has not started). Here `merged` means on the Lead Branch and not yet on the base (§2.2 Job). Each Job has `key`, `status`, `title`, `touches` and `waiting_on` (hs-d521: the blocker keys, absent when none or status is not `waiting`).

**The plan-level `jobs` array** (Plan `explore-view`). Beside `workflows`, every Plan of the output also carries `jobs`: its explore Jobs (`scout`, `research`; contract §2.2 "Job kinds") that are not `cancelled`, in `seq` order, each with `key`, `kind`, `status`, `tier`, `title`, `touches` and `waiting_on`. `status` is the display status: `waiting` when the Job is not Ready, the same rule as a Workflow Job's (contract §3.2 "Display status: waiting"), else the stored status. `tier` is the Tier the Job is displayed at (contract §3.4a). `touches` is the Job's parsed JSON (`[]` when null). `waiting_on` is present only when non-empty (the explore Dependencies that hold it). A Plan with only explore Jobs and no Workflow is listed like any other Plan, with an empty `workflows`: it is not empty output, and its `jobs` are its content. A **Lead-less** Plan (`lead_session` null, phase `shaping`; air-d19, air-d22) is listed the same way: `lead_session` is `null`, `workflows` is `[]`, and its explore Jobs are its `jobs`. A Lead-less Plan in `done` is excluded like any done Plan.

```json
{"ok": true, "context": "building-cpd",
 "plans": [{"id": "pay-4521", "title": "Retry failed payments", "phase": "dispatch", "lead_session": "596d007f-…",
            "jobs": [{"key": "scout-retry", "kind": "scout", "status": "running", "tier": "H2",
                      "title": "Scout the retry paths", "touches": []},
                     {"key": "research-idem", "kind": "research", "status": "waiting", "tier": "S2",
                      "title": "Research idempotency keys", "touches": ["docs/"], "waiting_on": ["scout-retry"]}],
            "workflows": [{"key": "api", "repo": "/home/clayton/projects/api", "base": "main", "status": "dispatch",
                     "lead_branch": "pay-4521/api", "pull_request": {"number": 212, "url": "https://github.com/acme/api/pull/212", "state": "OPEN"},
                     "jobs": [{"key": "retry-core", "status": "merged", "title": "Retry policy", "touches": ["src/retry.rs"]},
                              {"key": "retry-cli", "status": "waiting", "title": "Retry flag", "touches": ["src/cli.rs", "docs/commands.md"], "waiting_on": ["retry-core"]}]},
                    {"key": "old", "repo": "/home/clayton/projects/api", "base": "main", "status": "cancelled", "pull_request": null,
                     "waiting_on": [],
                     "jobs": []}]}]}
```

With `--markdown` the output is the same data as markdown: `# Pending work in <context>`, then per Plan `## <id> (<phase>): <title>`, per Workflow `### Workflow <key> (<repo>, base <base>): <status>` with its pull request (`#<n> <state> <url>`) or `no pull request` and when waiting, `waiting on <keys>` (hs-d521), then one line per Job `- <key> <status>: <title> (<touches, comma-separated>)` or `- <key> waiting on <keys>: <title> (…)`. After a Plan's Workflow sections, the Plan's explore Jobs get one `### Jobs` heading with one line per explore Job, `- <key> <kind> <status>: <title> (<touches, comma-separated>)`, a waiting one reading `- <key> <kind> waiting on <keys>: <title> (…)` (the same wording as a Workflow Job's); the section is absent when the Plan has no explore Job. A Plan with only explore Jobs is no longer header-only: it renders its `### Jobs` section under its heading. A Context with no active Plan prints `No pending work.`

Idempotent: yes; it only reads.

### 3.13 `context distill`

```
cpd context distill [--context <c>] [--batch <n>]
```

Curates one batch of the Context's records (contract §4.6 "The distiller curates" and "The distill run", hs-d549, hs-d551, replacing the digest-writing run of hs-d194 D1–D5; GXD1-GXD2 hs-d563: per-line acceptance, rejected lines stay uncurated): at most **N uncurated records** in force (FX4: N is `--batch` from 1 to 60, default 60, at most 49152 bytes of their text in batch.md, hs-d549, hs-d551) get a topic and a short form (for machines) and the run may propose retirements, written by one-shot pi and **checked structurally by cpd**, with each line validated independently so invalid lines do not fail the whole output (GXD1): lines the checks reject are re-asked for (at most 2 extra pi calls per run, below), a `short` still over 120 bytes after the re-asks is clamped and the clamp reported (`clamped`, below), and an empty pi answer gets one smaller-batch retry (below). The curations are read by `context show --topic` for discovery and retrieval. Engine E9 starts it detached when the Context has uncurated records in force and the newest of them is 10 minutes old, or 20 or more exist (contract §3.7); one batch per run, so a backlog (751 records for `building-cpd`) is curated by one run per tick. When a run for a state (the highest uncurated seq and count) fails (distill_invalid only when no line passes, distill_failed after the whole ladder, or a crash), E9 starts the next run for the same state with the next smaller batch (60 → 30 → 15 → 5 → 1, FX4) and records the batch size with the state; after batch 1 fails, it stops until the state changes (a success curates at least one record, GXD1, or a new record) or the engine restarts (contract §3.7 E9). Anyone may run it on demand and it then runs in the caller's process and waits for pi. The Context is `--context`, else the selected Plan's (§1.3). Its §2 row is added by the Job that implements it, as §10.9's was, so that `every_documented_command_exists` holds on every commit.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| a Context was selected (§1.3) | `context_required` | 2 |
| the Context exists | `context_not_found` | 4 |
| no other distill run of this Context is alive: `locks/distill-<context>.lock` is free (taken without waiting, held until the run ends) | `distill_running` | 3 |

An archived Context is not refused; engine E9 never starts one for it.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--batch <n>` | batch size from 1 to 60, default 60 (FX4 of hs-d549, hs-d551; the batch is at most `n` records and at most 49152 bytes of their text, contract §4.6 step 2) |

Effects (contract §4.6 "The distill run", steps 1–5, GXD1-GXD4 hs-d563):
- **Nothing to do**, `"already": true` and nothing written: no record in force is uncurated.
- **Skipped when not curable** (R4 of hs-d592): when the Context is archived, deleted, or under `context_curation_min_records` (§8.2), the command exits 0 before taking the lock, writes nothing, creates no Event and its JSON data is `{"context": "<c>", "skipped": "archived"}` for an archived Context, or `{"context": "<c>", "skipped": "young", "records": <n>, "floor": <N>}` for one under the floor (archived is checked first). This makes engine E9's runs skip non-curable Contexts without process, lock or Event (contract §3.7 R5, R8).
- **Otherwise**: the files `prompt.md`, `batch.md` (at most N uncurated records in force, oldest first, in full, where N is the batch size), `known.md` (the topics in use, a blank line, then `[<id>] <topic> | <short>` for every curated record in force when there are 80 or fewer curated records in force; above 80, the same header with all topics and only the batch's top-8 neighbours and forced records, oldest first, lexical only, contract §4.6 step 3, `core/src/context/distill_known.rs`) and `docs.md` (for each batch record, the `<repo>:<path>` hits of `git -C <repo> grep -l -w <id> -- docs '*.md'` on each repo of the Context's Plans' Workflows, run by cpd), then the distiller, `pi --mode json ...` at `context_distill_tier` (default `H0`; hs-d560, contract §4.6 step 4: a distill run has no ladder, one step only; contract §6.5 "Distiller", §8.2), JSON mode, read by cpd, killed after `timeouts.distill_minutes`. GXD3: when pi's stop reason is `length`, cpd keeps the text up to the last complete line (drops incomplete trailing line if any) and notes `cut: true`. **Empty answer, one smaller-batch retry**: when a pi call's final assistant message is empty (no text at all, `reason: "output"`), the run retries once, at the same Tier (not a ladder rung; `steps` still holds one Tier), with a smaller batch — at most half the call's records, at least one — before it fails with the one `distill_failed` error; only an empty answer retries this way, a `length` answer with no complete line does not (GXD3). **GXD1-GXD2 Per-line acceptance**: every line is validated independently; lines that pass stay curated, lines that fail are rejected (their record stays uncurated); the output lists all attempted lines with a `rejected` array (GXD2) of failures. One transaction calls `propose` with only the passing lines; the run succeeds when at least one line passes.
- **The checks** (contract §4.6 step 5, GXD1-GXD2 hs-d563): each line is validated independently; failures are collected (GXD2: listed in `rejected` array), not fatal to the whole output. For each line: valid UTF-8 JSON of the output shape; `id` in the batch (GXD1: missing records stay uncurated; id not in batch is ignored; id appearing twice means both lines rejected); field bounds (`topic` 1 to 40 characters matching `[a-z0-9-]{1,40}`, `short` 1 to 120 bytes with GXD4 100-byte rule hs-d563, `reason` one of three); `duplicate` target is a record in force not the record itself with seq < record's seq; `superseded` target in force not the record itself with seq > record's seq; `documented` target is one of that record's paths in `docs.md`.
