GXD4: prompt examples have short of 90–100 bytes, never say only `correction to <id>`. **Re-ask of rejected lines**: when the checks reject some lines, the run re-asks the model for **only the failing records** — each re-ask pi call carries each failing record's full text, its validator error and the byte budget — at most **2 extra pi calls per run**, at the same Tier (no ladder rung); the re-asked lines go through the same checks. **The clamp, never silent**: a `short` still over 120 bytes after the re-asks is clamped deterministically: cut to at most 120 bytes on a word boundary, always one line, never empty, never splitting a UTF-8 character; the clamped line is curated like any passing line, and the run's output gains a `clamped` array listing every clamp as `{id, bytes}` (`bytes` the clamped length), so a clamp is never silent. No repair turn, no `## Contradictions`, no cite-every-decision: removed (hs-d549, hs-d551); the re-ask above is not the removed repair turn — it re-asks only the lines the checks rejected.
- **Valid run** (GXD1: at least one line passes): one transaction calls `propose`: for each passing line, the curation and retirement proposal. A `duplicate` or `superseded` retirement is first confirmed by `kev-4b` and the judge (contract §4.6 "Retirement", "Distill confirmation"): `approved` when both give its reason, `pending` when `kev-4b` is unreachable or the judge errors (no further model call in the run), dropped otherwise, its curation still written. A `documented` retirement is `approved` (`git-grep`). Then appends the **Event** `context-curated` `{context, curated, retire}`, plus `rejected` (the count of rejected lines) when a line was rejected (contract §5.2; GXD2), and `records-retired` `{context, approved, rejected: []}` when a row was written `approved`. The output carries `approved` (the rows written `approved`), `dropped` (the proposals dropped), `rejected: [...]`, `clamped: [{id, bytes}]` (every clamp of the run, absent when none, above) and when any line was rejected or output was cut, raw text kept as `<upto_seq>.jsonl.invalid`. A `pending` proposal takes effect only when the User decides it (Inbox item `curate-retire`, §3.16–§3.17); an `approved` one takes effect at once. **Invalid run** (no line passes or output could not be parsed): the last output is kept as `run/context-digests/<context>/<upto_seq>.jsonl.invalid` (one per Context, replacing the previous; a valid run removes it) and the run fails (hs-d560: no ladder, no `distill-tier` item).
- **Run log**: every run that started pi appends a line to `run/context-digests/<context>/runs.jsonl` (`started_at`, `seconds`, `model`, `tier` (the Tier of that pi run, `context_distill_tier`, hs-d560), `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `cost`, `context`, `upto_seq`, `result`, `kind`, always `distill`; contract §4.6 "The run log"; GXD2: when any line was rejected or output was cut, `<upto_seq>.jsonl.invalid` is kept), also when it failed.
- **tmux:** none. **git:** read-only (`git grep`).

Failures, after the lock is taken. Each appends **one** `error` Event `{source: "context distill", code, message, details}` with no `context`, `plan` or `session` set (`details.context` names it; so no Lead gets a turn, contract §5.3), changes no curation and returns the same code:

| Failure | Code | Exit | `details` |
|---|---|---|---|
| pi could not start, exited non-zero (an error, or an answer cut at the output limit), ran longer than `timeouts.distill_minutes`, or its JSON stream had no final assistant text (GXD3: length with no complete line fails as distill_failed; an empty final assistant message gets one smaller-batch retry, above, before this failure) | `distill_failed` | 1 | `context`, `upto_seq`, `reason` (`spawn`, `exit`, `timeout` or `output`), `exit` (when it exited), `tail` (pi's last 60 stderr lines), `log` |
| the output fails any check above, after the last Tier of the ladder (GXD1: no line passes; GXD2: rejected lines listed in output; GXD3: output cut at length with no complete line) | `distill_invalid` | 1 | `context`, `upto_seq`, `errors` (every failure, each `{id?, line?, what}`; GXD2: rejected lines, each with id, line number from 1 and reason), `invalid` (the kept `.jsonl.invalid` file), `log` |

`log` is `run/context-digests/<context>/distill.log`, where the run writes its stderr (and, started by E9, its stdout too).

```json
{"ok": true, "context": "building-cpd", "distilled": true, "steps": ["H0"],
 "curated": 59, "rejected": 1, "clamped": [{"id": "hs-d655", "bytes": 118}],
 "retire": 4, "approved": 2, "dropped": 1, "remaining": 692,
 "run": {"seconds": 94.2, "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5:medium", "tokens_in": 61234, "tokens_out": 7410, "cost": 0.43}}
```

`curated`, `rejected` (GXD2) and `retire` are the counts of the `context-curated` Event (contract §5.2); `retire` counts every written row, `pending` and `approved` alike. `approved` (rows written `approved`, a part of `retire`) and `dropped` (proposals the confirmation dropped) are on a valid run, both `0` when there is none (contract §4.6 "Retirement", pro-d13). `remaining` the records in force still uncurated. `clamped` (the non-silent clamp, above) is present only when at least one `short` was clamped: one `{id, bytes}` per clamp, `id` the record and `bytes` the clamped short's byte length (at most 120). `steps` is present with `run` (hs-d538): the Tiers tried in order, e.g. `["H0", "H1"]`; `run` is that of the **last** step. `run` is present only when pi ran (`"distilled": true`); its fields are the run's `runs.jsonl` line without `started_at`, `context`, `upto_seq`, `result` and `kind` and `tokens_in`, `tokens_out` and `cost` may be `null`. On a failure the same figures are in the log line only, not in the Event.

Idempotent: yes. With no uncurated record it returns `"already": true` and runs nothing; a rerun after a failure runs the same batch again (on demand; E9 does not retry the same highest `seq`, contract §3.7).

### 3.13a `context curate`

```
cpd context curate [--context <c>] [--record <id>]
```

Experimental Feature `write_curation` (contract §4.6 "Write-time neighbour curation"; pro-d366, pro-d370, pro-a1). Curates **one** record of the Context: the oldest unchecked in-force record of kind `decision` or `note` written in the last 24 hours (the batch distiller keeps the older ones; there is no catch-up of old records). Engine E9 starts it detached for a Context that has a due record (contract §3.7); anyone may run it on demand, in the caller's process. The Context is `--context`, else the selected Plan's (§1.3). Callers: Lead only, not cockpit.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| a Context was selected (§1.3) | `context_required` | 2 |
| the Context exists | `context_not_found` | 4 |
| no other distill or curate run of this Context is alive: `locks/distill-<context>.lock` is free | `distill_running` | 3 |
| with `--record`, the id names a record of the Context | `record_not_found` | 3 |

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--context <c>` | the Context (§1.3) |
| `--record <id>` | curate that record, whatever its age and checked marker (a manual smoke) |

Effects:
- **Flag off**: with `experimental.write_curation` false the command returns `{"context": "<c>", "skipped": "off"}` with no port call and no file created (not even `vectors.db`).
- **Not curable**: as §3.13, `"skipped": "archived"` or `"skipped": "young"`, and nothing else.
- **The sweep** (contract §4.6 "Retirement", "The sweep"; pro-d13): before the pick, and also when no record is due, up to 3 of the Context's oldest `pending` `duplicate` or `superseded` rows (oldest by `proposed_at`, then `seq`) are decided by the pair rule of this command: `approved` (`decided_by` `kev-4b+gemini-3.8-flash`) when `kev-4b` and the judge agree, `rejected` (same `decided_by`) on a disagreement, an `independent` verdict, a failed quote or a wrong seq direction, left `pending` on `contradicts`, on a judge error, and on an unreachable `kev-4b`, which also stops the sweep. A `documented` row is never swept. The decisions are one `records-retired` Event, when the sweep decided at least one row. A sweep failure does not fail the run. The output gains `swept: {approved, rejected}` only when the sweep decided at least one row.
- **The pick**: `--record`, else the oldest due record. With none due (after the sweep): `"already": true`, `"remaining": 0`.
- **The gate**: `decision` and `note` records continue to the neighbours (contract §4.6): at most 8, FTS5 plus embedding cosine. An unreachable embedder, or a corrupt `vectors.db`, degrades the run to FTS5 only (`fts_only`).
- **The pair verdict**: `kev-4b` first; `independent` at the confidence bar is accepted free (`free`), no judge call. Every other result goes to the judge; a confirmed retirement needs agreement and a verbatim quote, else the pair counts `disagreed`, `quote_failed` or `rejected`. An unreachable or unusable classifier falls back to the judge alone (`kev_unreachable`).
- **The write**: all confirmed retirements are written once, through `propose_rejecting`: a `record_retirements` row `approved` (`decided_by` `kev-4b+gemini-3.8-flash`, `decided_at` = `proposed_at`) when `kev-4b` and the judge agreed, `pending` when `kev-4b` was unreachable and the judge alone gave the verdict (`kev_unreachable`); and a `record_curations` row for a retired record that has none (an existing curation is never overwritten). Then `context-curated`, and `records-retired` when a row was written `approved` (contract §4.6 "Retirement"). An independent pair writes nothing; with no retirement, no label and no provisional topic there is no write and no Event.
- **The provisional topic** (Plan `ctx-topics-surface`, pro-d11; contract §4.6 "Write-time neighbour curation"). After the pair verdicts and before the write, the pass asks the ClassifierPort (`kev-4b`) one question about the picked record, when the record is **accepted-independent**: no pair of it ended retire-class (`duplicate`, `supersedes`, `contradicts`) or was rejected or disagreed, where a pair is independent when `kev-4b` accepted it free or the judge confirmed `independent` (a record with no neighbours is accepted-independent); it has no `record_curations` row and no `record_topics` row; and this pass writes no label for it, so a provisional row never sits beside a curation written in the same pass.
  - **Labels (C1):** the curated topics in force of the Context (each topic a curated record in force carries, §3.3a). With none, there is no call.
  - **Write (C2):** one `record_topics` row (contract §4.4: `context`, `record`, `topic`, `model` the classifier's model version, `at`) only when the answer's label is one of those topics and its confidence is at least 0.80 (no confidence counts as below). Otherwise nothing is written.
  - **Fail-open (C3):** a classifier error, `classifier_unreachable` or a timeout writes no row and is no error; the pass continues (the port raises its own deduplicated notice).
  - **Once (C4):** one row per record, written `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; a record that already has a curation or a row is never classified. The record stays uncurated (no `record_curations` row), so the distiller (§3.13) still curates it. The step writes no Event.
  - **Off:** with `experimental.write_curation` off, the whole pass, this step included, makes no call and writes nothing (the Flag off bullet above).
- **`contradicts`** is listed in the JSON and retires nothing.
- **Telemetry** (Plan `ctx-observability`, pro-d13): the run measures its wall time with the Ports clock (`ms`) and sums the tokens it used: the embedder's (`embed_tokens`), `kev-4b`'s (`kev_tokens_in`, `kev_tokens_out`) and the judge's (`judge_tokens_in`, `judge_tokens_out`), each 0 when nothing was called or the gateway reported none. `cost` is the sum of the costs the gateway reported for the judge calls (Bifrost `usage.cost`, USD), `null` when none was reported; there is no rate table. `kev-4b` is local: it has tokens and no cost. Each run that gets past the skips (`off`, `archived`, `young`) and the `already` answer appends one line to `curate-runs.jsonl` (contract §4.6 "The curate run log"), best-effort. A failed run (the Failures table) appends nothing.
- **The checked marker**: a record whose run finished is entered in `context_checked` of `vectors.db`.
- **tmux:** none. **git:** none.

Failures. The record is left unchecked and nothing is written:

| Failure | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the judge could not be reached | `judge_unreachable` | 1 |
| the judge refused | `judge_refused` | 1 |
| the judge's reply was not usable | `judge_bad_reply` | 1 |
| `vectors.db` cannot be marked | `store_failed` | 1 |

An unreachable embedder or classifier is **not** a failure: the run finishes, exits 0 and says `fts_only` or `kev_unreachable` in the JSON. The engine backs off only after a failed run.

```json
{"ok": true, "context": "building-cpd", "record": "pro-d371", "kind": "decision",
 "neighbours": 8, "fts_only": false, "kev_unreachable": false,
 "free": 6, "judged": 2,
 "retire": [{"record": "pro-d371", "target": "pro-d120", "reason": "duplicate"}],
 "contradicts": [{"neighbour": "pro-d200", "quote": "...", "reason": "..."}],
 "swept": {"approved": 1, "rejected": 0}, "disagreed": 0, "quote_failed": 0, "rejected": 0, "remaining": 3,
 "ms": 4210, "embed_tokens": 312, "kev_tokens_in": 5400, "kev_tokens_out": 96,
 "judge_tokens_in": 1800, "judge_tokens_out": 240, "cost": 0.0042}
```

`remaining` is the count of records still due. The telemetry keys `ms` (integer milliseconds), `embed_tokens`, `kev_tokens_in`, `kev_tokens_out`, `judge_tokens_in`, `judge_tokens_out` (integers) and `cost` (a number in USD, or `null`) are present on every run that did work; the `skipped` and `already` answers do not carry them.

Idempotent: yes. A second run picks the next record, or says `"already": true`.

### 3.14 `context owner`

```
cpd context owner <login> [--context <c>]
```

Sets a missing owner or changes the owner (contract §8.3, hs-d288): a Context created before `context new --owner` existed may have no owner, which the migration could not fill because its Workflows had no pull request or pull requests of two owners (contract §4.5); a Context with an owner may change it, but only while no Plan of the Context has a Workflow row (Workflow rows are rows of `workflows` of Plans not deleted, in any status). The Context is `--context`, else the selected Plan's (§1.3).

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<login>` | the owner, a login of contract §2.1, else `usage`; stored lowercased |
| `--confirm-fallback` | optional: if the owner is unknown, create `policy/<login>/owner.toml` as a relative symlink to `../clayton-duarte/owner.toml` and proceed; if the owner is already known, the flag changes nothing (idempotent); if `policy/clayton-duarte/owner.toml` does not exist, fail `fallback_missing`. Without the flag, an unknown owner fails `owner_unconfirmed` |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| a Context was selected (§1.3) | `context_required` | 2 |
| the Context exists | `context_not_found` | 4 |
| the same owner again (no write, no Event) | `already` | 0 |
| the Context has an owner other than this one and a Workflow row exists; details: `context`, `owner` (the current owner), `workflows` (the Workflow rows as `<plan>/<key>`, sorted) | `owner_in_use` | 3 |
| the owner has a policy file, `$CPD_HOME/policy/<owner>/owner.toml`, else with `--confirm-fallback` create it as a relative symlink to `../clayton-duarte/owner.toml`; without the flag, `owner_unconfirmed` if the owner is unknown (details: `owner`, `file`, `fallback`, `flag`); `fallback_missing` if the fallback owner's file does not exist; `details.owner` and `details.file` | `owner_unconfirmed` (1), `fallback_missing` (1) |
| that file is valid; `details.file`, `details.key` | `policy_invalid` | 1 |

An archived Context is not refused: changing its owner changes no work.

Effects: **rows and Events**, one transaction with the checks and the UPDATE on `contexts.owner`. One `context-owner` Event `{owner}` appended for each change; none for `already`. Nothing else: the Context's existing Workflows keep their `name` and from now on resolve `Repo(<owner>, <name>)` (or `Owner(<owner>)` while their `name` is null, contract §8.3). Sessions already started keep the policy text they were given for the old owner until they restart (contract §8.3 'Delivery to agents').

```json
{"ok": true, "context": {"id": "building-cpd", "owner": "clayton-duarte"}, "already": false}
```

Idempotent: yes; the same owner again returns `"already": true` and writes nothing.

### 3.15 `context delete`

```
cpd context delete <id> [--yes]
```

Deletes a Context: its Plans' rows, its records, its Manager and its run files, worktrees and local branches (hs-d527). A Permanent Context (`cpd`, `host`, `codereview`) is never deleted: `context_permanent`, checked first (below). The `contexts` row and the row of each of its Plans, stay as **tombstones** (`deleted_at` set, once only) and so do the Leads' Session rows, which the tombstoned Plans reference: all hidden from every list, view and lookup (contract §2.2 "Deleted", which has the design). Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. Without `--yes` the command prints what would be deleted (a preview); with `--yes` it deletes.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|
| `<id>` | Context id (§2.1) |
| `--yes` | perform the delete; without it, print the preview only |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Context is not a Permanent Context (`cpd`, `host`, `codereview`), checked first; `details.context` | `context_permanent` | 3 |
| the Context exists and is not deleted; a deleted one is `already` (below) for this command and `context_not_found` for every other | `context_not_found` | 4 |
| **archived or asleep**: the Context is archived, or every one of its Plans is asleep or archived; `details: {blockers: [{kind, id}]}` lists what is not | `archive_blocked` | 3 |
| **nothing running**: no Job `queued` or `running`, no Attempt not `ended`, no Session `working`, `waiting` or `blocked`, every Escalation closed, no Plan review pending; `details.blockers` | `archive_blocked` | 3 |
| **no open Workflow**: every Workflow of every Plan is `merged` or `cancelled`; `details.blockers` | `archive_blocked` | 3 |
| **Manager not in chat**: the Context's Manager (§3.11) is not in the chat slot, as `context archive` requires; `details.next = cpd session park` | `in_chat_slot` | 3 |

Plans already deleted are not checked. Effects, with `--yes` only (**without it, no rows or files are written**):
1. **One transaction.** It re-checks the preconditions (race safety), then sets `deleted_at = now()` **first**, on every Plan not yet deleted and then on the Context (the triggers that guard the deletes read it, contract §4.4; a set `deleted_at` is never changed or cleared). Then it deletes the rows, each through the exception for a deleted Plan or Context and in an order that keeps the foreign keys whole:
   - The plannotator reviews and board posts of every Session of the Context (the Manager's and the Leads' included)
   - Every Inbox item of the Context, then every Event of the Context (those of its Plans, Plans deleted earlier included and those that have no Plan); Inbox items go first because they point to Events
   - For each Plan: its Escalations, Attempts, Dependencies, Jobs; its Workflow needs, Workflows, Plan reviews; every Session of it but the Lead
   - Every `record_retirements` and `record_curations` row of the Context (hs-d549; they point to the records, so they go first), then every `context_records` row of the Context (a Plan delete keeps them; `context_records_immutable` still refuses every update)
   - The Manager Session
   - The Leads' Session rows stay (each tombstoned `plans.lead_session` references one), hidden with their Plan.
   Every `DELETE` writes a `history` row with the whole old row (§4.4); the tombstones are `update` rows. They stay and the tamper check stays clean (contract §2.2). Last, in the same transaction, **one `context-deleted` Event** is appended, with the counts; it is never deleted by this delete.
2. **Session files** (after commit): every Session's file, the Leads' included; files that do not exist are skipped.
3. **Run files** (after commit): `$CPD_HOME/run/<plan>/` of each Plan and `$CPD_HOME/run/context-digests/<context>/`, with the summaries, renders, reviews, messages, specs, logs and distill artifacts under them.
4. **Worktrees and local branches** (after commit): `rm -rf` every Attempt worktree and Workflow Lead worktree, each with its `target/` (this, with the run files, is where the disk comes from: the database file does not shrink); then the stored `lead_branch` of each Workflow and `cpd/<plan>--<attempt>` from their repos (not on the remote), then the directories of step 3. The paths come from the live rows when the transaction commits and on a rerun from their `before` copies in `history`.

**Rerun.** The rows go in one transaction and steps 2–4 after it, so a crash leaves a tombstoned Context with files on disk. A rerun with `--yes` on a deleted Context writes **nothing** to the store (no row, no Event), finishes whatever file step is left (a missing file, directory or branch is not an error) and returns `"already": true`. A preview of a deleted Context returns `"already": true` and what is left on disk, not the counts of the first preview, which only the Event keeps.

Output without `--yes` (preview) or with `--yes` after a delete:

```json
{"ok": true, "preview": true, "already": false, "plans": [{"id": "cpd2", "jobs": 47, "attempts": 121}], "jobs": 47, "attempts": 121, "sessions": 3, "worktrees": 11, "disk_freed_mb": 342}
```

`sessions` counts every Session of the Context, the Leads included (their rows stay, their files go). With `--yes` the first time: `"preview": false`, `"already": false`. Rerun with `--yes`: `"preview": false`, `"already": true` and `worktrees` and `disk_freed_mb` of what this run removed (0 when nothing was left). Preview of a deleted Context: `{"ok": true, "preview": true, "already": true, "left": {"worktrees": 0, "branches": 0, "files": 0}}`.

Idempotent: yes; a Context already deleted returns `"already": true` and writes nothing to the store.

**Tests that assume otherwise change with this design** (hs-d527; for delete-core to have approved): `context_delete.rs` expects no Session with `context = <id>`, but the Leads' rows stay (tombstoned Plans reference them) and `plan_rows` as under `plan delete` counts the Leads and the Plans' `plan-deleted` Events; the Manager and every other Session are what is gone.

### 3.16 `context curation` (internal)

```
cpd context curation [--context <c>] [--limit <n>]
```

Lists the pending retirements of the Context: the proposals that no model pair confirmed and the User has not yet decided (contract §4.6 "Retirement"; hs-d549, hs-d551, pro-d13). Called by the cockpit when the User clicks a `curate-retire` Inbox item (§13.2), to fill the checklist dialog (hs-d568, hs-d569). Internal (§1.1): hidden in clap, as `plan decide` is. An archived Context or one under the floor (`context_curation_min_records`, §8.2) shows no Inbox item, its pending proposals stay pending and the command still works when run by hand (R6 of hs-d592).

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--context <c>` | the Context (§1.3) |
| `--limit <n>` | at most n entries per list (hs-d569 CD4), where n >= 1 (default: no limit; all entries) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `CPD_SESSION` and `CPD_ATTEMPT` are not set in the environment: only the User decides (hs-d551). The cockpit's views and popups carry neither: cpd's tmux client removes `CPD_SESSION` and `CPD_ATTEMPT` along with `TMUX` and `TMUX_PANE` (contract §6.1 "The one place, in Rust"), so even a tmux server started from inside an agent never passes them on and only the panes of a Session (`session run`, contract §6.5) get `CPD_SESSION`, through their `Spawn` | `user_only` | 3 |
| a Context was selected (§1.3) | `context_required` | 2 |
| the Context exists | `context_not_found` | 4 |
| `--limit` is a positive integer (if given) | (parse error in validation) | 2 |

Effects: none. Output: `retire`, the first n `pending` rows of `record_retirements` (oldest first by `proposed_at`, then the record's `seq`); `retire_total`, the count of ALL pending retirements. Each entry has `record` (the id), `kind` (the record's kind, §2.2), `text` (the record's full text, hs-d569 CD2), `short` (its short form, `record_curations.short`; a proposal is always written with its curation, contract §4.6), `reason` and `target`.

```json
{"ok": true, "context": "building-cpd", "retire_total": 56,
 "retire": [{"record": "hs-d12", "kind": "decision", "text": "engine: run one per machine", "short": "engine: one per machine", "reason": "superseded", "target": "hs-d77"}]}
```

Idempotent: read-only.

### 3.17 `context retire` (internal)

```
cpd context retire [--context <c>] [--approve <id,...>] [--reject <id,...>]
```

Decides pending retirements, the proposals that no model pair confirmed (contract §4.6 "Retirement"; hs-d549, hs-d551, pro-d13). A row `approved` by a model pair or by `git-grep` is not pending: it is refused `curation_not_pending`. Called by the cockpit when the User approves the checklist dialog of a `curate-retire` item (§13.2): `--approve` the ticked rows, `--reject` the unticked. Internal (§1.1): hidden in clap. Only the User decides: no agent runs it. An archived Context or one under the floor shows no Inbox item, its pending proposals stay pending and the command still works when run by hand (R6 of hs-d592).

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--context <c>` | the Context (§1.3) |
| `--approve <id,...>` | record ids (§2.1), comma-separated, whose pending retirement becomes `approved`: the record leaves force |
| `--reject <id,...>` | record ids whose pending retirement becomes `rejected`: the record stays in force and is never proposed again |

At least one of the two is required (`usage`).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `CPD_SESSION` and `CPD_ATTEMPT` are not set in the environment (as §3.16) | `user_only` | 3 |
| a Context was selected and exists | `context_required` (2), `context_not_found` (4) | |
| no id is in both lists | `args_invalid` | 2 |
| every id has a `pending` retirement in the Context; `details: {record}` names the first that has none (none at all, already decided) | `curation_not_pending` | 3 |

Effects: **one transaction**, all or nothing (a refusal writes nothing). **Rows:** each named `record_retirements` row gets its `status`, `decided_at` and `decided_by` `user`. **Event** (one): `records-retired` `{context, approved: [id], rejected: [id]}` (contract §5.2). A retirement writes no Context record. The Inbox item `curate-retire` follows at the engine's next E8 pass (contract §3.7): its count drops and it closes when none is pending.

```json
{"ok": true, "context": "building-cpd", "approved": ["hs-d12"], "rejected": ["hs-d30"]}
```

Idempotent: no. A rerun finds the rows decided and is refused `curation_not_pending`.

### 3.18 `context reads`

```
cpd context reads [--context <id>] [--since <iso>] [--channel <c,c>] [--min-sessions <n>]
```

Lists the Context records that Sessions have read or cited (the `context_reads` telemetry, contract §4.4, §4.6 "Reads"): per record, how many reads there are, how many distinct Sessions made them, and how many of those Sessions later cited it (`used`). The Context is `--context`, else the selected Plan's (§1.3).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| a Context was selected (§1.3) | `context_required` | 2 |
| the Context exists | `context_not_found` | 4 |
| `--since` is an ISO-8601 instant: a date and time with a zone (`Z` or `±hh:mm`) | `usage` | 2 |
| `--channel` is a comma list of the channels `pushed`, `search` and `show` only (`shadow` included) | `usage` | 2 |
| `--min-sessions` is an integer of at least 1 | `usage` | 2 |

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--since <iso>` | only rows with `read_at` at or after this instant (`>=`), compared as instants. The output's `since` is that instant in UTC, written as `read_at` is written (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ`); omitted, `since` is null and there is no lower bound |
| `--channel <c,c>` | the channels whose rows are counted; default all three. Output `channels` lists the chosen ones in the order `pushed`, `search`, `show` |
| `--min-sessions <n>` | only records with `sessions` at least n (default 1) |

**Callers** (as `context show`, §3.3): the Lead, the Manager and the **Worker**. Read-only.

Effects: none. No Context record changes, and no read is logged for this command.

**Counting.** Of the Context's `context_reads` rows, a row counts when its `channel` is chosen and its `read_at` is at or after `--since`. For each record with counted rows: `reads` is their count; `sessions` the distinct `session` values among them; `used` the distinct `session` values among them whose row has `used` = 1. A record is listed only when `sessions` is at least `--min-sessions`. `kind` is the record's kind (§2.2) from `context_records`; every kind is listed. Order: `reads` descending, then `sessions` descending, then `id` ascending.

Output: `context` (`{id, title, jira}`), `since`, `channels`, `min_sessions`, `records` (each `{id, kind, reads, sessions, used}`) and `markdown`: one line per record, `<id> <kind> reads=<n> sessions=<n> used=<n>`, the lines joined by newlines (an empty string when there are none). An empty result is `records: []`.

```json
{"ok": true, "context": {"id": "building-cpd", "title": "Building cpd", "jira": null}, "since": null,
 "channels": ["pushed", "search", "show"], "min_sessions": 2,
 "records": [{"id": "hs-d7", "kind": "decision", "reads": 9, "sessions": 4, "used": 2}],
 "markdown": "hs-d7 decision reads=9 sessions=4 used=2"}
```

Idempotent: read-only.

### 3.19 `context embed`

```
cpd context embed [--context <id>] [--limit <n>]
```

Backfills the Context's vector cache (contract §4.6 "Backfill"): embeds its in-force decisions and notes into `$CPD_HOME/vectors.db` for the embedder's model, so that `context search` can fuse a semantic list (§3.4). Search never embeds records; this command and `context curate` (§3.13a) are the writers of record vectors. The Context is `--context`, else the selected Plan's (§1.3). Callers: Lead; no cockpit.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| a Context was selected (§1.3) | `context_required` | 2 |
| the Context exists | `context_not_found` | 4 |
| `--limit` is not an integer of at least 0 | `usage` | 2 |

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--context <id>` | the Context (§1.3) |
| `--limit <n>` | at most `n` records are embedded in this run; default `100`; `0` is all |

Effects:
- **Records**: the Context's in-force decisions and notes, newest first. A Plan or brief record is never embedded (contract §4.6 kind gate). A record whose row's `content_hash` equals the lowercase hex SHA-256 of its text is **skipped**; any other record is **embedded**, one embedder call each, at 768 dims.
- **Each row is written at once** (`context`, `model`, `record`, `dims`, `vector`, `at`, `content_hash`), so an interrupted run resumes: the rows already written stay. A record that is not skipped is the only one sent to the embedder, so when every record is skipped the embedder is not called.
- **Counts**: `embedded` is the records written in this run, `skipped` the records whose row was current, and `remaining` the records whose row is missing or stale after the run. With `--limit`, the records not yet reached are counted in `remaining`.
- **Telemetry** (Plan `ctx-observability`, pro-d13): `ms` is the run's wall time measured with the Ports clock, `embed_tokens` the sum of the tokens the embedder reported (0 when none), and `cost` is always `null` (the embedder reports none). A run appends one line to `curate-runs.jsonl` with `kind` `"embed"` (contract §4.6 "The curate run log"), best-effort, also when it fails after embedding some records.
- Writes `$CPD_HOME/vectors.db` (§1.4), under `locks/store.lock`. Not gated by `experimental.write_curation`.
- **tmux:** none. **git:** none.

Failures. The command fails with the code, exit 1, and the rows already written stay:

| Failure | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the embedder could not be reached, timed out or failed with no answer | `embedding_unreachable` | 1 |
| the gateway refused the request | `embedding_refused` | 1 |
| the embedder's reply was not usable | `embedding_bad_reply` | 1 |
| `vectors.db` is corrupt or cannot be written | `store_failed` | 1 |

```json
{"ok": true, "context": "building-cpd", "model": "vertex/gemini-embedding-2", "embedded": 60, "skipped": 4, "remaining": 0,
 "ms": 21800, "embed_tokens": 5120, "cost": null}
```

`ms` is an integer (milliseconds), `embed_tokens` an integer and `cost` is `null`.

Idempotent: yes. A rerun embeds nothing when every row is current; its `skipped` is the count of current rows.

### 3.20 `context stats`

```
cpd context stats [--context <c>] [--all] [--since <iso>]
```

Reports what a Context holds, what writing and curating it costs, and how it is read (contract §4.6 "The curate run log" and "The search log"; Plan `ctx-observability`, pro-d13). Read-only: it writes nothing, creates no file and calls no port. The Context is `--context`, else the selected Plan's (§1.3). Callers: Lead; no cockpit.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| a Context was selected (§1.3), unless `--all` | `context_required` | 2 |
| the selected Plan exists (when the Context comes from `--plan` or `CPD_PLAN`) | `plan_not_found` | 4 |
| the Context exists | `context_not_found` | 4 |
| `--since` is an ISO 8601 UTC time | `usage` (`details.since`) | 2 |
| `--all` is not combined with `--context` | `usage` | 2 |

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--context <c>` | the Context (§1.3) |
| `--all` | every live Context (not deleted; archived ones included), one entry each, sorted by id |
| `--since <iso>` | count only what happened at or after this time: records written, distill and curate runs, embed runs, reads and searches. `sizes` is a snapshot of now and ignores it |

Effects: none. `contexts` is always a list: one entry without `--all`. A missing `curate-runs.jsonl`, `runs.jsonl` or `vectors.db` counts as zero lines or rows and is no error; a line of either file that is not valid JSON is skipped and is no error.

Sources, so that a figure can be checked: `sizes.records` and `sizes.curated` from `context_records`, `record_curations`, `record_topics` and `record_retirements`; `sizes.vectors` from `vectors.db` `context_embeddings` and `context_checked` of the Context; distill figures from `runs.jsonl` (`tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `cost`, `seconds` × 1000 for `ms`; contract §4.6 "The run log"); curate and embed figures from `curate-runs.jsonl`; reads from `context_reads`; searches from `search_log`.

**Output** (`ok` true, the data). `markdown` is concise: one `## <context>` heading per Context, then the four sections as short tables or lists.

```json
{"ok": true, "since": null,
 "contexts": [{
  "context": "building-cpd",
  "sizes": {
   "records": {
    "by_kind": {"decision": {"count": 210, "bytes": 184200}, "note": {"count": 96, "bytes": 51100}, "plan": {"count": 30, "bytes": 22400}, "brief": {"count": 30, "bytes": 61800}},
    "by_status": {"in_force": {"count": 240, "bytes": 230000}, "superseded": {"count": 80, "bytes": 60100}, "retired_approved": {"count": 10, "bytes": 7000}, "retired_pending": {"count": 6, "bytes": 4300}}},
   "curated": {"count": 190, "short_bytes": 15800},
   "provisional_topics": 12,
   "vectors": {"count": 300, "checked": 280, "blob_bytes": 921600}},
  "writing_and_curation": {
   "records_written": 14,
   "distill": {"runs": 3, "curations": 38, "retire": 4, "rejected": 1, "failed": 0},
   "curate": {"runs": 20, "free": 120, "judged": 31, "retire": 5, "contradicts": 2, "disagreed": 1, "quote_failed": 0, "kev_unreachable": 0},
   "retirements": {
    "duplicate": {"approved": 3, "pending": 2, "rejected": 0},
    "superseded": {"approved": 1, "pending": 0, "rejected": 0},
    "documented": {"approved": 0, "pending": 1, "rejected": 0}}},
  "cost": {
   "distill": {"runs": 3, "tokens_in": 91000, "tokens_out": 5200, "cost": 0.31, "ms": 180000},
   "curate": {"runs": 20, "kev_tokens_in": 108000, "kev_tokens_out": 1900, "judge_tokens_in": 36000, "judge_tokens_out": 4800, "cost": 0.084, "ms": 84000},
   "embed": {"runs": 2, "embed_tokens": 9800, "ms": 41000},
   "search": {"searches": 57, "embed_tokens": 640, "embed_ms": 22000, "fts_ms": 410},
   "total": {"tokens_in": 235000, "tokens_out": 11900, "embed_tokens": 10440, "cost": 0.394, "ms": 305000}},
  "retrieval": {
   "reads": {"pushed": 0, "search": 140, "show": 88},
   "reading_sessions": 17,
   "cited": {"used": 31, "conversion": 0.136},
   "unread_in_force": 71,
   "searches": {"total": 57, "hybrid": 50, "fts": 7, "zero_hit": 6,
    "recent_zero_hit_queries": ["engine socket path"],
    "fts_ms": {"mean": 7.2, "max": 31}, "embed_ms": {"mean": 440.0, "max": 1210}}}}],
 "markdown": "## building-cpd\n…"}
```

**`sizes`** (a snapshot):
- `records.by_kind` has the four keys `decision`, `note`, `plan` and `brief`, each `{count, bytes}`; a record of another kind (`question`, `answer`) is in neither map. `bytes` is the sum of the UTF-8 byte length of the records' `text`.
- `records.by_status` has the four keys `in_force`, `superseded`, `retired_approved` and `retired_pending`, each `{count, bytes}`, and counts the same records as `by_kind` does. The statuses are **exclusive**, with this precedence: `retired_approved` (a `record_retirements` row `approved`) over `superseded` (named in the `supersedes` of a later record) over `retired_pending` (a `record_retirements` row `pending`) over `in_force`. Invariant: the `count` of the four statuses sums to the `count` of the four kinds, and so do the `bytes`.
- `curated` is `{count, short_bytes}`: the `record_curations` rows of the Context and the sum of the byte length of their `short`.
- `provisional_topics` is the number of `record_topics` rows whose record has no `record_curations` row (a curated topic wins, §3.3a).
- `vectors` is `{count, checked, blob_bytes}`: the Context's rows in `context_embeddings` (all models), its rows in `context_checked`, and the sum of `length(vector)`. An absent `vectors.db` gives zeros.

**`writing_and_curation`** (in the `--since` window):
- `records_written` is the records of the Context with `at` in the window, of every kind.
- `distill` is taken from the lines of `runs.jsonl` with `started_at` in the window: `runs` is the number of lines, `failed` the lines whose `result` is `"failed"`, `rejected` the sum of the lengths of the `rejected` arrays the lines carry, `curations` and `retire` the counters a line carries (0 when it carries none).
- `curate` is taken from the lines of `curate-runs.jsonl` of kind `curate` with `at` in the window: `runs` is the number of lines and each other key is the sum of that counter.
- `retirements` counts the `record_retirements` rows of the Context whose `proposed_at` is in the window, by `reason` and by `status`.

**`cost`** (in the window; cost in USD; a `cost` is a sum of the costs that were reported, 0 when none was, and never null):
- `distill`: `runs`, the sums of `tokens_in`, `tokens_out` and `cost` of the lines (a null counts as 0), and `ms` the sum of `seconds` × 1000.
- `curate`: `runs`, and the sums of `kev_tokens_in`, `kev_tokens_out`, `judge_tokens_in`, `judge_tokens_out`, `cost` and `ms` over the lines of kind `curate`.
- `embed`: `runs` (lines of kind `embed`) and the sums of `embed_tokens` and `ms`.
- `search`: `searches` is the `search_log` rows in the window; `embed_tokens`, `embed_ms` and `fts_ms` are the sums (a null counts as 0).
- `total`: `tokens_in` = `distill.tokens_in` + `curate.kev_tokens_in` + `curate.judge_tokens_in`; `tokens_out` likewise; `embed_tokens` = the `embed_tokens` of `curate` lines, `embed` and `search`; `cost` = `distill.cost` + `curate.cost`; `ms` = `distill.ms` + `curate.ms` + `embed.ms` + `search.embed_ms` + `search.fts_ms`.

**`retrieval`** (in the window):
- `reads` counts the `context_reads` rows with `read_at` in the window by channel: `pushed`, `search`, `show` (the reserved `shadow` is not listed). `reading_sessions` is the number of distinct sessions among them.
- `cited.used` is the rows with `used` 1; `cited.conversion` is `used` ÷ the total of the rows, 0 when there are none.
- `unread_in_force` is the number of records that are `in_force` or `retired_pending` (the `by_status` rule above) and have no `context_reads` row at all (a snapshot: the window does not apply).
- `searches`: `total` is the `search_log` rows in the window; `hybrid` and `fts` split it by `mode` (`total` = `hybrid` + `fts`); `zero_hit` is the rows with `hits` 0; `recent_zero_hit_queries` is the `query` strings of the newest of those rows, at most 10, newest first. `fts_ms` and `embed_ms` are `{mean, max}` over the rows that have the value (`embed_ms` is null on a `fts` row); both are `null` when there is no sample.

Output: `since` is the `--since` value normalised to UTC, else `null`; `contexts` is the list of entries above; `markdown` is the report as GFM.

Idempotent: yes; with nothing new logged, a rerun returns the same figures.

## 4. `plan`

A Plan (§2.2) and its phases (§3.1). Replaces cpd 1's `workflow` group (D3) and `plan` group.

### 4.1 `plan new`

```
cpd plan new <id> --context <c> --title <text> [--jira <key>] [--brief-file <file>] [--by-user] [--tier <T>] [--runner <pi|durable>] [--shaping]
```

A Plan has no repo (R34, A12): its Workflows are added later with `workflow add` (§9.4) and its Lead starts in the User's home directory, whatever directory `plan new` runs from (contract §2.2, pro-d343). `--repo` and `--base` are gone: either is `usage` (exit 2). `--name` is gone too: it is `usage` (exit 2). The Lead's name is its agent key, `<context>:<plan>` (contract §2.2 "Agent key").

**`--shaping`** (air-d19, air-d22; A1, A2). The Context's live Manager creates a **Lead-less** Plan: `lead_session` null, phase `shaping`, no Lead Session row, no pane, no first message and no `run/<id>/lead-message.md`. The Manager adds the Plan's explore Jobs and is their subscriber (the paragraph "A Manager on a shaping Plan" below). Only a Manager may run it: a Lead, a Worker or the User's cockpit with `--shaping` is refused `shaping_manager_only` (exit 2). With `--shaping`, `--brief-file`, `--by-user`, `--tier` and `--runner` are refused `usage` (exit 2): a shaping Plan has no Lead to brief, register by-user, tier or run. `plan new` without `--shaping` is unchanged.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | Plan id (§2.1) |
| `--context <c>` | required: the Plan's Context (D2) |
| `--title <text>` | required; 1–200 characters, no control characters, else `usage` (§1.5) |
| `--jira <key>` | Jira ticket key, stored only |
| `--brief-file <file>` | the brief for the Lead (B3-A4): written as a Context record of kind `brief` and put into the Lead's first message in full |
| `--by-user` | (hs-d542 A2) when registering a new Lead, stores the flag on the Session and writes no first message (§1.4); `plan new` and `context manager` use it (§3.11); omit it and the Lead starts with its first message, as today |
| `--tier <T>` | the Lead's Tier (contract §2.2, §9): a Tier in the Tier flag syntax (§5), checked against the lead range (below). Omitted, the Tier is `lead_tier` (Effects, step 1) |
| `--runner <pi|durable>` | the new Lead's runner; omitted, `durable` when `experimental.durable_leads` is on, else the config key `lead_runner`, default `pi` (contract §6.19 "The config keys") |
| `--shaping` | (air-d19, air-d22) create a **Lead-less** shaping Plan, the Context's Manager only (below): no Lead Session, no pane, no first message, phase `shaping`, `lead_session` null. Refused `shaping_manager_only` for any other caller; `--brief-file`, `--by-user`, `--tier` and `--runner` are refused with it (`usage`) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Context exists | `context_not_found` | 4 |
| the Context has an owner (contract §8.3; null only for a Context made before the owner existed); the message names `cpd context owner <login> --context <c>` | `owner_unset` | 3 |
| `--tier` is not valid syntax (§5; effort 5 included), or an effort the catalog lacks for the Tier's model (the models of the Context, contract §8.3; the catalog is read only when `--tier` is given); `details.tier` and `details.efforts` for an effort | `tier_invalid` | 2 |
| `--tier` is outside the lead range, from `lead_tier` (the floor) up to the highest valid rung strictly below `manager_tier` (contract §9 "Roles and ranges", checked after `tier_invalid`); `details` `{tier, role: "lead", floor, ceiling, allowed: "<floor>-<ceiling>", key: "lead_tier"}`, message `Tier <T> is outside the lead range <floor>-<ceiling>, set by lead_tier and below manager_tier.` | `tier_not_allowed` | 2 |
| no Plan with this id, unless every flag matches it (then the result is `already`) | `plan_exists` | 3 |
| no Context row with this id, deleted ones included, when no Plan row has this id (a rerun for an existing Plan is `already` or `plan_exists`, as above) | `id_taken` | 3 |
| the Context is not archived; `details.next` = `cpd context unarchive <c>` | `archived` | 3 |
| `--runner` is neither `pi` nor `durable` | `usage` | 2 |
| the caller is not the Context's live Manager with `--shaping` | `shaping_manager_only` | 2 |
| `--shaping` together with `--brief-file`, `--by-user`, `--tier` or `--runner` | `usage` | 2 |

Effects, in this order:
1. **Rows**, one transaction: `sessions` (new UUID v4; `role = lead`; `context`; `plan = <id>`; `name` = `<context>:<plan>`; `cwd` = the User's home directory (contract §2.2, pro-d343), never the caller's cwd; `tier` = the Lead's Tier (the `--tier` flag; else `lead_tier`; contract §2.2); `forked_from` null; `by_user` = 1 when `--by-user`, else 0; `state = stopped`: the Lead is always fresh, never a fork, B3-A3); `plans` (`phase = grounding`, `lead_session` = the new Session); no `workflows` row. **Events** `plan-created` `{title, jira, lead_session, forked_from: null, cwd}` and `session-registered` `{role, name, forked_from, tier}`.
2. **Context records:** the record write of §3 (one transaction) with kind `plan` (letter `p`), `text` = the title, `plan` = `{id, machine, jira}` (`jira` omitted when null); **Event** `context-record`. With `--brief-file`, a second record of kind `brief` (letter `b`), `text` = the file's text, `plan` = `{id, machine}`; **Event** `context-record`. Then the citation marking of §3.5 (best-effort, the Session rule of §3.3), over the texts of the `plan` record and the `brief` record.
3. **First message**, when `by_user` is 0, written to `run/<id>/lead-message.md` (contract §4.6 "Consumers", hs-d655): a header (`You are the Lead of Plan <id> "<title>" in Context <c>. Phase grounding: follow the cpd-lead skill.`), the full brief (the file's text) if given, then, when `context topics` (§3.3a) has at least one topic, the `Topics:` line between the brief (or the header) and the pointer line: `Topics: engine (3), store (1)`, the `markdown` of `context topics` (§3.3a) with the prefix `Topics: `, a snapshot taken when the message is written, with no cap, its counts following C5 of §3.3a (none is written when `context topics` has no topic). Then the pointer line:
   ```
   Context on demand: cpd context search <query> · cpd context show --since <seq> · cpd context show --record <id>
   ```
   The Lead gets on-demand access to the Context through these commands. The Lead is always fresh (B3-A3): the grounded Lead and its forks are retired (contract §3.1), so there is no fork case. When `by_user` is 1, no file is written (hs-d542 A2).
4. **tmux:** start the server if it is not running (§6.1) and the cockpit session `cpd` if it is missing; then `new-window -d -t =cpd: -n park-<id> -c <cwd> -e CPD_HOME=… -e CPD_SESSION=<session> -e CPD_PLAN=<id> -P -F '#{window_id} #{pane_id}' -- cpd session run <session>` and `set -p -t <pane> @cpd_session <session>`, then `@cpd_title` to the Lead's pill (contract §6.1: its dynamic title when it has one, else its key `<context>:<plan>`; the Plan's title is never the pill). One transaction: `sessions.tmux_pane`; **Event** `session-moved` `{pane, window, place: "parked"}`. If any step after `new-window` fails (`set-option -p @cpd_session`, the row or the Event write), the new window is killed (`kill-window`) before the error is returned (teardown G11). **For a durable Lead** (`runner` `durable`, contract §6.19) this step and its `session-moved` are skipped: no tmux, no pane. The Session is left live and `stopped`, and the engine's hosts step starts its host at the next tick (contract §6.19); the output `lead.pane` and `lead.window` are null.
5. In the pane, `session run` (§10.8) starts a fresh Lead; when `by_user` is 1, it waits for the User's first prompt before starting pi (contract §10.8 step 3, hs-d542 A2). A durable Lead has no pane and no `session run`: its host is the engine's (§6.19).

**With `--shaping`** only step 1 runs, and it differs: one `plans` row (`phase = shaping`, `lead_session` NULL) and one `plan-created` `{title, jira, lead_session: null, forked_from: null, cwd}`; no `sessions` row and no `session-registered`, no Context record, no first message, no tmux and no `session run`. Its output carries `phase` and `lead_session` at the top level, in the shape below:

```json
{"ok": true, "plan": {"id": "pay-4522", "context": "payments", "title": "Retry failed payouts", "jira": null, "phase": "shaping", "lead_session": null, "workflows": []},
 "phase": "shaping", "lead_session": null}
```

When the cockpit session is missing, plan new creates it with the new Lead's park window as its first window; cpd tui builds main later.

```json
{"ok": true, "plan": {"id": "pay-4521", "context": "payments", "title": "Retry failed payouts", "jira": null, "phase": "grounding", "lead_session": "8d0e…", "workflows": []},
 "lead": {"session": "8d0e…", "name": "payments:pay-4521", "forked_from": null, "cwd": "/home/clayton", "pane": "%41", "window": "@17"},
 "record": "hs-p4"}
```

Idempotent: yes. With the same flags it returns `"already": true` and redoes any step that did not happen: the `plan` record when the Context has none for this Plan, the `brief` record when `--brief-file` is given and the Context has none for this Plan and step 4 when the Lead is `stopped` with no pane (in the stored `cwd`). The cwd is not a flag and is never the caller's: a rerun from another directory is still `already` and keeps the stored `cwd`. `--tier` is one of 'the same flags' only when it equals the stored `sessions.tier` of the Plan's Lead session: then the result is `already`, as above; a different Tier is `plan_exists` (exit 3, as for the other flags). The `--runner` flag is also one of 'the same flags': a rerun of an existing Plan with a different `--runner` is `plan_exists` (exit 3), as for a different `--title`. The `--tier` checks of the table run first, so a refused Tier is refused whatever the Plan's state. A rerun without `--tier` compares no Tier, whatever the Lead's stored Tier is. Different flags: `plan_exists`. The `--by-user` flag is part of 'the same flags': a rerun with or without it when the Plan exists is `plan_exists` (hs-d542 A1).

**A Manager on a shaping Plan** (air-d19, air-d22; A3). A **shaping Plan** is a Lead-less Plan: `lead_session` null, phase `shaping`, or `done` once a Lead-less shaping Plan has settled. On a shaping Plan of its own Context, a Manager names the Plan with `--plan <id>` (it has no `CPD_PLAN`) and runs `job add` (explore kinds only), `job list`, `job show`, `job cancel`, `job retry`, `attempt list`, `attempt show`, `attempt read`, `attempt abort` and `answer`. Each is refused:
- `plan_has_lead` (exit 3): the Plan has a Lead (`lead_session` not null); a Manager never runs a Lead's command on it;
- `plan_other_context` (exit 2): the Plan belongs to another Context;
- `shaping_explore_only` (exit 2): `job add` on a shaping Plan with `--kind` other than `scout` or `research`, or with `--workflow`, since a shaping Plan holds only explore Jobs.

`job add` of an explore Job on a `done` Lead-less Plan reopens it to `shaping`, as an explore Job on a Lead's `done` Plan reopens it to `plan`. The Lead-only commands stay Lead-only and are refused for a Manager as they are today: `plan phase`, `plan lock`, `plan review`, `plan outline`, `plan render`, `plan lint` and every `workflow` command name no Manager right.

### 4.2 `plan list`

```
cpd plan list [--context <id>] [--phase <phase>]
```

`--phase` is one of §3.1's phases. Archived Plans are listed, with `archived_at` (null, or a time). Each Plan carries `reviewed_pr` (contract §2.2 Plan: null, or the pull request a review Plan reviews, `{repo, number, url, title, state}`); this list is the cockpit's `plan` pane (contract §5.5). Effects: none. Each Plan carries `open_pr_checks`, `{passed, pending, failed}`: how many of its Workflows' pull requests are `open` with those `checks` (swr-github §10 (c)). Each Plan lists its Workflows (R34) in key order, `cancelled` ones included, with `key`, `repo`, `status`, `pr` (`{number, url, opened_at}` or null) and `pull_request` (hs-d96: its row of contract §2.2 "Pull request", `{repo, number, url, title, draft, state, review_decision, checks, mergeable, merge_state, created_at, merged_at}`, or null before `pr open`). The Workflows of a list carry no `posted` (pro-d77): `pr.posted` is `plan show` only (§4.3). A **Lead-less** Plan (`lead_session` null, phase `shaping`; air-d19, air-d22) is listed with phase `"shaping"`, `lead_session` `null` and `workflows` `[]`; its explore Jobs are not part of this output (`plan show` and `context pending` carry them).

```json
{"ok": true, "plans": [{"id": "cpd2", "context": "building-cpd", "title": "cpd in Rust", "phase": "dispatch", "lead_session": "596d007f-…", "archived_at": null,
  "counts": {"draft": 0, "queued": 2, "running": 1, "merged": 2, "failed": 0, "cancelled": 0},
  "open_pr_checks": {"passed": 0, "pending": 0, "failed": 0},
  "workflows": [{"key": "cpd", "repo": "/home/clayton/projects/cpd", "status": "dispatch", "pr": null, "pull_request": null}]}],
 "events_cursor": 48213}
```

Idempotent: read-only.

### 4.3 `plan show`

```
cpd plan show [--plan <id>]
```

Effects: none; one read transaction, so the result is one consistent snapshot. It is the TUI's snapshot of a Plan (§17).

Output: every field of the Plan (§2.2), `outline` included (hs-d502: the outline object of §4.13, parsed from `plans.outline`, or `null`), and `reviewed_pr` (contract §2.2 Plan: null, or `{repo, number, url, title, state}`, the `state` read from the effective row of `swr::github::effective_pr` (swr-github §6), not live, `null` when there is none); `workflows` (R34, A14), every Workflow of the Plan in key order, `cancelled` ones included, each with its fields (§2.2 Workflow: `key`, `repo`, `base`, `base_workflow` (the base Workflow as `<plan>/<key>`, derived from `base`, or null: hs-d324), `jira` (the Workflow's Jira ticket, the key or null: pro-d127, B2), `needs` (Workflow references: a bare key of this Plan, `<plan>/<key>` of another), `status`, `lead_branch`, `lead_worktree`, `pr` (`{number, url, opened_at}`, or null; when non-null it also carries `posted`, a boolean: true iff a `pr_posts` row exists for the Workflow, that is `cpd pr post` has posted it to Slack, pro-d77), `pull_request` (the effective row of `swr::github::effective_pr`, as in §4.2, `mergeable`, `merge_state` and `head_oid` included, and `feedback_open` repeated inside it, or null: swr-github §6 and §10 (c)), `closed_unmerged` (boolean: true iff the closed-unmerged predicate of contract §3.8 holds for the Workflow; in `plan show` only, `plan list`, `pr poll` and `context pending` are unchanged), `feedback_open` (integer: the number of open feedback items in the row's stored list, contract §2.2 "Feedback item"; null when the list is NULL, never read; pro-d68), `all_merged_at`, `start_failed_at`, `created_at`, `started_at`, `merged_at`) and `jobs`, the keys of its Jobs in `seq` order; `jobs` with each Job's fields (Spec included, `workflow`, `review` and `urgent` among them), `needs` and its Attempts (`id`, `number`, `tier`, `origin`, `status`, `outcome`, `cause`, `worker_session`, `started_at`, `ended_at`); `escalations` that are `open`; the latest Plan review; `counts`; `tamper` (the tamper report of §4.3: `{kind: "schema" | "fingerprint" | "history", …}`); `events_cursor`. A **Lead-less** Plan (`lead_session` null, phase `shaping`, or `done` after a Lead-less `shaping` Plan settled; air-d19, air-d22) has `lead_session` `null` and no Lead in `workflows` (there is none); its explore Jobs are in the top-level `jobs` array with `workflow` `null`.
