### 4.4 `plan phase`

```
cpd plan phase plan [--plan <id>]
```

The only phase moved by hand (cpd 1 §11 `workflow phase`, kept). Any other target is `illegal_transition` (exit 3).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the phase is `grounding` (already `plan`: `already`) | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| no explore Job (`scout`, `research`) of the Plan is `queued`, `running` or `failed`; `details` `{plan, jobs}` | `explore_pending` | 3 |

Effects (B3-A3; no grounded Lead is created, hs-d129): **rows**, one transaction: `plans.phase = plan`; **Event** `plan-phase` `{from: "grounding", to: "plan"}`. No Session, no `context-grounded` Event, no tmux. In phase `grounding`, the explore check (pro-d374, assumption A2) runs in the same transaction, before the change: `details.jobs` is the sorted list of the keys of the Plan's Jobs of kind `scout` or `research` that are `queued`, `running` or `failed`; a `merged` or `cancelled` explore Job does not block, and a refusal writes nothing.

```json
{"ok": true, "plan": "pay-4521", "phase": "plan"}
```

Idempotent: yes; in phase `plan` it returns `"already": true` and writes nothing.

### 4.5 `plan render`

```
cpd plan render [--plan <id>]
```

Effects: writes `run/<plan>/plan.md` and `run/<plan>/summary.md` (§1.4), nothing else. The render reads the Plan's Jobs, Workflows and outline, and the Tier advice (§3.4b; the catalog when needed); a catalog read may fail with the catalog's own error (`pi_not_found`, `catalog_failed`, `tier_model_unknown`, exit 1). Content of `plan.md`, kept from cpd 1 §11 `plan render` and grouped by Workflow (R34): title, Context and phase; a table of the Workflows that are not `merged`, with key, repo, base and needs, each row muted and marked `cancelled` when the Workflow is `cancelled` (hs-d518), with its `status` and `cancel_reason` or `superseded by <ref>` when the Event carries `superseded_by`; and, when there are two or more, a Mermaid `graph LR` of their needs (cancelled Workflows not in the graph, hs-d518); then the section `## Overlaps` (below); then one section per Workflow that is not `cancelled` (hs-d518), in the order of the needs graph (ties by key), headed `Workflow <key>`, with its repo, base and needs, a table of its Jobs with key, title, Tier, status, needs and touches, each row muted and marked `cancelled` when the Job is `cancelled` (hs-d518), with its `status` and `cancel_reason` (hs-d518), a Mermaid `graph TD` of its Jobs' Dependencies (cancelled Jobs not in the graph) and one subsection per Job that is not `cancelled` (hs-d518) with its Spec. The Tier column and each Job section's `Tier:` line show the Tier the Job is displayed at (contract §3.4a): the active Attempt's Tier, or `retry_tier` while queued at it after `job retry`, or the latest Attempt's Tier, or the stored `tier`. The `open` Job placeholder keeps `worker_tier`. **Waiting display** (hs-d521): a Job or Workflow table row whose status is `waiting` (display only, hs-d523) shows the blockers as `waiting on <keys>` in its status column or as a separate line (hs-d521); in the Mermaid graph (hs-d518), a cancelled Workflow is omitted and in the render's graph of needs a cancelled Workflow appears neither as a node nor in edges; in the per-Workflow Job graph, cancelled Jobs do not appear. **The open Job's placeholder** (hs-d497): a Workflow that has not started has no `open` Job yet (engine E4 adds it at the start), so the render shows one for each such Workflow, as the last row of its Jobs table and as the last Job section: key `open-<workflow>`, title `Open the pull request: <pull request title>`, Tier `worker_tier` (contract §8.2), status `—` (not a Job yet), needs `every other Job of the Workflow` and, in place of the Spec, `Added by cpd when the Workflow starts: merges the base only on a conflict, runs the Gate, pushes and opens the pull request ready.` It is not a row, is in no fingerprint and no Mermaid graph and is shown in every phase until the Workflow starts (once the Workflow has started the real `open` Job is shown as any Job, with its derived needs, contract §3.2). A Job's section is under its Workflow only. In a phase after `plan`, the Jobs that are not `draft` are Locked Jobs, shown as context: the render shows them as such and marks every `draft` Job **under review** except a `draft` `open` Job, which cpd added and the Lead does not review: it is shown as context, never `**under review**` (hs-d573) (in its table row and its section), because a review in these phases covers exactly the drafts (§4.6; User, hs-d173, hs-d174, hs-d179). In phase `plan` every Job is a draft and nothing is marked. A **stub draft** (no Tier or no Spec, §5.1) is shown as it is, visibly incomplete: `Tier: —` in its table row and section when it has no Tier and `Spec: not written yet` in place of its Spec subsection's goal, context, touches, acceptance and out of scope when it has none. GitHub-flavoured Markdown only: tables, code and Mermaid, no footnotes, no raw HTML (t4). It also writes the **Plan summary**, `run/<plan>/summary.md` (below, hs-d502). Output: the path, `summary` (the path of the summary), the plan fingerprint (§2.3: Jobs, Workflows and the outline when set), the number of `draft` Jobs (`draft_jobs`, not counting a `draft` `open` Job: it is not under review, hs-d573), the number of Workflows that are not `cancelled` and the overlaps.

**Kinds** (hs-d340, hs-d341). A Job's `kind` is a column of its row in the Workflow's table and a line of its section when it is not `work`; a `test` Job's section lists its `tests` and `test_files` and a Job's section lists its `resources` with the Spec when it has any. The Workflow's `open` Job, once the Workflow has started, is a Job of its Workflow like any other, with its derived needs (contract §3.2); before the start it does not exist, so the review of a Plan shows the template's Jobs and the `open` Job as `plan render`'s placeholder (§4.5, hs-d497), the one every Workflow will get.

**Overlaps** (B4-A3, hs-d78, hs-d172, hs-n201): the warning that another Plan is working on the same files. It is made here and so in the Plan review (§4.6) and nowhere else: `job add` does not warn. It looks at **open work** only, on both sides: the Jobs that are not `cancelled` (`draft`, `queued`, `running`, `failed`, or `merged` on its Lead Branch) of Workflows that are not `merged` and not `cancelled`. A Job of a `merged` Workflow is on its base already and cannot clash with anyone's work any more, so the Jobs of this Plan's `merged` Workflows are not checked. For each Workflow of this Plan that is not `merged` and not `cancelled`, every **other** active Plan (any Context; its phase is not `done` and it is not archived) is looked at when it has a Workflow in the same repo (the same `workflows.repo` realpath as stored) that is not `merged` and not `cancelled`. A Job of that Workflow overlaps a Job of this Workflow when a path in the `touches` of the one overlaps a path in the `touches` of the other. Two paths overlap when they are equal, or when one is a directory (ends with `/`) that contains the other. Nothing else is compared (no globs, no normalisation). A Plan's own Jobs are never listed. The warning is only that: nothing is refused and no state changes.

The overlaps are grouped: **one overlap per (this Job, other Plan, other Workflow)**. It lists every Job of that other Workflow that overlaps this Job, with its status and the paths of this Job that overlap one of them, each path once, in the order of the Job's `touches`. A broad path (`core/src/`) or a shared file is one entry of a row, not a row of its own for every pair of paths and Jobs (hs-n201: on a busy Context that made thousands of rows and nobody could read them in a Plan review).

`plan.md` has the section `## Overlaps` after the Workflows table (and its graph), before the Workflow sections: a table with one row per overlap, ordered by this Job's key, then the other Plan, then the Workflow; or, when there is none, the line `No other active Plan touches these files.` A Plan with no Workflow yet has no Workflows table and no section.

**The Explore section** (Plan `explore-roles`, R3, R9). When the Plan has explore Jobs (`scout`, `research`, §5.1), `plan.md` has the section `## Explore` after `## Overlaps` and before the Workflow sections: a table with the columns exactly `Job | Kind | Tier | Status | Needs | Question | Artefact`, one row per explore Job in key order (`Needs` its needs joined by `, `, `—` when none; `Question` the first line of its `goal`, at most 100 characters; `Artefact` `run/<plan>/explore/<key>.md`); then, for each merged explore Job, a `### <key>` heading and its `summary`. Both are absent when the Plan has no explore Job. Explore Jobs are in no other block of the render: not the Jobs of a Workflow's table, not a Workflow's Mermaid graph.

```
## Explore

| Job | Kind | Tier | Status | Needs | Question | Artefact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cache-key` | `scout` | H2 | merged | — | Where is the cache key built? | `run/pay-4521/explore/cache-key.md` |

### cache-key
The key is built in `core/src/cache.rs` from the repo path and the schema version.
```

```
## Overlaps

| Job | Other Plan | Workflow | Its Jobs (status) | Paths |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | `pay-4522` | `api` | `y` (queued), `z` (draft) | `core/src/x.rs`, `core/src/lib.rs` |
```

The columns are this Plan's Job, the other Plan, its Workflow, the Jobs of that Workflow that overlap this Job with their status (in the order they were created) and the paths of this Job that overlap them. `Paths` shows at most five paths and then `+N` for the N more, as in `` `a`, `b`, `c`, `d`, `e`, +2 ``. In the JSON output, `overlaps` lists the same rows, in the same order, as `{job, plan, workflow, other_jobs: [{key, status}], paths}`: `other_jobs` are the Jobs of the other Workflow that overlap `job` and `paths` are all the paths of `job` that overlap them, deduplicated (only the table is capped); `[]` when there is none.

```json
{"ok": true, "path": "/home/clayton/.cpd/run/pay-4521/plan.md", "summary": "/home/clayton/.cpd/run/pay-4521/summary.md", "fingerprint": "9f86d081…", "draft_jobs": 6, "workflows": 2, "warnings": [],
 "overlaps": [{"job": "x", "plan": "pay-4522", "workflow": "api", "other_jobs": [{"key": "y", "status": "queued"}, {"key": "z", "status": "draft"}], "paths": ["core/src/x.rs", "core/src/lib.rs"]}]}
```

Idempotent: yes (the same Workflows and Jobs, the same outline and the same other Plans, render the same two files). Change: cpd 1's `--out` is dropped; the file has one place.

**The Plan summary** (hs-d502, D4; User, 2026-10-20, hs-d502 supersedes hs-d468). A short text cpd generates from the Plan and its outline (§4.13), so the User approves a Plan from a screenful in the Lead's chat instead of reading the render (§15.5). `plan render` writes it to `run/<plan>/summary.md` and `plan review` (§4.6) writes the same text, with the review's heading, to `run/<plan>/summary-<review>.md`. It is derived and holds no information the Plan lacks: it carries no Spec, no Mermaid and no row for a Locked Job. GitHub-flavoured Markdown only (§4.5 above). Deterministic: the same Plan, outline, overlaps, review and path give the same bytes.

**Vocabulary.** A Job **under review** is a `draft` Job that has a Tier and a Spec, a `draft` `open` Job excepted (cpd's, shown as context, hs-d573); a **stub draft** is a `draft` Job without one of them (§5.1; the template's, before the lock, §9.4). A Job is **locked** when it is neither `draft` nor `cancelled`. A Workflow **counts** when it is not `cancelled`. Keys sort bytewise.

**Layout.** The file is a sequence of **blocks**, in the order below, separated by exactly one blank line and ends with one newline. A block that has nothing to say is left out, except the first, the Goal, the Jobs block and the last. A block is one or more consecutive lines.

| # | Block | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | heading | `# <review title>`, then `Plan <plan id>: <Plan title> · review <review id>`. In `summary.md` (no review): `# Plan: <Plan title>`, then `Plan <plan id> · phase <phase>` |
| 2 | goal | `Goal: <goal>` from the outline; `Goal: —` when the Plan has no outline |
| 3 | Workflows | `## Workflows`, then for each Workflow that counts and has a Job under review, in key order, `- <key> (<repo name>, base <base>): <pull request title>` and under it one line `  Done when: <line>` (two leading spaces) per line of the outline's `done_when[<key>]`, in order, none when the outline is null or has no entry for it. `<repo name>` is the Workflow's `name` (§2.2 Workflow), else the last path segment of its `repo`; `<base>` the Workflow's `base`; `<pull request title>` the Workflow's `title`, else `—` |
| 4 | decisions | `## Decisions`, then `D<n> <question> → <answer>` per outline decision, `n` from 1 in the outline's order |
| 5 | assumptions | `## Assumptions`, then `A<n> <text>` per outline assumption, `n` from 1 |
| 6 | Jobs | `## Jobs (<n> under review, <m> locked)`, `n` the number of Jobs under review and `m` the number of locked Jobs, then a table with the columns `Job`, `Title`, `Tier`, `Needs`, one row per Job under review in Workflow key order, then Job key order: its key, its title, its Tier and its `needs` joined by `, ` (`—` when none). The table has its header and separator rows even with no Job under review. No locked Job has a row |
| 7 | order | `Order: <items>`, the items joined by `, `: one `<need> → <key>` for every need of a Workflow that counts, whose need is a Workflow that counts too, in key order of the Workflow and then of the need; then, as the last item, the Workflows that count and neither need nor are needed by any other, joined by ` · ` (no such item when there is none). Then the line `Stacked on: <entries>`, one `<key> on <base Workflow>` per Workflow that counts and has a base Workflow (`base_workflow` of `plan show`, §4.3: `<plan>/<key>`), in key order, joined by `, `; `none` when none is stacked. Both lines are left out when no Workflow counts |
| 8 | overlaps | `Overlaps: none` when §4.5's overlaps are none; else `Overlaps: <n>`, `n` the number of overlaps (the rows of §4.5's table), then one row per overlap, in §4.5's order and at most 5: `- <path>: <other plan>/<other workflow>/<other job> (<status>)`, the first of the overlap's paths and the first of its other Jobs with its status, followed by ` +<k>` when the overlap has more (`k` = the other paths plus the other Jobs); when `n` is over 5, a last row `- +<n-5> more overlaps` |
| 9 | lint | `Lint: none` when there is no warning, never omitted (like `Overlaps`); else `Lint: <n>` and then one row per warning in finding order, at most 5, each `- <rule>: <row>`, and `- +<N> more warnings` for the rest. A `parallel_write_overlap` row is `<job> and <other> both name <paths>`: its paths joined by `, `, at most 3, then ` +<k>` for the k more, followed by ` (a hint, not a conflict prediction)` |
| 10 | decided | `Decided: <ids>`, the outline's `decided` record ids joined by `, `; left out when there are none |
| 11 | later | `Later: <items>`, the work this review does not cover, joined by `, `: the keys of the stub drafts in key order, then `Workflow <key>` for each Workflow that counts and has no Job under review, in key order; left out when there are none |
| 12 | risks | `## Risks`, then `R<n> <text>` per outline risk, `n` from 1 |
| 13 | out of scope | `## Out of scope`, then `- <text>` per outline entry |
| 14 | last line | for a review: `Approve \| Change` (the pipe literal); for `summary.md`: `Full plan (<path>)`, the absolute path of `plan.md` |

Blocks 4, 5, 10, 12 and 13 come from the outline and are left out when it is null or the list is empty. The sizes are bounded by the outline's own limits (§4.13: at most 3 risks, 5 out-of-scope entries, 3 done-when lines per Workflow) and by the overlap rows above; the decisions, assumptions and Jobs are as many as the Plan has. A `done_when` key of a Workflow that was cancelled after `plan outline` is not shown (the block lists Workflows that count).

```
# Plan review in chat
Plan plan-ux: Plan UX · review r2

Goal: Show a Plan review as a short summary in the Lead's chat, approved in one dialog

## Workflows
- cpd (cpd, base main): Summary, review in chat and outline
  Done when: plan review writes summary-<review>.md from the outline
  Done when: the adapter shows it in chat with Approve and Change

## Decisions
D1 Where is the review shown? → In the Lead's chat

## Assumptions
A1 The outline is written by the Lead, not inferred

## Jobs (2 under review, 1 locked)
| Job | Title | Tier | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| ux-docs | Docs for the review in chat | S3 | — |
| ux-summary | Summary and outline | O3 | ux-docs |

Order: cpd
Stacked on: none

Overlaps: none

Lint: none

Decided: hs-d502, hs-d503

Later: ux-remeasure

## Risks
R1 pi's dialog API differs between modes

## Out of scope


Approve | Change
```

**The Lint block** (§4.6). The warnings of the lint run on the Plan (contract §2.7, commands.md §4.15), never errors: `plan review` and `plan render` refuse with errors, but return warnings. The block lists warnings only. `Lint: none` when there is no warning, never omitted (like `Overlaps`); else `Lint: <n>` and then one row per warning in finding order, at most 5: `- <rule>: <row>`, and `- +<N> more warnings` for the rest. A `parallel_write_overlap` row is `<job> and <other> both name <paths>`: its paths joined by `, `, at most 3, then ` +<k>` for the k more, followed by ` (a hint, not a conflict prediction)`; `Finding::row(&self)` (core/src/plan/lint.rs) builds the `<row>` after the rule (an error rule's row being its message). In the JSON output, `warnings` is an array of Finding JSON (`Finding::to_json`, one per warning in finding order, `[]` when none; see commands.md §4.15). A Plan with no PR and no cancelled PR has no `## Lint` section (like `## Overlaps`).

### 4.6 `plan review`

```
cpd plan review [--plan <id>] --title <text>
```

`--title` is **required** (hs-d291): it names what the drafts under review do, so the User sees it as the heading of the review, in the summary in the Lead's chat and in the full render. It has the rule of a Workflow's title: 1–72 characters, one line, no control characters; a bad or missing one is `usage` (exit 2). It is stored as `plan_reviews.title` (contract §2.2).

Requests the User's approval of the draft Jobs (§2.2 Plan review). In phase `plan` the review covers the whole plan, as before; in every phase after `plan` it covers **exactly the draft Jobs** the Lead added: its fingerprint is over those drafts only (§2.3; a `draft` `open` Job is not one of them, so engine E4 adding one never voids a pending review, hs-d573) and the rendered plan marks them under review and shows the Locked Jobs as context (§4.5). A Lead that planned several batches adds the later ones as drafts (`job add --draft`, §5.1) and asks for one review per batch. The Lead runs it directly; the pi adapter shows the summary in the Lead's chat, with the approval dialog, when the `plan-review` Event arrives (§15.5), so the review opens from any caller, in whatever phase the Plan is. The User approves or asks for a change.

Explore Jobs (`scout`, `research`) are in no review (Plan `explore-roles`, R3): they are never `draft`, are in no block of the review's copy (the Jobs block counts the Jobs under review and the locked Jobs of the Workflows; the Explore section of §4.5 is not in the copy) and are in no fingerprint (§2.3), so adding one never voids a pending review.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the phase is `plan`, or any phase after it (not `grounding`) | `illegal_phase` | 3 |
| at least one Job is `draft` (in a phase after `plan` too: the drafts are what is reviewed; a `draft` `open` Job does not count, it is not under review, hs-d573) | `no_draft_jobs` | 3 |
| every `draft` Job has its Tier and its Spec (hs-d241, R1: no stub draft is approvable); `details.jobs` lists `[{key, missing}]`, `missing` being `["tier"]`, `["spec"]` or both | `draft_incomplete` | 3 |
| the Plan has an outline (§4.13; hs-d502, D3); `details.next` = `cpd plan outline --file <outline.json>` | `outline_missing` | 3 |
| every Workflow that has a `draft` Job (under review, since the previous row passed) has an entry in the outline `done_when`; `details.workflows` lists the Workflow keys without one, in key order | `outline_incomplete` | 3 |
| every `impl` Job that is a `draft` needs at least one `test` Job of its Workflow (hs-d341; `details.jobs` lists the `impl` Jobs) | `test_job_required` | 3 |
| every `verify` Job that is a `draft` needs at least one `impl` Job of its Workflow that is not `cancelled` (pro-d80; `details` `{plan, job, jobs}`; checked after `test_job_required` and before `shape_incomplete`) | `impl_job_required` | 3 |
| every Workflow of shape `tdd` that has not opened has at least one `test` and one `impl` Job that is not `cancelled` (hs-d497, contract §2.2 "Job kinds"; `details` `{workflow, missing}`) | `shape_incomplete` | 3 |
| a Workflow that is not `cancelled` has no `draft` Job, or the Plan has no Workflow that is not `cancelled` (phase `plan` only; `details.workflows`, and `details.next` = `cpd workflow add` when the Plan has no live Workflow; checked after `shape_incomplete`) | `workflow_empty` | 3 |
| the `needs` of the draft Jobs contain a cycle (`details.cycle`; after `workflow_empty`) | `dependency_cycle` | 3 |
| two draft Jobs under review with no dependency path between them and files they both name (as in `spec.touches`); no "system" file (lockfile, autogen'd); see contract §2.7 (warning only, details `{}`) | `parallel_write_overlap` | 2 |
| a `draft` or `queued` Job of a Worker kind runs a Tier dearer than history favours (contract §2.7, hs-d556, hs-d608); a downward advise only, at a rate threshold (FLOOR = 10 first Attempts); one row per Job; for a `draft` the message suggests a change, `for a `queued` Job it does not; details `{}` (warning only) | `tier_advice` | 2 |

Effects:
- **Files:** renders the plan to `run/<plan>/plan.md` and `run/<plan>/summary.md` (§4.5) and copies the summary to `run/<plan>/summary-<review>.md`, so a later render cannot change what the User reviews. The summary copy is the Plan summary of §4.5 with the review's heading (block 1) and its last line (block 14) and no other difference; it is what the User reviews (§15.5). The copy opens with `# <review title>`, then one line `Plan <plan id>: <Plan title> · review <review id>`, then the rendered content (hs-d291); `plan.md`, made without a review (`plan render`, §4.5), keeps `# Plan: <Plan title>`. The reviewed file carries the `## Overlaps` section of §4.5, as it is at that moment, so the User sees the warning in the review: one row per open Job of this Plan and per other Workflow that overlaps it, short enough to read (hs-n201); it is a warning only and the review is requested all the same.
- **Closing other reviews:** every other pending review of the Plan (always older) closes `superseded` in the same transaction that inserts the new review request (the new `pending` Event comes after their `superseded` Events). Their Events say why: "Plan review r<k> of Plan P is superseded by r<k+1>." When the latest review is already pending for the current fingerprint (the `already: true` path) nothing is written, nothing closes.
- The refusals `outline_missing` and `outline_incomplete` come **before anything is written** (D3): no render, no file, no row, no Event.
- **Rows**, one transaction: `plan_reviews` (`id = r<k>`, `k` = 1 + the highest, `fingerprint` = the plan fingerprint (§2.3: it includes the outline), `title` = `--title`, `status = pending`). **Event** `plan-review` `{review, fingerprint, status: "pending"}`.

```json
{"ok": true, "review": {"id": "r3", "fingerprint": "9f86d081…", "status": "pending", "requested_at": "…"}, "summary": "/home/clayton/.cpd/run/pay-4521/summary-r3.md", "warnings": [],
 "next": "The User reviews the plan summary in your chat and decides there. Stop and wait for the decision message."}
```

**Stubs** (hs-d241, R1). A draft without its Tier or its Spec (a stub, §5.1) cannot be approved, so the review is **not requested**: it is refused `draft_incomplete` (exit 3) with `details.jobs` = `[{"key": "api-1", "missing": ["spec"]}, …]`, in key order, `missing` holding `"tier"` and/or `"spec"`. Nothing is rendered or written on refusal. The Lead completes each stub with `job edit --tier --spec` (§5.2) or cancels it, then asks again. The plan fingerprint covers a stub as it is (contract §2.3), so completing one changes it.

Idempotent: yes. When the latest review is `pending` for the current fingerprint, it returns that review with `"already": true` (its `path`, `summary` and `warnings` too) and writes nothing; the two refusals above are still checked first, so a Plan with no outline is refused even when a review made before the outline existed is pending. When the Jobs or Workflows changed since, it requests a new review and closes the older one `superseded`; the older one stays in the database, closed.

### 4.7 `plan decide` (internal)

```
cpd plan decide <review> (--approve | --reject) [--feedback-file <file>] [--plan <id>]
```

Records the User's decision. Called by the pi adapter with the result of the chat dialog (§15.5); replaces cpd 1's `plan decision` (cpd 1 §11), whose `--pending` step is now `plan review`. The cpd-lead skill forbids the Lead to run it. Internal (§1.1): hidden in clap, run only by the pi adapter.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the review is `pending` (decided the same way: `already`); a review with status `approved`, `rejected`, or `superseded` is refused `review_decided` | `review_decided` | 3 |

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: `plan_reviews.status`, `feedback` (the file's text, or null), `decided_at`. **Event** `plan-review` `{review, fingerprint, status, feedback}`.

In a phase after `plan`, or in a re-planned `plan` (`locked_at` set, A1), an **approval** also queues the drafts the review covered (§2.2, §3.2) in the same transaction:
- **Rows:** every `draft` Job of the Plan becomes `queued` and gets its Locked-Job fingerprint (§2.3), as an appended Job has at `job add`; `appended` stays 1. A `draft` `open` Job is one of them: it is queued here with the others, so a Workflow's `open` Job is `queued` exactly when its other Jobs are (contract §3.7 E4, hs-d573) and the `jobs` of the Event lists it too. The engine schedules each as soon as it is Ready (§3.2). **A draft of an `open` Workflow** that becomes `queued` here is a `work` Job and reaches the pull request by its own merge (§5.1; contract §3.8 "Updating"); no `update` Job is queued.
- **Event:** the same `plan-review` Event, whose `data` gains `jobs: [key]`, the Jobs it queued, in key order. No new Event kind. `plan-phase` is not appended in a phase after `plan`: the phase does not change. On a re-planned `plan`, the approval also returns the Plan to `dispatch` (A3): `plan-phase` `{from: "plan", to: "dispatch"}` is appended in the same transaction, and `locked_at` is kept.
- Only a **current** approval queues (*decided*: a stale one would queue drafts the User never saw): when the drafts changed since the review (`current` false), the decision is recorded and nothing is queued, `jobs` is absent and `next` asks for a new `cpd plan review`.
- A **rejection** queues nothing: the drafts stay drafts, editable, as in phase `plan`; the Lead revises them (`job edit`, `job add --draft`, `job cancel`) and asks again.
- On an unlocked `plan`, `plan decide` writes only what it did above and `plan lock` (§4.8) works as before.

```json
{"ok": true, "review": {"id": "r3", "status": "approved", "fingerprint": "9f86d081…", "feedback": null, "decided_at": "…"}, "current": true, "next": "cpd plan lock"}
```

`current` says whether the review's fingerprint is still the plan fingerprint; `next` is `cpd plan lock` only when approved and current on an unlocked Plan in phase `plan`; otherwise an approved and current review has no `next` and its result lists `jobs` (the Jobs queued). Idempotent: yes, as stated.

### 4.8 `plan lock`

```
cpd plan lock [--plan <id>]
```

On a re-planned Plan (`locked_at` set, A1) with no `draft` Job and no Workflow with a `draft` Job, the lock is the no-draft lock below and none of the rows that follow applies; with a draft Job or a Workflow with one, they apply in full.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the phase is `plan` (`dispatch`: `already`) | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| at least one Job is `draft` | `no_draft_jobs` | 3 |
| every `draft` Job has its Tier and its Spec, as `plan review` requires (§4.6; `details.jobs` as there) | `draft_incomplete` | 3 |
| every `impl` Job needs at least one `test` Job of its Workflow, as `plan review` requires (§4.6; `details.jobs` as there) | `test_job_required` | 3 |
| every `verify` Job needs at least one `impl` Job of its Workflow that is not `cancelled`, as `plan review` requires (§4.6; `details` as there; after `test_job_required`) | `impl_job_required` | 3 |
| every Workflow of shape `tdd` has a `test` and an `impl` Job that is not `cancelled`, as `plan review` requires (§4.6; `details` as there) | `shape_incomplete` | 3 |
| the latest Plan review is `approved` for the current plan fingerprint (§2.3: Jobs and Workflows) | `plan_not_approved` | 3 |
| at least one Workflow is not `cancelled` and each such Workflow has at least one `draft` Job; `details.workflows` lists the empty Workflows (none at all: `details.next` = `cpd workflow add`) | `workflow_empty` | 3 |
| the Dependency graph of the draft Jobs is acyclic and so is the graph of the Workflows' needs and base Workflows (`details.cycle`, qualified references) | `dependency_cycle` | 3 |
| for each Workflow with no needs and no base Workflow: its Lead worktree path does not exist, except a leftover of an interrupted lock (a worktree of the Workflow's repo on its Lead Branch), which is removed first; `details.workflow` names the Workflow | `worktree_exists` | 3 |
| for each Workflow with no needs and no base Workflow: its Lead Branch and its parent path do not exist in its repo, except a leftover of an interrupted start (§2.1); `details.workflow` | `branch_exists` | 3 |
| for each Workflow with no needs and no base Workflow: `origin/<lead branch>` does not exist, or it does not conflict with `origin/<base>` (`git merge-tree`, §7.2, hs-d490; `details.files` the conflicted paths); a repo with no `origin` has no remote check; `details.workflow` | `branch_exists` | 3 |
| for each Workflow with no needs and no base Workflow: `pre-start` passed in its new Lead worktree (§7.3); `details.workflow`, `details.tail`, `details.log` | `setup_failed` | 1 |

**Explore Jobs** (Plan `explore-roles`, R3) are invisible to the lock. A Plan whose only Jobs are explore Jobs has no `draft` Job and, while unlocked, is refused `no_draft_jobs`, as a Plan with no `draft` Job is (a re-planned Plan takes the no-draft lock above). An explore Job is `queued` from its `job add` and is not queued again here.

**The no-draft lock** (A4, pro-d433). On a re-planned Plan (`locked_at` set) with no `draft` Job and no Workflow with a `draft` Job, `plan lock` needs no approved review and no draft. It moves the Plan `plan → dispatch` (`plan-phase` `{from: "plan", to: "dispatch"}`; `locked_at` kept) and then the done guard settles it (contract §3.1, `settle_done`): a Plan whose Workflows are all `merged` and whose Jobs are all final ends `done` with `plan-done`. This is how a Lead finishes a Plan when an explore Job found nothing to change.

Effects (§3.1, §3.8, §7.2; R34, A8): every Workflow's `draft` Jobs are approved at once and the Workflows with no needs and no base Workflow **start**, all or nothing; the Workflows with needs and the **stacked** Workflows (contract §2.2 "The base Workflow"; a base Workflow of the same Plan included: the lock orders no worktrees), stay `waiting` until engine E7 (or `workflow start`, §9.7) starts them once their needs are `merged` and their base Workflow is `open`.
- **git**, for each Workflow with no needs and no base Workflow, in its repo (§7.2, R35 per Workflow branch, A5): `fetch origin <base>`; `ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin <lead branch>`. When it is on the remote and does not conflict with `origin/<base>` (`merge-tree --write-tree --name-only` exits 0; a base that merely moved ahead is no conflict, hs-d490): reuse it, `fetch origin <lead branch>` and `worktree add --no-track -b <lead branch> <lead worktree> origin/<lead branch>`. When it is absent: `worktree add --no-track -b <lead branch> <lead worktree> origin/<base>`. A repo with no `origin` (A3): no remote check and no push, `worktree add --no-track` from `<base>`. `--no-track`: a Lead Branch has no upstream, so nothing writes `.git/config` (hs-d243, contract §7.2). Then `pre-start` in the worktree, output in `run/<plan>/logs/lead-<key>.pre-start.log`. Every started Workflow's worktree is created and its `pre-start` run before anything is pushed; if one fails, every worktree and branch the lock created is removed, nothing is pushed, nothing in the database changes and the lock fails with that Workflow's refusal. When all have passed, each new Lead Branch is pushed, `push origin <lead branch>` from its Lead worktree (no `-u`, hs-d243). A failed push does not fail the lock: one `error` Event with code `push_failed` and `details.workflow` is appended per failed Workflow and the next merge or `pr open` pushes again.
- **Rows**, one transaction, with a compare-and-swap on `phase = 'plan'` and on the review read: `plans.phase = dispatch`, `locked_at`; every `draft` Job of every Workflow `queued` with its Locked-Job fingerprint; for each started Workflow, with a compare-and-swap on `status = 'waiting'`: `status = dispatch`, `lead_worktree`, `started_at`. **Events** `plan-phase` `{from: "plan", to: "dispatch", jobs: [key], workflows: [key]}` (`workflows`: the Workflows started) and one `workflow-started` `{workflow, repo, base, lead_branch, lead_worktree, base_sha, reused, pushed, by: "lock"}` per started Workflow. If the transaction fails, the worktrees and branches are removed.
- **Open Jobs:** the lock adds none. Engine E4 adds each started Workflow's `open` Job in the first tick after the lock (contract §3.7, hs-d340).
- **tmux:** `watch --ensure` (§12): starts `cpd watch` in `cpd-work:watch` when `locks/watch.lock` is free.

`workflows` lists every Workflow that is not `cancelled`, in key order: a started Workflow with its Lead worktree, `base_sha`, `reused` and `pushed` (R35); a `waiting` one with its `needs` and null for the rest. Every row has `base_workflow`: the base Workflow the Workflow still waits for, as `<plan>/<key>` (its base Workflow, contract §2.2 "The base Workflow", has not opened: it is `waiting` or `dispatch`), else null. It is what `details.base_workflow` of `workflow start`'s `workflow_not_ready` is (§9.7), so a stacked Workflow the lock leaves `waiting` shows its base Workflow, where `needs` alone would be empty; a started Workflow has null.

```json
{"ok": true, "plan": "pay-4521", "phase": "dispatch", "jobs": ["api-schema", "worker", "ui"],
 "workflows": [{"key": "api", "status": "dispatch", "needs": [], "base_workflow": null, "lead_branch": "pay-4521/api", "lead_worktree": "/home/clayton/projects/pay.pay-4521.api", "base_sha": "4b825dc…", "reused": false, "pushed": true},
         {"key": "ui", "status": "waiting", "needs": ["api"], "base_workflow": null, "lead_branch": "pay-4521/ui", "lead_worktree": null, "base_sha": null, "reused": null, "pushed": null},
         {"key": "ui2", "status": "waiting", "needs": [], "base_workflow": "pay-4521/api", "lead_branch": "pay-4521/ui2", "lead_worktree": null, "base_sha": null, "reused": null, "pushed": null}],
 "watch": {"started": true, "pane": "%3"}}
```

If the engine cannot be started, the Plan stays locked and the result is `watch_start_failed` (exit 1) with `details.next` = `cpd watch --ensure` (cpd 1's `watch_pane_failed`, renamed). Idempotent: yes; in phase `dispatch` it returns `"already": true` and still runs `watch --ensure`.

### 4.9 `plan rename`

```
cpd plan rename [--plan <id>] --title <text>
```

Changes the Plan's title, the label the tree shows (contract §2.2). `--title` is required, as `plan new`'s: 1–200 characters, no control characters, else `usage` (§1.5).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Plan exists | `plan_not_found` | 4 |

Effects: an unchanged title: `"already": true`, nothing written. Otherwise **rows**, one transaction: `plans.title`; **Event** `plan-renamed` `{title}`; **tmux**: none. The Plan's title is not a pane pill (contract §6.1): the Lead's `@cpd_title` is its dynamic `title` or its key, and neither changes when the Plan is renamed, so no pane is touched. The Context store's `plan` record keeps the old title. Archived Plans can be renamed.

```json
{"ok": true, "plan": {"id": "cpd2", "context": "building-cpd", "title": "cpd in Rust, done"}}
```

Idempotent: yes.

### 4.10 `plan archive`

```
cpd plan archive [--plan <id>]
```

Archives the Plan with its Lead and its side forks (contract §2.2 "Archived").

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the caller is not an agent: neither `CPD_SESSION` nor `CPD_ATTEMPT` is set and non-empty (checked first, before the Ledger is opened); `details` `{command, session, attempt}`, `session` and `attempt` the values of those variables or `null` | `agent_forbidden` | 3 |
| the Plan exists | `plan_not_found` | 4 |
| the archive rule holds for the Plan's cascade, all or nothing (contract §2.2 "Archived"): (a) no Session of the Plan (its Lead and side forks) is `working`, `waiting` or `blocked`; (b) every Workflow of the Plan is `merged` or `cancelled`, and no `cancelled` one has an `open` pull request; (c) no Job of the Plan is `queued`, `running` or `failed` (a `draft` one: the row below); (d) no Escalation of the Plan is `open` and no Plan review is `pending`. An open Inbox item does not block it, and neither does a Plan not in phase `done`, `deploy` included (pro-d421; E8 closes the Inbox items of an archived Session). The automatic sleep and archive of E13 and E14 (`LEAD_FINISHED`, §3.7) still require phase `done` and no open undismissed Inbox item. A Workflow of the Plan that a Workflow of another Plan (itself not `merged` or `cancelled`) names as base Workflow or need blocks too (`kind` `workflow`, `id` `<plan>/<key>` of the Workflow named, as hs-d324 has it). `details.blockers` lists each as `{kind, id, plan?, reason}`: kind `session` (`Session <name> is <state>.`), `workflow` (`id` the Workflow key, `plan` the Plan id, `Workflow <key> of Plan <plan> is <status>.`, or `Workflow <key> of Plan <plan> is cancelled with an open pull request.`), `job` (`id` the Job key, `plan` the Plan id, `Job <key> of Plan <plan> is <status>.` for `queued`, `running` and `failed`), and `escalation` and `review` (as before) | `archive_blocked` | 3 |
| the Plan has no `draft` Job (hs-d731, contract §2.2 "Archived"); `details.blockers` has `{kind: "job", id: "<plan>/<key>", reason: "draft"}` for each and the message says `cpd plan cancel` abandons a Plan and `cpd job cancel` one draft | `archive_blocked` | 3 |
| neither the Lead nor a side fork is in the chat slot; `details.next` = `cpd session park` | `in_chat_slot` | 3 |

The engine archives on its own (E12 Worker archive, E14 Plan archive after sleep, contract §3.7); the User archives from the cockpit or the CLI.

Since the migration `review-superseded` and its enforcement rule, a Plan that is `done` has no pending review: every pending review of the Plan is closed `superseded` when the Plan reaches `done`.

Effects, in this order (all or nothing):
1. **Check** every object of the cascade; nothing is written if any blocks.
2. **tmux:** close every live Lead pane as `session close` does (§10.9).
3. **Rows**, one transaction that re-checks the rule: `archived_at` = now on the Plan and each of its Sessions not archived yet. One **Event** per object: `plan-archived` `{archived: true}`, `session-archived`. A durable Session of the Plan has its host stopped within one engine tick of this step (contract §6.19).

```json
{"ok": true, "archived": [{"kind": "plan", "id": "cpd2"}, {"kind": "session", "id": "596d007f-…"}], "closed": ["%41"]}
```

Idempotent: yes; already archived: `"already": true`, nothing written, nothing closed.

### 4.11 `plan unarchive`

```
cpd plan unarchive [--plan <id>]
```

Clears `archived_at` on the Plan and its Sessions.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the caller is not an agent: neither `CPD_SESSION` nor `CPD_ATTEMPT` is set and non-empty (checked first, before the Ledger is opened); `details` `{command, session, attempt}`, `session` and `attempt` the values of those variables or `null` | `agent_forbidden` | 3 |
| the Plan exists | `plan_not_found` | 4 |
| the Plan's Context is not archived; `details.next` = `cpd context unarchive <c>` | `archived` | 3 |

The engine archives on its own (E12 Worker archive, E14 Plan archive after sleep, contract §3.7); the User archives from the cockpit or the CLI.

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: `archived_at = NULL` on the Plan and each archived Session of it; one **Event** per object (`plan-archived`, `session-archived`, each `{archived: false}`). No tmux and no archive rule.

```json
{"ok": true, "archived": [{"kind": "plan", "id": "cpd2"}, {"kind": "session", "id": "596d007f-…"}], "closed": []}
```

Idempotent: yes; not archived: `"already": true`, nothing written.

### 4.12 `plan cancel`

```
cpd plan cancel [--plan <id>] [--reason <text>]
```

Abandons a Plan (E1, hs-d203): cancels every Job that is not merged, closes the Plan's pull requests that are not merged, closes its Lead and its forks and archives it. cpd never closes an adopted pull request (§9.4) and never deletes its branch: step 5 leaves it open and the output lists it under `left_open`. Branches and worktrees of cancelled Workflows are removed by the next `cpd janitor` pass (§29, pro-d70, pro-d71), every `watch.janitor_minutes` minutes (default 60) or by hand. `--reason` is kept in the Events' `reason`; default `plan cancelled`. The Plan may be in any phase, `done` included (nothing is left to cancel; it is then archived).

| Precondition or failure | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Plan exists | `plan_not_found` | 4 |
| neither the Lead nor a side fork is in the chat slot; `details.next` = `cpd session park` | `in_chat_slot` | 3 |
| every running Attempt has ended within 60 s of its stop request (below); `details.attempts` lists those still running | `cancel_timeout` | 5 |
| each `gh pr close` succeeds, or its pull request is already closed or merged; `details` is `{argv, exit, stderr}` | `gh_failed` | 1 |

A Session `working`, `waiting` or `blocked` and a Job `running` do not block (unlike `plan archive`): the command stops them. The caller's own Lead is in that case.

Effects, in this order; each step is idempotent, so a rerun after any failure continues where it stopped:
1. **Check** the preconditions above that need no write.
2. **Plan reviews:** every pending review of the Plan becomes `superseded` with `decided_at` = now and `feedback` null, **Event** `plan-review` `{review, fingerprint, status: "superseded"}` (reason: "Plan review r<k> of Plan P is superseded: the Plan was cancelled.") The User sees the reason in the Event's `text` (contract §5.2) and the dialog closes in the pi adapter (§15.5).
3. **Jobs**, as `job cancel` (§5.3) for every Job not `merged` and not `cancelled` (the explore Jobs, `scout` and `research`, included: they have no Workflow, so step 5 does not touch them), with the reason, **but no Job is refused `shape_incomplete`**, in particular not the last `test` or `impl` Job of a `tdd` Workflow (cancelling a Plan is never refused by the shape check, hs-d573; the skip is an internal parameter of the path, never a flag, option or environment variable): `draft`, `queued` and `failed` become `cancelled` with **Event** `job-cancelled`; a `running` Job gets `job-cancel-requested` and engine E2 or the driver ends its Attempt `cancelled` at the next safe point (contract §3.4). The command then waits, polling, up to 60 s until no Attempt of the Plan is not `ended`. Dependents cannot start, as for `job cancel`; they are cancelled themselves by this step.
4. **Escalations:** each `open` Escalation of the Plan becomes `expired`, **Event** `escalation-expired`.
5. **Pull requests:** for each Workflow of the Plan with status `open` whose pull request is not `merged`, `gh pr close <number> --repo <owner/repo>`. The Workflow rows keep their status (`open`; Workflow statuses never end this way, contract §3.8); the next `pr poll` reads the closure and appends no `pr-feedback` for an archived Plan. A `waiting` Workflow has no pull request: nothing. A `merged` Workflow is never touched. A Workflow with `head_ref` (adopted, §9.4) is never closed: its pull request stays open and is listed under `left_open` (`[{workflow, number}]`).
6. **tmux:** close every live Lead pane as `session close` does (§10.9).
7. **Rows**, one transaction: `archived_at` = now on the Plan and its Sessions, with **Event** `plan-archived` `{archived: true}` and `session-archived` per object, as `plan archive` (§4.10).

No new Event kind and no schema change. The command's own Events are the existing ones named above.

```json
{"ok": true, "cancelled": ["api", "ui"], "closed_workflows": [{"workflow": "ui", "number": 813}], "left_open": [{"workflow": "card", "number": 3748}], "closed": ["%41"], "archived": [{"kind": "plan", "id": "cpd2"}, {"kind": "session", "id": "596d007f-…"}]}
```

Idempotent: yes (a rerun continues where it stopped). An archived Plan with nothing left to cancel: `"already": true`, nothing written. A rerun after a failure repeats steps 2 to 6 on what is left; Jobs already `cancelled` and pull requests already closed are skipped.

### 4.13 `plan outline`

```
cpd plan outline --file <outline.json> [--plan <id>]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--file <outline.json>` | required; the outline, JSON (below); readable UTF-8, else `file_unreadable` (§1.5) |
| `--plan <id>` | the Plan (§1.3) |

Sets the Plan's **outline** (hs-d502, D1; contract §2.2 Plan `outline`): what the Lead has settled with the User and says in a Plan review's summary (§4.5), which cpd cannot derive from Jobs. It **replaces** the outline whole; there is no partial edit and no way to clear it. It works in **every phase**, so a Lead that plans a later batch writes the outline of that batch before it asks for its review (§4.6).

**The outline file**, JSON, parsed once at the boundary (§1.5). A JSON object; unknown fields are refused. Every value is a string, array or object as written here; every "line" is a string of 1–200 characters on one line, with no control character (so no line break and no tab):

| Field | Value | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `goal` | line | required |
| `decisions` | `[{question, answer}]` | each `question` and `answer` a line; may be empty |
| `assumptions` | `[line]` | may be empty |
| `risks` | `[line]` | 0 to 3 |
| `done_when` | `{<Workflow key>: [line]}` | each value 1 to 3 lines; every key is a Workflow of the Plan that is **not `cancelled`** (checked against the Plan) |
| `out_of_scope` | `[line]` | 0 to 5 |
| `decided` | `[record id]` | Context record ids (§2.1) of the Plan's Context; each must exist there (any kind, superseded included), else `outline_invalid` |

Every field but `goal` may be absent; an absent one is stored as `[]` (`{}` for `done_when`). The stored form, `plans.outline`, is the **canonical JSON** of the object with all seven fields: keys sorted, no whitespace, strings as parsed. So an outline that says the same stores the same text, whatever its key order or spacing.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the file is readable UTF-8 | `file_unreadable` | 2 |
| the file is a JSON object with no unknown field and every field has the shape and limits above. Checked in this order, the first failure being the result: not JSON, or not an object (`details.field` `$`); an unknown field (its name, the first in byte order); then `goal`, `decisions`, `assumptions`, `risks`, `done_when`, `out_of_scope`, `decided`, each element in order; `details.field` is the path of the failure, as `goal`, `decisions[1].answer`, `risks[3]`, `done_when.api[0]`, `decided[0]` | `outline_invalid` | 2 |
| the Plan exists | `plan_not_found` | 4 |
| the Plan is not archived (§1.3) | `archived` | 3 |
| every key of `done_when` is a Workflow of the Plan that is not `cancelled`; `details.field` = `done_when.<key>`, `details.key` = the key | `outline_invalid` | 2 |
| every id of `decided` is a record of the Plan's Context; `details.field` = `decided[<i>]`, `details.record` = the id | `outline_invalid` | 2 |

Effects:
- The same canonical JSON as stored: `"already": true` and **nothing written**, no row, no Event.
- Otherwise **rows**, one transaction: `plans.outline` = the canonical JSON. **Event** `plan-outlined` `{replaced}` (contract §5.2), `replaced` true when the Plan had an outline. Nothing else is written: no file, no tmux. The plan fingerprint changes (§2.3: it includes the outline), so a Plan review made before this write is no longer current and the Lead asks for a new one (§4.6).
- The outline is checked when it is written only: a Workflow cancelled afterwards leaves its `done_when` entry in it, which the summary does not show (§4.5) and `plan review` does not need (§4.6).

```json
{"ok": true, "plan": "pay-4521", "replaced": false,
 "outline": {"assumptions": ["The outline is written by the Lead"], "decided": ["hs-d502"],
             "decisions": [{"answer": "In the Lead's chat", "question": "Where is the review shown?"}],
             "done_when": {"api": ["plan review writes summary-<review>.md"]},
             "goal": "Show a Plan review as a short summary in chat", "out_of_scope": [], "risks": []}}
```

`outline` is the stored object. Idempotent: yes. The same file twice changes nothing and writes one Event only the first time (`"already": true` the second time, `replaced` absent).

### 4.14 `plan delete`

```
cpd plan delete <id> [--yes]
```

Deletes a Plan: its Jobs, Attempts and the other rows below, its Sessions but the Lead and its run files, worktrees and local branches (hs-d527). The `plans` row stays as a **tombstone** (`deleted_at` set, once only) and so does the Lead's Session row, which the tombstone references (`plans.lead_session`): both hidden from every list, view and lookup (contract §2.2 "Deleted", which has the design). The Context's records are kept. Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. Without `--yes` the command prints what would be deleted (a preview); with `--yes` it deletes.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|
| `<id>` | Plan id (§2.1) |
| `--yes` | perform the delete; without it, print the preview only |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Plan exists and is not deleted; a deleted one is `already` (below) for this command and `plan_not_found` for every other | `plan_not_found` | 4 |
| **archived or asleep**: the Plan is archived or asleep; `details: {blockers: [{kind, id}]}` lists what is not | `archive_blocked` | 3 |
| **nothing running**: no Job `queued` or `running`, no Attempt not `ended`, no Session `working`, `waiting` or `blocked`, every Escalation closed, no Plan review pending; `details.blockers` | `archive_blocked` | 3 |
| **no open Workflow**: every Workflow of the Plan is `merged` or `cancelled`; `details.blockers` | `archive_blocked` | 3 |
| **Lead not in chat**: the Plan's Lead Session (§3.1) is not in the chat slot; `details.next = cpd session park` | `in_chat_slot` | 3 |

Effects, with `--yes` only (**without it, no rows or files are written**):
1. **One transaction.** It re-checks the preconditions (race safety), then sets `plans.deleted_at = now()` **first** (the triggers that guard the deletes read it, contract §4.4; a set `deleted_at` is never changed or cleared). Then it deletes the rows, each through the exception for a deleted Plan, in an order that keeps the foreign keys whole:
   - The plannotator reviews and board posts of the Plan's Sessions (the Lead's included)
   - Every Inbox item of the Plan, then every Event of the Plan
   - Every Escalation, Attempt, Dependency and Job of the Plan
   - Every `swr_mutations` row of system `jira` whose `context_json` names the Plan (`swr-jira.md` §11), before the Workflows it refers to
   - Every Workflow need, Workflow and Plan review of the Plan
   - Every Session of the Plan but the Lead (Workers and forks); the Lead's row stays, with its `plan` unchanged, hidden with the Plan
   - The Context's records stay (hs-d527)
   Every `DELETE` writes a `history` row with the whole old row (§4.4); the tombstone is an `update` row. They stay and the tamper check stays clean (contract §2.2). Last, in the same transaction, **one `plan-deleted` Event** is appended, with the counts; it is never deleted by this delete. The Plan's `pull_requests` rows are no Plan's: the poll deletes them once no Workflow points to them (§7.6 step 5).
2. **Session files** (after commit): every Session's file, the Lead's included; files that do not exist are skipped.
3. **Run files** (after commit): everything under `$CPD_HOME/run/<plan>/`: summaries, renders, reviews, messages, specs, logs and distill artifacts.
4. **Worktrees and local branches** (after commit): `rm -rf` every Attempt worktree and Workflow Lead worktree, each with its `target/` (this, with the run files, is where the disk comes from: the database file does not shrink); then the stored `lead_branch` of each Workflow and `cpd/<plan>--<attempt>` from their repos (not on the remote), then the directory of step 3. The paths come from the live rows when the transaction commits and on a rerun from their `before` copies in `history`.

**Rerun.** The rows go in one transaction and steps 2–4 after it, so a crash leaves a tombstoned Plan with files on disk. A rerun with `--yes` on a deleted Plan writes **nothing** to the store (no row, no Event), finishes whatever file step is left (a missing file, directory or branch is not an error) and returns `"already": true`. A preview of a deleted Plan returns `"already": true` and what is left on disk, not the counts of the first preview, which only the Event keeps.

Output without `--yes` (preview) or with `--yes` after a delete:

```json
{"ok": true, "preview": true, "already": false, "jobs": 47, "attempts": 121, "sessions": 3, "worktrees": 11, "disk_freed_mb": 342}
```

`sessions` counts every Session of the Plan, the Lead included (its row stays, its file goes). With `--yes` the first time: `"preview": false`, `"already": false`. Rerun with `--yes`: `"preview": false`, `"already": true` and `worktrees` and `disk_freed_mb` of what this run removed (0 when nothing was left). Preview of a deleted Plan: `{"ok": true, "preview": true, "already": true, "left": {"worktrees": 0, "branches": 0, "files": 0}}`.

Idempotent: yes; a Plan already deleted returns `"already": true` and writes nothing to the store.

**Tests that assume otherwise change with this design** (hs-d527; for delete-core to have approved): `plan_rows` of `cli/tests/flow/plan_delete.rs` counts Sessions with `plan = <id>` and Events with `plan = <id>`, but the Lead's row stays with its `plan` and the `plan-deleted` Event names the Plan; the Jobs, Attempts, Workflows, the other Sessions and the other Events are what is gone.

### 4.15 `plan lint`

```
cpd plan lint [--plan <id>]
```

Checks the Plan's drafts and its shape, and returns every error and warning in one list. The rules, their severities and the refusal each error carries are in contract §2.7; this section does not repeat them. The lint reads the Plan's Jobs, Workflows and outline, the Tier advice (§3.4b; the catalog when needed), and writes nothing: no Event and no file; a catalog read may fill the `tier_catalog` cache (§14.3). It runs fresh on every call.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--plan <id>` | the Plan (§1.3) |

Callers: Lead; no cockpit. The about line (the clap doc comment, shown in `docs/interface.md`): `Check the Plan's drafts: every error and warning in one list (§4.15)`.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the phase is not `grounding` (`details` as `plan review`'s, §4.6) | `illegal_phase` | 3 |
| the Plan exists | `plan_not_found` | 4 |
| the Tier advice needs the catalog (§3.4b; no catalog read when no qualifying cell exists): the catalog is found and readable | `pi_not_found`, `catalog_failed`, `tier_model_unknown` | 1 |
| at least one finding is an error; the message names the rules of the errors, in the order of the list below | `lint_failed` | 3 |

The refusal `lint_failed` has the message `Plan <id> has <n> lint errors: <rules joined by ", ">. Fix them, then ask again.` and `details` `{plan, errors, warnings, findings}`, where `findings` is every finding, errors first, in the order of contract §2.7.

**Output** on success, that is with no error finding:

```json
{"ok": true, "plan": "pay-4521", "errors": 0, "warnings": 1, "findings": [
  {"rule": "parallel_write_overlap", "severity": "warn",
   "message": "api-2 and api-3 have no dependency path and both name api/src/lib.rs. A hint, not a conflict prediction: on the ledger of 2026-10-30, 5 of 209 such pairs (2.4%) hit a merge conflict. Settle it with cpd job edit api-2 --needs api-3, or narrow touches.",
   "pr": "api", "job": "api-2", "other": "api-3", "paths": ["api/src/lib.rs"], "details": {}}]}
```

Every finding has every key, so the output is byte-stable: `{"rule": "<id>", "severity": "error"|"warn", "message": "<text>", "pr": <key|null>, "job": <key|null>, "other": <key|null>, "paths": [<sorted paths>], "details": {<the refusal's details for an error rule; {} for a warning>}}`.
- An error finding has `job` and `other` null and `paths` `[]`: its subjects are in `details`, as in the refusal it carries. Its `pr` is null, except for `shape_incomplete`, whose `pr` is the Workflow it names.
- A `parallel_write_overlap` finding has `pr`, `job`, `other` and `paths` set, and `details` `{}`.

The `parallel_write_overlap` message is exactly: `<job> and <other> have no dependency path and both name <paths joined by ", ">. A hint, not a conflict prediction: on the ledger of 2026-10-30, 5 of 209 such pairs (2.4%) hit a merge conflict. Settle it with cpd job edit <job> --needs <other>, or narrow touches.` The pair is defined in contract §2.7: `job` is the draft under review (the smaller key when both are drafts under review), `other` the other Job. The rule is a warning and never a refusal; it covers equal files only, exempts the lockfiles, and its limits are in contract §2.7.

A `tier_advice` finding has `pr` null, `job` the Job’s key, `other` null, `paths` `[]` and `details` `{}`. For a `draft` Job its message names `cpd job edit <job> --tier <A>`; for a `queued` Job (Locked), it does not suggest a change. The row in the summary (contract §2.7) is `<job> is <T>, history favours <A> for <kind>`.

`plan review` and `plan render` also return the warnings, and `plan review` refuses with the first error finding’s own code, never with `lint_failed`.

Idempotent: yes. The same Plan twice gives byte-equal stdout, and nothing is written.

## 5. `job`

Jobs, Specs and Dependencies (§2.2, §3.2). Kept from cpd 1 §11 "Jobs" except where stated.

**Spec file** (`--spec`), JSON, every field required, unknown fields refused (`spec_invalid`, exit 2, with the JSON path in `details`):

```json
{"goal": "…", "context": "…", "touches": ["docs/commands.md"], "acceptance": ["…"], "out_of_scope": ["…"]}
```

`touches` and `acceptance` have at least one non-empty string; `out_of_scope` may be empty. Change: cpd 1's `outOfScope` is now `out_of_scope`, the column's name.

**A `test` Job's Spec file** (kind `test`, hs-d341) has two more fields: `tests`, the named tests (one or more distinct one-line strings) and `test_files`, the files that hold the red tests (one or more repo-relative paths or, ending in `/`, directory prefixes; no `..`, no leading `/`, the rule of the `protected` list, contract §7.5):

```json
{"goal": "…", "context": "…", "touches": ["cli/tests/it/pr_open_job.rs", "core/src/pr/"], "acceptance": ["…"], "out_of_scope": ["…"],
 "tests": ["pr_open_job::merges_the_base", "pr_open_job::opens_the_pull_request"], "test_files": ["cli/tests/it/pr_open_job.rs"]}
```

Both are required for a `test` Job that is not a stub and refused for every other kind (`spec_invalid`, exit 2, with the JSON path in `details`). An `impl` Job names no tests: its tests are the union of its test Jobs' (contract §2.2 "Job kinds").

**The optional `resources` Spec field** (contract §2.2): a list of one or more distinct names, each matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`; absent means none. It names the declared resources (contract §8.3 "The `resources` domain") the Job is the tenant of from its first Attempt until it is merged or cancelled (contract §3.4 "Tenancy"):

**Tier flag** (`--tier`): `^(G|H|S|O)([0-4]|X)$` (contract §9): one letter, then an effort digit `0`–`4` or `X`. Every letter is alike, `G` included. A digit is valid only when the letter's model offers that effort (`cpd tiers`, §14.3; digits may skip, as O's efforts `0, 2, 3, 4` do); `X` is valid on EVERY model (air-d16, air-d17, air-d21). Effort 5 is never valid for any letter. A Tier that breaks the syntax, or uses a digit its model does not offer, is `tier_invalid` (exit 2, `details.tier`), with `details.efforts` listing the valid efforts for an effort. A Job's Tier must also be in the range of its role: the worker range for a Job, the explore range for `scout` and `research` (contract §9 "Roles and ranges", "Where the ranges are enforced"). A Tier outside it is `tier_not_allowed` (exit 2, §1.2; §5.1, §5.2, §5.4, §5.5). The fixed Worker list of pro-d84 and the fixed ranges of pro-d82 and hs-d554 are superseded (pro-d328 to pro-d332). A store that already holds a Job on a refused Tier is not rewritten: §5.5 and contract §9 ("Where the ranges are enforced") say what happens to it.

### 5.1 `job add`

```
cpd job add <key> --title <text> --tier <T> --spec <file> [--workflow <key>] [--kind <work|docs|test|impl|verify|scout|research>] [--needs <k1,k2>] [--draft] [--urgent] [--plan <id>]
cpd job add <key> --title <text> --tier <T> --spec <file> [--draft] [--workflow <key>] [--kind <work|docs|test|impl|verify|scout|research>] [--needs <k1,k2>] [--plan <id>]
```

`--tier` and `--spec` are always required, with `--draft` too (`usage`, exit 2; pro-d404): a draft exists only while it is being edited in the current turn or covered by a Plan review (contract §2.2 "A parked draft", rule 1). The only incomplete drafts are the template's stub drafts of `workflow add` before the lock (§9.4), which the Lead completes with `cpd job edit <key> --tier <T> --spec <file>` (§5.2). A follow-up Workflow is added after the lock with `workflow add <key> --repo … --needs … --jobs <file.json>` (§9.4), which queues its Jobs.

**The draft law** (pro-d404; contract §2.2 "A parked draft" states it in full), for `job add` and `workflow add`:

1. A `draft` Job exists only while it is being edited in the current turn or is covered by a current Plan review (§4.6). A draft is never a waiting state.
2. After the lock, `cpd workflow add` always requires `--jobs <file.json>` for every Workflow it adds that is not adopted (`--adopt`), a Workflow that waits for another Workflow included (§9.4). Without `--jobs` it is refused `draft_parked` (exit 3) and writes no row.
3. `cpd job add` always requires `--tier` and `--spec`, even with `--draft`: without them it is refused `usage` (exit 2). After the lock, `draft_parked` (exit 3) refuses any draft, by `job add --draft` or `job edit`, whose Workflow waits for another Workflow or whose needs chain, through drafts, reaches a `queued`, `running` or `failed` Job (the row below).
4. `parked_drafts` counts every uncovered non-open draft, incomplete template drafts before the lock included, so the turn-end `cpd reminder` (§15.8) and the `drafts-parked` Inbox item (§21) name it. Work that waits on a Job or a Workflow is queued with `--needs`; work that needs codebase or external information depends on a `scout` or `research` Job; work that needs clarification blocks on `ask_user_question` or `cpd_plan_review`.

`--tier <T>` is any allowed Tier of the machine's catalog (`cpd tiers`) and it is the Tier the Job **starts** at: no ladder surprise, the first Attempt runs at it (hs-d796). A Tier that is not valid at all is refused `tier_invalid`, a Tier outside its role's range `tier_not_allowed` (both rows below). **The `-r` replacement recipe** (hs-d796): to replace a Job that is on the wrong Tier, cancel it with `cpd job cancel <key> --reason <why>` and add its replacement with `cpd job add <key>-r1 --tier <T> --spec <spec>.json` — same `--workflow`, a Spec describing the same work. The `-r1` suffix is the Lead's choice; no naming rule is enforced beyond the Job-key syntax (§2.1). The cancel-then-add pattern is the one hs-n614/hs-n615 describe, and it is how the `update` Job of an open Workflow is replaced too (contract §3.8 "Updating").

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<key>` | Job key (§2.1). Change: positional, like every other `job` command (cpd 1 had `--key`) |
| `--workflow <key>` | the Job's Workflow (R34, A14), selected by §1.3's rule: required when the Plan has two or more Workflows that are not `cancelled`, defaulted to the one when it has one. Not for `scout` or `research`: `--workflow` is refused `explore_workflow_forbidden` and an explore Job belongs to the Plan (below) |
| `--needs <k1,k2>` | Dependencies, comma-separated, no duplicates (`usage`); Jobs of the same Workflow only (A7) |
| `--draft` | add the Job as a `draft` in a phase after `plan` too (User, hs-d173, hs-d174, hs-d179: every planned batch is visible in the Plan view before it is approved): `status = draft`, `appended = 1`, no fingerprint; the engine never runs it and it becomes `queued` only at the approval of a Plan review of the drafts (§4.7). In phase `plan` every Job is a draft, so `--draft` changes nothing there. Its needs may be drafts. `--tier` and `--spec` are required with it too (`usage`). A Job that only carries out a recorded User decision, with no open design choice, is added without `--draft` (User, hs-d301, amending hs-d173, hs-d174, hs-d179); drafts are for design the User has not decided and when unsure it is a draft. **After the lock a draft is refused when its Workflow waits for another Workflow, or its needs chain, through drafts, to a queued, running or failed Job** (`draft_parked`, the row below; contract §2.2 "A parked draft", rule 3). Not for `scout` or `research` (`explore_no_draft`): an explore Job is never a draft (below) |
| `--urgent` | add the Job with `urgent = 1` (contract §2.2): engine E3 starts it before every non-urgent Ready Job and may run it as one Attempt beyond `concurrency` (§3.7). Use it **only when the User explicitly asks**, usually for something that blocks all work or an incident. Not a Locked field and not in any fingerprint (§2.3); works with `--draft` and in every phase `job add` works in. To mark an existing Job, see §5.8 |
| `--kind <work\|docs\|test\|impl\|verify\|scout\|research>` | the Job's kind (hs-d341, contract §2.2 "Job kinds"); default `work`. `scout` and `research` are the explore kinds, below. `verify` adds checks (end-to-end, smoke, load, contract) and changes no product behaviour: it has no Spec section of its own (no `tests` or `test_files`, `spec_invalid`) and its submit runs only the tamper check; it needs an `impl` Job of its Workflow (`impl_job_required`). `open` and `update` are cpd's: `kind_reserved`. The Workflow's stored shape (§9.4) decides which kinds it may have (`shape_violation`, below). A `test` Job's Spec file has `tests` and `test_files` (§5), an `impl` Job needs a `test` Job of its Workflow and both need the repo's `[test-commands]` (below). |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--tier` or `--spec` is missing, with or without `--draft` (contract §2.2 "A parked draft", rule 3, pro-d404) | `usage` | 2 |
| the phase is `plan`, `dispatch`, `deploy` or `done` (`done` only with `--draft` and then only into a Workflow that is not `merged` or `cancelled`: none exists until `workflow add` has reopened the Plan); `grounding`: `illegal_phase` (except for the explore kinds, below) | 3 |
| the Workflow is not `merged` or `cancelled` (§3.2) | `workflow_ended` | 3 |
| no Job with this key, unless its Locked fields (`workflow` included) and needs are identical (then `already`) | `job_key_exists` | 3 |
| every `needs` key is a Job of the Plan | `needs_unknown` | 3 |
| every `needs` Job is in the same Workflow; `details.jobs` lists those that are not | `needs_other_workflow` | 3 |
| no `needs` Job is `cancelled` or `failed`, because a Dependency on a `failed` Job is refused | `needs_unavailable` | 3 |
| without `--draft`, in a phase after `plan`: no `needs` Job is a `draft` (`details.jobs` lists them; its message says to add this Job with `--draft`, or to approve the drafts first), because a `queued` Job could start before the draft it needs exists | `needs_unavailable` | 3 |
| `--kind open` or `update`; `details.kind` | `kind_reserved` | 3 |
| no `needs` Job is an `open` or `update` Job (nothing waits for them: contract §2.2 "Job kinds"); `details.jobs` | `needs_unavailable` | 3 |
| `--kind test` or `impl`: the Workflow's repo policy has `[test-commands]` (contract §7.7; none when there is no repo file or the file lacks the table) | `tests_unconfigured` | 3 |
| every `touches` entry of the Spec is checked against the tree the Job will start from (the Workflow's Lead Branch head once the Workflow started, else its base, contract §2.1; a Workflow stacked on a base Workflow that is `waiting` or `dispatch` and is itself still `waiting` has no start tree yet, its base being that Workflow's Lead Branch, which does not exist until the base Workflow opens (contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows"): nothing is checked and the entries pass): a literal path must exist in that tree, or its parent directory must (a new file); a glob must match a file, or its fixed prefix directory must exist; cpd's own `open` and `update` Jobs are not checked (contract §3.7 E4, hs-d512) and neither is an explore Job (its `touches` is its artefact, below); `details: {missing: [entries], tree: <ref>}` | `touches_missing` | 3 |
| without `--draft`, an `impl` Job needs at least one `test` Job of its Workflow; `details.jobs` | `test_job_required` | 3 |

| with `--draft`, in phase `dispatch`, `deploy` or `done` (phase `plan` is never refused: the Lead composes the first batch there): the draft's Workflow waits for another Workflow, or its needs chain, through drafts, to a `queued`, `running` or `failed` Job (contract §2.2 "A parked draft", rule 3, pro-d404; `job edit` (§5.2) is refused the same way). Never refused: the `open` Job's draft, and a draft that waits on nothing. `details` `{plan, job, workflow, needs}`; the message names the legal forms: add the Job it waits for `queued` with `--needs` and no `--draft`; or put the draft under a Plan review in the same turn; or, when it only carries out a recorded decision, add it queued (no `--draft`, hs-d301) | `draft_parked` | 3 |
| the Workflow's stored shape allows the kind, while the Workflow is `waiting` or `dispatch` (hs-d497, contract §2.2 "Job kinds"): `tdd` allows `docs`, `test`, `impl`, `verify`; `docs` allows `docs`; `config` allows `work`; `free` allows every kind; `details` `{workflow, shape, kind, allowed}`. **A Workflow whose status is `open` allows only `work`** (pro-d68, contract §2.2 "Job kinds"): `docs`, `test`, `impl` and `verify` are refused whatever the shape, `details` `{plan, workflow, status: "open", shape, kind, allowed: ["work"]}` | `shape_violation` | 3 |
| the Spec file has `tests` and `test_files` exactly when the kind is `test` and the Job is not a stub (§5) | `spec_invalid` | 2 |
| every string of the Spec (each field, each `touches` entry, each `acceptance` item and their `test` and `test_files` for a test Job) names only repo-relative paths, not the primary checkout of any Workflow's repo (contract §8.3); a match is a substring ending at the end of the string or before a non-letter, non-digit, `.`, `_` or `-` character; `details: {path, primary, workflow}` names the JSON path, the root realpath (or `~`/`$HOME` prefix) and the Workflow | `spec_invalid` | 2 |

For `scout` the explore range: letter `H`, effort ≥ 1 or `X`, up to the worker ceiling; for `research` letter `S`, effort ≥ 1 or `X`, up to the worker ceiling (Plan `explore-roles`, R6; contract §2.2, A17). `details` name the kind and its range; a Tier of the other letter, `O`, effort 0 or an effort above the ceiling is refused | `tier_not_allowed` | 2 |

A stub draft has no Spec of the Lead's and no check (the `open` Job's Spec is cpd's and names no `resources`); `plan review` and `plan lock` do not check again | `resource_undeclared` | 3 |
| `--workflow` with `--kind scout` or `research` | `explore_workflow_forbidden` | 3 |
| `--draft` with `--kind scout` or `research` | `explore_no_draft` | 3 |
| an explore Job's `needs` are all explore Jobs and no other Job needs an explore Job; `details.jobs` lists the Jobs on the other side. `needs_other_workflow` does not apply to an explore Job, which has no Workflow | `explore_needs_mixed` | 3 |
| an explore Job's Spec has exactly the four fields of the explore Spec (below): `touches`, `tests`, `test_files` or `resources` is refused, with the JSON path in `details` | `spec_invalid` | 2 |

Effects: the Job's write as above; for an explore Job added in phase `dispatch`, `deploy` or `done`, the same transaction first moves the Plan to `plan` (`plan-phase` `{from, to: "plan"}`, pro-d429; the explore paragraph below). Then the citation marking of §3.5 (best-effort, the Session rule of §3.3, the Session read from the environment): in the Plan's Context, the text of `goal`, `context`, each `acceptance` item and `out_of_scope` is scanned (`RecordId::scan`, contract §2.1) and each record id it cites that the Session read gets `used` = 1. A failed marking never fails the command or changes its output or exit status.

### Explore Jobs (`scout`, `research`)

Explore Jobs (Plan `explore-roles`, R1-R9; contract §2.2 "Explore Jobs") answer one question from this machine, or also from outside it for `research` and leave one Markdown artefact and a bounded summary. Only a Lead adds one, or a Manager on a shaping Plan of its own Context (§4.1, "A Manager on a shaping Plan"; air-d19, air-d22). Together they are the explore kinds; a Job of one is an explore Job.

- **Belongs to the Plan.** No `--workflow` (`explore_workflow_forbidden`; for a Manager on a shaping Plan the same flag is `shaping_explore_only`, §1.3); `workflow_required` is not raised, also when the Plan has two or more Workflows. The Job's `workflow` is null (`plan show`, `job show`).
- **No draft, no review, no lock.** The Job is `queued` at once, with its Locked-Job fingerprint, in phase `grounding`, `plan`, `dispatch`, `deploy` or `done`; `--draft` is `explore_no_draft`. In phase `dispatch`, `deploy` or `done` the accepted add moves the Plan back to `plan` (decision pro-d429, which supersedes clause (1) of pro-d407; contract §3.1): in the same transaction, before `job-added`, `plan-phase` `{from, to: "plan"}` is appended, `done_at` is cleared when it was `done`, and `locked_at` is kept. In phase `grounding` or `plan` the add changes no phase. The Plan stays in `plan` until its Lead moves it on (`plan lock`, an approved batch of drafts or `workflow add`, §4.7, §4.8, §9.4). A refused add leaves the Plan where it was, and a rerun of an add already made (`already`) appends no second `plan-phase`. It is in no plan fingerprint and invisible to `plan review` and `plan lock` (§4.6, §4.8): adding one never invalidates an approved review.
- **The Spec is four fields**: `goal` (the one question), `context` (where to look and what a good answer contains; it may name absolute machine paths, the repo-relative rule is waived for these kinds), `acceptance` (what the file must answer and cite) and `out_of_scope`, all required. `touches`, `tests`, `test_files` and `resources` are `spec_invalid`. cpd derives and stores `touches` = `["run/<plan>/explore/<job-key>.md"]`, the artefact, a path relative to `$CPD_HOME`; the `touches_missing` check does not run for it.
- **Tier**: `scout` letter `H`, `research` letter `S`, effort ≥ 1 or `X`, up to the worker ceiling (the ladder climbs to the next valid effort inside the letter, contract §9 'Next rung'; after the top rung a `no_submit` fails the Job). A `crashed` or `merge_conflict` there is retried at the same Tier under the cap; it never leaves its letter (`job retry` and §9 as for any Job).
- **Needs**: an explore Job needs only explore Jobs and no other Job needs one (`explore_needs_mixed`).
- **Deliverable and end.** The Worker writes one Markdown artefact at `$CPD_HOME/run/<plan>/explore/<job-key>.md` and runs `cpd attempt submit <attempt> --summary-file <path>` (§6.1), a summary of at most 1500 characters. On a pass the Attempt and the Job end `merged` with no git merge; the Lead's `job-merged` carries the summary, never the file (§15.3). `cpd job show` shows both (§5.7).
- **The Attempt** has no worktree, no `pre-start` and no Lead Branch. Its worktree is the explore directory `$CPD_HOME/run/<plan>/explore/`, created if missing, which is also the Worker's cwd. Its timeout is `timeouts.explore_minutes` (§14.2, default 20). It takes a Worker slot under `concurrency` like any Job. Its guards are §15.22.

### A Spec names no primary checkout

A Spec must name only repo-relative paths. A Worker works in its own worktree (contract §7.2), not the repo's primary checkout (contract §15.16: the adapter refuses any write into a primary checkout). When reading the latest main, the Worker runs `git fetch origin` and then `git show origin/main:<path>`. cpd checks every Spec string (`goal`, `context`, each `touches` entry, each `acceptance` item and for a `test` Job its `tests` and `test_files`), searching for the root realpath of each Workflow's repo (or `~`, `$HOME` or `${HOME}` as a prefix of it), as a substring ending at the end of the string or before a character that is not a letter, a digit, `.`, `_` or `-`: for example `<root>/docs/x.md`, `<root>` followed by a space, a quote, a backtick or a comma match; `<root>-old` and `<root>.wt/x` do not. The first match in field order (goal, context, touches, acceptance, out_of_scope, tests, test_files) and Workflow order is reported as `spec_invalid`, with `details: {path, primary, workflow}` the JSON path, the root and the Workflow key. Nothing is written when the check refuses. **Explore Jobs** (Plan `explore-roles`, R5): the check does not run for an explore Job's Spec, whose `context` may name absolute machine paths; and the Spec of any other Job may cite the artefact `$CPD_HOME/run/<plan>/explore/<job-key>.md`, which this check does not refuse.

**A stub draft**, the template's Job laid out before the lock (§9.4; `job add` never writes one), stores `tier` and the Spec fields `goal`, `context`, `touches`, `acceptance` and `out_of_scope` as null, as the template gives neither, and its `job-added` Event has `tier: null`.
