A draft that lacks its Spec or its Tier is **incomplete**: it is never queued or run (contract §3.2), a Plan review of it is refused `draft_incomplete` (§4.6) and so is `plan lock` (§4.8). `needs` and `workflow` work as for any draft.

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: `jobs` (`workflow` = the Workflow's key; `kind` (`work` by default); `tests` and `test_files` from the Spec file of a `test` Job; `resources` from the Spec file (null when absent); `urgent` = 1 with `--urgent` (else 0); `status = draft`, `appended = 0`, no fingerprint, in phase `plan`; `status = draft`, `appended = 1`, no fingerprint, with `--draft` in any later phase; `status = queued`, `appended = 1`, fingerprint stored, in a later phase without `--draft`); one `dependencies` row per need. **Event** `job-added` `{workflow, kind, status, appended, tier, needs, urgent}`. A Job appended to a Workflow keeps the Workflow's `open` Job waiting until it is `merged` or `cancelled`: that Job's Ready rule counts every Job of the Workflow (contract §3.2). (Before hs-d340 the add also re-armed `all-merged`; that step and Event are retired, contract §3.7 E4.) No cycle is possible: nothing needs a new Job yet. An appended Job of a `waiting` Workflow is not Ready until its Workflow starts (§3.2); an appended draft is not Ready at all until its review is approved; one of an `open` Workflow (a `work` Job, above) reaches its pull request by its own merge (contract §3.8 "Updating"): **no `update` Job is queued**, no Gate runs. `pr push` (§9.9) is the repair after a `push_failed` and `pr rebase` (§9.3) the repair for the rest. And, when the Plan's working Lead runs it, it names the Workflow as the Lead's Workflow (§1.3).

**Feedback fixes chain after the open Job** (pro-d103, pro-d105; A1–A5): when a Workflow is `open` and its `open` Job is `merged`, on an `open` Workflow a Lead appends only `work` Jobs (contract §3.8 "Updating") as feedback fixes. The chain rule (A2): the **leaves** are the non-cancelled Jobs of the Workflow that come after the merged `open` Job and that no other such Job needs; the `open` Job itself is a leaf if it has no Dependent Job yet, or once all Dependents end. A `--needs` arg given to a feedback-fix `job add` is merged (union, A3) with the leaves, so `--needs` may be empty or omit the leaves. Drafts and `update` Jobs are never leaves (A2): they never hold and a `queued` `update` Job would deadlock a fix Job that needs it. A queued Job that needs a Job that is not merged, if the needed Job is `failed` and no other appended Job of the Workflow needs it and is not itself `failed`, is refused `needs_unavailable` with a failed-leaf error: the pool of available Dependents is empty, the fix Job cannot go forward and adding to it deadlocks the chain (A4). The chain stays idempotent (A3): rerunning `job add` with the same fix and flags recomputes the leaves without that fix itself and without Jobs that transitively need it, so the second call appends the same `--needs` and exits `already`.

```json
{"ok": true, "job": {"key": "api-schema", "workflow": "api", "kind": "work", "status": "draft", "appended": false, "tier": "S2", "needs": [], "urgent": false}}
```

Idempotent: yes, as stated (`--draft` and `--urgent` are not Locked fields: the call that found an identical Job returns `already` whatever its status).

### 5.2 `job edit`

```
cpd job edit <key> [--title <text>] [--tier <T>] [--spec <file>] [--workflow <key>] [--kind <work|docs|test|impl|verify>] [--needs <k1,k2> | --no-needs] [--plan <id>]
```

**Completing a stub draft** (hs-d241, R1): `cpd job edit <key> --tier <T> --spec <file>` sets the Tier and the Spec of a draft that lacks them (a draft is editable, so this is an ordinary edit; `fields` lists `tier` and `spec`). Once the draft has both, it is complete and a Plan review may approve it (§4.6). The edit changes the plan fingerprint (contract §2.3), which covers a stub as it is.

**A queued Locked Job's Spec** (ADR-0014, User, Context record pro-d79; contract §3.2 "Locked"): `cpd job edit <key> --spec <file>` also works, in any phase after the lock, on a Job that is `queued`, has no Attempt row of any status (not even an ended one) and is not an `open` or `update` Job. `--spec` is the **only** flag such a Job takes: `--title`, `--tier`, `--workflow`, `--kind`, `--needs` or `--no-needs` is refused whole with `job_locked` and nothing is written. The Lead only: a Worker (`CPD_ATTEMPT` set) is refused `not_a_lead`. The new Spec is checked as a draft's `--spec` is (`spec_invalid`, the no-primary-checkout rule, `touches_missing`; a `test` Job keeps its `tests` and `test_files`). One write transaction re-reads the Job's status and Attempts, updates the Spec columns, recomputes `jobs.fingerprint` (contract §2.3) and appends one `job-edited` Event whose `fields` lists the changed Spec columns and whose text says it is a Locked Job's edit; the `history` rows keep the old and the new text. There is no Plan review and no User approval: tell the User in chat what you changed. A change that alters nothing writes nothing (`"already": true`). An explore Job (`scout`, `research`) is `queued` from its add, so the same rule makes `--spec` its only flag and its Spec is the four-field one of §5.1 (Plan `explore-roles`).

**`--kind`** (hs-d341) changes a draft's kind, never to `open` or `update` (`kind_reserved`); a Job that is not a draft is Locked. The Spec's `tests` and `test_files` must fit the new kind (`spec_invalid`: a `test` Job that is not a stub has both, every other kind neither) and the rules of §5.1 apply as there (`tests_unconfigured`; `test_job_required` where an `impl` Job stops being a draft and `impl_job_required` where a draft becomes a `verify` Job (by `--kind verify` or `--needs`) and stops being one, both at the review or the lock; `shape_violation` when the Workflow's shape does not allow the new kind). `fields` lists `kind`.

A draft is editable in **every phase** (User, hs-d173, hs-d174, hs-d179), including one added after the lock, whose review may be pending: the edit changes the fingerprint of the drafts, so the pending review no longer matters (§4.6). `--needs` may name drafts. `--no-needs` removes every Dependency (cpd 1 had no way to). `--workflow <key>` moves the draft Job to another Workflow (R34, A14); it is a field flag, so §1.3's default does not apply: without it the Job keeps its Workflow. Dependencies stay inside one Workflow (A7): a Job that changes Workflow keeps none of its old needs, so give `--needs` with Jobs of the new Workflow, or `--no-needs` and no other Job may need it.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| at least one field flag | `nothing_to_edit` | 2 |
| with `--tier`: the Tier is outside the range of the Job's role, checked after `tier_invalid` (§5.1): the worker range, from `worker_tier` up to just below `lead_tier`, or for a `scout` or `research` Job its explore range; `details` as §5.1. A draft stored with a refused Tier before pro-d82 is now allowed; a draft stored with a refused Tier before hs-d554 is repaired by this edit; an edit that does not give `--tier` is not blocked by the Tier it holds | `tier_not_allowed` | 2 |
| after the lock, the edit leaves a draft that the door refuses (contract §2.2 "A parked draft", rule 3, pro-d404): its Workflow waits for another Workflow, or its needs chain, through drafts, to a `queued`, `running` or `failed` Job. Any change of a draft (`--needs`, `--no-needs`, `--tier`, `--spec`, `--title`, `--kind`, `--workflow`) is refused when the result is such a draft, by the rule and with the `details` and message of §5.1; phase `plan` is never refused | `draft_parked` | 3 |
| the Job is `draft`, in whatever phase; a Job that is not `draft` is Locked; an `open` or `update` Job is cpd's and always refused (its Spec is cpd's), also while the `open` Job is a `draft` (hs-d573) | `job_locked` | 3 |
| `--workflow` names a Workflow of the Plan | `workflow_not_found` | 4 |
| that Workflow is not `cancelled` | `workflow_ended` | 3 |
| the needs exist and are usable | `needs_unknown`, `needs_unavailable` | 3 |
| every Dependency after the edit links two Jobs of the same Workflow: the needs are in the Job's Workflow (the new one with `--workflow`) and with `--workflow` the Job keeps no old needs and no Job needs it; `details.jobs` lists the Jobs on the other side (§4.4 `dependencies_same_workflow`, `jobs_workflow_dependencies`) | `needs_other_workflow` | 3 |
| the new needs make no cycle | `dependency_cycle` | 3 |
| with `--spec`: every `touches` entry is checked as in `job add` (§5.1), against the tree the Job will start from (contract §2.1, hs-d512; for a Workflow stacked on a `waiting` or `dispatch` base Workflow that is itself still `waiting` there is no tree yet, so nothing is checked, §5.1); `details: {missing: [entries], tree: <ref>}` | `touches_missing` | 3 |
| with `--spec`: the Spec names only repo-relative paths, not the primary checkout of any Workflow's repo (§5.1 "A Spec names no primary checkout"); `details: {path, primary, workflow}` | `spec_invalid` | 2 |
| with `--spec`: the Spec's `resources` is valid for the kind (§5) | `spec_invalid` | 2 |
| with `--spec` of an explore Job: `touches`, `tests`, `test_files` or `resources` is refused, the explore Spec of §5.1 (the `touches_missing` check does not run for it) | `spec_invalid` | 2 |
| with `--spec`, or with `--workflow` for a Job that has `resources`: every name is declared for the (new) Workflow, as in `job add` (§5.1); `details` `{job, workflow, resource, declared, file}` | `resource_undeclared` | 3 |

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: the changed `jobs` columns; `dependencies` rows deleted and inserted to match (§4.4 allows deletion only for `draft`); with `--workflow`, in the order §4.4 states: delete the old Dependencies, update `workflow`, insert the new ones. **Event** `job-edited` `{fields: [name]}`, listing only the fields whose value changed (`workflow` among them). And, when the Plan's working Lead runs it, it names the Workflow as the Lead's Workflow (§1.3).

```json
{"ok": true, "job": {"key": "api-schema", "status": "draft"}, "fields": ["tier", "needs"]}
```

The Event is `job-edited` in both cases. Idempotent: yes; when no value changes it writes nothing and returns `"already": true`.

### 5.3 `job cancel`

```
cpd job cancel <key> --reason <text> [--plan <id>]
```

A Manager may run this on a shaping Plan of its own Context (§4.1, "A Manager on a shaping Plan"; air-d19, air-d22), refused `plan_has_lead` (exit 3) or `plan_other_context` (exit 2).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Job is not `merged` | `job_merged` | 3 |
| the Job is not the last `test` or the last `impl` Job (not `cancelled`) of a Workflow of shape `tdd` that has not opened (hs-d497: add the replacement first); `details` `{workflow, missing}`. Applies to `job cancel` typed by the Lead only: `workflow cancel` (§9.6) and `plan cancel` (§4.12) cancel their Jobs without it (hs-d573) | `shape_incomplete` | 3 |

Effects (§3.2 "Cancel"):
- `draft` (in any phase: a draft added after the lock is cancelled like one in phase `plan`), `queued` or `failed`: one transaction, `status = cancelled`, `cancel_reason`, `cancel_requested_at`; **Event** `job-cancelled` `{reason}`.
- `running`: one transaction, `cancel_reason` and `cancel_requested_at` only; **Event** `job-cancel-requested` `{reason}`. Engine E2 sets the Attempt's `stop_request = cancelled` and the driver or E2 ends it `cancelled` at its next safe point (§3.4), which appends `job-cancelled`. No tmux action by this command.
- **Dependents (hs-d647)**: in the same transaction, every Job of the Plan that needs the cancelled Job, directly or transitively through any status, becomes `failed` (when `queued`: `failed_cause` is `its need <cancelled-key> was cancelled`, one `job-failed` Event) or `cancelled` (when a `draft`: `cancel_reason` the same string, one `job-cancelled` Event); one already `failed`, `merged` or `cancelled` is untouched. The result's `failed` and `cancelled` arrays name the Jobs this changed and are absent when empty. In the `running` case the dependents are failed in the transaction that makes the Job `cancelled` (the engine's, 3.4), not by this command.
- **The done guard** (contract §3.1, decision pro-d398): after the dependents above, in the same transaction, when the Plan is in `deploy`, every Workflow that is not `cancelled` is `merged`, at least one is, and no Job of the Plan is still non-final (`draft`, `queued`, `running` or `failed`): the Plan moves `deploy → done` with `done_at`, one `plan-done` and the pending plan reviews superseded, and the output carries `phase`. Otherwise the phase stays `deploy` and nothing else changes. So cancelling the last non-final Job of a Plan whose Workflows are all merged or cancelled ends the Plan, and a `failed` Job ends only by this command or by a retry that merges. A `running` Job's cancel does this in the engine's transaction that ends it `cancelled` (contract §3.4), not here.
- And, when the Plan's working Lead runs it, it names the Workflow as the Lead's Workflow (§1.3).

```json
{"ok": true, "job": "worker", "status": "cancelled", "cancel_requested": false, "failed": ["dep"], "cancelled": ["draft-dep"]}
```

Idempotent: yes; a `cancelled` Job, or one with a request already recorded, returns `"already": true` (the first reason is kept). Dependents of a `failed` Job stay `queued`: `job retry` recovers the need, so that wait is legal. **Cancelling a Workflow's `open` Job stands** (contract §3.7 E4, §3.8): engine E4 adds no fresh one, so the Workflow stays `dispatch` with no live `open` Job. It is not a way to start over: to open its pull request later the Lead runs `pr open --workflow <key>` (§9.1, the repair, not refused `open_job_live` since no `open` Job is live); to give it up, `workflow cancel <key>` (§9.6), which also cancels every `draft`, `queued` or `failed` Job of the Workflow, its `open` Job included, with the Workflow and adds nothing back. `job retry` (§5.4) takes a `failed` Job only and runs it again at another Tier.

### 5.4 `job retry`

```
cpd job retry <key> --tier <T> [--plan <id>]
```

A Manager may run this on a shaping Plan of its own Context (§4.1, "A Manager on a shaping Plan"; air-d19, air-d22), refused `plan_has_lead` (exit 3) or `plan_other_context` (exit 2).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--tier` is outside the range of the Job's role, checked after `tier_invalid`: **`job retry --tier` refuses a Tier outside the worker range** (from `worker_tier` up to just below `lead_tier`, `details` `{tier, role: "worker", floor, ceiling, allowed, key: "worker_tier"}`), so a Job that failed at the ceiling cannot be retried higher; its remedy is the same Tier or a new Job with a better Spec. For an explore Job the range is its kind's (`scout`: letter `H`; `research`: letter `S`; effort ≥ 1 or `X`, up to the worker ceiling) and `details` name the kind and its range. Checked first, so a refused Tier changes nothing | `tier_not_allowed` | 2 |
| the Job is `failed` (or `queued` with this `retry_tier` and no Attempt since: `already`) | `job_not_failed` | 3 |
| no `needs` Job is `cancelled` (`needs_unavailable`, exit 3, `details.needs` lists them): a Job held by a cancelled need can never start, so cancel it and add a replacement whose needs do not name the cancelled Job. A `failed` need is allowed: retrying recovers it | `needs_unavailable` | 3 |

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: `status = queued`, `retry_tier = <T>`, `failed_cause = null` (the Job's `tier` field is left unchanged). **Event** `job-retried` `{tier}`. The next Attempt has `origin = retry` and this Tier and the ladder restarts from it with a fresh cap (§9; for an explore Job the ladder stays in its kind's range and climbs to the next valid effort inside the letter, and after the top rung a `no_submit` fails the Job, while a `crashed` or `merge_conflict` there is retried at the same Tier under the cap, Plan `explore-roles`, R6; Attempts whose driver never started are never counted). The Plan view, `plan render` and `context pending` show the Tier the Job is displayed at (contract §3.4a), which is `retry_tier` while the Job is queued at it; `plan show` and `job show` print both `tier` and `retry_tier` as raw field values. And, when the Plan's working Lead runs it, it names the Workflow as the Lead's Workflow (§1.3).

```json
{"ok": true, "job": "worker", "status": "queued", "tier": "S4"}
```

Idempotent: yes, as stated. (The engine also retries a `failed` open or update Job of the same Workflow when its fix merges, contract §3.2 "Engine auto-retry on fix merge" (pro-d89); a Lead normally retries only when no fix is needed or when a fix did not restart the Job.)

### 5.5 `job dispatch`

```
cpd job dispatch <key> [--plan <id>]
```

Starts one Ready Job now: the same step as engine E3 (cpd 1 §11, kept).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Job is Ready (§3.2) | `job_not_ready` | 3 |
| an `open` Job's Workflow has a stored `description` and, if not adopted (`head_ref` null), is treated as not Ready: the Job is not started; the same refusal at engine E3 as for `tier_not_allowed`, one `error` Event, the Job starts at the first tick after the description is stored (§9.5a); an `update` Job and an adopted Workflow's open Job need none | `description_required` | 3 |
| an `open` Job's Workflow's policy sets `workflow.jira_required` and the Workflow has no stored `jira` and, if not adopted (`head_ref` null), is treated as not Ready: the Job is not started; the same refusal at engine E3 as for `tier_not_allowed`, one `error` Event, the Job starts at the first tick after `cpd workflow edit <key> --jira <KEY>` (§9.5); an `update` Job and an adopted Workflow's open Job need none (pro-d127) | `jira_required` | 3 |
| an `open` Job's Workflow's policy sets `workflow.jira_required`, the Workflow is not adopted (`head_ref` null) and its title is not `<type>[!]: <KEY>/<summary>` for its stored `jira` (pro-d399, contract §7.6 "The Jira title"): the Job is not started; the same refusal at engine E3 as for `tier_not_allowed`, one `error` Event, the Job starts at the first tick after `cpd workflow edit <key> --title "<type>: <KEY>/<summary>"` (§9.5); checked after the ticket check; an `update` Job and an adopted Workflow's open Job need none | `jira_title_invalid` | 3 |
| its fingerprint matches | `locked_job_tampered` | 3 |
| the driver lock is free (§3.4 step 1) | `cas_lost` | 3 |
| a linear Attempt of the Job's Workflow is live (pro-d52, contract §3.7 E3 item 1) | `cas_lost` | 3 |
| every resource of the Job's Spec is still declared for the Workflow (contract §3.4 "Resources of a Job"); `details` `{job, workflow, resource, declared, file}` | `resource_undeclared` | 3 |
| the Job's acquisition has a free slot in every pool: `workers` and every resource of the Spec, all or none, decided by the starter under the pools' guards after the driver lock and before the Attempt row exists (contract §3.4 "Resources of a Job"); a Job that is already a tenant (a retry) needs none; `details` `{job, resource, holders}`. It changes nothing: no Attempt and the Job stays `queued` | `resource_busy` | 3 |
| fewer than `concurrency` Attempts are not `ended` (an urgent Job: fewer than `concurrency + 1`, contract §3.7) | `no_slot` | 3 |
| the Job's Tier for the Attempt is outside its range (§5.1: the worker range, or the explore range of a `scout` or `research` Job, contract §9 "Roles and ranges"); a Tier that is not valid at all is `tier_invalid`, checked first. A Job stored on such a Tier is not started here, as engine E3 does not start it and raises one `error` Event per such Job (contract §3.7 E3); `details` as §5.1 | `tier_not_allowed` | 2 |

Effects (§3.4 "The driver lock"): take `locks/attempt-<plan>--<attempt>.lock`; **rows**, one transaction: `attempts` (`starting`, Tier from §9, `origin`), Job `running` and the Jira transition `in_progress` of the Job's Workflow (`swr-jira.md` §7) (`swr-jira.md` §7: the first Attempt of any Job of the Workflow queues it, later ones change nothing; engine E3's start is the same); **Event** `attempt-started` `{number, tier, origin}`; then spawn `cpd attempt run <attempt> --plan <plan>` with `setsid`, fd 3 = the lock, stderr to `run/<plan>/logs/attempt-<attempt>.log` and record `driver_pid` (a data write, no Event). If the spawn fails, the command ends the Attempt `failed` / `crashed` with `driver_pid` still null (`attempt-retry` at the same Tier, not counted against `retry_cap`, §3.4) and returns `spawn_failed` (exit 1).

```json
{"ok": true, "attempt": "api-schema-a1", "tier": "S2", "origin": "ladder", "pid": 81234}
```

Idempotent: no. A second call finds the Job `running` and is refused `job_not_ready`.

### 5.6 `job list`

```
cpd job list [--status <status>] [--plan <id>]
```

A Manager may run this on a shaping Plan of its own Context (§4.1, "A Manager on a shaping Plan"; air-d19, air-d22), refused `plan_has_lead` (exit 3) or `plan_other_context` (exit 2).

`--status` is one of §3.2's statuses and may repeat. Each Job carries `urgent` (a boolean) and `kind`. Effects: none.

```json
{"ok": true, "jobs": [{"key": "api-schema", "workflow": "api", "title": "…", "status": "merged", "tier": "S2", "appended": false, "kind": "work", "urgent": false, "needs": [], "attempts": 1, "merged_sha": "c0ffee…"}]}
```

### 5.7 `job show`

```
cpd job show <key> [--plan <id>]
```

A Manager may run this on a shaping Plan of its own Context (§4.1, "A Manager on a shaping Plan"; air-d19, air-d22), refused `plan_has_lead` (exit 3) or `plan_other_context` (exit 2).

Effects: none. Output: every field of the Job (§2.2; `urgent`, a boolean; `kind` and `tests`, `test_files` and `test_approved` where the kind has them; `resources`, the Spec's list (null when it has none); `waiting_for`, present only for a `queued` Job that is not a tenant (contract §3.4 "Tenancy": it has no Attempt yet) and that lists resources, or whose Ready turn finds no free Worker slot (it then has the entry for `workers`, contract §8.3): an array of `{"resource":"<name>","scope":"host"|"owner"|"repo","slots":<n>,"holders":[…]}` for each pool it needs that has no free slot right now, `scope` and `slots` those of the resolved declaration (contract §8.3) and `holders` the holders of contract §1.4 of the pool (`{slot, holder}`, command slots then Job tenants with `slot` null; `[]` when every pool has a free slot; the key is absent for every other Job, a retried Job included, which holds its resources). A Job in `waiting_for` is skipped, in order, by E3 (contract §3.7 "the skip order"): it waits without holding anything; the `needs` of an `open` or `update` Job is the derived list of contract §3.2), `needs`, `needed_by` and every Attempt with all its fields (`check_tail`, `gate_hook`, `gate_command`, `gate_exit`, `metrics`, `actual_files` and `footprint`, the values `attempt show` prints, §6.3) and its Escalations (cpd 1 §11, kept). It also has `addenda`, the addenda of `job addendum` (§5.10), oldest first: `[{"number", "attempt", "session", "created_at", "text"}]`, with `attempt` and `session` null when none was addressed, and `[]` when there are none (contract §3.4 "Addenda").

```json
{"ok": true, "job": {"key": "worker", "workflow": "api", "status": "failed", "failed_cause": "timed_out", "tier": "S2", "urgent": false, "fingerprint": "9f…", "retry_tier": null, "…": "…"}, "needs": ["api-schema"], "needed_by": ["ui"],
 "attempts": [{"id": "worker-a1", "status": "ended", "outcome": "failed", "cause": "timed_out", "check_tail": null, "escalations": []}]}
```

For an explore Job (`scout`, `research`) it shows `summary` (the Worker's summary, null until the Job is `merged`) and `artefact` (`run/<plan>/explore/<key>.md`, relative to `$CPD_HOME`) and `workflow` is null (Plan `explore-roles`, R9).

`tamper` is the tamper report of §4.3, as in `plan show` (empty when the Job is intact). Both are read-only.

### 5.8 `job urgent`

```
cpd job urgent <key> [--plan <id>]
```

Marks an existing Job **urgent** (contract §2.2): engine E3 starts urgent Ready Jobs first, then by `jobs.seq`, across Plans and may start one urgent Job beyond `concurrency` (§3.7). A Lead or Manager runs it **only when the User explicitly asks**, usually for something that blocks all work or an incident. `urgent` is not a Locked field and in no fingerprint (§2.3), so it is allowed on a Locked Job: a `queued` one.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Job exists in the Plan | `job_not_found` | 4 |
| the Job is `queued` or `draft`; a `running`, `merged`, `failed` or `cancelled` Job is refused (*decided*: the flag only matters to scheduling and E3 only starts `queued` Jobs; `job retry` makes a `failed` one `queued`, then mark it) | `illegal_transition` | 3 |

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: `jobs.urgent = 1`. **Event** `job-edited` `{fields: ["urgent"]}` (no new Event kind). Nothing else changes: status, fingerprint, `appended` and Dependencies stay as they are. There is no command to clear the flag. And, when the Plan's working Lead runs it, it names the Workflow as the Lead's Workflow (§1.3).

```json
{"ok": true, "job": {"key": "hotfix", "status": "queued", "urgent": true}, "fields": ["urgent"]}
```

Idempotent: yes; a Job that is already urgent writes nothing and returns `"already": true` with `"fields": []`.

### 5.9 `job approve-tests`

```
cpd job approve-tests <job> --path <p> [--path <p> …] --reason <text> [--plan <id>]
```

The Lead's approval for an `impl` Job to change a red test (hs-d341; contract §2.2 "Job kinds", §7.5). The files of the `test` Jobs an `impl` Job needs are guarded: its submit is refused `tests_tampered` (§6.1) when it changes one. A Worker that needs a red test changed asks the Lead (`cpd ask`); the Lead decides and, to allow it, runs this. **The Lead only**, through `CPD_ATTEMPT` (hs-d497): the command is refused `not_a_lead` when `CPD_ATTEMPT` is set, which cpd sets in every Worker's pane (§6.5). That is all the check there is: the command is **unauthenticated, like `cpd answer`** (a Worker that unsets the variable gets through) and the approval is visible afterwards in the `job-edited` Event (`fields: ["test_approved"]`, with the `--reason`).

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<job>` | the `impl` Job |
| `--path <p>` | repeated: a path or, ending in `/`, a directory prefix, that is guarded: equal to, or inside, an entry of the `test_files` of a `test` Job the `impl` Job needs |
| `--reason <text>` | why (§1.5); it is in the Event's `text` |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `CPD_ATTEMPT` is not set | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| the Job exists | `job_not_found` | 4 |
| its kind is `impl` | `not_an_impl_job` | 3 |
| its status is `queued`, `running` or `failed` | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| every `--path` is guarded; `details.paths` lists those that are not | `path_not_guarded` | 3 |

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: `jobs.test_approved` becomes the union of its old value and the paths. **Event** `job-edited` `{fields: ["test_approved"]}`, its `text` naming the paths and the reason. It takes effect at the Job's next check, a running Attempt's included (contract §7.7). `test_approved` is not a Locked field and is in no fingerprint (§2.3). And, when the Plan's working Lead runs it, it names the Workflow as the Lead's Workflow (§1.3).

```json
{"ok": true, "job": {"key": "api-impl", "status": "running", "kind": "impl"}, "approved": ["cli/tests/it/pr_open_job.rs"], "fields": ["test_approved"]}
```

Idempotent: yes; paths already approved write nothing and a call with none new returns `"already": true`.

### 5.9a `job approve-touches`

```
cpd job approve-touches <job> --path <p> [--path <p> …] --reason <text> [--plan <id>]
```

The Lead's approval for a Job to change a path outside its Spec `touches` (hs-n641; contract §2.2 "Job kinds", §7.5). The `touches` guard refuses a submit (§6.1) that changes a path outside the Job's Spec `touches`; a Worker that needs an out-of-touches file changed asks the Lead (`cpd ask`), who decides and, to allow it, runs this. **The Lead only**, through `CPD_ATTEMPT` (hs-d497): the command is refused `not_a_lead` when `CPD_ATTEMPT` is set, which cpd sets in every Worker's pane (§6.5). That is all the check there is: the command is **unauthenticated, like `cpd answer`** (a Worker that unsets the variable gets through) and the approval is visible afterwards in the `job-edited` Event (`fields: ["touches_approved"]`, with the `--reason`).

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<job>` | the Job |
| `--path <p>` | repeated: a path, or a directory prefix, that the check (§7.5) refuses. The command validates no path against the touches list: what the check refuses is what the Lead approves |
| `--reason <text>` | why (§1.5); it is in the Event's `text` |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `CPD_ATTEMPT` is not set | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| the Job exists | `job_not_found` | 4 |
| its status is `queued`, `running` or `failed` (a draft is not checked, an ended one never will be) | `illegal_transition` | 3 |

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: `jobs.touches_approved` becomes the union of its old value and the paths. **Event** `job-edited` `{fields: ["touches_approved"]}`, its `text` naming the paths and the reason. It takes effect at the Job's next check, a running Attempt's included (contract §7.7). `touches_approved` is not a Locked field and is in no fingerprint (§2.3). And, when the Plan's working Lead runs it, it names the PR as the Lead's Workflow (§1.3).

```json
{"ok": true, "job": {"key": "api-work", "status": "running", "kind": "work"}, "approved": ["cli/src/"], "fields": ["touches_approved"]}
```

Idempotent: yes; paths already approved write nothing and a call with none new returns `"already": true`.

### 5.10 `job addendum`

```
cpd job addendum <job> (<text> | --file <path>) [--plan <id>]
```

The Lead adds information to a Job after its Spec was locked: a fact, a decision, a constraint or a pointer that the Job's Worker lacks (contract §3.4 "Addenda"). A running Worker gets it as a steered message and its Attempt is not stopped; the Spec of every later Attempt of the Job lists it (§16.1). An addendum is **additive only**: it never changes the Goal, Files you may touch, Acceptance or Out of scope. A Job that must deliver something else is cancelled and re-added (§5.3). **The Lead only**, through `CPD_ATTEMPT` (as §5.9): the command is refused `not_a_lead` when `CPD_ATTEMPT` is set, which cpd sets in every Worker's pane (§6.5). Like `cpd answer`, it is **unauthenticated**: nothing else checks the caller. A `draft` Job is not locked: its Spec is edited with `job edit --spec` (§5.2).

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<job>` | the Job, of any kind (`open`, `update` and explore Jobs too) |
| `<text>` | the addendum, a `Text` (1–20 000 characters, no NUL, §1.5), kept verbatim |
| `--file <path>` | the addendum read whole from a file, as UTF-8, kept verbatim, with the same limits; exactly one of `<text>` and `--file` is given (both or neither is `usage`) |
| `--plan <id>` | the Plan (§1.3) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `CPD_ATTEMPT` is set and not empty | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| exactly one of `<text>` and `--file` is given; the text is not 1–20 000 characters or has a NUL | `usage` | 2 |
| `--file` cannot be read as UTF-8 | `file_unreadable` | 2 |
| the Plan exists | `plan_not_found` | 4 |
| the Job exists in the Plan | `job_not_found` | 4 |
| the Job is `draft`, `merged` or `cancelled`: a draft is not locked (`job edit --spec`); an ended Job takes no new information | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| the Job is `running` and its latest Attempt is `starting` (its Spec is being rendered), `merging` (the Worker has submitted) or `ended` (the next Attempt is about to start); nothing is written, and the Lead runs the command again in a moment | `attempt_not_running` | 3 |

The checks run in this order and the first that fails is the result. The Plan's phase is not checked. A `running` Attempt always has its Worker Session; a row without one is a store defect, not a refusal.

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: one `job_addenda` row (§4.4, append-only): `number` = the Job's highest addendum number + 1 (1 for the first); `attempt` and `session` = the running Attempt and its Worker Session, both null when the Job is `queued` or `failed` (no Attempt runs); `text` verbatim; `created_at`. **Event** `job-addendum`, always appended: `plan` and `job` set; `attempt` and `session` set exactly when the row's are; `data` = `{"text": <the addendum text, verbatim>}`. Its `text` has two shapes. When addressed to a running Attempt: `Addendum <n> from the Lead on Job <job> (Attempt <attempt>). It adds to your Spec and replaces nothing in it: your Goal, Files you may touch, Acceptance and Out of scope stand as written.`, then a blank line, then the addendum text verbatim. When not addressed: `Addendum <n> added to Job <job>: no Attempt is running, so it reaches the next Attempt's Spec. Next: cpd job show <job> --plan <plan>`, then a blank line, then the text verbatim. **Untouched**: the `jobs` row (every Spec column and `fingerprint`), the Locked-Job fingerprint, the Plan fingerprint, an approved Plan review, the Job's status and Tier, and every Attempt: a running Attempt is never stopped or restarted. And, when the Plan's working Lead runs it, it names the Job's PR as the Lead's Workflow (§1.3); a Job with no PR (an explore Job) names none.

**Delivery** (§15.3; §11.2 for `--session`): a Worker's follower gets the Event once, as a steered message (`deliverAs: "steer"`, which starts a turn when the Worker is idle); a Plan Lead's adapter ignores it, since the Lead sent it; the Manager is never addressed. A `--session` follower drops it once a later `attempt-started`, `job-merged`, `job-failed` or `job-cancelled` of its Job exists (contract §5.4). Nothing waits on the Worker: cpd does not know whether it read the addendum, so there is no read receipt and no submit refusal. `delivered` means sent, never read; check the Attempt with `cpd attempt read` before relying on it.

```json
{"ok": true, "job": {"key": "api-impl", "status": "running", "kind": "impl"}, "addendum": {"number": 2, "attempt": "api-impl-a1", "delivered": true}}
```

```json
{"ok": true, "job": {"key": "ui", "status": "queued", "kind": "work"}, "addendum": {"number": 1, "attempt": null, "delivered": false}}
```

`delivered` is true exactly when the Event is addressed to a Worker Session. A `queued` or `failed` Job's addendum is read when its next Attempt starts (§16.1).

Idempotent: no; each `job addendum` call is a new addendum, with its own row and Event.

## 6. `attempt`

### 6.1 `attempt submit`

```
cpd attempt submit <attempt> [--summary-file <path>] [--plan <id>]
```

Run by the Worker, from its worktree. Preconditions are §7.3's list, in that order, after the Attempt's own state:

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Attempt is `running` (already `merging` or later with `submitted_sha` = the worktree's HEAD: `already`) | `attempt_not_running` | 3 |
| the Attempt was ended by `attempt abort` | `attempt_aborted` | 3 |
| the caller's cwd is inside the Attempt worktree, on the Attempt branch; for a linear Attempt, the worktree is the Lead worktree and the branch is the Lead Branch | `wrong_worktree` | 3 |
| clean tree, untracked files included | `dirty_tree` | 3 |
| at least one commit ahead of `base_sha`; **for an `open` or `update` Job none is required** (the base may not have moved, so there may be nothing to commit, hs-d340) | `no_commits` | 3 |
| the tamper check passes (§7.5; a protected path whose Attempt version equals the Lead tip's or `origin/<base>`'s, as a base merge brings it, is allowed); `details.paths` lists the protected paths touched that are not allowed | `gate_tampered` | 3 |
| the touches guard passes (§7.5): a path outside the Job's Spec `touches` is refused, unless a base merge brought it, the repo's `[generated] paths` (§8.3) match it, or the Lead approved it with `job approve-touches` (§5.9a); `details.paths`, `details.touches`, `details.generated` (contract §7.5, §7.7) | `touches_violation` | 3 |
| (kind `impl`) it changes no path guarded by the `test_files` of a `test` Job it needs, unless `job approve-tests` (§5.9) approved it; `details.paths`, `details.jobs` (contract §7.5, §7.7) | `tests_tampered` | 3 |
| (kind `test`) every `test_files` entry matches a path the Job changed (`git diff --name-only --no-renames <lead branch>...HEAD`); `details.paths` lists the entries that match none | `test_files_missing` | 3 |
| (kinds `test`, `impl`) the Workflow's repo policy has `[test-commands]` (none when there is no repo file or the file lacks the table) | `tests_unconfigured` | 3 |
| (kinds `test`, `impl`) the repo's `build` exits zero; `details` `{job, tests, tail, log}` | `tests_build_failed` | 3 |
| (kinds `test`, `impl`; the repo's `[test-commands]` has `list`) the `list` command exits zero for every named test, run once per name with the variable `test`; `details` `{job, tests, tail, log}`, `tests` the names that match nothing (hs-d497) | `tests_not_found` | 3 |
| (kind `test`) the repo's `run` of the named tests exits non-zero: they fail, for a reason other than a build error | `tests_not_red` | 3 |
| (kind `impl`) the repo's `run` of the derived tests exits zero | `tests_failed` | 3 |
| (kinds `test`, `impl`) the commands ran (not killed, not `hook_invalid`) | `tests_error` | 1 |
| (kinds `open`, `update`) the Workflow's policy resolves (contract §8.3): its Context has an owner | `owner_unset` | 3 |
| its owner has a policy file; its policy files are valid | `owner_unconfirmed`, `policy_invalid` | 1 |

Effects:
- **One check span** (contract §7.7, hs-d679): the checks of the table run inside ONE span, `what` `checks`, in this order: for an `open` or `update` Job the policy read (the policy rows), then the tamper check, the red-test guard and the `test` or `impl` kind check. The Gate runs at the merge, not in the span (contract §7.4, hs-d679). The preconditions of §7.3 run before it.
- **Hooks:** none at submit. The quick check (`pre-commit`) and the Gate (`pre-merge`) run at the merge, not here (§7.3, §7.4 step 6, hs-d679), and their logs are written there.
- **Kind checks** (contract §7.7, hs-d340, hs-d341), for the kinds that have one: a `test` or `impl` Job's `[test-commands]` commands (`build`, then `run`; output in `run/<plan>/logs/<attempt>.tests-build.log` and `<attempt>.tests-run.log`; with `list`, once per name between them, `<attempt>.tests-list.log`). An `open` or `update` Job has none: its only check beyond the tamper check is the policy read above. Its title, ticket, closed-pull-request, base and Gate checks are the merge's and end the Attempt there, not here (contract §7.4 steps 5, 6 and 8b). The span holds `locks/check-<plan>--<attempt>.lock`; it appends `attempt-status` with `check` `start` (before the first check) and `end` (contract §5.2; on a pass in the transaction of the Rows below, on a refusal before the error returns), so the Attempt's timeout and the stall kill do not count it, the tamper check included. A refusal changes nothing else: the Worker fixes, commits and submits again and the checks run again.
- **Rows**, one transaction with a compare-and-swap on `status = 'running'` and on the HEAD checked: Attempt `merging`, `submitted_sha`, `submitted_at`; the Job stays `running`; the span's `end` Event is appended in the same transaction. Submit writes no Gate column: `check_tail`, `gate_hook`, `gate_command` and `gate_exit` are written by the merge's Gate, and only when it fails `gate_failed` (contract §7.4 step 6). **Event** `attempt-status` `{from: "running", to: "merging"}`.
- The driver sees `merging` at A5 and starts the merge (A8, §7.4). An `open` or `update` Job's merge does not rebase, pushes the Lead Branch and, for an `open` Job, opens the pull request and moves the Workflow in step 10's transaction (contract §7.4, §7.7): `pr-opened` and `plan-phase` follow its `job-merged`.

```json
{"ok": true, "attempt": "api-schema-a1", "submitted": true, "sha": "a1b2c3d…", "next": "Stop now. Do not make more changes."}
```

Idempotent: yes, as stated; a HEAD that moved after a successful submit is refused `attempt_not_running`.

**An explore Attempt** (`scout`, `research`; Plan `explore-roles`, R8). The Worker runs `cpd attempt submit <attempt> --summary-file <path>` from its cwd, the explore directory `$CPD_HOME/run/<plan>/explore/`, which is not a worktree. The rows above that name a worktree, a commit, a branch, a check or the Gate do not apply to it; `attempt_not_running` does. Then, in this order, each refused with exit 3 and nothing changed:

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| there is no non-empty artefact at `$CPD_HOME/run/<plan>/explore/<job-key>.md` | `artefact_missing` | 3 |
| there is no `--summary-file`, or the file is missing or empty | `summary_missing` | 3 |
| the summary has more than 1500 characters, counted as characters and not bytes; `details` `{length, cap}`, `cap` 1500. It is never truncated: the Worker shortens it and submits again | `summary_too_long` | 3 |

Effects, for an explore Attempt that passes:
- **Checks that do not run:** the quick check, the tamper check, the red-test check, the kind check and the Gate. There is no worktree and no commit to check.
- **The atomic end** (one transaction, no compare-and-swap, so no merge-recovery case): the Attempt `ended` / `merged`; the Job `merged` with `jobs.summary` the summary; the SHA-256 (hex) of the artefact in the Job's `merged_sha`, the Attempt's `merged_sha` and `submitted_sha` and the `job-merged` Event's `sha` (no commit exists, so the existing CHECKs on merged rows hold); the Attempt's `actual_files` = `[]` (no repo file is written). The `job-merged` Event's `data` is `{sha, tier, kind, summary, artefact, turn}` (text in §15.3).
- **A driver that died before the transaction** leaves an ordinary dead Attempt, which E2 ends `crashed`; the submit never stops the Worker (the driver's A9 does, or E2 for a dead driver).

### 6.2 `attempt read`

```
cpd attempt read <attempt> [--lines <n>] [--plan <id>]
```

A Manager may run this on a shaping Plan of its own Context (§4.1, "A Manager on a shaping Plan"; air-d19, air-d22), refused `plan_has_lead` (exit 3) or `plan_other_context` (exit 2).

A readable transcript (cpd 1 §11, kept): one line per assistant text line (`assistant: …`) and one per tool call (`tool: <name>`), in session order. The source is the Worker Session's `runner`:
- `pi`: the Worker's session file (`sessions.file`). A partial last line of a file being written is skipped.
- `durable`: the Attempt's store `run/<plan>/durable/<attempt>.sqlite`, the `entries` table. Only the rows whose `record` `kind` is `pi.assistant` are read, in `id` order: each `model[0].content` text block gives an `assistant: …` line and each `toolCall` block a `tool: <name>` line, as for `pi`. The `file` field is the `.sqlite` path. There is no partial-line rule.

`--lines` (default 40) keeps the last n.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session is registered and its `file` is known and exists (`pi`); the store `run/<plan>/durable/<attempt>.sqlite` exists (`durable`) | `session_not_found` | 4 |
| every complete line is a JSON session entry (`pi`); every `pi.assistant` row's `record` is an assistant entry, its `model[0]` an assistant message with a `content` array (`durable`) | `session_malformed` | 1 |

Example for `pi`:

```json
{"ok": true, "attempt": "api-schema-a1", "session": "c1a2…", "file": "/home/clayton/.pi/agent/sessions/…/…_c1a2….jsonl", "total": 412,
 "lines": ["tool: bash", "assistant: The schema compiles; committing."]}
```

Example for `durable`:

```json
{"ok": true, "attempt": "api-schema-a1", "session": "d4e5…", "file": "/home/clayton/.cpd/run/api-schema/durable/api-schema-a1.sqlite", "total": 57,
 "lines": ["assistant: The schema compiles; committing.", "tool: bash"]}
```

Read-only.

### 6.3 `attempt show` and `attempt list`

```
cpd attempt show <attempt> [--plan <id>]
cpd attempt list [--job <key>] [--active] [--plan <id>]
```

A Manager may run these on a shaping Plan of its own Context (§4.1, "A Manager on a shaping Plan"; air-d19, air-d22), refused `plan_has_lead` (exit 3) or `plan_other_context` (exit 2).

`show` returns every field of the Attempt (§2.2), its Escalations and the paths it uses: `spec_path`, `check` (`run/<plan>/logs/<attempt>.pre-commit.log`, null when no quick check ran), `log` (`run/<plan>/logs/attempt-<attempt>.log`) and the Worker's session file. Its `attempt` carries `runner` (`pi` or `durable`) and `worker_pid` (null for `pi` and before a `durable` Worker starts) and so do the attempts of `job show` (contract §3.4 "The Worker runner and its seam", §4.4). Its `attempt` carries `actual_files` (an array of the repo-relative paths the Attempt wrote, or null; contract §2.2, §7.3); it also carries `footprint`: null, or `{class, undeclared, untouched}` derived on read from `actual_files` and the Job's `touches` (contract 7.3 "The footprint"), null for the kinds `open`, `update`, `scout` and `research`, for a Job with no Spec and for a null `actual_files`; `list` does not. The Gate fields `check_tail`, `gate_hook`, `gate_command` and `gate_exit` are set exactly when the Attempt ended `gate_failed` and are null otherwise, `gate_error` included (contract §2.2, §7.4 step 6). An Attempt ended `aborted` (hs-a8, `attempt abort`, §6.5, contract §3.4) has `outcome` `failed` and `cause` `aborted` in both `show` and `list`. `list` returns `id`, `job`, `number`, `tier`, `origin`, `status`, `outcome`, `cause`, `started_at`, `ended_at`; `--active` keeps those not `ended`.

```json
{"ok": true, "attempts": [{"id": "api-schema-a1", "job": "api-schema", "number": 1, "tier": "S2", "origin": "ladder", "status": "ended", "outcome": "merged", "cause": "merged", "started_at": "…", "ended_at": "…"}]}
```

`attempt show`:

```json
{"ok": true, "attempt": {"id": "api-schema-a1", "job": "api-schema", "status": "merging", "tier": "S2", "…": "…"},
 "escalations": [], "paths": {"spec": "…/specs/api-schema-a1.md", "check": "…/logs/api-schema-a1.pre-commit.log", "log": "…/logs/attempt-api-schema-a1.log", "worker_file": "…"}}
```

Both are read-only.

### 6.4 `attempt run` (internal)

```
cpd attempt run <attempt> --plan <id>
```

The Attempt driver, steps A1–A9 of §3.4, started detached by E3 or `job dispatch` with the driver lock as fd 3. It starts at nice 19 and I/O class idle (§6.5 hs-d528), set at spawn so its process tree (the Worker's pi, cargo, rustc and every tool) inherits it. Not for agents.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| fd 3 is the driver lock file (same device and inode) | `driver_lock_missing`, printed to its log; nothing is written (§3.4 step 4) | 1 |
| the Attempt is `starting` | `illegal_transition` | 3 |

Effects: everything of §3.4 A1–A9, §7.2, §7.3, §7.4: the worktree and `pre-start`; the rendered Worker Spec (§16.1); the Worker, started by the Attempt's `runner` (contract §3.4 "The Worker runner and its seam"): for `pi` its window `cpd-work:<plan>--<attempt>` (`new-window` with the Worker's argv of §6.5, `@cpd_session`) and the Session rows (`session-registered`, `session-moved` `{place: "work"}`); for `durable` a child process with no window and no `session-moved`, its `worker_pid` stored, restarted and stopped as that section says; the nudge (`attempt-nudge`); the stall kill (a Worker's session file idle for `timeouts.stall_seconds` inside one tool call: pi's descendant processes are killed, pi is not, the Attempt goes on; one driver-log line, no Event; contract §3.4 A4); the merge, with no lock (hs-d243: rule S and rule P, contract §7.4); the end (`metrics` from the end report, the Worker's stop by runner, worktree removal on `merged`). Each status change is one transaction with the Event of §3.4.

Output, printed when it exits (stdout goes to its log): `{"ok": true, "attempt": "api-schema-a1", "outcome": "merged", "cause": "merged"}`. Unexpected failures append `error` `{source: "attempt run", code, message, details}` and end the Attempt `failed` / `crashed` when it is not already ended. An error with the same `code` and `message` as one appended for the same Plan less than `watch.error_repeat_seconds` ago appends nothing (contract §3.7). Idempotent: no; a second driver cannot get fd 3.

### 6.5 `attempt abort` (hs-a8, the User, 2026-10-31)

```
cpd attempt abort <attempt> [--plan <id>]
```

A Manager may run this on a shaping Plan of its own Context (§4.1, "A Manager on a shaping Plan"; air-d19, air-d22), refused `plan_has_lead` (exit 3) or `plan_other_context` (exit 2).

The Lead's abort of a running Attempt (hs-a8, the User, 2026-10-31; contract §3.4 "attempt abort"): the Lead ends a `running` Attempt `failed` / `aborted` in ONE write transaction (contract §3.4). It refuses a Worker that types it (`not_a_lead` exit 3), the same `CPD_ATTEMPT` check as `job approve-tests` (§5.9); the Attempt must be `running` (`attempt_not_running` exit 3). A Worker that needs a stopped Attempt talks to the Lead, or runs `cpd ask`.

The command refuses a `starting` Attempt: its setup failure is `setup_failed` (contract §3.4), and the abort never touches it. A `merging` or `ended` Attempt is refused `attempt_not_running`: the natural ending stands, and the abort never rewrites its cause. The command re-reads the Attempt's status in its write transaction (ADR-0014): if the Attempt ended between the command's read and write, the transaction ends with the natural ending, refused `attempt_not_running`, nothing written.

Effects (contract §3.4): in one transaction the Attempt goes `running` → `ended` / `failed` / `aborted` (a no-ladder cause: the engine requeues nothing and climbs nothing), the Job goes `running` → `failed`, `stop_request = aborted` is set when a merge step of the Attempt is running (the merge unwinds per its own rules, never torn down mid-write), and two Events are appended: `attempt-aborted` (§5.2) and `job-failed` (§5.2), whose text names the abort and the Tier-fix route `cpd job retry <key> --tier <T>`. The Worker is stopped by the existing teardown (contract §3.4 "attempt abort"): the `runner`'s stop seam (`core/src/driver/runner.rs::stop`, through the driver's A9, `core/src/driver/run.rs`) when the driver is live; when it is dead, the crash-recovery teardown (`core/src/merge/recover.rs::recover_attempt`, its `rest_of_a9`/`kill_worker`, the E2/R path). Exactly one command writes the two Events; no second command writes them again.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `CPD_ATTEMPT` is not set | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| the Attempt exists | `attempt_not_found` | 4 |
| the Attempt is `running` | `attempt_not_running` | 3 |

```json
{"ok": true, "attempt": "api-schema-a1", "outcome": "failed", "cause": "aborted"}
```

Idempotent: no; a second call finds the Attempt not `running` and is refused `attempt_not_running`.

## 7. `review`

Removed by R19 (no Job-level Reviewer).

### 7.1 `review decide`

Removed by R19 (no Job-level Reviewer).

## 8. `ask` and `answer`

Escalations from a Worker to its Lead (§2.2, §3.5).

### 8.1 `ask`

```
cpd ask <attempt> <question> [--timeout-minutes <n>] [--plan <id>]
```

Run by the Worker; it blocks until the answer. `--timeout-minutes` defaults to `ask_minutes`.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Attempt is `running` | `attempt_not_running` | 3 |
| answered before the timeout | `ask_timeout` | 5 |

Effects:
1. **Rows**, one transaction: `escalations` (`<attempt>-q<k>`, `open`, `asker_pid` = its own pid); the Worker Session `waiting` with label `φ: question to the Lead` (it waits for its Lead, not for the User: hs-d303; contract §3.6). **Events** `escalation` `{escalation, question}` (the Lead's adapter delivers it with a turn) and `session-state`.
2. It polls its row every 500 ms (a read; cpd 1 §11, kept).
3. Answered: one transaction setting the Worker Session `working` (`session-state`); prints the answer. Timeout: one transaction, `status = expired`, `expired_at`, **Event** `escalation-expired` `{escalation, reason: "timeout"}`, Session `working`; prints `ask_timeout`. If the process dies, E1 expires it (`reason: "asker_dead"`) and, in the same transaction, sets the Worker Session `working` (`session-state`, `waiting` to `working`) unless another Escalation of the Attempt is still `open`.

```json
{"ok": true, "escalation": "api-schema-a1-q1", "answer": "Use the v2 field names."}
```

**How a Worker runs it** (pro-d274). As a call of its own, in the foreground, with the bash tool's `timeout` input set to 7200 seconds (above the default `ask_minutes`, 60 minutes, so that `cpd ask` ends its own wait), never under the `timeout` command, in a pipeline or in the background. While the Escalation is `open` the Worker's pi sits inside a silent tool call: the stall rule spares it (contract §3.4 A4) and an explore Worker's guard lets it wait (§15.22). A bash call that ends before the Escalation (a harness timeout, a kill) leaves it `open` until E1 expires it; the Worker has the tool's error, its Attempt is not failed and it is sent no text, and it asks again (a new Escalation).

Idempotent: no. Each call is a new Escalation; ids are never reused (§3.5).

### 8.2 `answer`

```
cpd answer <escalation> <answer> [--plan <id>]
```

A Manager may run this on a shaping Plan of its own Context (§4.1, "A Manager on a shaping Plan"; air-d19, air-d22), refused `plan_has_lead` (exit 3) or `plan_other_context` (exit 2).

Run by the Lead. On a Lead-less shaping Plan the Manager receives the Worker's Escalation as a `session-message` that wakes it: `Worker <agent-key> of Plan <plan> asks: "<question, first 300 characters>" (escalation <id>). Answer with: cpd answer <id> "<text>" --plan <plan>` (contract §5.3). It runs `cpd answer <id> "<text>" --plan <plan>`; the answer resolves the Escalation as it does for a Lead and the Worker's `ask` returns it. A `job-merged` message carries the summary and the artefact path, which the Manager may not read and cites in the brief of a later Plan.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Escalation is `open` | `escalation_answered`, `escalation_expired` | 3 |

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: `status = answered`, `answer`, `answered_at`. **Event** `escalation-answered` `{escalation}`. The waiting `ask` sees it at its next poll. And, when the Plan's working Lead runs it, it names the Workflow as the Lead's Workflow (§1.3).

```json
{"ok": true, "escalation": "api-schema-a1-q1", "attempt": "api-schema-a1", "answered_at": "…"}
```

Idempotent: no; §3.5 refuses `answer` on an Escalation that is not `open`, so a second answer is `escalation_answered`.

## 9. `workflow` and `pr`

Two command groups (R3). **`workflow`** is the object's group (contract §2.2 Workflow): `cpd workflow add`, `cpd workflow edit`, `cpd workflow describe`, `cpd workflow cancel` and `cpd workflow start` (§9.4–§9.7). **`pr`** keeps the commands that act on a Workflow's pull request through `gh` (§7.6): `cpd pr open`, `pr poll`, `pr rebase`, `pr view`, `pr reply`, `pr post`, `pr rerun`, `pr push` and `pr merge` (§9.1–§9.3, §9.8–§9.10); `pr` is GitHub's word, unchanged. **The old forms are usage errors, no alias, shim or deprecation** (pro-d138): `cpd pr add`, `cpd pr edit`, `cpd pr describe`, `cpd pr cancel` and `cpd pr start` are refused `usage` (exit 2) as unknown subcommands, and so is `--pr <key>` on the commands that now take `--workflow <key>` (R4). Quotes that keep the current words are verbatim strings, not names of the object: the stored `cancel_reason` `pr merged`, the Inbox subjects `pr:<owner>/<repo>#<n>`, the dialog title `Post Pull Request`, and `gh`'s own arguments.

`gh` failures are `gh_failed` (exit 1) with its stderr tail. Every command here works on **one Workflow** (through its pull request, for the `pr` group): `pr open`, `pr rebase`, `pr push`, `pr view`, `pr reply`, `pr rerun` and `pr post` select it by `--workflow <key>` (§1.3: omitted, the Plan's one Workflow that is not `cancelled`); `workflow add`, `workflow edit`, `workflow describe`, `workflow cancel` and `workflow start` (§9.4, §9.5, §9.5a, §9.6, §9.7) take its key as their argument; `pr poll` has no `--workflow`: it polls every open pull request of the User. `<repo>`, `<base>`, `<lead branch>` and `<lead worktree>` are the selected Workflow's (§7); `gh` runs with cwd = its Lead worktree, so it addresses the Workflow's repo.

### 9.1 `pr open`

**The repair** (hs-d340). A Workflow is opened by its `open` Job (contract §7.7), not by the Lead: engine E4 adds the Job to every started Workflow, its Worker merges the base and its submit runs the Gate, pushes and opens the pull request in its merge. `pr open` stays for what that cannot cover: a Workflow whose `open` Job is `failed` (the Lead decides between `job retry <job> --tier <T>` (§5.4) and this command), an engine that is down, or a Workflow whose `open` Job the Lead cancelled (`job cancel` stands, §5.3: E4 adds no new one, so this is how the Workflow is opened later; to give it up, `workflow cancel`, §9.6). It is refused `open_job_live` while the Workflow has an `open` Job that is `draft`, `queued` or `running` (hs-d573) and its `jobs_not_done` counts every Job of the Workflow except its `open` and `update` Jobs. Nothing else here changes: the steps and refusals below are the ones the Job's submit and merge share (contract §7.6 steps 0, 1, 3, 4).

`pr open` belongs to the **Deploying** step of the Dispatch stage (contract §3.9): it runs the Gate, then opens the pull request. Review follows the opening, not the Gate. **The Gate runs only when the Workflow's `gate.merge` is `local` (for `pr open` and `pr push`) or `gate.pr` is `local` (for `pr rebase`)** (contract §8.3, hs-d292; the Workflow's policy key, `Repo(<owner>, <name>)`): with `none`, cpd's default (`core/src/policy/default.toml`), `pr open` runs no Gate, the repo's CI is the check and the two Gate rows below do not apply.

```
cpd pr open [--workflow <key>] [--plan <id>]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--workflow <key>` | the Workflow to open (R34, A14), selected by §1.3's rule: required when the Plan has two or more Workflows that are not `cancelled`, defaulted to the one when it has one. Only as the repair above |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Workflow is `dispatch`, or `cancelled` with its pull request `OPEN` on GitHub (the reopen below, pro-d362; `open` or `merged`: `already`, nothing written); `waiting`, or `cancelled` with no open pull request | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| the Workflow is `cancelled` and rebinding it finds its Lead worktree path or its local Lead Branch still on disk (the janitor kept them, dirty or unpushed); nothing is discarded or written (as a failed start, `setup_failed` in §9.7) | `setup_failed` | 1 |
| the Workflow has no `open` Job that is `draft`, `queued` or `running`; `details.job` (hs-d340, hs-d573) | `open_job_live` | 3 |
| every Job of the Workflow but its `open` and `update` Jobs `merged` or `cancelled`, at least one `merged` | `jobs_not_done` | 3 |
| the Workflow has a stored title (hs-d285): a Workflow that existed before migration `pr-title` has none and there is no fallback to the Plan's title. The message says to run `cpd workflow edit <key> --title "<text>"`. Checked before the Gate | `workflow_title_required` | 3 |
| the Workflow has a stored description (§9.5a): a Workflow without one is refused until the Lead runs `cpd workflow describe <key> --file <body.md>`. The message says the same. Checked before the Gate | `description_required` | 3 |
| the Workflow's policy sets `workflow.jira_required` (B4, pro-d127) and the Workflow has a stored `jira` (§9.4), unless the Workflow is adopted (`head_ref` set, exempt as for the description); the message says to run `cpd workflow edit <key> --jira <KEY>`, then open it again. Checked before the Gate, after the description | `jira_required` | 3 |
| the Workflow's policy sets `workflow.jira_required`, the Workflow is not adopted and its title is not `<type>[!]: <KEY>/<summary>` for its stored `jira` (pro-d399; "The Jira title", contract §7.6); the message says to run `cpd workflow edit <key> --title "<type>: <KEY>/<summary>"`, then open it again. Checked before the Gate, after the ticket | `jira_title_invalid` | 3 |
| the newest pull request of the Lead Branch is not closed without a merge (a merged one is adopted, below); `details.number`, `details.url` | `pr_closed` | 3 |
| **stacked** (the Workflow's base Workflow, contract §2.2, is not `merged`: a merged one was unstacked first, below): the base Workflow's Lead Branch, `<base>`, is on the remote (`git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin <base>`), checked before the fetch and the Gate; `details` is `{workflow, base, base_workflow}` (hs-d324) | `base_not_found` | 4 |
| after `git fetch origin <base>`, G (the Lead Branch's head, read once: the commit that is gated, pushed and opened) does not conflict with `origin/<base>` (`git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only`; checked before the Gate, with `gate.merge` and `gate.pr` are `none` as with `local`; hs-d490, contract §7.6 step 1). A base that merely moved ahead is no refusal, and neither is a merged base with main ahead without a conflict: the poll queues the Workflow's `update` Job, `reason` `base-merged`, which merges `origin/<base>` without a rebase (hs-d794, hs-n617; contract §3.7 E5). `details` is `{workflow, base, base_sha, sha, files, next}`, `sha` = G, `files` the conflicted paths, `next` = `["git -C <lead worktree> merge --no-edit origin/<base>", "cpd pr open --workflow <key>"]` | `base_conflict` | 3 |
| the Workflow's policy resolves (contract §8.3 "Validation", `details` as there): its Context has an owner | `owner_unset` | 3 |
| its owner has a policy file | `owner_unconfirmed` | 1 |
| its policy files are valid | `policy_invalid` | 1 |
| the `pre-start` passes before the Gate runs; `details.tail` is its last 60 lines, `details.log` the full log `run/<plan>/logs/workflow-<key>.pre-start.log` | `gate_error` | 1 |
| the Gate passes (§7.3, contract §7.4, hs-d679); `details.tail` is its last 60 lines, `details.log` the full log | `gate_failed` | 3 |
| the Gate ran (not killed, not `hook_invalid`); `details.tail`, `details.log` as above | `gate_error` | 1 |
| the Workflow's status is still `dispatch` at the transaction (another `pr open` committed first) | `cas_lost` | 3 |
| the caller is not an agent, OR the incident is off, OR the resolved Workflow's Plan is not held (hs-d643): `CPD_SESSION` set and non-empty names an agent; a held Plan is in the incident; `details` is `{workflow, plan, incident}` | `incident_hold` | 3 |

The Lead worktree's local changes refuse nothing: the Gate does not run there (hs-d243; `dirty_target` is no longer a refusal of this command).

**A stacked Workflow** (hs-d324, hs-d325, hs-d301, contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows" step 7): when its base Workflow is `merged`, the command first **unstacks** it, **before the lookup and before every precondition below, `base_not_found` included** (its `base` becomes the base Workflow's own `base`, normally `main`, walking a chain of merged base Workflows to its end; in its own transaction, **Event** `workflow-base-changed` with `by` `pr open`, one per step, §5.2; the unstack is kept even when a later check refuses) and goes on with the new base, because GitHub deleted the merged base Workflow's branch: that branch is never looked up. The poll already unstacks such a Workflow when it records the base Workflow's merge (`by` `poll`, contract §7.6 step 6), so this is the case where no poll did yet. Otherwise `<base>` is the base Workflow's Lead Branch, so the conflict check, the Gate (its `target` the base Workflow's Lead Branch) and `gh pr create --base <base>` all run on top of it and GitHub will not land the stacked pull request before the base Workflow. The Lead Branch contains the base Workflow's work, because it was started from the base Workflow's head (§9.7); a base Workflow that has moved on since is merged in only when it conflicts (`base_conflict`, `next`; hs-d490). Opened ready, never a draft, like every Workflow.

**Ready, never a draft** (hs-d329): the pull request is opened only after the conflict check above and, with `gate.pr` is `local`, the Gate; `gh pr create` never has `--draft` and no cpd command makes a pull request a draft or ready (contract §7.6 "Ready, never a draft"). Under `ci` the conflict check still applies and the pull request opens ready (the Lead's reading of hs-d329: `ci` skips only the Gate).

**An adopted Workflow** (`head_ref` set, §9.4): the pull request is found by `gh pr list --head <head_ref> --state all`, the Gate runs as above and rule P pushes to `refs/heads/<head_ref>`, plain, never forced; `gh pr create` is never run, the pull request that exists is adopted (its own title kept). `push_rejected` (§9.9) names `cpd pr rebase` (the catch-up, §9.3) as the next step. Steps 0 and 3 and the merged check name `<head_ref>`, not the Lead Branch.

**A cancelled Workflow whose pull request is reopened** (pro-d362; contract §3.8 "Reopening a cancelled Workflow"). For a `cancelled` Workflow, `pr open --workflow <key>` rebinds it when GitHub reports its pull request `OPEN` (`gh pr view <number> --json state`): the pull request is the Workflow's kept `pull_request` (A1), or, for a legacy row whose `pull_request` is NULL, the pull request of its repo whose head is its Lead Branch, only when exactly one `cancelled` Workflow of that repo matches (A7; otherwise it stays refused as above). The legacy rule (pro-d362 follow-up; contract §3.8 "Reopening a cancelled Workflow"): the poll tries a legacy row only while the store holds an unowned open authored pull request (a `pull_requests` row with `state` `open` and `authored` 1 that no Workflow's `pull_request` links to; global, not per repo). `pr open --workflow` is not gated by it: a legacy row whose pull request is not `OPEN` on GitHub is refused here as above, `illegal_transition` (exit 3), and the poll skips it with no `error` Event (contract §3.7 E5). A row with a kept `pull_request` is unchanged. On this path the command runs none of the steps below, its Gate and push included: the pull request already holds the commits it was opened with.

The effects, in order: the Lead worktree is recreated at its path from `origin/<lead_branch>` (`origin/<head_ref>` for an adopted Workflow) after `git fetch origin <branch>`, as the start does (§9.7); a worktree or local branch still there is never discarded (`setup_failed`, above). Then one transaction, with a compare-and-swap on `status = 'cancelled'` (`cas_lost`): the Workflow `status = open`, `lead_worktree` and `started_at` set again, `pr_number`, `pr_url`, `pr_opened_at` and `pull_request` as kept; the Lead Session's `asleep_at` NULL, so engine E2 restarts a stopped Lead into a parked window (A4); when the Plan is `done`, `phase` `deploy` and `done_at` NULL (§3.1). **Events**: `workflow-reopened` `{workflow}`, then `plan-phase` `{from: "done", to: "deploy"}` when the Plan moved. The output carries `ok`, `plan`, `phase` and `workflow`, with `"reopened": true`, and no `sha`, `pushed` or `remote`. A second run on the `open` Workflow is `already` and writes nothing (A5). Engine E5 does the same rebind when the poll sees the pull request reopened (contract §3.7 E5).

Effects:
- **Title** (hs-d285): the pull request is titled with the Workflow's stored title, passed through the one seam in `core/src/workflow/` that turns it into the GitHub title (unchanged today; hs-d277 may change it later). Under `workflow.jira_required` (pro-d399) the stored title already conforms to `<type>[!]: <KEY>/<summary>`: `pr open` refuses one that does not (`jira_title_invalid`), so GitHub gets that title. The title no longer comes from the Plan's title and a Plan with several Workflows no longer gets ` (<key>)` appended.
- **Body** (§9.5a): the pull request body is the Workflow's stored description, verbatim, set by `cpd workflow describe`.
- **No lock** (hs-d243, contract §7): merges into the Workflow go on during the command; no R first (an unrecorded merge leaves its Job `running`, which `jobs_not_done` refuses).
- **Adopting a merged pull request** (before the Gate; contract §7.6 `pr open` step 0): `gh pr list --head <lead branch> --state all --json number,url,state`, the newest decides. When it is `MERGED`, the Gate and the push are skipped (hs-d267 forbids skipping the Gate only when *opening* a pull request where `gate.pr` is `local`, hs-d292): one transaction records the pull request (its `pull_requests` row, `state` `merged`; the Workflow's `pr_number`, `pr_url`, `pull_request`) and moves the Workflow `dispatch → open → merged` exactly as `pr poll` does when it sees a merge: `pr-merged` (no `pr-opened`); `plan-phase` `dispatch → deploy` when every Workflow that is not `cancelled` is then `open` or `merged` and `plan-done` (`deploy → done`) when every one is `merged` and the done guard holds (contract §3.1: no Job of the Plan is non-final; otherwise the Plan stays `deploy`). Before the `plan-done` Event, every pending review of the Plan is closed `superseded`, reason "Plan review r<k> of Plan P is superseded: the Plan is done." The next `pr poll` cleans up the merged Workflow's worktrees. The output carries `"adopted": "merged"`. When it is `CLOSED` without a merge the command is refused `pr_closed` (reopen it on GitHub, or move the work to a new branch); when it is `OPEN`, it is adopted after the Gate and the push, as below.
- **Conflict check** (contract §7.6 step 1, hs-d490): `git -C <repo> fetch origin <base>` (no `origin`: skipped, `refs/heads/<base>` used), `B = rev-parse origin/<base>` read once, `G = rev-parse refs/heads/<lead branch>` read once, then `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only B G`; exit 1 is `base_conflict` with nothing run, pushed or written, any other failure `git_failed`. No ancestry test: a base that moved ahead is not a refusal and starts no Gate. It also applies to the adoption of an open pull request, not to a merged one. B is not fetched again after the Gate.
- **Hooks:** with `gate.pr` is `local` (contract §8.3, hs-d292), the Gate runs in the Lead worktree at G: `pre-start` (output `run/<plan>/logs/workflow-<key>.pre-start.log`), then `pre-merge` from the Workflow's policy (output `run/<plan>/logs/workflow-<key>.pre-merge.log`), with the template variable `branch` = the Lead Branch. With `ci`, none. On `gate_failed` or `gate_error` nothing is pushed, no row is written and the Workflow stays `dispatch`: the Lead appends fix Jobs to it (`job add --workflow <key>`) and runs `pr open --workflow <key>` again once they are Merged (hs-d679, hs-d680).
- **Re-read:** after the Gate the Workflow is read again; when it is no longer `dispatch` (a concurrent `pr open` opened it), the first precondition answers (`already`) and nothing is pushed.
- **git:** rule P (contract §7.4): `git -C <lead worktree> push --porcelain origin G:refs/heads/<lead branch>` (no `-u`). The Lead Branch is usually on the remote already: the Workflow's start pushed it and every merge pushed it (§7.2, §7.4, R35), so this push is normally a no-op and it pushes again what an earlier `push_failed` left behind. A rejected ref (any `!` line, rule P) when the remote tip already contains G (a merge during the Gate pushed a descendant) is a success with `pushed` false; any other git failure is `git_failed`.
- **gh:** the lookup above (`--state all --json number,url,state,createdAt`, only considering pull requests whose `createdAt` is at or after the row's `workflows.started_at`, except for an adopted Workflow); when it found an open pull request (an earlier run died before its transaction) that one is adopted; else `gh pr create --base <base> --head <lead branch> --title <title> --body <description>` (never `--draft`). When `gh pr create` fails, the `gh pr list` lookup runs again with the same filter and a pull request it finds (a concurrent `pr open` created it) is adopted; otherwise the failure stands. `<title>` is the Workflow's stored title (Title, above); `<description>` is the Workflow's stored description (§9.5a), verbatim.
- **Rows**, one transaction, with a compare-and-swap on the Workflow's `status = 'dispatch'`: the `pull_requests` row of the pull request (inserted from `gh`'s URL, `repo`, `number`, `url`, the title given to `gh`, `draft` 0, `state` `open`, `review_decision` and `checks` `none`, `mergeable` and `merge_state` `unknown`; kept as it is when the poll stored it first; hs-d96, D6), then the Workflow `status = open`, `pr_number`, `pr_url`, `pr_opened_at`, `pull_request` (the row's id). **Event** `pr-opened` `{workflow, number, url}`. When every Workflow that is not `cancelled` is now `open` or `merged` (A10), the same transaction sets `plans.phase = deploy` and appends `plan-phase` `{from: "dispatch", to: "deploy", workflows: [{key, number, url}]}` (§3.1); otherwise the Plan stays in `dispatch`.

`phase` is the Plan's phase after the command.

`sha` is G, the gated commit; `pushed` is false when the remote already had G or a descendant of it; `remote` is the remote branch's tip after the push, past G when merges that landed during the Gate were pushed (hs-d243).

```json
{"ok": true, "plan": "pay-4521", "phase": "dispatch", "workflow": {"key": "api", "status": "open", "pr": {"number": 812, "url": "https://github.com/acme/pay/pull/812", "opened_at": "…"}}, "sha": "77aa01e…", "pushed": false, "remote": "77aa01e…"}
```

A merged pull request adopted (no Gate, no push), `phase` after the transition, `workflow.status` `merged`:

```json
{"ok": true, "adopted": "merged", "plan": "pay-4521", "phase": "done", "workflow": {"key": "api", "status": "merged", "pr": {"number": 812, "url": "https://github.com/acme/pay/pull/812", "opened_at": "…"}}}
```

Idempotent: yes, as stated.

### 9.2 `pr poll`

```
cpd pr poll [--plan <id>]
```

The pull request poller (hs-d96, D8; contract §7.6): one poll of **all of the User's open pull requests**. Run by engine E5 every `pr_poll_seconds` as a subprocess, without `--plan` (§3.7), and at once when a cpd action has requested one (`run/pr-poll-now`, contract §1.4); also by a Lead, right after `pr open` or whenever it needs the current status (D12). The poll removes `run/pr-poll-now` right before it reads GitHub, so a by-hand poll serves a pending request too (contract §3.7 E5).

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--plan <id>` | adds that Plan's Workflows, each with its `pull_request` row, to the output (`--plan` or `CPD_PLAN`; neither: no `workflows` key). It does not narrow the poll: every open pull request is polled anyway. There is no `--workflow` |

| Precondition or failure | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the lock `locks/pr-poll.lock` within 60 s | `lock_timeout` | 5 |
| `--plan` names no Plan | `plan_not_found` | 4 |
| a `gh` call fails, times out (15 s each), prints an empty or non-JSON body, answers the search with `errors`, or answers the lookup with no `data`; `details` is `{argv, exit, stderr, call, transient, reason, rate_limited}`: `call` is `search` or `lookup`, `transient` is true for an HTTP 5xx (`gh`'s `HTTP 5xx` in its message), a 15 s timeout, or a cut response (`gh` exited non-zero with `unexpected end of JSON input` in its stderr and no complete stdout, hs-d354), false for everything else and `reason` is `HTTP <status>`, `timeout`, `unexpected end of JSON input` or null (contract §7.6 step 4, hs-d354); `rate_limited` is true for a RATE_LIMITED reply, which E5 handles as a pause and not as an error (contract §3.7 E5, pro-d394) | `gh_failed` | 1 |

There is no precondition on the phase: a Plan in any phase gets the poll.

**Superseded for the github Workflow (`swr-github.md`).** A pass is **one** `gh api graphql` read document (its §3): the searches, the absent-pull-request reads, the checks and feedback reads and the rate limit are selections of that one document, and the rows it writes are those of its §2 and §4. Its `gh` failures are `swr_endpoints('github')` failures (its §7). While the endpoint is paused the pass makes no call and the command answers `{"ok": true, "paused_until": <time>}`, exit 0, polling nothing. The output keys of step 7 are kept; `rate_limit` is the pass's own `rateLimit`. Steps 1, 3, 3a, 3b, 4, 5 and 8 of contract §7.6 are superseded as its §1 says.

**A transient `gh_failed`** (`details.transient` true) is still exit 1 and writes nothing (a failed deploy read, which comes after the rows, leaves them): the command never retries, waits or keeps state, so a Lead's `pr poll` by hand fails at once. The tolerance is engine E5's (contract §3.7): it logs a `watch.log` line, polls again at the next due time and raises an `error` Event only after `watch.pr_poll_transient_minutes` (default 10) of the same call failing (the cut response counts, with `reason` `unexpected end of JSON input`), keeping the first failure's time in `run/pr-poll-failing.json`. A RATE_LIMITED reply is no `error` Event: E5 pauses the polls instead (contract §3.7 E5). Every other `gh_failed` is an `error` Event at once.

**A gh call with cwd `$CPD_HOME`:** `$CPD_HOME` is not a git repository, so a gh call cpd makes there names its repo itself: in the endpoint (`repos/<owner>/<repo>/...`), in GraphQL (`repository(owner:, name:)`) or with `--repo`. A bare `gh pr ...` and the `{owner}/{repo}` placeholders (which gh fills from the cwd's git repository) fail there. The calls this covers are the poll's, the deploy read's, `workflow edit --title`'s, `workflow describe`'s (§9.5a, which takes its repo from the Workflow's row) and the team review lookup's. Calls made in a Lead worktree or a repo checkout resolve through its `origin` and may rely on it.

Effects (contract §7.6 gives the query, the mapping and the caveats):
- **Lock:** `flock` on `locks/pr-poll.lock`, held for the whole poll, so two polls never overlap.
- **gh:** one `gh api graphql` call with two searches (`is:pr is:open author:@me archived:false sort:created-asc` and `review-requested:@me is:pr is:open archived:false sort:created-asc`, the oldest 100 each; every pull request is read with its `baseRefName`, for the base follow below and, in the `author:@me` search only, with `latestOpinionatedReviews(first: 20) { nodes { state author { __typename login } } }` after `reviewDecision`, pro-d158 (the review-requested search's fields are contract §7.6 step 1's, A7, pro-d392): one point more per poll, measured 2026-10-28, unverified beyond that one measurement; contract §7.6 step 1), then, for the pull requests where at least one holds (a) the Workflow is owned and neither search listed it, (b) `authored` is 1 and the `author:@me` search did not list it, or (c) `review_requested` is 1 and the `review-requested:@me` search did not list it, the pull request not being archived (A4, pro-d392), one direct read call with one alias per pull request (hs-d565, contract §7.6 step 3). No candidate, no call. **The feedback read** (pro-d68, contract §7.6 step 3a): every pull request also reads `updatedAt` (still 1 point); for each pull request that the rule of contract §7.6 step 3a makes due (pro-d231), ONE more `gh api graphql` call reads the review threads, issue comments and reviews of all such pull requests, with `viewer { login }` and the poll stores the items (contract §2.2 "Feedback item") in `feedback` with `updated_at`. More than 100 threads, comments, reviews or comments in a thread is `gh_failed` (`details` name the Workflow and the number; nothing is written); a pull request no Plan owns is never read.
