Stdout is parsed whatever the exit code (gh exits 1 when an alias is `NOT_FOUND`). The direct read adds `viewerDidAuthor` and `viewerLatestReviewRequest { id }` (both required); answers tell what changed. **The checks read** (pro-d75, contract §7.6 step 3b): for each pull request that is owned and whose checks rollup is `failed` with `pr.feedback.checks` `any` or a non-empty resolved `pr.excused_labels` (pro-d447), or `pending` with a non-empty `pr.human_gated_contexts`, or (owned or authored) `passed` or `none` with a non-empty `pr.required_checks` of the repo's policy (contract §7.6 step 3b's three triggers, hs-d743), ONE more `gh api graphql` call reads the checks: CheckRun and StatusContext nodes, with `startedAt` and `checkSuite { workflowRun { workflow { name } } }` on a CheckRun and `createdAt` on a StatusContext (pro-d230); it applies the newest-run reduction of contract §7.6 step 3b (pro-d230: the newest run of each check wins; the reduction needs every entry, so the pagination of step 3b stays), then the per-check mapping (FAILURE, TIMED_OUT, ACTION_REQUIRED, STARTUP_FAILURE, ERROR are failing; CANCELLED is not; pending checks never fail), with the policy-hold excuse (pro-d447: on a pull request whose labels match the resolved `pr.excused_labels`, a failing `danger` counts as passed), the human-gated rule of contract §7.6 step 3b (pro-d151, pro-d153) and its required-names rule (hs-d743) and stores the result in the pull request's `checks` field (contract §7.6 step 3b, §2.2). The pending trigger makes this read every poll while the rollup stays `pending`: +1 point whatever the number of pull requests, the aliases sharing one call (unverified against the hourly budget). The same call reads the pull request's labels, `labels(first: 100) { nodes { name } }` beside `commits`, at 0 extra rate-limit points (measured, pro-d229: the query cost 1 with them), for the policy hold of contract §7.6 step 3b (pro-d216, pro-d229, pro-d447); a reply without `labels` is `gh_failed`. More than 100 contexts is `gh_failed` (details name the Workflow and the number; nothing is written); a pull request neither owned nor authored, or matching no trigger, makes no such call.
- **The deploy read** (pro-d100; contract §7.6 step 8), after the rows below are written: for each workflow a repo policy file declares in `[deploys] workflows`, `gh api "repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/workflows/<file>/runs?status=waiting&per_page=100"` and for each run of the User's (`triggering_actor.login` equal, case-insensitively, to `gh api user --jq .login`) one `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/runs/<id>/pending_deployments`; the runs with a pending deployment the User can approve are written to `run/deploy-runs.json` (contract §1.4). A failure is `gh_failed` with `call` `lookup`, exit 1, the Workflow poll's own writes standing; the failed workflow keeps its earlier runs.
- **Rows**, one transaction for every change, none when nothing changed: `pull_requests` rows inserted or updated (`changed_at` = now) when a value changed: `authored` and `review_requested` set by searches that list the Workflow (hs-d565); the direct read updates them as contract §7.6 step 3 says, and `archived` from `repository.isArchived` (A4, pro-d392). The poll does not delete rows (hs-d565): a row stays while it is in either search or a Workflow points to it; when it is in neither and no Workflow points to it, both flags 0 and no owner stays. The `authored` rows are what the Dispatch column shows (§13.2, §17); the Inbox kinds read them all (§21).
- **The containment flag** (contract §2.2 "Ready to merge", migration `20261107T1905-pr-base-contained`): in the rows transaction, for every open pull request whose `base_ref` is its `default_branch`, the poll sets and refreshes `pull_requests.base_contained` from the same fresh gh comparison the merge gate reads at merge time (commands.md §9.10): 1 when the head contains the current default-branch head (the head itself or an ancestor of it), 0 when it does not; it is refreshed again whenever the base or the head moves. A pull request whose `base_ref` is not its `default_branch` — a stacked pull request — is not subject to the rule and its flag stays NULL. A pull request whose head does not contain the current default-branch head (or whose flag is NULL or 0) is **not ready to merge**: its `pr-ready` Inbox row is never shown as `ready to merge` (contract §2.2 STATUS row 6) and offers no Merge action (§13.2).
- **Events**, in that transaction, for the Plan whose Workflow points to the pull request only: **Event** `pr-feedback` (data of contract §5.2) when the checks became `failed` (the newest-run reduction and the per-check mapping of step 3b, pro-d230: FAILURE, TIMED_OUT, ACTION_REQUIRED, STARTUP_FAILURE, ERROR; not CANCELLED or pending checks; the human-gated rule of step 3b only turns a pending check passed, and the policy-hold excuse of step 3b turns a failing `danger` on a pull request on hold passed, so it raises nothing here, pro-d447) and the Workflow's `pr.feedback.checks` is `any` (contract §8.3, hs-d292; with `none` failing checks raise nothing; a Workflow whose repo has no policy file is polled with the owner and default policy, contract §8.3 "Keys and resolution"), the review `changes_requested`, the state `closed` (from anything else, once per transition), the pull request turning ready to post (reason `ready_to_post`, pro-d225; the rule is contract §5.2), the review `approved` by a human for a posted Workflow (reason `approved`; a bot's approval never sends it, pro-d158, contract §7.6 step 2) or **`comments`** (pro-d68: the row's new `feedback` list holds an item whose `last` is the `last` of no item of the old list, a NULL old list counting as empty; items that close tell nothing; the Event's `text` states the number of new and of open comments and says `cpd pr view`; `pr.feedback.checks` does not apply to it; contract §7.6 step 6); a conflict is no longer a reason (hs-d340: it queues an `update` Job, below). A pull request that became `merged`: the Workflow `status = merged`, `merged_at`, **Event** `pr-merged` `{workflow, number, url, merged_at}` and every `draft` Job of the Workflow becomes `cancelled` in the same transaction (hs-d731: `cancel_reason` `pr merged`, one **Event** `job-cancelled` each, as `workflow cancel` does for its drafts, §9.6; contract §3.2); when every Workflow that is not `cancelled` is then `merged`, the same transaction closes every pending review of the Plan `superseded` (reason "Plan review r<k> of Plan P is superseded: the Plan is done.") and appends `plan-done` `{workflows: [{key, number, url, merged_at}]}`, once each time the Plan reaches `done`: again when a reopened Plan's last Workflow merges (§3.1, D2). The plan phase transitions to `done` after the reviews are closed. Pull requests no Plan owns get no Event, nor does one only in the review-request search: `pr-feedback` is unchanged, still only for the author's Plans.
- **The base follow** (hs-d325, hs-d326; contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows" step 8, §7.6 step 6): for a Workflow whose status is `open` and whose pull request a search lists `OPEN`, when `baseRefName` differs from the Workflow's `base`, the same transaction sets the Workflow's `base` to it and appends **Event** `workflow-base-changed` `{workflow, from, to, from_workflow, to_workflow, by: "poll", number, url}`. This is what happens when a base Workflow merges: GitHub deletes its branch and repoints the stacked pull request to `main` (or to the base Workflow's own base); the poll learns it and **cpd follows GitHub, it never retargets** (no command edits a pull request's base). The Workflow is then unstacked, or stacked on the next Workflow when the new base is that Workflow's Lead Branch (contract §2.2 "The base Workflow"). **No Gate, no draft, no `pr-feedback`, no status change**: the pull request's tree is unchanged, so a ready Workflow stays ready (hs-d326); a conflict with the new base queues an `update` Job (below), and so does the repoint itself when the old base was a base Workflow's Lead Branch and the new base is the pull request's default branch with main ahead of the Lead Branch without a conflict, `reason` `base-merged` (hs-d794, hs-n617; the bullet below). A base Workflow closed unmerged is not repointed by GitHub: nothing changes for the Workflow above it (contract §3.8 step 9). A poll that finds no base changed writes nothing for this.
- **Unstacking the Workflows stacked on a merged Workflow** (hs-d301, contract §7.6 step 6): in the transaction that records a Workflow's merge, every `waiting` or `dispatch` Workflow whose `base` is the merged Workflow's Lead Branch (any Plan) gets the merged Workflow's own `base` and one `workflow-base-changed` (`by` `poll`, `number` and `url` null) for its own Plan. No `pr-feedback`, no Gate, no start.
- **Starting the Workflows that waited for it** (A9): `pr poll` does not start a Workflow itself. Engine E7, which runs after E5 in the same tick (§3.7), starts every `waiting` Workflow whose needs are now all `merged`  and whose base Workflow, if any, is `open`, from a fresh `fetch origin <base>` (a stacked Workflow from its base Workflow's head, §9.7); when `pr poll` was run by hand, the next tick does, or the Lead runs `workflow start <key>` (§9.7).
- **A pull request closed without a merge** (A11, hs-d329): `pr-feedback` with `reasons: ["closed"]`, once; the poll never ends the Workflow: it stays `open` in cpd, every Workflow that needs it stays `waiting` and the Lead decides. A Lead may have closed it itself, to reopen it on GitHub once it is ready again (contract §7.6 "Ready, never a draft"): reopened, the same pull request is in the search again and the poll writes its row `state` `open`, with no Event for the reopening; the Workflow was `open` throughout. To give it up the Lead runs `workflow cancel <key>` (§9.6).
- **A conflict** (hs-d340, hs-d497; contract §3.7 E5, §7.6 step 6): in the same transaction, for the Workflow that is `open` and points to the pull request, when `mergeable` becomes `conflicting` (from anything else, once per transition; a moved base with no conflict, `merge_state` `behind` included, queues nothing unless the merged-base cause below applies, hs-d794, hs-n617), the row's `state` is `open`, the Plan is not archived, the Workflow's policy resolves and the Workflow has no `update` Job that is `queued` or `running`: one `update` Job is inserted, with the Event `job-added` `{kind: "update", by: "poll", reason}`, `reason` `conflict`. No `pr-feedback`, no Gate here, nothing becomes a draft (hs-d329). A pull request that is a draft anyway is only stored (`draft`, `merge_state` `draft`): no Event.
- **A merged base** (hs-d794, hs-n617; contract §3.7 E5, §3.8 "Stacked Workflows" step 8): in the same transaction, for the Workflow that is `open`, when the base follow above repointed the Workflow's `base` — the old base (`from`) was a base Workflow's Lead Branch and the new base (`to`) is the pull request's default branch, the Workflow's `pull_requests.default_branch` — and the ahead test holds, `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only origin/<default> <lead-branch>` exiting 0 (no conflict) with the default branch not an ancestor of the Lead Branch: one `update` Job is inserted as for a conflict, with the Event `job-added` `{kind: "update", by: "poll", reason}`, `reason` `base-merged`. One update Job per repoint: the same de-dup as above (the Workflow has no `update` Job that is `queued` or `running`) keeps an already queued or running update Job from duplicating, and when the default branch is contained in the Lead Branch (ancestor or equal) nothing is queued. On this cause the Job's Worker merges `origin/<default>` into the Lead Branch even without a conflict, and cpd then runs the Gate and pushes; no rebase (hs-n611 pattern, contract §7.7). No `pr-feedback`, no Gate here, nothing becomes a draft (hs-d329).
- **After a Workflow is merged or cancelled** (hs-d517, pro-d70, pro-d71): the poll records the status and cleans nothing. When the poll records a merge, the same transaction queues the Workflow's `done` Jira transition (`swr-jira.md` §7), as `cpd pr merge` does (§9.10). The Workflow's status is the queue (§3.8). `cpd janitor` (§29) removes merged and cancelled Workflows' worktrees and branches, every `watch.janitor_minutes` minutes (default 60) or by hand.

Output: `polled`, the number of distinct pull requests in either search; `changed`, one entry for each pull request whose row was inserted or updated; `base_changed`, the `{plan, workflow, from, to}` of each Workflow whose `base` followed GitHub (empty when none); `feedback`, `merged` and `done`, the `{plan, workflow}` pairs that got `pr-feedback` or `pr-merged` and the Plans that became `done` (hs-d565); `update_jobs`, the `{plan, workflow, job, reason}` of each `update` Job the poll queued, `reason` `conflict` or `base-merged` (hs-d340, hs-d794, hs-n617); `rate_limit`, the search's `cost`, `remaining` and `reset_at` (E5 reads it, §3.7); and, only with a Plan, `workflows`, one entry for each of its Workflows in key order that is not `cancelled`, with its `status` and its `pull_request` row (or null).

```json
{"ok": true, "polled": 3,
 "changed": [{"repo": "acme/pay", "number": 813, "state": "open", "draft": false, "checks": "failed", "review_decision": "none", "mergeable": "conflicting", "merge_state": "dirty"}],
 "base_changed": [{"plan": "pay-4521", "workflow": "ui", "from": "cpd/pay-4521/api", "to": "main"}],
 "feedback": [{"plan": "pay-4521", "workflow": "ui"}],
 "update_jobs": [{"plan": "pay-4521", "workflow": "ui", "job": "up-ui", "reason": "conflict"}],
 "merged": [{"plan": "pay-4521", "workflow": "api"}],
 "done": [],
 "rate_limit": {"cost": 1, "remaining": 4987, "reset_at": "2026-10-20T11:00:00Z"},
 "workflows": [{"key": "api", "status": "merged", "pull_request": {"repo": "acme/pay", "number": 812, "url": "https://github.com/acme/pay/pull/812", "title": "Retry failed payouts (api)", "draft": false, "state": "merged", "review_decision": "approved", "checks": "passed", "mergeable": "unknown", "merge_state": "unknown", "created_at": "…", "merged_at": "…"}},
         {"key": "ui", "status": "open", "pull_request": {"repo": "acme/pay", "number": 813, "url": "https://github.com/acme/pay/pull/813", "title": "Retry failed payouts (ui)", "draft": false, "state": "open", "review_decision": "none", "checks": "failed", "mergeable": "conflicting", "merge_state": "dirty", "created_at": "…", "merged_at": null}}]}
```

Idempotent: yes; the rows hold what was reported, so a rerun with no change on GitHub reports nothing new (`changed`, `base_changed`, `feedback`, `update_jobs` and `merged` empty or 0) and writes nothing.

### 9.3 `pr rebase`

```
cpd pr rebase [--workflow <key>] [--plan <id>] [--continue | --abort]
```

Rebases the Workflow's Lead Branch onto its base and pushes (§7.6); never required for a base that merely moved ahead (hs-d490), and never required for a merged base: the poll queues the Workflow's `update` Job, `reason` `base-merged`, whose Worker merges `origin/<base>` into the Lead Branch without a rebase, and cpd runs the Gate and pushes (hs-d794, hs-n617; contract §3.7 E5). **The repair**, not how fix Jobs reach an `open` Workflow (a fix Job's own merge does, contract §3.8 "Updating"): for a failed `update` Job, an engine that is down, or a conflict the Lead resolves itself. On a conflict the rebase **stays in progress in the Workflow's Lead worktree** and the command exits `rebase_conflict`; the Lead resolves the files and runs `--continue` (the rest of the rebase, the Gate and the lease push) or `--abort` (hs-d289; contract §7.6 "The conflict stop"). The Gate runs only when the Workflow's `gate.merge` is `local` (for `pr open` and `pr push`) or `gate.pr` is `local` (for `pr rebase`) (contract §8.3, hs-d292); with `ci` there is no Gate and the two Gate rows below do not apply.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--workflow <key>` | the Workflow to rebase, selected by §1.3's rule: required when the Plan has two or more Workflows that are not `cancelled`, defaulted to the one when it has one |
| `--continue` | finish the rebase stopped at a conflict, then Gate and push (below); no other flag but `--workflow`/`--plan`; not with `--abort` (`usage`, exit 2) |
| `--abort` | `git rebase --abort` in the Lead worktree: the Lead Branch back where it was |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Workflow is `open`, before the Gate and again after it | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| the Workflow is not stacked (contract §2.2 "The base Workflow"): a stacked Workflow takes its base Workflow's new commits by merge and publishes with `pr push`, never by rebase (contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows" step 4, hs-d325); checked before the `fetch`, nothing changed; `details` is `{workflow, base, base_workflow, next}`, `next` = `["git -C <lead worktree> merge --no-edit origin/<base>", "cpd pr push --workflow <key>"]` | `stacked_rebase` | 3 |
| `git merge-tree` reports no conflict and the rebase has no unexpected one; else the rebase is left **in progress** in the Lead worktree (nothing pushed, nothing else changed); `details.files` the conflicted paths, `details.worktree` its path, `details.next` the `--continue` command, `details.abort` the `--abort` command | `rebase_conflict` | 3 |
| no rebase is already in progress in the Lead worktree (a stop of an earlier run); `details.next`, `details.abort` as above | `rebase_in_progress` | 3 |
| the Lead worktree has no tracked local changes, which `git rebase` would refuse (checked only when a conflict needs the rebase there); `details.files` lists them | `lead_worktree_dirty` | 3 |
| guard U: an Attempt of the Workflow whose compare-and-swap is in the snapshot and whose driver lives ends within 60 s; `details.attempt` names it; rerun | `cas_lost` | 3 |
| the Lead Branch's compare-and-swap succeeds within 3 tries (merges kept moving it) | `cas_lost` | 3 |
| no Attempt of the Workflow of any kind (work, open, update) is running (pro-d103, pro-d105); `details` is `{workflow, jobs: [keys], attempts: [ids]}`; the message tells the Lead to message the Worker to do the rebase instead; checked before the fetch, nothing is changed | `attempt_running` | 3 |
| the Workflow's policy resolves (contract §8.3 "Validation", `details` as there): its Context has an owner | `owner_unset` | 3 |
| its owner has a policy file | `owner_unconfirmed` | 1 |
| its policy files are valid | `policy_invalid` | 1 |
| the `pre-start` passes before the Gate runs; `details.tail` is its last 60 lines, `details.log` the full log `run/<plan>/logs/workflow-<key>.pre-start.log` | `gate_error` | 1 |
| the Gate passes on the rebased Lead Branch (§7.3, contract §7.4, hs-d679); `details.tail` is its last 60 lines, `details.log` the full log | `gate_failed` | 3 |
| the Gate ran (not killed, not `hook_invalid`); `details.tail`, `details.log` as above | `gate_error` | 1 |
| the caller is not an agent, OR the incident is off, OR the resolved Workflow's Plan is not held (hs-d643): `CPD_SESSION` set and non-empty names an agent; a held Plan is in the incident; `details` is `{workflow, plan, incident}` | `incident_hold` | 3 |

The Lead worktree's local changes refuse nothing (hs-d243; `dirty_target` is no longer a refusal of this command).

Effects: no lock (hs-d243); merges into the Workflow go on during the command. §7.6 steps 1–9: `fetch origin <base>`; the snapshot `S`; `merge-tree`; a temporary rebase worktree detached at `S` for the rebase, giving `R'`; guard U (R for an Attempt of the Workflow with a dead driver whose compare-and-swap is in `S`; a wait of at most 60 s for one with a live driver); the lease `X0`, the tracking ref `refs/remotes/origin/<lead branch>` read then (what cpd last saw of the remote branch, its own pushes and those of the merges guard U waited for included, so a push cpd has not seen refuses instead of being overwritten; Escalation nl-pr-a1-q1); `update-ref -m "cpd: pr rebase <plan>/<key>" refs/heads/<lead branch> R' S`, back to the snapshot when the ref moved; rule S on the Lead worktree (a stop appends `error` `lead_worktree_stale` and does not fail the command); with `gate.pr` is `local` (contract §8.3, hs-d292) the Gate in the temporary rebase worktree, `pre-start` then `pre-merge` from the Workflow's policy (hs-d679), outputs to `run/<plan>/logs/workflow-<key>.pre-start.log` and `workflow-<key>.pre-merge.log`, then the temporary worktree removed; the Workflow re-read; `push --porcelain --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<lead branch>:<X0> origin R':refs/heads/<lead branch>`, then, when the Lead Branch moved past R' during the Gate, rule P with its tip (a failure of either push is `git_failed`, except a rejection of the first when the remote tip already contains R', which is a success: two `pr rebase` of the Workflow at once push the same R' and the second can lose the race inside the remote; Escalation nl-pr-a1-q2). On `gate_failed` or `gate_error` nothing is pushed; the rebased Lead Branch stays (the compare-and-swap moved it before the Gate) and the Lead appends fix Jobs to the Workflow, then runs `pr rebase --workflow <key>` again once they are Merged. **Rows**: none; the Ledger does not record the Lead Branch's SHA, so there is no Event. On an unexpected rebase conflict: `git rebase --abort` in the temporary worktree, which is removed, then the conflict stop below.

```json
{"ok": true, "plan": "pay-4521", "workflow": "api", "rebased": true, "old": "4b825dc…", "new": "77aa01e…", "pushed": true}
```

**An adopted Workflow** (`head_ref` set, §9.4) takes the **catch-up**: the command never rebases onto the base. It fetches `origin <head_ref>` and rebases the Lead Branch's commits that `origin/<head_ref>` lacks onto `origin/<head_ref>` (the machinery above: gate worktree, guard U, compare-and-swap of the Lead Branch, rule S, the Gate when `gate.pr` is `local`, `--continue` and `--abort`), then pushes with rule P: `git push --porcelain origin <sha>:refs/heads/<head_ref>`, no lease, no force; history stays linear and is never deleted. It is allowed in `open` and in `dispatch` once every Job of the Workflow but its `open` and `update` Jobs is `merged` or `cancelled` (`jobs_not_done` otherwise, as `pr open`). When `origin/<head_ref>` is already in the Lead Branch the outcome is `already`. The Lead runs it when an `open` or `update` Job ends `push_failed`, or when `pr open` or `pr push` is refused `push_rejected`; cpd never runs it by itself. A conflict of an adopted Workflow with its base stays the `update` Job's: its Worker merges the base (a merge commit) and cpd pushes plain.

Idempotent: yes; a base that has not moved gives `"rebased": false` and only the Gate (with `gate.pr` `local`) and the push run. A run that stops at a conflict is repeatable only through `--continue`/`--abort`: a second plain run answers `rebase_in_progress`.

**The conflict stop** (contract §7.6). On a conflict nothing is aborted: the Lead worktree holds the rebase, stopped at the first conflicting commit and the Lead Branch ref is unchanged until the rebase finishes. The error:

```json
{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "rebase_conflict", "message": "…", "details": {"files": ["src/a.rs"], "worktree": "/…/repo.pay-4521.api", "next": "cpd pr rebase --workflow api --continue", "abort": "cpd pr rebase --workflow api --abort"}}}
```

The Lead edits the files and runs `git -C <worktree> add <files>` (no `git commit`, no `git push`), then `--continue`.

### `pr rebase --continue`

Finishes the stopped rebase, then the Gate and the lease push of `pr rebase`. Order, each refusal changing nothing:

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--continue` and `--abort` together | `usage` | 2 |
| the Workflow is `open`, before the Gate and again after it | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| the Workflow's policy resolves (§8.3): `owner_unset` (3), `owner_unconfirmed` (1), `policy_invalid` (1), as above | as listed | |
| a rebase is in progress in the Lead worktree | `no_rebase_in_progress` | 3 |
| no conflict marker remains: no unmerged path, no `<<<<<<<` / `=======` / `>>>>>>>` line at column 0 in a changed file; `details.files` lists the paths, `details.next` the same command | `rebase_conflict` | 3 |
| the Lead Branch is still at the tip the rebase started from (a merge landed during the stop otherwise); `details.reason` `lead_branch_moved`, `details.tip`; the Lead runs `--abort`, then `pr rebase` | `cas_lost` | 3 |
| guard U (as above; `details.attempt`) | `cas_lost` | 3 |
| `GIT_EDITOR=true git rebase --continue` does not stop at the next conflicting commit; if it does, `details.files` are that commit's and the Lead repeats | `rebase_conflict` | 3 |
| `git rebase --continue` fails otherwise; `details.stderr`; the rebase stays in progress | `git_failed` | 1 |
| `gate_error` and `gate_failed` as the rows above; nothing is pushed, the rebased Lead Branch stays | `gate_error` / `gate_failed` | 1 / 3 |
| the push, as above: `--force-with-lease` against `X0`, `X0` read after guard U | `git_failed` | 1 |

Effects: no lock; guard U and the lease as `pr rebase` (the snapshot `S` is the tip the rebase started from, `rebase-merge/orig-head`); `GIT_EDITOR=true git -C <lead worktree> rebase --continue` (no editor; messages kept); `R'` the Lead worktree's `HEAD`; no rule S (that worktree was the one rebased); the Gate in the Lead worktree at `R'` and the push exactly as `pr rebase` (contract §7.4 R2, hs-d679), the Gate only when `gate.pr` is `local`. No `fetch`: the rebase ends on the `origin/<base>` it started from. **Rows**: none; no Event. Output as `pr rebase`, `"rebased": true`, `old` = `S`, `new` = `R'`. Idempotent: no; a second run is `no_rebase_in_progress`.

### `pr rebase --abort`

`git -C <lead worktree> rebase --abort`: the Lead Branch and the Lead worktree as before the stop. Refuses `no_rebase_in_progress` (exit 3) when none is in progress. It asks no Workflow status, runs no Gate and no `fetch`, pushes nothing, appends no Event; then rule S on the Lead worktree (a stop appends `error` `lead_worktree_stale`, never fails it). Output `{"ok": true, "plan": "pay-4521", "workflow": "api", "aborted": true, "tip": "4b825dc…"}`. Idempotent: no; a second run is `no_rebase_in_progress`.

### 9.4 `workflow add`

```
cpd workflow add <key> --repo <path> --title <text> [--jira <KEY>] [--adopt <number> [--confirm-author <login>]] [--shape <tdd|docs|config>] [--jobs <file.json>] [--base <branch> | --base <key> | --base <plan>/<key>] [--needs <r1,r2> | --no-needs] [--plan <id>]
```

Adds a Workflow to the Plan, `waiting` (R34, A13, §3.8). In `grounding` and an unlocked `plan` it is part of the plan fingerprint (§2.3), so the Plan needs a review that includes it; in `dispatch`, `deploy` and `done`, and in a re-planned `plan` (`locked_at` set, A1), it is **appended**, like `job add` and engine E7 starts it once its needs are `merged` (at once when it has none, §3.7). In `deploy`, `done` and a re-planned `plan` it also **moves the Plan back to `dispatch`** (A3, pro-d429; hs-d87: a merged Workflow can hold a bug or a regression, so a Plan takes follow-up work at any time; no Plan review of the Workflow itself, D4; the Jobs added to it as drafts are reviewed, §4.6). A follow-up Workflow is registered at once, even when it cannot run yet: `workflow add <key> --repo … --needs …`. Before the lock its template's stub drafts follow (§9.4); after the lock it takes `--jobs <file.json>`, which queues the template's Jobs (pro-d404: a Job that waits is queued with its needs, never a draft; contract §2.2 "A parked draft", rule 2). With `--adopt` it adopts an existing pull request whose head branch does not equal the stored `lead_branch` of any Workflow of that repo: cpd works it like a Plan (Jobs that address review comments and failing CI checks) and pushes to the pull request's own head branch, never a second pull request (pro-n8).

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<key>` | Workflow key (§2.1), chosen by the Lead, e.g. `schema`, `web` |
| `--repo <path>` | required: the Workflow's repo; stored as the realpath of its main worktree. Several Workflows of one Plan may share a repo. Its `origin` must be a GitHub repo of the Context's owner (below) |
| `--title <text>` | required (hs-d285): the Workflow's own title, which names its change and becomes the pull request's title and then, when the repo squash-merges, the squash commit's subject on `main`. 1–72 characters, one line, no control characters, else `usage` (§1.5). `workflow add` is the only place a Workflow is created. With `--jira` under `workflow.jira_required` and not adopted, the title must compose with the key: `<type>[!]: <summary>` gets `<KEY>/` after `<type>[!]: `, and any other title is refused `jira_title_invalid` (exit 3, nothing written, the message says to run `cpd workflow edit <key> --title "<type>: <KEY>/<summary>"`; the rule is contract §7.6 "The Jira title") |
| `--base <key>` | **stack on a Workflow**, the bare form (hs-d324, hs-d325, A1, A2): the Workflow `<key>` of this Plan in the Workflow's repo (this Plan's own included; for `workflow edit`, the new repo with `--repo`) becomes the **base Workflow** and the stored `base` is its Lead Branch, so the Workflow starts from that branch's head and its pull request targets it (contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows"). A Workflow key of the Plan in the repo wins over a branch of the same name; any other bare value is a branch name (`base_not_found`), so a bare key of a Workflow in another repo, of another Plan, or of no Workflow is a branch (contract §2.2 "A Workflow reference") |
| `--base <branch>` | the branch the pull request targets, for a value that is no Workflow of the Plan in the repo; default the repo's `origin` HEAD branch, else `main` (cpd 1 §11 `workflow init`, kept) |
| `--base <plan>/<key>` | **stack on a Workflow** (hs-d324, hs-d325): the Workflow `<key>` of Plan `<plan>` (this Plan's own included) becomes the **base Workflow** and the stored `base` is its Lead Branch, so the Workflow starts from that branch's head and its pull request targets it (contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows"). The value is a Workflow when it has the form `<plan>/<key>` and a Plan `<plan>` exists, else a branch (contract §2.2 "A Workflow reference") |
| `--needs <r1,r2>` | Workflow references (contract §2.2): keys of other Workflows of the Plan (`<plan>/<key>` of the Plan itself is read as the bare key; another Plan's is refused `workflow_other_plan`, hs-d522), that must be `merged` before this one starts, comma-separated, no duplicates (`usage`). Default: in `grounding` and `plan` none; in `dispatch` none: one flag is required (`needs_required`, pro-d46); in `deploy` or `done` every `merged` Workflow of the Plan. Within a repo, stack on the earlier Workflow with `--base <key>` instead; a need is for another repo's Workflow or a Workflow that must start from fresh `main` (contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows") |
| `--no-needs` | no needs, the way a Workflow with no needs is stated in `dispatch` when the default does not apply; exclusive with `--needs` (`usage`); in `grounding`, `plan`, `deploy` or `done` it changes the default to explicitly none |
| `--title <text>` | required (hs-d285): the Workflow's own title, which names its change and becomes the pull request's title and then, when the repo squash-merges, the squash commit's subject on `main`. 1–72 characters, one line, no control characters, else `usage` (§1.5). `workflow add` is the only place a Workflow is created. Under `--adopt` it is a local label (it names the stub Jobs): cpd never sends it to GitHub, the pull request keeps its own title, and an adopted Workflow is exempt from the Jira title rule (`jira_title_invalid`) |
| `--jira <KEY>` | optional (pro-d127, B1): the Workflow's own Jira ticket, a key matching `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$` (else `usage`, exit 2, as `context new --jira`). One ticket per Workflow: the Plan's `jira` never fills it. Set here or by `workflow edit <key> --jira <KEY>` (§9.5); needed before the Workflow opens when its owner's policy sets `workflow.jira_required` (§9.1, §5.5); under that policy the title must compose with it (`--title` above, §9.5) |
| `--adopt <number>` | adopt the existing pull request `<number>` of `--repo`'s `origin` (below). The Workflow's base is the pull request's `baseRefName` (it must exist as `origin/<base>`: `base_not_found`) and its head is `head_ref`, stored in `workflows.head_ref` |
| `--confirm-author <login>` | the pull request's author, when it is not the User (`adopt_foreign`); accepted and does nothing when the author is the User. Needs `--adopt` |
| `--base <key>` | exclusive with `--adopt`. **Stack on a Workflow**, the bare form: the Workflow `<key>` of this Plan in the repo, as in the table above (contract §2.2 "A Workflow reference") |
| `--base <branch>` | exclusive with `--adopt` (`usage`, exit 2: the base is the pull request's). The branch the pull request targets; default the repo's `origin` HEAD branch, else `main` (cpd 1 §11 `workflow init`, kept) |
| `--base <plan>/<key>` | exclusive with `--adopt`. **Stack on a Workflow** (hs-d324, hs-d325): the Workflow `<key>` of Plan `<plan>` (this Plan's own included) becomes the **base Workflow** and the stored `base` is its Lead Branch, so the Workflow starts from that branch's head and its pull request targets it (contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows"). The value is a Workflow when it has the form `<plan>/<key>` and a Plan `<plan>` exists, else a branch (contract §2.2 "A Workflow reference") |
| `--needs <r1,r2>` | Workflow references (contract §2.2): keys of other Workflows of the Plan (`<plan>/<key>` of the Plan itself is read as the bare key; another Plan's is refused `workflow_other_plan`, hs-d522), that must be `merged` before this one starts, comma-separated, no duplicates (`usage`). Default: in phase `deploy` or `done` (the reopen, hs-d118), **every `merged` Workflow of the Plan**; in other phases none. Within a repo, stack instead (`--base <key>`); a need is for another repo's Workflow or a Workflow that must start from fresh `main` (contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows") |
| `--no-needs` | no needs, also in phase `deploy` or `done`; exclusive with `--needs` (`usage`) |
| `--shape <tdd\|docs\|config>` | the template the Workflow starts with (hs-d341, contract §2.2 "Job kinds"; its stub drafts before the lock, queued with `--jobs` after it), default `tdd`: `<key>-docs` (kind `docs`), `<key>-tests` (`test`, needs `<key>-docs`), `<key>-impl` (`impl`, needs `<key>-tests`). **`docs`**: only `<key>-docs`; **`config`**: only `<key>-config`, kind `work`: a docs-only or config-only Workflow says so here and has no test Job. **Stored in `workflows.shape` and enforced** (hs-d497; contract §2.2 "Job kinds"): the kinds the Workflow may have (`shape_violation` at `job add`, `job edit --kind`) and the ones a `tdd` Workflow must keep (`shape_incomplete` at `plan review`, `plan lock` and `job cancel` typed by the Lead); never changed afterwards. `workflow cancel` of the whole Workflow is the way out and cancels the `test` and `impl` Jobs itself (§9.6, hs-d573) `workflow_exists`'s comparison includes it |
| `--jobs <file.json>` | **after the lock** (phase `dispatch`, `deploy` or `done`, or a re-planned `plan`; pro-d404, hs-d731): required for every Workflow not adopted (`--adopt`), a Workflow that waits for another Workflow included; the template's Jobs as decided work. One JSON object keyed by the template suffix (shape `tdd`: `docs`, `tests`, `impl`; `docs`: `docs`; `config`: `config`), each value `{"tier": "<T>", "spec": <the Spec object `job add --spec` takes; a test Job's has `tests` and `test_files`>}`; every key of the shape is required and no other key is allowed. Before the lock it is refused `usage` (in phase `plan` every Job is a draft). Effects in "The template" below |

|---|---|---|

| the repo is keyed from its `origin` (below); `details.url` (null when there is no `origin`) | `repo_unkeyed` | 1 |
| the repo's owner is the Context's; `details.owner` (the Context's), `details.repo_owner` | `owner_mismatch` | 3 |
| the owner has a policy file, `$CPD_HOME/policy/<owner>/owner.toml`; `details.owner` | `owner_unconfirmed` | 1 |
| the owner's and the repo's policy files are valid; `details.file`, `details.key` | `policy_invalid` | 1 |

| the base Workflow (`--base <plan>/<key>`) and every need are Workflows of the Plan, not of another Plan; `details` is `{workflow, reference, plan}` (the Workflow being added, the reference as given, the other Plan) | `workflow_other_plan` | 3 |
| the base Workflow is not `cancelled` and not `merged` (name its base branch instead); a need is not `cancelled`; `details.workflow` | `base_workflow_unavailable` (base Workflow), `needs_unavailable` (need) | 3 |
| the base Workflow of the `<plan>/<key>` form is in the same repo as this Workflow (the same realpath; a bare `--base <key>` of another repo is a branch, §2.2 "A Workflow reference"); `details` is `{workflow, repo, base_repo}` | `base_workflow_other_repo` | 3 |

| the base Workflow is not also in `--needs` (a need is merged before this Workflow starts, a base Workflow is the implied need met when it is `open`) | `usage` | 2 |
| no Workflow of the Plan has this key, `cancelled` ones included, unless its repo, base, title, shape, needs and `jira` (compared only when `--jira` is given) equal the resolved flags, the default needs included (then `already`) | `workflow_exists` | 3 |
| in phase `dispatch`, one of `--needs` or `--no-needs` is required; an existing Workflow key is compared first (`already` when the flags match, else `workflow_exists`), so a rerun is never refused (idempotence, pro-d46) | `needs_required` | 3 |

| no Workflow of the Plan has this key, `cancelled` ones included, unless its repo, base, title, shape, head_ref, needs and `jira` (compared only when `--jira` is given) equal the resolved flags, the default needs included (then `already`) | `workflow_exists` | 3 |

| no need is `cancelled`; `details.needs` lists them | `needs_unavailable` | 3 |

The five `adopt_*` rows are checked in the order above, after every other check of this command, with nothing written. `--confirm-author` without `--adopt` is `usage`.

**What `--adopt` reads** (A2), with the working directory the repo, so `gh` resolves the pull request through its `origin`: `gh pr view <number> --json number,url,state,isCrossRepository,headRefName,baseRefName,author` and `gh api user --jq .login`. The first answers `{"number":7,"url":"https://github.com/acme/pay/pull/7","state":"OPEN","isCrossRepository":false,"headRefName":"feat/x","baseRefName":"main","author":{"login":"alice"}}`. The author is the User when `author.login` equals the login of `gh api user`, compared case-insensitively (pro-n4: the User's own pull request is adopted without asking; another author's needs a warning and the User's confirmation first). A `gh` failure is `gh_failed`. The pull request's number is not stored: `pr open` finds it by head (`gh pr list --head <head_ref> --state all`, §9.1).

Any phase is allowed: `grounding`, `plan`, `dispatch`, `deploy` and `done`, so no `illegal_phase`. A new Workflow has no dependents, so it creates no cycle of its own; `dependency_cycle` is possible only through `workflow edit` (§9.5).

**The template** (hs-d341). Before the lock the shape's Jobs are **stub drafts** (§5.1: a title, no Tier and no Spec; the exception is the `open-<workflow>` Job, below, which has Tier `worker_tier` and cpd's fixed Spec from the insert): `jobs` rows with their `kind`, the titles `Docs: <Workflow title>`, `Red tests: <Workflow title>`, `Implement: <Workflow title>` and `Config: <Workflow title>`, `status = draft`, `appended` 0, no fingerprint and for `tdd` the `dependencies` rows `<key>-tests → <key>-docs` and `<key>-impl → <key>-tests`. The Lead completes each (`job edit --tier --spec`, §5.2) or cancels the ones it does not need (never, one by one, the `test` and `impl` Jobs of a `tdd` Workflow: `job cancel` is refused `shape_incomplete`; `workflow cancel` of the whole Workflow cancels them itself, §9.6, hs-d573) and adds the Workflow's other Jobs with `job add --workflow`. The engine runs nothing of them until the batch is approved (§4.6, §4.8). **After the lock** (pro-d404) the template is written only **with `--jobs`**: the non-open Jobs are written `queued`, as `job add` without `--draft` writes them (`appended` 1, Tier, Spec, fingerprint, `tests` and `test_files` of the `test` Job, the same titles and kinds and for `tdd` the same chain of `dependencies` rows), one `job-added` Event each, and the Workflow's `open` Job stays the draft it is; without `--jobs` a Workflow that is not adopted is refused `draft_parked`, waiting or not (the row above). The Workflow's `open` Job is a **draft** laid out by the template, Tier `worker_tier` (contract §8.2), no Dependencies, and a stored Spec: cpd's fixed text, written by `workflow add` when it inserts the Job and never edited (`job edit` refuses it, `job_locked`); the Lead may cancel it. Engine E4 (§3.7) is a **fallback**: when the Workflow becomes `dispatch`, if it has no `open` Job at all, E4 adds a fresh one `queued`; a `draft`, `queued`, `running`, `failed` or `cancelled` one it leaves alone and it still promotes a `draft` opener to `queued` when no other draft of its Workflow remains (contract §3.7, hs-d573).

**The repo's key** (contract §8.3, hs-d288). `workflow add` parses the repo's `origin` once, at the boundary: `git -C <repo> remote get-url origin`, which must be `https://github.com/<owner>/<name>` or `git@github.com:<owner>/<name>`, each with or without `.git`, `<owner>` and `<name>` valid by contract §2.1 (stored lowercased). Nothing else is accepted: no `origin`, another host, or an SSH host alias (`git@github-work:<work-owner>/x.git`) is `repo_unkeyed`; cpd never asks the network to resolve one. `<owner>` must be the Context's (`owner_mismatch`): one GitHub owner per Context and a Plan may span several repos of it. The Workflow stores `<name>` only; its owner is the Context's.

**Legacy Lead Branches** (superseded by pro-d112, migration `lead-branch-name`). A Workflow created before the migration keeps its stored `lead_branch` name unchanged; nothing is renamed on disk or on the remote (A3).

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: in `deploy`, `done` or a re-planned `plan`, `plans` (`phase = dispatch`, `done_at = null`, `locked_at` kept); `workflows` (`status = waiting`, `repo`, `name`, `base` (the base Workflow's `lead_branch` when stacked), `title`, `jira` (null without `--jira`), `shape`, `lead_branch = <plan>/<key>` (with `--adopt`, the local branch of the Lead worktree; and `head_ref`, the pull request's head branch, set here only: the trigger `workflows_head_ref_fixed` refuses any later change with `workflow_locked` and the partial unique index `workflows_head_ref_live` allows one live Workflow per repo and head), `created_txn`, `created_at`; `lead_worktree` null); one `workflow_needs` row per need; and the shape's template Jobs (below). **Events**, in this order: in `deploy`, `done` or a re-planned `plan`, `plan-phase` `{from: "plan"|"deploy"|"done", to: "dispatch"}`; then `workflow-added` `{workflow, repo, base, base_workflow, title, needs, appended, head_ref, author}` (`head_ref` and `author` null for a cpd Workflow), `appended` true in phases `dispatch`, `deploy` and `done`, and on a re-planned `plan`; then one `job-added` (`kind`, `status` `draft`, or `queued` with `--jobs`) per template Job. Engine E7 then starts the Workflow like any appended Workflow (at once when it has no needs). No tmux and no other git write: the Lead Branch and Lead worktree are created when the Workflow starts (§3.8, §7.2). And, when the Plan's working Lead runs it, it names the Workflow as the Lead's Workflow (§1.3).

```json
{"ok": true, "workflow": {"key": "web", "repo": "/home/clayton/projects/web", "name": "web", "base": "main", "base_workflow": null, "title": "Add the web client", "jira": null, "needs": ["api"], "status": "waiting", "lead_branch": "pay-4521/web", "head_ref": null, "appended": false, "jobs": ["web-docs", "web-tests", "web-impl"]}}
```

An adopted pull request (`--adopt 3748`): the same object with `"head_ref": "feat/EEC-3238/review-submit-polish"`, `"base": "main"`, `"lead_branch": "pay-4521/card"`; `plan show` (§4) carries `head_ref` in its Workflow objects too.

A Workflow stacked on a Workflow of its Plan, needing another (`--base pay-1/api --needs schema`): `"base": "pay-1/api", "base_workflow": "pay-1/api", "needs": ["schema"]`.

Idempotent: yes, as stated; the same flags again, `--adopt` included, are `already` (the comparison includes head_ref and `--jira` when it is given, and the title as stored: a composed title is compared composed). The comparison uses the resolved repo and base (a base Workflow by its Lead Branch) and needs (as references), so a rerun without `--base` matches a Workflow whose base was defaulted to the same branch.

### 9.5 `workflow edit`

```
cpd workflow edit <key> [--repo <path>] [--base <branch> | --base <key> | --base <plan>/<key>] [--needs <r1,r2> | --no-needs] [--title <text>] [--jira <KEY>] [--plan <id>]
```

Changes a `waiting` Workflow before the lock (A13) and, with `--title`, a Workflow's title in any phase (below). `--needs` replaces the whole list; `--no-needs` removes every need. `--base` and `--needs` take what `workflow add` takes (§9.4): a branch or, to stack, a base Workflow by its bare key `<key>` (a Workflow of the Plan in the repo) or in the form `<plan>/<key>` and Workflows of the Plan (contract §2.2 "A Workflow reference"); `--base <branch>` on a stacked Workflow unstacks it. A Workflow that another Workflow is stacked on keeps its repo: `--repo` is refused `workflow_in_use` (`details.workflows`), because the stacking is derived from the repo and the base and a change would silently unstack the Workflow above it (hs-d324). The Workflow's Jobs stay with it. A changed `--repo` keeps the stored base unless `--base` is given and that base must exist in the new repo; the new repo's `origin` is parsed as `workflow add` parses it (§9.4 "The repo's key") and replaces `name`. After the lock, the link (`--needs` and `--base`) changes only by the restack or the retarget (below) and is otherwise stated at `workflow add` with a required flag (pro-d46, §2.2).

Changes a `waiting` Workflow before the lock (A13) and, with `--title`, a Workflow's title in any phase (below). `--needs` replaces the whole list; `--no-needs` removes every need. `--base` and `--needs` take what `workflow add` takes (§9.4): a branch or, to stack, a base Workflow by its bare key `<key>` (a Workflow of the Plan in the repo) or in the form `<plan>/<key>` and Workflows of the Plan (contract §2.2 "A Workflow reference"); `--base <branch>` on a stacked Workflow unstacks it. An **adopted** Workflow (`head_ref` set, §9.4) takes its repo and its base from the pull request: `--repo` or `--base` is refused `workflow_adopted` (`details` is `{workflow, flag}`), checked first. A Workflow that another Workflow is stacked on keeps its repo: `--repo` is refused `workflow_in_use` (`details.workflows`), because the stacking is derived from the repo and the base and a change would silently unstack the Workflow above it (hs-d324). The Workflow's Jobs stay with it. A changed `--repo` keeps the stored base unless `--base` is given and that base must exist in the new repo; the new repo's `origin` is parsed as `workflow add` parses it (§9.4 "The repo's key") and replaces `name`. `workflow edit` writes no Job row and changes no open or update Job's stored Spec: the Worker is told the live base, read from the Workflow row at A3 (contract §3.4).

Changes a `waiting` Workflow before the lock (A13) and, with `--title`, a Workflow's title in any phase (below). `--needs` replaces the whole list; `--no-needs` removes every need. The Workflow's Jobs stay with it. A changed `--repo` keeps the stored base unless `--base` is given and that base must exist in the new repo; the new repo's `origin` is parsed as `workflow add` parses it (§9.4 "The repo's key") and replaces `name`.

**After the lock, the restack** (contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows" step 10; User, 2026-10-28 EDT): `cpd workflow edit <key> --base <A> --needs <rest>` or `cpd workflow edit <key> --base <A> --no-needs` restacks a `waiting` Workflow onto `<A>`, the one link edit the lock allows. `<A>` is read as `--base` is (contract §2.2 "A Workflow reference": a bare `<key>` or `<plan>/<key>`). It is allowed when the Workflow is `waiting` and not adopted; `--repo` is not given; `<A>` is a Workflow of the same Plan and repo that is not `cancelled` and not `merged` and the graph stays acyclic (the refusals of §2.2 "Validation of a reference", as before the lock); `<A>` is one of the Workflow's current needs or already its base Workflow; and the Workflow's needs after the edit are exactly its current needs without `<A>` (so `--no-needs` only when no need other than `<A>` is left). The result: `base` is `<A>`'s Lead Branch, the need on `<A>` is gone and the Event is `workflow-edited` with `fields` `["base","needs"]` (the fields that changed). Run again it is `already` (exit 0, nothing written). `--title` and `--jira` combine with a restack. Every other `--repo`, `--base`, `--needs` or `--no-needs` after the lock is refused `workflow_locked`, the retarget excepted, and so is any such flag on a Workflow that is not `waiting`; `--base <A>` alone is `workflow_locked` too. The table below gives the codes.

**After the lock, the retarget** (pro-d379, extending pro-d375; User, 2026-11-03): `cpd workflow edit <key> --base <branch>`, where `<branch>` is a plain branch and not a Workflow reference (`<key>` or `<plan>/<key>`), with no `--repo`, `--needs` or `--no-needs`, sets the Workflow's `base` to `<branch>` on a `waiting` or a `dispatch` Workflow that is not adopted. `<branch>` must exist as `origin/<branch>` (`base_not_found`, as for `workflow add`). Nothing else changes: no need is added or removed, no Job, branch or worktree is touched, and no GitHub state changes (a `dispatch` Workflow has no pull request). It exists for a `dispatch` Workflow whose external base branch was merged or deleted on origin: it can retarget (for example to `main`) before its pull request opens. On a stacked Workflow the same flag also unstacks it, as `--base <branch>` does before the lock: the implied need on its base Workflow goes with the stacking, so the Workflow may then start without waiting for that base Workflow. A Workflow reference as `--base` after the lock stays the restack of a `waiting` Workflow, as above. Its event is `workflow-edited` with `fields` `["base"]`, and its refusals are the restack's codes in the table below.

`--title <text>` (hs-d285) works in **every phase and every Workflow status but `merged` and `cancelled`** (a Workflow that is over; `cancelled` is the Workflow status that stands for a closed Workflow, §3.8): 1–72 characters, one line, no control characters, else `usage` (§1.5). The title is **not a Locked field**: it is outside the plan fingerprint (§2.3) and `workflows_locked`'s columns (§4.4), so editing it never invalidates a review or a lock and the phase and status rules below (`workflow_locked`, `illegal_transition`) apply to the other flags only. A `merged` or `cancelled` Workflow's title is history: `workflow_ended`. When the Workflow has an **open** pull request, the command also retitles it on GitHub, through the seam of §9.1, with `gh api -X PATCH repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n> -f title=<text>`. It must **not** use `gh pr edit`: on 2026-10-19 that fails on this repo with "Projects (classic) is being deprecated … (repository.pullRequest.projectCards)", while the `gh api` PATCH works (both verified on #99). `workflow describe` (§9.5a) does not use it either. A failing GitHub update is `gh_failed` and leaves the stored title unchanged. Under `workflow.jira_required` with a stored `jira`, and not adopted, the new title must compose with that key ("The Jira title", contract §7.6): a title in the form `<type>[!]: <summary>` gets `<KEY>/` inserted after `<type>[!]: `, and the composed title is what is stored and retitled. A title with no valid type, an empty summary, another key leading its summary, or more than 72 characters after composition is refused `jira_title_invalid` (exit 3) and nothing changes.

`--jira <KEY>` (pro-d127, B1) calls `adopt_ticket`, which re-enqueues the Workflow's ticketless Jira rows and also enqueues the target of its status (`merged` `done`, `open` `in_review`, `dispatch` with a started Job `in_progress`; a covered target is not enqueued again; `swr-jira.md` §7, pro-d454). It works in the same phases and Workflow statuses as `--title`: **every phase and every Workflow status but `merged` and `cancelled`** (`workflow_ended`), an adopted Workflow included. The key matches `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$` (the boundary type `Jira`, as `context new --jira`), else `usage` (§1.5). The ticket is **not a Locked field**: it is outside the plan fingerprint (§2.3) and `workflows_locked`'s columns (§4.4), so setting it never invalidates a review or a lock. The same key again is `already`, with no transaction and no Event; a different key replaces the stored one; no flag clears it. The Plan's own `jira` never fills a Workflow's ticket: one ticket per Workflow and `cpd workflow edit <key> --jira <KEY>` gives each Workflow its own. It changes no GitHub state, except the retitle of a composed title (below). A Workflow whose owner's policy sets `workflow.jira_required` (`cpd policy show --workflow <key>`) cannot open without a ticket (`jira_required`, §9.1, §5.5). Under that policy, and not adopted, its stored title is composed with the key, `--jira` alone included ("The Jira title", contract §7.6): a title in the form `<type>[!]: <summary>` gets `<KEY>/`; a title that already holds another key, or has no valid type, is refused `jira_title_invalid` (exit 3, nothing written), and the Lead edits the title too: `cpd workflow edit <key> --title "<type>: <KEY>/<summary>"`. With an open pull request the composed title is retitled on GitHub as `--title` does (`gh_failed`: nothing changes).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| at least one field flag; the message names the flags, `--jira` among them | `nothing_to_edit` | 2 |
| the Workflow is not adopted when `--repo` or `--base` is given; `details` is `{workflow, flag}` | `workflow_adopted` | 3 |
| with `--title` or `--jira`, the Workflow is not `merged` or `cancelled` | `workflow_ended` | 3 |
| under `workflow.jira_required` with a stored `jira`, not adopted: the title (given or stored) does not compose with the key (`--title` and `--jira` above; contract §7.6 "The Jira title") | `jira_title_invalid` | 3 |
| for the flags other than `--title` and `--jira`: the phase is `grounding` or `plan`; after the lock a Workflow is Locked (§4.4 `workflows_locked`) except for the restack and the retarget (below); a restack needs a `waiting` Workflow that is not adopted and no `--repo`; a retarget needs a `waiting` or `dispatch` Workflow that is not adopted, a plain branch as `--base`, and no `--repo`, `--needs` or `--no-needs` | `workflow_locked` | 3 |
| after the lock, a Workflow reference as `--base` without `--needs` or `--no-needs`; `--base <branch>` with `--needs` or `--no-needs`; `--needs` or `--no-needs` without `--base`; a Workflow reference as `--base` on a `dispatch` Workflow; or a restack whose `<A>` is not one of the Workflow's current needs or its base Workflow, or whose needs after the edit are not exactly its current needs without `<A>` | `workflow_locked` | 3 |
| for the flags other than `--title` and `--jira`: the Workflow is `waiting` (a `cancelled` one is terminal); `dispatch` is also allowed for the retarget (`--base <branch>` alone after the lock) | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| `--repo` is inside a git repository | `not_a_git_repo` | 3 |
| with `--repo`: the new repo is keyed from its `origin`, as for `workflow add` (§9.4) | `repo_unkeyed` | 1 |
| with `--repo`: the new repo's owner is the Context's, as for `workflow add` | `owner_mismatch` | 3 |
| the base exists in the Workflow's repo (the new one with `--repo`), as for `workflow add` | `base_not_found` | 4 |
| a base Workflow, as for `workflow add`: `base_workflow_unknown`, `workflow_other_plan`, `base_workflow_unavailable`, `base_workflow_other_repo` (against the new repo with `--repo`), `archived` (§9.4) | as there | 3 |
| every need is a Workflow (of the Plan, or of another by its reference), other than this one | `needs_unknown` | 3 |
| no need is `cancelled` | `needs_unavailable` | 3 |
| the graph of Workflow needs and base Workflows stays acyclic across every Plan; `details.cycle` lists the references | `dependency_cycle` | 3 |
| with `--repo`: no Workflow of the Plan is stacked on this Workflow (it has no dependents by base); `details.workflows` lists them | `workflow_in_use` | 3 |
| with `--repo`: the Workflow's Lead Branch and its parent path do not exist in the new repo | `branch_exists` | 3 |
| with `--title` and an open pull request: the `gh api -X PATCH` succeeds; `details` is `{argv, exit, stderr}` | `gh_failed` | 1 |

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: the changed `workflows` columns (`name` with `repo`; `base`, a base Workflow's Lead Branch when stacked; `title`; `jira`); `workflow_needs` rows deleted and inserted to match (§4.4 allows deletion in `grounding` and `plan` and after the lock only of the need that is the base Workflow of the restack, §3.8 step 10). **Event** `workflow-edited` `{workflow, fields: [name]}`, listing only the fields whose value changed (`repo`, `base`, `needs`, `title`, `jira`). The plan fingerprint changes with `repo`, `base` and `needs`, never with `title` or `jira` (§2.3). With `--title` and an open pull request, the GitHub update runs before the transaction and a failure writes nothing. And, when the Plan's working Lead runs it, it names the Workflow as the Lead's Workflow (§1.3).

```json
{"ok": true, "workflow": {"key": "web", "status": "waiting"}, "fields": ["base", "needs"]}
```

Idempotent: yes; when no value changes it writes nothing and returns `"already": true`.

### 9.5a `workflow describe`

```
cpd workflow describe <key> --file <path> [--plan <id>]
```

Stores the Workflow's description, verbatim, which becomes the pull request body (the description is required before `pr open`). The `--file` argument is a filesystem path or `-` for stdin; the file must be readable UTF-8, else `file_unreadable` (exit 2). The description is stored non-empty after trimming and at most 65536 characters; else `description_invalid` (exit 3). The command is allowed in **every phase and every Workflow status but `merged` and `cancelled`** (a Workflow that is over; like `workflow edit --title`, §9.5). When the Workflow has an **open** pull request, the command also updates it on GitHub first, with `gh api -X PATCH repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n> --input -`, the JSON `{"body": <the description>}` on stdin. `<owner>/<repo>` is `pull_requests.repo` of the Workflow's open pull request, never the cwd: the command runs with cwd `$CPD_HOME`, which is not a git repository (§9.2, the rule on a gh call with cwd `$CPD_HOME`). A repo that is not `owner/name` (each part only `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`) is `gh_failed` and nothing is sent. It must not use `gh pr edit`, for the reason §9.5 gives for `--title`. A failing GitHub update is `gh_failed` and leaves the stored description unchanged. An **adopted** Workflow (`head_ref` set, §9.4) is refused `workflow_adopted` (exit 3; its pull request's body is the Lead's to fill, so `describe` on it is disallowed), checked first. The Workflow's open Job does not start until the description is stored.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Workflow is not `merged` or `cancelled` | `workflow_ended` | 3 |
| the Workflow is not adopted when it has an open pull request; `details.workflow` | `workflow_adopted` | 3 |
| `--file` is readable UTF-8 | `file_unreadable` | 2 |
| the description, trimmed, is non-empty and at most 65536 characters | `description_invalid` | 3 |
| with an open pull request: the `gh api -X PATCH repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n> --input -` call succeeds; `details` is `{argv, exit, stderr}` | `gh_failed` | 1 |
| with an open pull request: `pull_requests.repo` is not `owner/name`; nothing is sent; `details` is `{repo}` | `gh_failed` | 1 |

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: the Workflow's stored `description` column (inserted or updated, the description verbatim). **Event** `workflow-described` `{workflow}` only when the description changed (idempotent). With an open pull request, the GitHub update is the `describe` op's drain (swr-github §9): the command enqueues it and returns `{queued, mutation_id}`; the rows above are written when the command runs, and a failed drain is a `failed` mutation with an `error` Event, not a refusal. And, when the Plan's working Lead runs it, it names the Workflow as the Lead's Workflow (§1.3).

```json
{"ok": true, "workflow": {"key": "api", "status": "dispatch"}}
```

Idempotent: yes; when the description is unchanged it returns `"already": true` and writes nothing.

### 9.6 `workflow cancel`

```
cpd workflow cancel <key> [--superseded-by <plan>/<key>] [--plan <id>]
```

`--superseded-by <ref>`: the Workflow is `dispatch` and its work was carried by another Workflow, `<ref>` (`<plan>/<key>`, or a bare `<key>` of the Plan); its `merged` Jobs no longer hold it (hs-d301, contract §3.8 "Ending a `dispatch` Workflow whose work was superseded").

Three uses (contract §3.8) and a fourth with `--superseded-by`. Before the lock it removes a `waiting` Workflow from the Plan: `waiting → cancelled` (A13). After the lock it ends a started Workflow with nothing left to do, `dispatch → cancelled`, so a Workflow whose Jobs were all cancelled, or that never had one, cannot keep the Plan out of `done` (hs-n271); and an **`open`** Workflow whose pull request was closed on GitHub without a merge, `open → cancelled` (hs-d329). The Workflow keeps its key either way, so `workflow add` cannot reuse it. Locked Jobs are never edited or deleted: only the Workflow's status moves. The Workflow's `draft`, `queued` and `failed` Jobs, of every kind, go with it (below, hs-d573), so they need not be cancelled first; for a `waiting` Workflow the needs on it still have to go (`workflow edit`). `workflow cancel` is never refused by the shape check: the last `test` and `impl` Jobs of a `tdd` Workflow are cancelled with it, which is how a `tdd` Workflow left in draft is removed (hs-n421, hs-d573); and after it no Job of the Workflow is `queued` or `running`, so `plan archive` is not blocked by it. The status decides the path; a `cancelled` Workflow is `already` in any phase; a `merged` Workflow is refused. A **closed-unmerged** Workflow (contract §3.8) shows in the Inbox (`pr-closed`), in `plan show` (`closed_unmerged`), in the Lead's turn-start line and in one wake, until it is cancelled or its pull request is reopened or merged; cpd never cancels it itself, and this command is how it is given up. A `cancelled` Workflow whose pull request GitHub reopens comes back to `open` (§9.1, "A cancelled Workflow whose pull request is reopened"; contract §3.8, pro-d362), and its kept pull request identity is what `workflow cancel` leaves on it (below).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Workflow is `open`, `dispatch`, `waiting` or `cancelled` (`cancelled`: `already`, in any phase; `merged`: `illegal_transition`); a `dispatch` Workflow only after the lock; an `open` Workflow is in phase `dispatch` or `deploy` | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| `--superseded-by` on a Workflow that is not `dispatch` (`cancelled`: `already`), or naming a superseding Workflow that is `cancelled` | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| `--superseded-by` names a Workflow that is not in any Plan (`details.plan`, `details.workflow`) | `workflow_not_found` | 4 |
| `--superseded-by` names a Workflow that is not of a Plan of this Context | `workflow_not_found` | 4 |
| `--superseded-by` names the Workflow itself | `usage` | 2 |
| **`waiting`, `dispatch`**: no Job of the Workflow is `running` and none is `merged` unless `--superseded-by` is given (with it `merged` Jobs are work another Workflow carried and do not hold it); a `draft`, `queued` or `failed` Job, of any kind, never holds it: this command cancels it (below, hs-d573). And no Workflow that is not `cancelled`, of any Plan, needs it or is stacked on it (contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows"); `details.jobs` lists the holding Jobs and `details.workflows` the Workflows, as references (`<plan>/<key>` for another Plan's) | `workflow_in_use` | 3 |
| **`open`**: the Workflow's `pull_requests` row is `state = closed`, as the last poll stored it (no `gh` call: run `pr poll` first); `details` is `{workflow, number, url, state}` | `pr_not_closed` | 3 |
| **`open`**: no Workflow of the Plan that is not `cancelled` needs it or is stacked on it (its Jobs are not checked: a `draft`, `queued` or `failed` Job never holds it and it is cancelled by this command, below; hs-d573); `details.workflows` lists the Workflows as references | `workflow_in_use` | 3 |
| **`open`**: the Workflow is still `open` at the transaction | `cas_lost` | 3 |

Every check runs before the first write: a refused `workflow cancel` writes nothing (hs-d573).

Effects, **`waiting`** and **`dispatch`**: **rows**, one transaction: the Workflow `status = cancelled` and every Job of the Workflow whose status is `draft`, `queued` or `failed`, of every kind (`docs`, `test`, `impl`, `work`, `open`, `update`), cancelled in that transaction with `status = cancelled`, the constant reason `workflow cancelled` (also with `--superseded-by`), `failed_cause` cleared and `cancel_requested_at` set (one `job-cancelled` each; a Job already `cancelled` is untouched and gets no Event; one that is `running` is a live Job and refuses `workflow_in_use`; contract §3.8, hs-d573); a `dispatch` Workflow also loses its `lead_worktree` (the Lead worktree) and `started_at` (the table allows neither on a `cancelled` Workflow). **Worktrees and branches are removed by the next `cpd janitor` pass** (every `watch.janitor_minutes` minutes, default 60, or by hand, §29; pro-d70, pro-d71: idle check, dirty or unpushed kept untouched with one `cleanup_failed` Event from the first janitor pass that sees it, later passes retry silently). **Event** `workflow-cancelled` `{workflow}` and `superseded_by` (the superseding Workflow as a reference: the bare key in the Plan itself, else `<plan>/<key>`) with `--superseded-by`. Before the lock the plan fingerprint changes (§2.3: it covers the Workflows that are not `cancelled`). After the lock, when no Workflow of the Plan is left `waiting` or `dispatch` and one is not `cancelled`, the same transaction moves the Plan as `pr open` and the poll do: `dispatch → deploy` with `plan-phase` and `deploy → done` with `plan-done` when every Workflow left is `merged` and the done guard holds (§3.1: no Job of the Plan is non-final); the output then has `phase`. A Plan whose Workflows are all `cancelled` stays in `dispatch`. And, when the Plan's working Lead runs it, it names the Workflow as the Lead's Workflow (§1.3).

Effects, **`open`** (contract §3.8): **rows**, one transaction: the Workflow `status = cancelled` (and its `draft`, `queued` and `failed` Jobs, cancelled as above, in the same transaction; hs-d573), with `lead_worktree` (the Lead worktree) and `started_at` set to null. `pr_number`, `pr_url`, `pr_opened_at` and `pull_request` are **kept** (pro-d362, A1): the Workflow stays bound to its pull request, so when GitHub reopens it, `pr open --workflow <key>` (§9.1) or the poll brings it back to `open`. The old `lead_worktree` and `started_at` stay in the history rows. **Events** `workflow-cancelled` `{workflow}`, its `text` naming the pull request, the Lead worktree and the Lead Branch, which the next `cpd janitor` pass removes unless the worktree is dirty or unpushed (§29); then, when every Workflow that is not `cancelled` is now `merged` and at least one is, and the done guard holds (§3.1: no Job of the Plan is non-final), the Plan `deploy → done` with `done_at` and `plan-done`; otherwise the phase stays. The plan fingerprint does not change after the lock (§2.3). The output also carries `phase` and `released`, `{number, url, lead_worktree, lead_branch}` as they were. And, when the Plan's working Lead runs it, it names the Workflow as the Lead's Workflow (§1.3).

```json
{"ok": true, "workflow": {"key": "web", "status": "cancelled"}, "phase": "done"}
```

`phase` is present only when the Plan moved.

An `open` Workflow given up, `phase` after the command:

```json
{"ok": true, "workflow": {"key": "api", "status": "cancelled"}, "phase": "deploy", "released": {"number": 116, "url": "https://github.com/acme/pay/pull/116", "lead_worktree": "/home/me/projects/pay.pay-4521.api", "lead_branch": "pay-4521/api"}}
```

Idempotent: yes, as stated.

### 9.7 `workflow start`

```
cpd workflow start <key> [--plan <id>]
```

Starts a `waiting` Workflow whose needs are all `merged` and whose base Workflow, if it has one, is `open` (A9, §3.8, hs-d324): the Lead's retry after engine E7 failed to start it (the `error` Event with code `workflow_start_failed`), once the cause is fixed. It does what E7 does.

**An adopted Workflow** (`head_ref` set, §9.4; the same for E7 and `plan lock`'s start): the Lead worktree path is as always; `git fetch origin <head_ref>` runs (a failure is `workflow_start_failed` with `step` `remote`) and the local branch `<plan>/<key>` is cut from `origin/<head_ref>`. There is no conflict check against the base (a conflict with the base is the `update` Job's), nothing is pushed at the start and the User's own local branch of the head's name is never read or touched.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the phase is `dispatch` | `illegal_phase` | 3 |
| the Workflow is `waiting` (`dispatch`, `open` or `merged`: `already`; `cancelled`) | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| every need is `merged` (`details.needs` lists those that are not, as keys) and the base Workflow, if the Workflow is stacked, is `open` (`details.base_workflow` is its reference when it has not opened); a `merged` base Workflow is not a refusal: the Workflow is unstacked first (below) | `workflow_not_ready` | 3 |
| its Lead worktree path does not exist, except a leftover of an interrupted start (a worktree of the Workflow's repo on its Lead Branch), which is removed first | `worktree_exists` | 3 |
| its Lead Branch and its parent path do not exist in its repo, except a leftover of an interrupted start (§2.1) | `branch_exists` | 3 |
| `origin/<lead branch>` does not exist, or it does not conflict with `origin/<base>` (§7.2, hs-d490) | `branch_exists` | 3 |
| the worktree, the remote check and `pre-start` succeeded; `details` is `{workflow, step, tail?, log?}`, as in `workflow_start_failed` | `setup_failed` | 1 |

Effects (§3.8 "The start", §7.2):
- **Unstack** (contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows" step 7, hs-d301): when the Workflow's base Workflow is `merged`, a first transaction sets the Workflow's `base` to the base Workflow's own `base` (a chain of merged base Workflows is walked to its end, one `workflow-base-changed` per step) and appends `workflow-base-changed` with `by` `workflow start` (E7 does the same with `by` `engine`; the poll with `by` `poll` when it recorded the merge), before the start's checks, then the start goes on with the new base (the start point is `origin/<new base>`, never the merged Workflow's deleted branch). This is also why `workflow_not_ready` is never about a `merged` base Workflow.
- **git**, in the Workflow's repo: `fetch origin <base>` (fresh, so the Workflow contains what its needs merged; for a **stacked** Workflow, `<base>` is its base Workflow's Lead Branch, fetched only when it is on the remote and the Lead Branch is created from the base Workflow's Lead Branch **head**, the local branch, not from `origin/<default branch>`, contract §7.2), the remote check and the reuse or creation of its Lead worktree exactly as `plan lock` (§4.8) does for one Workflow, then `pre-start` in the new Lead worktree, output in `run/<plan>/logs/lead-<key>.pre-start.log`; on failure the worktree and branch are removed, nothing in the database changes (`start_failed_at` keeps its value) and the result is `setup_failed`. After `pre-start` passed, a new Lead Branch is pushed (`push origin <lead branch>`, no `-u`; the worktree is added with `--no-track`, hs-d243); a failed push does not fail the start: one `error` Event with code `push_failed` and `details.workflow`.
- **Rows**, one transaction, with a compare-and-swap on `status = 'waiting'`: `status = dispatch`, `lead_worktree` (the Lead worktree), `started_at`, `start_failed_at = null`. **Event** `workflow-started` `{workflow, repo, base, lead_branch, lead_worktree, base_sha, reused, pushed, by: "workflow start"}`. The Workflow's `queued` Jobs are now Ready (§3.2) and engine E3 schedules them.

```json
{"ok": true, "workflow": {"key": "ui", "status": "dispatch", "lead_branch": "pay-4521/ui", "lead_worktree": "/home/clayton/projects/pay.pay-4521.ui", "base_sha": "9c1e7a2…", "reused": false, "pushed": true}}
```

Idempotent: yes, as stated; a Workflow that E7 started meanwhile returns `"already": true`.

### 9.8 `pr view`

```
cpd pr view [--workflow <key>] [--plan <id>]
```

The detail behind a `pr-feedback` (hs-d98, D10; contract §7.6): the checks, reviews and comments of one Workflow's pull request, which the poller does not store. Read-only.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--workflow <key>` | the Workflow to view, selected by §1.3's rule (omitted: the Plan's one Workflow that is not `cancelled`) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Workflow is `open` or `merged` (`waiting`, `dispatch` or `cancelled`: it has no pull request), as `pr rebase` | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| the Workflow's policy resolves (contract §8.3 "Validation", as `pr post`, §9.8b): its Context has an owner | `owner_unset` | 3 |
| its owner has a policy file | `owner_unconfirmed` | 1 |
| its policy files are valid (`details` as in §8.3) | `policy_invalid` | 1 |
| *(superseded, swr-github §6: no call is made, so no `gh` call fails)* | — | — |

Effects: **none**. **Superseded (swr-github §3, §6):** `pr view` makes no `gh` call and reads the cache: the effective row of `swr::github::effective_pr` and its `swr_pr_detail`. Its `checks` list is the head's check contexts of the detail, each with its conclusion unmodified; `reviews` is the detail's `latestReviews`; `comments` its issue comments; `inline_comments` the comments of its review threads. It writes nothing and appends no Event. Until the first hydrate of the pull request, `detail` is `null` and the lists are empty (swr-github §3.2).

Output: `plan`; `pr`, the Workflow (`head_oid` is new: the pull request's head at the last pass, swr-github §2)'s `key`, `number`, `url`, `title`, `jira` (the Workflow's Jira ticket, the key or null: pro-d127, B2), `base` (the pull request's base branch on GitHub, `baseRefName`), `base_workflow` (the base Workflow as `<plan>/<key>`, derived from the Workflow's stored `base`, or null: it differs from `base` only until the poll has followed a repoint, contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows" step 8), `state` (`open`, `closed` or `merged`), `review_decision` (`none`, `approved` or `changes_requested`; `approved` only on a human's approval in `reviews`, the rule of contract §7.6 step 2 and `pr view` knows a bot by its login alone, the `[bot]` suffix or `inbox.bot_reviewers`, because `gh pr view --json reviews` carries no actor type: a bot outside that list can show `approved` here while the poll stores `none`) and `checks` (`none`, `passed`, `pending` or `failed`; the newest-run reduction of contract §7.6 step 3b (pro-d230), then its per-check mapping: FAILURE, TIMED_OUT, ACTION_REQUIRED, STARTUP_FAILURE, ERROR are failing; CANCELLED is not; pending checks never fail; the summary applies the human-gated rule and the required-names rule of contract §7.6 step 3b with the Workflow's resolved `pr.human_gated_contexts` and `pr.required_checks` (hs-d743) and `pr view` resolves the Workflow's policy and refuses `owner_unset`, `owner_unconfirmed` and `policy_invalid` as `pr post` does, §9.8b); `checks`, one entry for each run of each check, `{name, conclusion, url?}`, every entry `gh pr view` lists, superseded ones included (pro-d230), with their conclusions unmodified (the reduction and the mapping apply to the summary only); `reviews`, `{id, author, state, body}`; `comments`, `{id, author, body}`; `inline_comments`, the pull request's review comments, `{id, author, path, body}`; `feedback` (pro-d68), the row's stored list of open feedback items (contract §2.2 "Feedback item"; null when the poll never read it), which is what `pr reply --to` names; and `post` (pro-d65, contract §2.2), null for an unposted Workflow, else `{channel, ts, link, posted_at, reaction, reacted_at, refusal}`; `reacted_at` and `refusal` are read from the queue row of (post channel, post ts, post emoji); `reacted_at` is null until the reaction succeeds, `refusal` is null until the reaction is refused (parking the row) and both are never set together. `reviews`, `comments` and `inline_comments` are as before and list everything, a bot's included.

```json
{"ok": true, "plan": "pay-4521",
 "pr": {"key": "ui", "number": 813, "url": "https://github.com/acme/pay/pull/813", "title": "Retry failed payouts (ui)", "jira": "PAY-813", "base": "main", "base_workflow": null, "state": "open", "review_decision": "changes_requested", "checks": "failed"},
 "checks": [{"name": "ci/test", "conclusion": "FAILURE", "url": "https://github.com/acme/pay/actions/runs/1"}, {"name": "ci/lint", "conclusion": "SUCCESS"}],
 "reviews": [{"id": "PRR_kwDO…", "author": "reviewer", "state": "CHANGES_REQUESTED", "body": "Please add a test."}],
 "comments": [{"id": "IC_kwDO…", "author": "reviewer", "body": "Thanks for the fix."}],
 "inline_comments": [{"id": "1893", "author": "reviewer", "path": "src/payout.rs", "body": "This retry never backs off."}],
 "post": null}
```

Idempotent: yes (a read).

### 9.8a `pr reply`

```
cpd pr reply --workflow <key> --to <item-id> (--body <text> | --body-file <path>) [--plan <id>]
```

Answers one feedback item (contract §2.2 "Feedback item"; pro-d68, Plan fb-path). **Callers:** Lead; not cockpit, not internal (§2). **Approval (pro-d451):** when `$CPD_SESSION` is set and non-empty and the resolved policy has `pr.feedback.reply = bots_only` (contract §8.3), a reply to any item except a bot review thread (`item.bot` true and `kind` `thread`) is refused `approval_required` unless the Session holds a live approval for that Workflow and item (§9.8d). Replies to bot threads, every reply under `pr.feedback.reply = all` (the default) and every call without `$CPD_SESSION` are unchanged. The Lead fixes each open item or decides not to and answers it either way, saying what it did or why not. It **never resolves a thread** (no flag, no `resolveReviewThread`): the reviewer does.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--workflow <key>` | the Workflow, selected by §1.3's rule |
| `--to <item-id>` | the `id` of an item in the Workflow's stored `feedback` list (`pr view` prints it) |
| `--body <text>`, `--body-file <path>` | the reply; exactly one of them |

| Precondition or failure | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| not exactly one of `--body` and `--body-file`, or the body empty after trimming | `usage` | 2 |
| `--body-file` unreadable | `file_unreadable` | 2 |
