| the Workflow is not `open` (`details` `{workflow, status}`) | `workflow_not_open` | 3 |
| `--to` is the `id` of no item in the Workflow's stored list (`details` `{workflow, to, open: [ids]}`); nothing is posted | `feedback_not_found` | 3 |
| `$CPD_SESSION` is set, `pr.feedback.reply = bots_only`, the item is not a bot review thread and the Session holds no live approval for the Workflow and item (§9.8d); checked after `feedback_not_found` (it needs the item) and before the mutation is written (`details` `{workflow, to, kind: "reply"}`); nothing is posted | `approval_required` | 3 |
| the `gh` call fails (§1.3) | `gh_failed` | 1 |

Effects: **enqueue** (swr-github §9, A6), not a call. The command writes one `swr_mutations` row, op `reply`, target `github:pr:<owner/repo>#<n>`, `vars` `{to, body}`, with the optimistic patch that takes the item `to` out of `feedback` at once, and returns. The engine's drain posts the reply as the User's own GitHub login. For an item of kind `thread`: `addPullRequestReviewThreadReply(input: {pullRequestReviewThreadId: <id>, body})`. For kind `comment` or `review`: `addComment(input: {subjectId: <the pull request's node id>, body})`, the body prefixed by `Re: <item url>` and a blank line. **Every posted body ends with a blank line and the marker `<!-- cpd:reply -->`** (contract §2.2), so the next poll sees the answer and the item leaves the list within one poll. It writes the one `swr_mutations` row and appends no Event: a drain that fails is a `failed` mutation with an `error` Event (swr-github §9). When an approval was needed (above), the reply **consumes** it, removing its file, only after the mutation was written; a refused reply leaves it for the 10 minutes it lives.

Output: `{"ok": true, "queued": true, "mutation_id": <id>, "workflow", "to"}`. The posted comment's `url` is the drain's result, read with `cpd swr mutation show <id>`.

```json
{"ok": true, "queued": true, "mutation_id": 41, "workflow": "ui", "to": "PRRT_kwDO…"}
```

Idempotent: no (every run queues a reply). A reply to the same item with the same body while the first is active returns that active mutation's id and writes nothing (`Dedupe`, swr-github §9).

### 9.8b `pr post`

**From the Slack cutover (`docs/architecture/swr-slack.md` §5.1).** `pr post` enqueues the send as an outbox mutation (`op_kind` `post`) and returns `{ok, plan, workflow, queued: true, mutation_id, message}`; engine E24 sends it, then writes the `pr_posts` row, the `in_review` Jira row and the `auto_merge` mutation. Check 8 reads the merge methods and `autoMergeAllowed` from `swr_repos`, not from `gh`. Check 2 also refuses `already_posted` while a `post` mutation of the Workflow is active. The checks and refusals below are otherwise as written.

```
cpd pr post [--workflow <key>] [--plan <id>]
```

Posts a Workflow's pull request to Slack for review, so an agent never calls Slack tools by hand (pro-d64, pro-d65). **Callers:** Lead; not cockpit, not internal (§2). The Lead asks the User and posts only on the User's yes. **Approval (pro-d451):** when `$CPD_SESSION` is set and non-empty and the resolved policy has `pr.post.require_approval` true, the command is refused `approval_required` (exit 3, `details` `{workflow, kind: "post"}`) unless the Session holds a live approval of kind `post` for the Workflow (§9.8d); this check runs before every check below and before any of their side effects, and the approval is consumed only after the send succeeded and the `pr_posts` row was written. Without `$CPD_SESSION`, or with `pr.post.require_approval` false (the default), nothing changes. A Workflow may be posted only once: a second attempt is refused `already_posted` once its `pr_posts` row exists. A post that fails writes nothing and may be run again; a post whose outcome is unknown is confirmed later by the engine's Slack poll of the team channel, never by `pr post` itself (Order and unknown outcomes, below). It reads the stored `pull_requests` row of the Workflow (the poll keeps it, every `watch.pr_poll_seconds`; `cpd pr poll` makes it fresh). Its only GitHub calls are the one read of check 8, before the Slack send, and the auto-merge mutation after the send (Auto-merge, below). The cockpit's Inbox menu runs it too (**Post** on a `ready for user review` `pr-ready` row, §13.2), at once with no confirm popup, through the cockpit's command runner, which runs without `$CPD_SESSION`, so it is never asked for an approval and stays one click; a failure opens the error dialog titled `Post Pull Request`.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--workflow <key>` | the Workflow to post, selected by §1.3's rule: required when the Plan has two or more Workflows that are not `cancelled`, defaulted to the one when it has one |

Check order; the first failure refuses and then nothing is sent and nothing is written:

1. the Workflow's status is not `open` (`details` `{workflow, status}`) → `workflow_not_open` (exit 3)
2. a `pr_posts` row exists for the Workflow (`details` `{workflow, channel, ts, link, posted_at}`; a row is written only after a sent post, Order and unknown outcomes below) → `already_posted` (exit 3)
3. the owner's policy resolves for the Workflow (`policy_invalid`, `owner_unset`, `owner_unconfirmed`, contract §8.3 "Validation") → refusal with listed exit codes (1 or 3)
4. `policy.pr.post.enabled` is false (`details` `{workflow, key: "pr.post.enabled"}`) → `post_disabled` (exit 3). `pr.post.enabled` is set only by an owner or repo file (contract §8.3 "Key exposure", pro-d126): a machine file with a `pr.post` table makes check 3 fail `policy_invalid` before any post
5. the stored pull request is not `authored` (`details` `{workflow, number}`) → `not_authored` (exit 3)
6. the channel is `policy.pr.post.channel` when not empty, else the machine config's `inbox.team_channel` when not empty, else (`details` `{keys: ["pr.post.channel", "inbox.team_channel"]}`) → `post_unconfigured` (exit 3)
7. `postable::unready(&row)` (contract §2.2, §8.3, the eight Unready reasons: `not_open`, `draft`, `conflicting`, `changes_requested`, `checks_failed`, `checks_pending`, `comments_unread`, `bot_comments`) is not empty (`details` `{workflow, number, url, reasons: [<as_str of each>]}`) → `pr_not_ready` (exit 3)
8. ONE `gh api graphql` read of the repository and the pull request (the auto-merge read query: `autoMergeAllowed`, the pull request's `id`, `autoMergeRequest { enabledAt }`, `squashMergeAllowed`, `mergeCommitAllowed`, `rebaseMergeAllowed`): all three methods false (`details` `{repo, number, squash, merge, rebase}`) → `no_merge_method` (exit 3); a read that fails or cannot be parsed → `gh_failed` (exit 1, `details` `{argv, exit, stderr}`). Both refuse before the Slack send: nothing is sent and nothing is written

| Refusal | Exit | Details |
|---|---|---|
| `approval_required` | 3 | `{workflow, kind: "post"}`: `$CPD_SESSION` set, `pr.post.require_approval` true, no live approval (§9.8d); refused before checks 1 to 8 |
| `workflow_not_open` | 3 | `{workflow, status}` |
| `already_posted` | 3 | `{workflow, channel, ts, link, posted_at}` |
| `policy_invalid` | 1 | `{key: "pr.post.*", …}` as contract §8.3 |
| `owner_unset` | 3 | contract §8.3 |
| `owner_unconfirmed` | 1 | contract §8.3 |
| `post_disabled` | 3 | `{workflow, key: "pr.post.enabled"}` |
| `not_authored` | 3 | `{workflow, number}` |
| `post_unconfigured` | 3 | `{keys: ["pr.post.channel", "inbox.team_channel"]}` |
| `pr_not_ready` | 3 | `{workflow, number, url, reasons: ["draft", "changes_requested", …]}` |
| `no_merge_method` | 3 | `{repo, number, squash, merge, rebase}`: the repo allows no merge method (check 8) |
| `gh_failed` | 1 | the read of check 8 failed or was unparseable; `{argv, exit, stderr}` |
| `slack_auth` | 3 | the Slack sign-in in pi's MCP credentials is missing or invalid (§21.7); run `pi mcp login slack`; nothing was sent and nothing is written |
| `slack_not_configured` | 3 | no `slack` server in `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` (§21.7); run `pi mcp add slack --url https://mcp.slack.com/mcp --exposure hidden`; nothing was sent and nothing is written |
| `slack_failed` | 1 | the helper could not send the message (timeout, network, Slack service failure) (§21.7); the outcome is unknown: nothing is written, the message may have reached the channel, and the engine's Slack poll records it if it did (Order and unknown outcomes); the post is retryable |
| `slack_unparseable` | 1 | the helper's response is not the expected JSON (§21.7); the message may have been posted: the outcome is unknown, as for `slack_failed` (Order and unknown outcomes) |
| `slack_helper_failed` | 1 | the helper could not load pi's MCP modules (§21.7); nothing was sent and nothing is written |
| `spawn_failed` | 1 | the helper could not be started; nothing was sent and nothing is written |
| `store_failed` | 1 | the `pr_posts` row could not be written after the message was sent (§21.7, D5): the message WAS posted to the channel, the link is in `details`, and nothing is written; the engine's Slack poll records the post later (Order and unknown outcomes) |

**Order and unknown outcomes** (User, 2026-11-05 EST; supersedes the pending-row order of pro-d408 and every Slack lookup inside `pr post`). `pr post` does no lookup. The `pr_posts` row is written only after an OK send, with the sent message's `ts` and `link`: there is no pending row, and nothing is written ahead of the send. **Any error writes nothing**: a refusal of checks 1 to 8, `slack_auth`, `slack_not_configured`, `slack_helper_failed`, `spawn_failed`, `slack_failed`, `slack_unparseable` and `store_failed`. So a failed post writes no row: it is retryable with no workaround, and a second `pr post` sends the message again. A post whose outcome is unknown (`slack_failed`, `slack_unparseable`) may still have reached the channel. The engine's Slack poll E11 (§21.5) confirms it, and so confirms a post the User made by hand: the earliest message of the team channel that the User authored (`author_id` = `inbox.slack_user_id`), that carries the pull request's url `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>` and that was posted at or after the pull request opened, is recorded in `pr_posts` with that message's `ts` and a `link` `https://<workspace>.slack.com/archives/<channel>/p<ts without the dot>` (the match rule and the workspace: contract §2.2 "PR post"). Nothing is written before a send: the row comes only from a message the channel already holds. So a post whose outcome was unknown needs no retry workaround: once recorded, its Inbox row reads `waiting for peer review` instead of `ready for user review` (contract §2.2 "The authored pull request rule"), and a second `pr post` is refused `already_posted`. **Not built yet:** the recording is a later Job; until it lands, nothing records an unknown outcome, so check the channel before a retry of a post whose outcome was unknown.

**Superseded for the github Workflow (swr-github §9).** `pr post` enqueues one op, the Slack send (op `post`, executed by the slack Workflow's drain), and returns `{queued, mutation_id}`. The auto-merge request is queued once, by the Slack source, when the send confirms the post (swr-slack §6.2: op `auto_merge`, target `github:pr:<owner/repo>#<n>`). The refusals of step 8 are read at enqueue from the merge methods of `swr_repos`, the cache. The drain's writes are the ones below, unchanged in content; its result is read with `cpd swr mutation show`.

Effects: **Slack**, through the helper (§21.7), one `slack_send_message` call with the rendered message from `policy.pr.post.template` (contract §8.3), sent with `unfurl_app_links: false` (pro-d245), so Slack shows no GitHub preview under it. Rows: one `pr_posts` row (contract §4.4), whose `last_posted_at` is set to its `posted_at` (the first post; `cpd pr repost`, §9.8b2, sets it at each repost, pro-d388) and, in the same transaction, the Jira transition `in_review` of the Workflow (`swr-jira.md` §7) (`swr-jira.md` §7; queued only when the `pr_posts` insert is new); the only later write is `reacted_at` (Workflow `react`). `pr post` never calls Jira (an open pull request already queued `in_review` when the Workflow bound it, `swr-jira.md` §7, pro-d454): the `jira` source of engine E24 does (`swr-jira.md` §8). Events: none (contract §5.1). Limits: a crash after the send and before the row is written leaves the message posted with no row until the engine's Slack poll records it, and a retry before then can post it twice; `pr post` takes no lock, so two simultaneous runs of the same Workflow can both send, and the second's insert then fails `already_posted`; the stored row is up to `watch.pr_poll_seconds` old, `cpd pr poll` first makes it fresh and a Workflow the poll never read for comments is `comments_unread`.

Output: `{"ok":true,"plan":<id>,"workflow":<key>,"number":<n>,"url":<the pull request's url>,"post":{"channel":"C…","ts":"1793040197.490209","link":"https://missionlane.slack.com/archives/C…/p1793040197490209","posted_at":<time>,"reaction":<emoji name or null>,"reacted_at":null},"message":<rendered text>,"auto_merge":{"state":<state>,"reason":<text or null>}}`. `post.reaction` is the policy's value at post time (never changed on a policy edit; the final emoji for the reaction is resolved from the current policy when E17 places it, contract §3.7 A1, §8.3). `reacted_at` is null when the post is created; it is set by engine E17 (§21.9) after the reaction is added to the queue and successfully delivered.

```json
{"ok": true, "plan": "pay-4521", "workflow": "api", "number": 813, "url": "https://github.com/acme/pay/pull/813", "post": {"channel": "C02JU6C2Z1D", "ts": "1793040197.490209", "link": "https://missionlane.slack.com/archives/C02JU6C2Z1D/p1793040197490209", "posted_at": "2026-10-26T21:36:37.490209Z", "reaction": "git-merge", "reacted_at": null}, "message": "Retry failed payouts (api)\nhttps://github.com/acme/pay/pull/813", "auto_merge": {"state": "enabled", "reason": null}}
```

**Auto-merge** (pro-d117, pro-d254, pro-d261). The read of check 8 precedes the send; the Slack post and the `pr_posts` row still come first, and the mutation's outcome never undoes them. After them the command reuses that read (no second read) and reports `auto_merge` `{state, reason}`, `state` one of `enabled`, `deferred`, `not_allowed`, `refused`, `failed`, in this order of cases: (a) `autoMergeAllowed` is false, stacked or not: `not_allowed`, stored `none`, no mutation, no Event; `reason` is one line saying the repo does not allow auto-merge and cpd merges the Workflow when it is ready (the cockpit's Merge, or the Lead with `cpd pr merge` after a human approves); (b) the Workflow is stacked (its base is another `workflows` row's Lead Branch): `deferred`, stored `pending`, no mutation; (c) the Workflow already has an auto-merge request: `enabled`; (d) otherwise the mutation `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` with `mergeMethod` the first allowed of squash, merge, rebase in upper case (§9.10): `enabled`, `refused` (GitHub's own error message; stored `refused`) or `failed` (gh failed; stored `pending`, retried by engine E18). `reason` is null for `enabled`. The post and the command's exit status never depend on the mutation's outcome.

Idempotent: no (every run tries to post).

### 9.8b2 `pr repost`

**From the Slack cutover (`docs/architecture/swr-slack.md` §5.1).** `pr repost` enqueues one `repost` mutation and returns `queued: true` with its `mutation_id`; E24 sends it, and `last_posted_at` is set on completion. The checks below are as written.

```
cpd pr repost [--workflow <key>] [--plan <id>]
```

Sends ONE reminder in the Slack thread of a Workflow's post (pro-d386, pro-d388; Plan pr-post-bump). **Callers:** none; the cockpit only (the Inbox menu's **RePost** on a `review overdue` row, §13.2; the table of §2 lists no Lead caller). **Nothing runs it automatically**: no engine Step calls it (E23 is retired, contract §3.7). It does not check that the post is overdue: the menu shows the action only then, and a repost by hand is allowed. **Approval (pro-d451):** exactly as `pr post` (§9.8b): when `$CPD_SESSION` is set and non-empty and `pr.post.require_approval` is true, `pr repost` is refused `approval_required` (exit 3, `details` `{workflow, kind: "post"}`) unless the Session holds a live approval of kind `post` for the Workflow, checked before the checks below and before the helper call; the approval is consumed only after the reminder was sent. The cockpit's RePost runs without `$CPD_SESSION` and stays one click.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--workflow <key>` | the Workflow whose post to repeat, selected by §1.3's rule (as `pr post`) |
| `--plan <id>` | the Plan (default `$CPD_PLAN`; `plan_required` without one) |

Code: `core/src/pr/repost.rs`, `#[derive(clap::Args, Debug)] pub struct RepostArgs { #[command(flatten)] workflow: WorkflowArg, #[command(flatten)] plan: PlanArg }` and `pub(super) fn repost(ports: &Ports, args: RepostArgs) -> Result<Output, CpdError>`; `core/src/pr/mod.rs` adds `/// Repeat the Workflow's post in its Slack thread (§9.8b2)` `Repost(repost::RepostArgs)` to `Command` and `Command::Repost(args) => repost::repost(ports, args)`; `cli/src/interface.rs` `TABLE` gains `("pr repost", &[], true)`.

Check order; the first failure refuses and then nothing is sent and nothing is written:

1. the Workflow's status is not `open` (`details` `{workflow, status}`) → `workflow_not_open` (exit 3)
2. no `pr_posts` row exists for the Workflow (`posts::find` is `None`; `details` `{workflow}`) → `post_not_found` (exit 3)

Then ONE call of the helper through the `Runner` port, built with `slack::call(&env.config, "slack-post.ts", &[("channel", post.channel), ("thread-ts", post.ts), ("reply-broadcast", "true")], Some(b"Bibbidi-bobbidi-bump!".to_vec()), DEADLINE)` (the helper's grammar, §21.7 "Thread flags"): the arguments are exactly `--channel <post.channel> --thread-ts <post.ts> --reply-broadcast true` and stdin is exactly `Bibbidi-bobbidi-bump!` (no newline). `post.channel` and `post.ts` are the stored post's own, so the reply goes to the first post's thread and, with `reply_broadcast`, to the channel. The helper's failures are those of `pr post` and leave the row unchanged: `slack_auth`, `slack_not_configured`, `slack_failed`, `slack_unparseable`, `slack_helper_failed` and `spawn_failed` (same codes, exits and details as §9.8b's table).

| Refusal | Exit | Details |
|---|---|---|
| `approval_required` | 3 | `{workflow, kind: "post"}`: as §9.8b |
| `workflow_not_open` | 3 | `{workflow, status}` |
| `post_not_found` | 3 | `{workflow}`: the Workflow has no post (§21.7 lists its other use) |
| `slack_auth`, `slack_not_configured` | 3 | as §9.8b |
| `slack_failed`, `slack_unparseable`, `slack_helper_failed`, `spawn_failed` | 1 | as §9.8b; `last_posted_at` unchanged |
| `store_failed` | 1 | the store write after a sent message failed; the message WAS sent and the thread link is in `details` |

Effects: **enqueue** (swr-github §9): one `post` op of kind `repost`, whose drain sends the thread reply as above; the command returns `{queued, mutation_id}`. On success, in one write transaction (`store.write("pr repost", …)`), `posts::mark_bumped(tx, plan, workflow)` sets `pr_posts.last_posted_at` to the transaction's time (contract §4.4), which restarts the 24-hour clock: the row's `review overdue` label goes at E8's next tick and returns 24 hours later if the pull request is still unreviewed. No other column changes, no Event (contract §5.1), no Jira call, no GitHub call. A refusal or a helper failure leaves `last_posted_at` unchanged. Limits: a crash between Slack's answer and the write sends twice on a rerun; a timeout leaves the outcome unknown, check the thread.

Output: `{"ok": true, "queued": true, "mutation_id": <id>}`. The drain's result is that object above, read with `cpd swr mutation show <id>`.

Idempotent: no (every run sends one reply).

### 9.8d `pr approve`

**Internal** (§1.1; as `host approve`, §9.11). Callers: Lead (the adapter's pi tool `cpd_external_approve` runs it after the User's Allow once; an agent does not run it by hand). Not cockpit (§2).

```
cpd pr approve --kind reply|post --workflow <key> [--to <item-id>] [--plan <id>]
```

Records the User's one-shot approval (pro-d451) of one guarded action by the calling Session. It needs `$CPD_SESSION`, else `usage`. The approval is one JSON file `$CPD_HOME/run/pr/approve/<uuid>.json` (directory mode 0700, file mode 0600, written atomically by a temp file and rename; contract §3.7 layout) holding `{session, kind, plan, workflow, to, at}`, `to` absent for `post`. It is **bound** to the calling Session (`$CPD_SESSION`), the `kind`, the Workflow and, for `reply`, the item id: another Session, kind, Workflow or item does not match it. It **lives 10 minutes** from `at`, checked when read; an expired file is ignored. It is **one-shot**: the guarded command removes the file only after its action succeeded (`pr reply` after its mutation is written, `pr post` and `pr repost` after the send), so a refused or failed action leaves it. Kind `post` approves one `pr post` **or** one `pr repost` of that Workflow, whichever consumes it first. Approvals of one Session and key may coexist; each is consumed once.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--kind reply\|post` | the action approved: `pr reply` (§9.8a) or `pr post` / `pr repost` (§9.8b, §9.8b2) |
| `--workflow <key>` | the Workflow, selected by §1.3's rule |
| `--to <item-id>` | `reply` only: the feedback item's `id` (§9.8a); required for `reply`, refused for `post` |
| `--plan <id>` | the Plan (default `$CPD_PLAN`; `plan_required` without one) |

| Failure | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `$CPD_SESSION` unset or empty | `usage` | 2 |
| `--kind` not `reply` or `post`, `--to` missing for `reply`, or `--to` given for `post` | `usage` | 2 |
| the Workflow is not one of the Plan's | `workflow_not_found` | 4 |

`agent_forbidden` is not used: the adapter's guard, not the command, keeps an agent from approving for itself (§15). Effects: writes the approval file; nothing in the store, no Event, no `gh` or Slack call.

Output: `{"ok": true, "approved": {"kind", "workflow", "to", "expires_at"}}`, `to` null for `post`, `expires_at` 10 minutes after `at`.

```json
{"ok": true, "approved": {"kind": "reply", "workflow": "ui", "to": "PRRT_kwDO…", "expires_at": "2026-11-06T20:50:24.968Z"}}
```

Idempotent: no (every run writes a new file).

### 9.8c `pr rerun`

```
cpd pr rerun [--workflow <key>] [--plan <id>]
```

Re-runs the failed GitHub Actions workflow runs of a Workflow's head commit (pro-d155), so a Lead never runs `gh run rerun` itself and never asks the User to click Re-run failed jobs. **Callers:** Lead; not cockpit, not internal (§2). Use it when the log of a failed check shows an infrastructure or transient runner failure, not a code defect on the branch: a code defect needs a fix Job (§9.8, `pr-feedback`).

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--workflow <key>` | the Workflow, selected by §1.3's rule |
| `--plan <id>` | the Plan, else `CPD_PLAN` (§1.3) |

Check order; the first failure refuses and then nothing is re-run:

1. the Workflow's status is not `open` → `workflow_not_open` (exit 3, `details` `{workflow, status}`); no `gh` call is made
2. `gh pr view` gives the head commit, `head_sha`, read fresh from GitHub
3. `gh run list --commit <head_sha>` lists the GitHub Actions workflow runs of that commit. A run is **failed** when its `conclusion` is `failure`, `timed_out` or `startup_failure`, compared case-insensitively (`gh` prints them in lower case, GraphQL in upper case). A run still running has an empty conclusion and is not failed. `cancelled`, `skipped`, `neutral`, `action_required`, `stale` and `success` are not failed.
4. no run is failed → `no_failed_run` (exit 3, `details` `{workflow, head_sha, runs: [{id, name, status, conclusion}]}`, every run of the commit so the Lead can see why); nothing is re-run

| Precondition or failure | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Workflow is not `open` (`details` `{workflow, status}`); no `gh` call is made | `workflow_not_open` | 3 |
| no GitHub Actions workflow run of the head commit is failed (`details` `{workflow, head_sha, runs}`); nothing is re-run | `no_failed_run` | 3 |
| a `gh` call fails (§1.3); the loop stops there, `details` is `{argv, exit, stderr, rerun}`, `rerun` the runs already re-run, `[{id, name}]`, empty when it failed before the first re-run | `gh_failed` | 1 |

**Superseded for the github Workflow (swr-github §9).** `pr rerun` enqueues op `rerun` and returns `{queued, mutation_id}`. Its head and failed runs come from the effective row and its detail: `head_sha` is the head at the last pass, and the failed runs are the check contexts of that head whose `conclusion` is `failure`, `timed_out` or `startup_failure`, their id `workflowRun.databaseId`. `gh run list --commit` is no longer called. The steps below are the drain, and its `gh run rerun` calls are unchanged.

Effects: **gh**, as the User's own GitHub login, with cwd = the Workflow's Lead worktree, so `gh` addresses the Workflow's repo (§9):

1. `gh pr view <number> --json headRefOid`: `head_sha`, the head commit of the pull request, read fresh from GitHub, not from the stored row
2. `gh run list --commit <head_sha> --json databaseId,name,status,conclusion --limit 100`: the GitHub Actions workflow runs of that commit, as `gh` lists them (at most the first 100)
3. for each failed run, in the order listed: `gh run rerun <databaseId> --failed` (only its failed jobs)

It writes nothing in the store and appends no Event (contract §5.1).

Output: `{"ok": true, "workflow": "<key>", "head_sha": "<sha>", "rerun": [{"id": <databaseId>, "name": "<run name>"}]}`, one entry for each run re-run, in listing order.

```json
{"ok": true, "workflow": "api", "head_sha": "4c1e7b2f9a0d3e58", "rerun": [{"id": 12345678901, "name": "CI"}]}
```

Idempotent: no (each call re-runs what has failed). A second call right after the first finds those runs in progress (empty conclusion) and is refused `no_failed_run`.

### 9.9 `pr push`

```
cpd pr push [--workflow <key>] [--plan <id>]
```

Publishes an `open` Workflow's Lead Branch with a plain push, after the Gate when the Workflow's `gate.merge` is `local` (for `pr open` and `pr push`) or `gate.pr` is `local` (for `pr rebase`) (hs-d139, hs-d292; contract §7.6, §8.3; with `ci` there is no Gate and the two Gate rows below do not apply). It does not rebase: use it (the repair, as `pr rebase`; a fix Job's own merge pushes for itself, contract §3.8 "Updating"; after a `push_failed` it is the command to run) when the branch carries a merge of the base, which `pr rebase` would drop (§9.3), when the remote has not moved and the Jobs Merged since only need to reach the pull request, or for a stacked Workflow that took its base Workflow's new commits. It checks nothing about the base (hs-d490): a Lead Branch that lacks a base that moved ahead is pushed as it is.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--workflow <key>` | the Workflow to push, selected by §1.3's rule: required when the Plan has two or more Workflows that are not `cancelled`, defaulted to the one when it has one |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Workflow is `open`, before the Gate and again after it (merged during the Gate: nothing pushed) | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| the `pre-start` passes before the Gate runs; `details.tail` is its last 60 lines, `details.log` the full log `run/<plan>/logs/workflow-<key>.pre-start.log` | `gate_error` | 1 |
| the Workflow's policy resolves (contract §8.3 "Validation", `details` as there): its Context has an owner | `owner_unset` | 3 |
| its owner has a policy file | `owner_unconfirmed` | 1 |
| its policy files are valid | `policy_invalid` | 1 |
| the Gate passes (§7.3, as `pr open` step 2); `details.tail` is its last 60 lines, `details.log` the full log `run/<plan>/logs/workflow-<key>.pre-merge.log` | `gate_failed` | 3 |
| the Gate ran (not killed, not `hook_invalid`); `details.tail`, `details.log` as above | `gate_error` | 1 |
| the push is a `(non-fast-forward)` or `(fetch first)` rejection and the remote tip does not contain G (the remote moved: a `pr rebase` pushed, or someone else); `details.stderr` is git's stderr; the Lead runs `pr rebase`. Any other rejection or failure is `git_failed`, with git's reason in its message (rule P) | `push_rejected` | 3 |
| the caller is not an agent, OR the incident is off, OR the resolved Workflow's Plan is not held (hs-d643): `CPD_SESSION` set and non-empty names an agent; a held Plan is in the incident; `details` is `{workflow, plan, incident}` | `incident_hold` | 3 |

The Lead worktree's local changes refuse nothing (hs-d243; `dirty_target` is no longer a refusal of this command).

For an **adopted** Workflow (§9.4) the push is `git push --porcelain origin G:refs/heads/<head_ref>`, plain, never forced; `push_rejected` names `cpd pr rebase` (the catch-up, §9.3) as the next step.

Effects: no lock and no R first (hs-d243, §7.4): `G = rev-parse refs/heads/<lead branch>`, read once; with `gate.pr` is `local`, the Gate in the Lead worktree at G: `pre-start` (output `run/<plan>/logs/workflow-<key>.pre-start.log`), then `pre-merge` from the Workflow's policy (output `run/<plan>/logs/workflow-<key>.pre-merge.log`) (hs-d679, hs-d680); the Workflow re-read; then rule P, `git -C <lead worktree> push --porcelain origin G:refs/heads/<lead branch>` (no `-u`, never `--force` or a lease). A rejection whose remote tip already contains G (a merge during the Gate pushed a descendant) is a success that pushed nothing. Any other git failure is `git_failed`. **Rows**: none; no Event.

```json
{"ok": true, "plan": "pay-4521", "workflow": "api", "pushed": true, "sha": "77aa01e…", "remote": "77aa01e…"}
```

`sha` is G, the gated commit (the Lead Branch's tip when the command read it); `remote` is the remote branch's tip after the push, past G when merges that landed during the Gate were pushed (hs-d243). Idempotent: yes; a G the remote already has (git's porcelain status `=`, "up to date"), or has a descendant of, still runs the Gate (with `gate.pr` is `local`), pushes nothing and returns `"pushed": false`.

### 9.10 `pr merge`

```
cpd pr merge <owner>/<repo>#<n>
```

Merges a pull request on GitHub: the Dispatch column's merge button (§13.2; hs-d272, hs-d273, hs-d274), or the Lead after a peer approves a posted Workflow (pro-d64, §9.10). **Callers:** the User, through the cockpit (`cockpit` true); the Lead, after a `pr-feedback` with reason `approved` of a posted Workflow; none of the other agent roles and no guard against them calling it (hs-d248). It takes a pull request, not a Plan's Workflow key: it needs no Plan or Context and `<owner>/<repo>#<n>` is the form the Dispatch column shows. Per-owner merge rules (repo-policy, hs-d263) are later.

**One required-check gate** (air-d48). The required-check gating of `pr merge` and the pr-ready readiness of the Inbox (contract §2.2 STATUS, §9.2) are one persisted evaluation: the poll computes it from its live GitHub read each pass (§9.2 "The checks read", contract §7.6 step 3b) and persists the verdict with the missing, pending and failed required names; the Inbox reads that record to label a pull request ready to merge, and `pr merge` reads the same record. `pr merge` refuses `required_check_not_passed` (exit 3) only when that evaluation says not passed, and the refusal lists the real missing, pending and failed check names that evaluation holds. No cache — `swr_pr_detail` or any other — gates the merge independently.

**One up-to-date gate.** Beside the required checks, `pr merge` — and every cpd merge path that calls it: the Dispatch column's merge button and merge menu (§13.2), the WebUI's merge, and the Inbox `pr-ready` item's merge action — merges only when the pull request's head contains the current default-branch head, read fresh at merge time. The default branch is the pull request's stored `default_branch` (contract §2.2, migration `pr-base`); its head is read fresh from GitHub at the moment of the merge, never from a cache or the stored row, and the head contains it when it is the head itself or an ancestor of the head (GitHub's compare of the two oids answers `ahead` or `identical`). **A pull request whose base is not the default branch — a stacked pull request — is never checked**: its base Workflow's own merge brings the base's commits, and GitHub holds it until then. When the head is behind, the merge is refused `head_behind_main` (exit 3) with the message `behind main, updated, waiting for gate` and `details` `{repo, number, head, main}` — and the refusal is not only a refusal: cpd queues the Workflow's `update` Job (the Workflow found through the pull request's `workflows` row), the one whose Worker merges the default branch into the Lead Branch and whose push runs the Gate (contract §7.4, §7.7), and arms an automatic merge: cpd will merge the pull request by itself, as this command, once the required checks pass on a head that contains main (the same two conditions, read from the poll's stored rows at each pass; the fresh read happens again when the automatic merge actually calls `pr merge`). The armed intent is cleared when the pull request merges, is closed, or the User cancels it; re-running `pr merge` while it is armed is idempotent, one intent. The `expected_head_oid` guard below is unchanged: the up-to-date gate decides whether to merge, the guard that the merge lands on the head it checked. A pull request with no cpd Workflow (no `workflows` row points to it) is refused only: there is no Workflow to queue an `update` Job for and nothing is armed.

**Superseded for the github Workflow (swr-github §9).** `pr merge` enqueues the `merge` op and returns `{"ok": true, "queued": true, "mutation_id": <id>, "repo", "number"}`. Its refusals `usage`, `merge_not_clean` and `no_merge_method` are checked at enqueue against the effective row, its `swr_pr_detail` and `swr_repos` (the methods of step 2a), `required_check_not_passed` is checked at enqueue against the stored required-check evaluation (above), and `head_behind_main` is checked at enqueue against the fresh read of the up-to-date gate (above), and all refuse without enqueueing; a `head_behind_main` refusal still queues the `update` Job and arms the automatic merge, as the up-to-date gate says. The steps below are the drain: step 1's read is the settled row of the pass before the drain, GitHub enforces `--match-head-commit`, and a refusal or `gh` failure the drain finds is a `failed` mutation with one `error` Event. The drain re-checks the up-to-date gate itself, immediately before `gh pr merge`: the containment is read fresh again through the Runner (a read, never a write), and a head that no longer contains the default branch is not merged — the intent stays armed and the Workflow's `update` Job is queued, so a base that moved between the enqueue and the drain is not merged behind it. The warnings of step 4 are kept on the mutation (`context_json`), and the drain's output below is what the mutation records.

Steps:

1. Read the pull request fresh from GitHub: `gh pr view <n> --repo <owner/repo> --json state,mergeStateStatus,headRefOid,title,mergedAt`. The stored `pull_requests.merge_state` is not trusted: it can lag.
2. Refuse, failing loud, unless `state` is `OPEN` and `mergeStateStatus` is `CLEAN`. **A refusal (`merge_not_clean`) stores the state it read first** (User, 2026-11-05 EST): before it refuses, `store_refused_state` sets the `pull_requests` row's `merge_state` to the `mergeStateStatus` read in step 1, in one `UPDATE` (`changed_at` now) that runs only when the row exists, is `open` and holds another `merge_state`, modelled on the merge store of the Effects paragraph below. It makes no extra GitHub call; the refusal's code, text and `details` are unchanged, and no column is added for a note: the pull request's Inbox row relabels itself from the stored state at the next reconcile (contract §2.2, STATUS table).
2a. Read the methods the repo allows: `gh repo view <owner/repo> --json squashMergeAllowed,mergeCommitAllowed,rebaseMergeAllowed`. It runs after the OPEN/CLEAN check and before the merge, so a pull request that is not OPEN and CLEAN is refused `merge_not_clean` and this read is skipped. All three false: refused `no_merge_method`, no `gh pr merge`. A non-zero exit or an unparseable answer: `gh_failed`, no `gh pr merge`.
3. `gh pr merge <n> --repo <owner/repo> --<method> --match-head-commit <headRefOid>`, `<method>` being `squash`, `merge` or `rebase`. `--match-head-commit` makes GitHub refuse when the branch moved after step 1's check. The method is the first allowed of squash, merge, rebase (the `--squash`, `--merge`, `--rebase` flags; GraphQL `SQUASH`, `MERGE`, `REBASE`), read fresh on every call and never cached: a cached permission that goes stale merges the wrong way. The order: squash is cpd's default and gives one commit titled by the Workflow (pro-d117); a merge commit before rebase is the User's choice (pro-d261): a merge commit leaves the Lead Branch's commits unrewritten, and rebase is the last resort. A repo that allows one method gets that one. cpd never passes `--delete-branch` and never deletes a remote branch: the branch is deleted by the repo's own `delete_branch_on_merge` setting, which repoints a pull request stacked on it to the base before it deletes the branch (contract §3.8 "Stacked Workflows" step 8; pro-d240). cpd's own clean-up never touches remote branches (§9.2 "After a Workflow is merged") and nothing in cpd runs `git fetch --prune`, so the local clean-up is unaffected. When `gh pr merge` exits non-zero and its stderr contains `asynchronous merge REST API` or `part of a stack` (GitHub's GraphQL refusal when another open pull request targets this pull request's head branch, a stack base), `pr merge` falls back to `gh api --method PUT repos/<owner/repo>/pulls/<n>/merge-async -f merge_method=<method> -f sha=<headRefOid>`, `<method>` being `squash`, `merge` or `rebase`: the same method, with the same head-SHA guard as `--match-head-commit`. The fallback passes no branch deletion either: branch deletion and the repointing of a stacked pull request stay with `delete_branch_on_merge` (pro-d240). The merge is asynchronous, so `pr merge` still reads the pull request back once after it (the Effects paragraph): `stored` is true only when that read says `MERGED`; otherwise `stored` is false, the command succeeds, and the next poll records the merge. If the `gh api` call fails, the result is `gh_failed` with that call's `{argv, exit, stderr}`. Any other `gh pr merge` failure is `gh_failed` with the `gh pr merge` call's `{argv, exit, stderr}`, and no `gh api` call is made.

**Effects** (hs-d550 B1): after `gh pr merge` succeeds, one store transaction: read the pull request back once with `gh pr view <n> --repo <owner/repo> --json state,mergeStateStatus,headRefOid,title,mergedAt` (the precheck, hs-d550 B1: `gh::view_for_merge`). When it reads `state` `MERGED` the store transaction writes: the `pull_requests` row of <owner>/<repo>#<n>, when one exists, gets `state` `merged` and `merged_at` GitHub's `mergedAt` (else the transaction's time, changed_at now); when a `workflows` row points to it, exactly the poll's merge (contract §7.6 pr poll step 6: `workflows` `merged` with `merged_at`, `pr-merged`, the Workflow's `draft` Jobs `cancelled` with reason `pr merged` and one `job-cancelled` each (hs-d731, §9.2), Plan `done` with `plan-done` when it was the last Workflow and the done guard holds (contract §3.1), the unstack of Workflows stacked on it). The open `pr-ready` item of subject `pr:<owner>/<repo>#<n>` is closed (closed_at, `inbox-closed`, as E8's reconcile closes one). The command output's `stored` is true. When it reads anything else, or the read fails, nothing is written and `stored` is false. The command succeeds either way. No stored row: nothing is written and the merge still succeeds. (hs-d550 B2: the precheck reading MERGED writes the merge as (A) does, with GitHub's `mergedAt`.) A row already stored merged writes nothing (idempotent). (hs-d550 B1, C: a failing `cpd pr poll` after the merge no longer matters, the merge is already stored; `pr merge` now opens the store.) GitHub's search listed the pull request after its merge (hs-n415: evidence of why B1 changed the contract).

4. **The setting read** (pro-d240): once the merge is stored, or the read-back said otherwise, run `gh repo view <owner/repo> --json deleteBranchOnMerge`. `true` adds nothing. `false` adds the warning `auto_delete_off`: the merged branch stays on GitHub, and a pull request stacked on it is not repointed to the base, so turn the repo's setting on. A failed or unparseable read adds the warning `auto_delete_unread`, whose `text` carries the `gh` error's message. This read never fails the command: the merge, the store write and the exit status are the same whatever it says. It is skipped when the merge is refused or fails.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the argument is `<owner>/<repo>#<n>`, `n` a positive integer | `usage` | 2 |
| the re-check finds the pull request not `OPEN` or its `mergeStateStatus` not `CLEAN`; `details` is `{repo, number, state, merge_state}` (GitHub's words), and the `merge_state` it read is stored first (step 2); when the precheck reads `MERGED` (hs-d526), it writes the merge transaction and is still refused | `merge_not_clean` | 3 |
| with a non-empty repo policy `pr.required_checks`, when the stored required-check evaluation (the poll's live-read one, read by the pr-ready readiness too; no cache gates here) says any required name is missing, pending or failed; `details` is `{repo, number, missing: [names], pending: [names], failed: [names]}`, the real names of that evaluation | `required_check_not_passed` | 3 |
| the up-to-date gate finds the head behind: the current default-branch head, read fresh at merge time (the stored `default_branch`'s head, from GitHub), is neither the pull request's head nor an ancestor of it; a stacked pull request is never checked; `details` is `{repo, number, head, main}`, the head oid and the default branch; the message is `behind main, updated, waiting for gate`; the refusal queues the Workflow's `update` Job and arms an automatic merge (the up-to-date gate, above) | `head_behind_main` | 3 |
| the repo allows no method: `squash`, `merge` and `rebase` are all false in the read of step 2a (only reached when the pull request is `OPEN` and `CLEAN`); `details` is `{repo, number, squash, merge, rebase}`; the message is `<owner/repo> allows no merge method: squash, merge commit and rebase are all off in its settings, so cpd cannot merge #<n>. Allow one in the repo's settings.` | `no_merge_method` | 3 |
| each `gh` call succeeds (also when `--match-head-commit` makes GitHub refuse, and the methods read of step 2a: a non-zero exit or an unparseable answer; the fallback `gh api` call of step 3 is one of these calls, and its failure's `details` are that call's `{argv, exit, stderr}`); `details` is `{argv, exit, stderr}` | `gh_failed` | 1 |

The setting read of step 4 is never a `gh_failed`: a failed read is the `auto_delete_unread` warning, and the exit status does not change.

Output:

```json
{"ok": true, "repo": "<owner/repo>", "number": 31, "method": "squash", "stored": true, "warnings": []}
```

`method` is the method step 3 used: one of `squash`, `merge`, `rebase`.

`warnings` is always present: `[]` when there is nothing to say, else a list of objects `{"code": ..., "text": ...}` with the codes of step 4, `auto_delete_off` and `auto_delete_unread` (pro-d240). The former field that said whether the branch was deleted is gone: cpd does not report it; `warnings` reports the repo's setting.

**Rows** (hs-d550 B1): one store transaction, recorded immediately after `gh pr merge` succeeds (when the precheck reads `MERGED`, hs-d550 B2), never delayed to the next poll. The `pull_requests` row of <owner>/<repo>#<n>: when it exists, `state` becomes `merged` and `merged_at` is GitHub's `mergedAt` from the precheck's `gh pr view`, or the transaction's time when GitHub was not read or did not return it (changed_at now); when a `workflows` row points to it, the Workflow `dispatch → open → merged` or `waiting → merged` with `merged_at`, Events `pr-merged`, the cancelled drafts' `job-cancelled` (above) and, when every Workflow that is not `cancelled` is then `merged` and the done guard holds (contract §3.1), the Plan `deploy → done` with `plan-done` (contract §7.6 poll step 6). The same transaction queues the Workflow's `done` Jira transition (`swr-jira.md` §7), next to the merge reaction. The open `pr-ready` Inbox item of subject `pr:<owner>/<repo>#<n>` is closed in the same transaction (closed_at, `inbox-closed`, hs-d550 B1, hs-n404). When no row exists, nothing is written and the merge still succeeds. No Event otherwise.

Idempotent: (A), (B), (C) yes, by the rows: a row already `merged` is compared with GitHub and written only if a value changed; when none do (already merged with the same `merged_at`), nothing is written. A second call of (A) finds the pull request `MERGED` and is refused `merge_not_clean`; (B) and (C) would have written it the first time, so the second call writes nothing (idempotent). The refusal is the same: `merge_not_clean` with `state` `MERGED`. The refusal's store (step 2) writes only a changed `merge_state`, so a second refusal that reads the same state writes nothing.

### 9.11 `host approve` and `host repair`

**Manager only, internal commands.** The host Manager approves and executes a cpd checkout repair when the install is skipped (contract §3.7 E6).

```
cpd host approve
cpd host repair
```

**`cpd host approve`** (internal; written by the adapter's `cpd_host_approve` tool after the User's Allow once): creates a private approval file for the Session, valid 10 minutes, one repair. Output: `{"ok": true}`.

**`cpd host repair`** (Manager only; contract §3.7 E6): repairs the skipped cpd install by resetting the checkout's main branch to origin/main, saving the diff and old HEAD. Needs an approval of the calling Session. Steps, all `git -C $HOME/projects/cpd`: (a) `rev-parse HEAD` (old head); (b) `diff HEAD` and, when non-empty, write to `$CPD_HOME/run/cpd-install-backups/<ts>.patch` (0600; <ts> = UTC `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`); (c) `update-ref refs/cpd-host/<ts> <old head>`; (d) `checkout --force -B main origin/main`; (e) `rev-parse HEAD` (new sha). Untracked files, other branches and stashes are never touched; no fetch (the script fetched). The approval is consumed only after step (e) succeeds. A failing git step stops it with `git_failed` naming the argv. Output JSON: `{"ok":true,"saved":{"ref":"refs/cpd-host/<ts>","patch":"<path or null>"},"head":"<new sha>"}`. The pill clears at the next sync tick after a repair (contract §3.7 E6).

### 9.12 `cpd tui action host`

(internal): what a click on the red version pill runs when `@cpd_host_alert` is set. Reads the install state file; when it is not `skipped` it does nothing. First ensures Context `host` (§3.11, contract §3.7 E22), which returns its live Manager, registering it when there is none; a failure of ensure is reported on the client with `display-message -c <client>` and nothing is sent. Then brings that Manager into the chat slot as `session open` does (a stopped or asleep Manager is resumed), then, when `$CPD_HOME/run/cpd-install-notified` does not hold this incident's `since`, sends the Manager one message (as the User, `session send` with `--unblocks "cpd install skipped"`) and writes `since` and a newline to that file atomically; a later click on the same incident only opens the Manager. Message text (fixed): `cpd install skipped: <reason> (since <since>). Checkout: ~/projects/cpd. Read it with git -C ~/projects/cpd status / diff / log origin/main..HEAD (read only; never write in the checkout). Show the User what a repair would discard, ask with the tool cpd_host_approve, then run cpd host repair.` (contract §3.7 E6, §1.4, commands.md §15.18).

### 9.13 `cpd tui action incident`

(internal): what a click on the incident pill runs (contract §6.1). Reads the incident's stored Lead (`incident.lead`); when it is null, resolves the `lead_session` of the alphabetically first Plan in `incident_plans`. Brings that Lead into the chat slot as `session open` does (a stopped or asleep Lead is resumed), sends it no message. With incident mode off it reports on the client with `display-message -c <client>` `no incident: nothing to open`; with no resolvable Lead `incidents require a lead`. It prints nothing on stdout or stderr and exits 0, as every `cpd tui action` does..

## 10. `session`

Sessions (§2.2, §3.6) and their tmux panes (§6). Every tmux call is `tmux -L <tmux.socket> …` with `TMUX`, `TMUX_PANE`, `CPD_SESSION` and `CPD_ATTEMPT` removed (§6.1; hs-d551); a failing call is `tmux_failed` (exit 1). A Session's **place** is the `place` of its latest `session-moved` Event (`chat`, `parked`, `work` or `none`), or `none` when it has none.

**The chat slot.** **Amends contract.md §6.2** (the Lead's answer to Escalation `contract-commands-a1-q1`): the chat slot is the pane of `cpd:main` that has `@cpd_session` **or** `@cpd_view = chat`. A pane with `@cpd_view = chat` is the **placeholder**: it runs `cpd tui view chat`, which reads `No Lead here: pick a Plan in the session tree` and it holds the slot while no Lead is there. **Amends §6.2's list of `@cpd_view` values** with `chat`. Why: the slot must hold a pane before any Lead exists (the first `cpd tui` on a machine) and after its Lead is parked (`swap-pane` needs a pane to swap in). At most one placeholder exists and only ever in the slot: `session park` creates it there (§10.5) and `session open` kills it with its window when a Lead takes the slot (§10.4).

### 10.1 `session list`

```
cpd session list [--context <id>] [--plan <id>] [--role <role>] [--state <state>] [--archived]
```

Filters combine with AND; `--role` and `--state` may repeat. Without filters: every Session except archived ones (`archived_at` is null). With `--archived`: archived Sessions are listed too, live and archived together (hs-d516); the flag is given once (clap refuses it repeated). Here `--context` and `--plan` are filters only: neither falls back to `CPD_PLAN`.

Effects: none; one read transaction.

```json
{"ok": true, "sessions": [
  {"id": "596d007f-…", "role": "lead", "context": "building-cpd", "plan": "cpd2", "attempt": null, "name": "building-cpd:cpd2", "key": "building-cpd:cpd2", "runner": "pi", "state": "waiting", "state_label": "φ: Worker question", "state_at": "…", "archived_at": null, "asleep_at": null,
   "place": "chat", "tmux_pane": "%12", "file": "/home/clayton/.pi/agent/sessions/…_596d007f-….jsonl", "forked_from": null, "plan_lead": true, "tier": "O3", "cwd": "/home/clayton/projects/cpd", "title": "Dynamic session titles contract", "titled_at": "…"}],
 "events_cursor": 48213}
```

`runner` is `pi` or `durable` (contract §2.2): how the Session runs, set at creation (contract §6.19); a `durable` Lead or Manager has a null `tmux_pane` and `place` `none` by design (contract §3.6). `role` is `lead`, `worker` or `manager` (B3-A1; a Manager has `plan` null, `attempt` null and `plan_lead` false; `--role manager` lists them). `plan_lead` is true for the Session that is its Plan's `lead_session`. `title` and `titled_at` are the dynamic title (contract §2.2, hs-d257) and when it was written, both null until the first `session retitle`. `archived_at` and `asleep_at` are null unless the Session is archived or asleep.

`key` (string or null) is the Session's **agent key** (contract §2.2 "Agent key"), next to `name`: `sessions.name` for a Manager (`<context>`), for a Lead that is not a fork (`<context>:<plan>`) and for a Worker (`<context>:<plan>:<job>`); null for a fork, whose `name` (`<source name> (fork)`, or what `session rename` set) is free text and no agent key. `key` is the **only** field a script or the pi adapter uses to tell a fixed name from a free one: a non-null `key` is the name `session rename` refuses (`key_fixed`, §10.7); a null `key` may be renamed. Read-only.

### 10.2 `session show`

```
cpd session show [<id>]
```

`<id>` defaults to the selected Session (`CPD_SESSION`); it accepts any form of §1.3. Output: the fields of `session list` (`runner` and `key` included) plus `created_at`, `registered_event` (the id of its `session-registered` Event, the pi adapter's first cursor, §15.2), `model` and `thinking` (the row's `tier` as pi is told it, below: hs-d506), `loop_guard_turns` (the config value, for every Session), `switch` (null or a failed switch record, below) and, for a Plan's Lead, `open_escalations` (ids). Effects: none.

`model` is from the policy's `[model]` table for the key of the row's `tier` (contract §8.3, §9) (`<provider>/<model-id>`) and `thinking` is the level of the tier's digit (`off`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, contract §9): the two halves of the `--model <model>:<thinking>` argument `session run` passes (§10.8), computed by the one function both use. The models are read at each call, so a policy edit shows at once.

`switch` (DEFECT 2) is null when the Session's last model switch succeeded or has not been attempted; otherwise it is `{tier, code, message, at, next}` where `tier` is the `tier` the switch tried, `code` and `message` are from the adapter error, `at` is the RFC 3339 UTC time and `next` is the exact `cpd session run <id>` command that relaunches this Session's pi so it starts on the current `tier` (contract §6.5, §10.4, §10.8). **A `durable` Session has no `next` key** (DEFECT 2, the pane hint): it has no pane and no pi to relaunch, so its `switch` is `{tier, code, message, at}` with the same values and no `next` key at all, never a `cpd session run` command. A `pi` Session keeps `next`. Tests: `session_retier::a_durable_sessions_switch_failure_has_no_next_hint` (a durable Session's `switch` has no `next` key) and `session_retier::a_pi_sessions_switch_failure_keeps_the_session_run_hint` (a pi Session's `switch.next` is `cpd session run <id>`).

```json
{"ok": true, "session": {"id": "596d007f-…", "role": "lead", "context": "building-cpd", "plan": "cpd2", "attempt": null, "name": "building-cpd:cpd2", "key": "building-cpd:cpd2", "runner": "pi", "state": "idle", "state_label": null, "place": "chat", "tmux_pane": "%12", "file": "…", "forked_from": null, "plan_lead": true, "tier": "O3", "model": "github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5", "thinking": "high", "loop_guard_turns": 20, "switch": null, "cwd": "/home/clayton/projects/cpd", "title": null, "titled_at": null, "created_at": "…", "registered_event": 40117},
 "open_escalations": ["contract-commands-a1-q1"]}
```

Read-only.

### 10.3 `session fork`

```
cpd session fork <source> [--plan <id>] [--name <name>] [--message-file <file>]
```

§6.7, §6.8. Registers a new Lead Session forked from `<source>` and starts it in a parked window; the waiting for the source to be idle happens in that window, so the command returns at once.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<source>` | the Session to fork (any form of §1.3); a Lead. This command is for **tangents the User starts** (a bug, an idea), B4; no Worker is a fork (pro-d163) |
| `--plan <id>` | the new Session's Plan; default the source's Plan. The fork is a **side session** of the Plan: the Plan's `lead_session` does not change, so Plan Events still go to the Plan's Lead only (§15.2). It is drawn in the tree **directly under its Context**, after the Context's Plans, never under the Plan or under `<source>` (B1, §13.2) |
| `--name <name>` | default `<source name> (fork)`, cut to 98 characters (contract §2.2 "Agent key") |
| `--message-file <file>` | its first message, copied to `run/<plan>/messages/<session>.md`; without it the fork starts with no message |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the source is a `lead` Session | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| the source's `runner` is `pi`; a `durable` source has no pane (contract §3.6), refused before any write or tmux call (§1.3) | `durable_session` | 3 |
| a Plan is known: `--plan`, else the source's Plan (a Manager has none) | `plan_required` | 2 |
| the source is not archived; `details.next` = `cpd session unarchive <source>` | `archived` | 3 |
| the cockpit's tmux session (`tmux.cockpit_session`) exists, checked before anything is written; `details.next` = `cpd tui` | `no_cockpit` | 3 |

Effects:
- **Rows**, one transaction: `sessions` (new UUID v4, `role = lead`, the Plan's Context, `forked_from = <source>`, `cwd` = the source's, `tier = lead_tier`, `stopped`). **Event** `session-registered`.
- **tmux:** `new-window -d -t =cpd: -n park-<label> -c <cwd> -e CPD_HOME=… -e CPD_SESSION=<id> -e CPD_PLAN=<plan> -- cpd session run <id>`; `@cpd_session`. One transaction: `tmux_pane`, **Event** `session-moved` `{place: "parked"}`.
- If the cockpit disappears between that check and `new-window`, the command fails with `tmux_failed` after the Session is registered (Escalation `rs-session-a1-q2`). If a later step fails (`@cpd_session`, the row or the `session-moved` write), the new window is killed (`kill-window`) before the error is returned (teardown G11).

```json
{"ok": true, "session": {"id": "a41b…", "name": "cpd rust lead (fork)", "plan": "cpd2", "forked_from": "596d007f-…", "pane": "%52", "window": "@23"}}
```

Idempotent: no; each call registers a new Session.

### 10.4 `session open`

```
cpd session open <id>
```

Brings a Lead, or a Context's Manager, into the chat slot (§6.4). `<id>` accepts any form of §1.3, so `cpd session open <plan id>` opens that Plan's Lead.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session is a `lead` or a `manager` (B3-A2) | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| it is not archived; `details.next` = `cpd session unarchive <id>` | `archived` | 3 |
| its `runner` is `pi` and the cockpit's `main` window and its chat slot exist; `details.next` = `cpd tui`. A `durable` Session has no pane and skips the chat slot and this check (contract §6.19) | `no_cockpit` | 3 |

Effects:
- **Durable** (`runner` `durable`, contract §6.19): no pane and never the chat slot, so `require_pane` is not applied. When the Session is asleep or labelled `host crash loop`, one transaction clears `asleep_at` and `state_label` (and, for the crash loop, resets the stored restart bound, contract §6.19); the command then waits for the host's socket at `$CPD_HOME/run/host/<id>.sock` to accept (retrying on ENOENT/ECONNREFUSED with a back-off, a 30 s deadline, else `host_timeout`, exit 5) and returns `{"session": <id>, "pane": null}`. The engine's hosts step starts the host; the command starts nothing and writes no `session-moved`.
- In the chat slot already: nothing; `"already": true`.
- **tmux:** when the Session has no live pane (`stopped`, or its pane is gone): first `kill-pane` on a dead pane of the Lead, if one is still there, so it never adds a second window; then `new-window -d -t =cpd: -n park-<label> … -- cpd session run <id>` first, which resumes it (`pi --session <file>`, §6.5) and `tmux_pane` is recorded; the pane's `@cpd_title` is set by the precedence of contract §6.1 (the dynamic `title`, else the key, or the name of a fork). Then `swap-pane -d -s <its pane> -t <chat slot pane>` and `rename-window -t <window> park-<displaced label>` for the window that now holds the displaced Lead. When the displaced pane is the placeholder or a history pane (`@cpd_view` `chat` or `history`, §10.12), `kill-pane` on it instead, which closes the now-empty park window with it, so placeholders and history panes never pile up in park windows.
- If a step after the new window is created fails (`set-option -p @cpd_session`, the swap, the row or the `session-moved` write), that new window is killed (`kill-window`) before the error is returned (teardown G11).
- **Rows**, one transaction: clear `asleep_at` when the Session was asleep (hs-d515); **Events** `session-moved` `{place: "chat"}` for this Session and `{place: "parked"}` for the displaced one.

```json
{"ok": true, "session": "8d0e…", "pane": "%41", "displaced": "596d007f-…"}
```

Idempotent: yes.

### 10.5 `session park`

```
cpd session park [<id>]
```

Moves the Lead in the chat slot back into a parked window (§6.4). `<id>` defaults to the Session in the chat slot; it accepts any form of §1.3.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the cockpit exists | `no_cockpit` | 3 |
| the Session is a `lead` | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| its `runner` is `pi`; a `durable` Session has no pane (contract §3.6) and is never in the chat slot, refused before any write or tmux call (§1.3) | `durable_session` | 3 |

Effects:
- Not in the chat slot: nothing; `"already": true`. A history pane in the slot (§10.12) has no Lead to park: nothing; `"already": true`.
- **tmux** (**amends contract.md §6.4**, which says only that park moves the Lead into a parked window): `new-window -d -t =cpd: -n park-<label> -P -F '#{window_id} #{pane_id}' -- cpd tui view chat` (a new park window holding a placeholder), `set -p -t <placeholder> @cpd_view chat`, then `swap-pane -d -s <placeholder> -t <chat slot pane>`. The Lead keeps its pid and is now alone in `park-<label>`; the placeholder fills the slot.
- **Rows**, one transaction: **Event** `session-moved` `{place: "parked"}`.

```json
{"ok": true, "session": "8d0e…", "pane": "%41", "window": "@31"}
```

Idempotent: yes.

### 10.6 `session state` (internal)

```
cpd session state <working|waiting|blocked|idle|stopped> [--label <text>] [--reply] [--session <id>]
```

How the pi adapter reports its agent state (§3.6, D4). `--session <id>` takes any form of §1.3. `waiting` (an agent waits for another agent) and `blocked` (the User has to act) say why: `--label` is required with them and refused with any other state (`usage`); 1–80 characters. `waiting` is entered from `working`, `idle` and `blocked` and left for `working`, `idle`, `blocked` or `stopped` (§3.6). `--reply` (hs-d278) is allowed only with `idle`, else `usage`: it says the run that ended answered a message the User wrote to this Session (§15.4). Internal (§1.1): hidden in clap, run only by the pi adapter.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the transition is in §3.6's table | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| `blocked` with the label `φ: Worker question` or `φ: question to the Lead` (both are agent waits, `waiting` only: contract §3.6, pro-d427) | `usage` | 2 |

Effects: when the state and label are unchanged, nothing (`"already": true`, no Event, §3.6). Otherwise **rows**, one transaction: `state`, `state_label` (null unless `waiting` or `blocked`), `state_at`. **Event** `session-state` `{from, to, label}`, plus `reply: true` when `--reply` was given (contract §5.2); `reply` is written only on a real change, so a call that changes nothing (`"already": true`) records no reply. For a Session in Context `codereview` whose Plan is in phase `done`, the Event records `reply` false even with `--reply` (pro-d391, contract §3.6), so it opens no `replied` Item. No tmux.

```json
{"ok": true, "session": "596d007f-…", "state": "waiting", "label": "φ: Worker question", "from": "working"}
```

Idempotent: yes.

### 10.7 `session rename`

```
cpd session rename <name> [--session <id>]
```

cpd 1 §11 `session rename`, kept; the queue file becomes an Event. `--session` accepts any form of §1.3.

**Refused `key_fixed`** (exit 3, `details` `{session, key}`) for a Session that is a Manager, a Lead that is not a fork (`forked_from` null) or a Worker: its name is its agent key (contract §2.2 "Agent key"). This is checked first, whatever the new name, so the unchanged name is refused too; nothing is written and no `session-renamed` Event is appended. A fork (`forked_from` set) is renamed as below.

Effects: unchanged name: `"already": true`, nothing written. Otherwise **rows**, one transaction: `sessions.name`. **Event** `session-renamed` `{name}`, addressed to the Session (`session` set), which its adapter applies with `pi.setSessionName` (§15.4). **tmux**: sets `@cpd_title` to the new name on the Session's pane when it has one **and the Session has no dynamic `title`** (hs-d257, contract §6.1: the title wins; the rename still writes `sessions.name` and appends its Event); nothing else.

```json
{"ok": true, "session": "596d007f-…", "name": "cpd rust lead"}
```

Idempotent: yes.

### 10.8 `session run` (internal)

```
cpd session run <id> [--adopt <pid>]
```

`<id>` accepts any form of §1.3. The program in every Lead pane (§6.2): owns its terminal (§1.2). Steps of §6.7:
1. If the Session's file exists, resume: `pi --model <model>:<thinking> --session <file>` with the Lead's `[-e …]` (§6.5). **The model is the row's current `tier`'s** (hs-d506): pi, given `--model`, uses it instead of the model its session file recorded (pi 1.3.0 `core/sdk.js`: the file's model is restored only when none is given) and applies the `:<thinking>` level (`main.js` `buildSessionOptions`); so a Session `session retier` moved (§10.15) and then restarted (a reload for a new pi, the watchdog, Enter after pi exited, `session open`) runs on its new Tier, with its whole conversation.
2. Else, if `forked_from` is set, wait until the source is idle (§6.7 step 1, every 2 s, showing the waiting line), then `pi … --fork <source file> --session-id <id> -n <name> [-- @<first message file>]`.
3. Else start a fresh Lead: `pi --model … --session-id <id> -n <name> -- @<first message file>` for a non-by-user Session, or `pi --model … --session-id <id> -n <name>` for a by-user Session (hs-d542 A2: no `@<file>` when `sessions.by_user = 1`; the User's first prompt carries the first message with the queued turns, §15). Steps 2 and 3 take `--model` from the row's `tier` **when pi starts**, not from the `tier` the row had at registration (hs-d506).

Before it starts pi (steps 1–3) every pi a `session run` starts (§19), a Lead's and a Manager's, there are no ports to assign. Before it starts a Lead's pi, `session run` also removes any stale quit marker, `run/quit/<session-id>` (below), so a marker that an earlier pi left (a nonzero exit, a crash) never archives this one.

**Reload on install** (hs-d33, hs-d38, hs-d49, hs-d151; §6.7 "Reload on install"; incident hs-n141, cause hs-n148). The wrapper detects a new install by the identity of its executable (§3.4 of the contract), checked at every iteration of its loop **before any store access**. On a new cpd it re-execs **at once**, with no idle wait, whatever the Lead's place or state and **keeps pi running**: pi is its child and survives the `exec`. It `exec`s the same path with the same argv plus the internal argument `--adopt <pid>` (**internal**: written only by the wrapper's own `exec`, not an interface of the User or an agent); the new `session run` skips steps 1–3, starts no pi, `waitpid`s that pid as its own child and continues the same loop on it (watchdog, `Press Enter to resume`). The adapter reloads itself at idle (hs-a5, §15.6); a cpd install does not restart pi. Before the `exec` it runs `<path> --version` and re-execs only when that succeeds and `store` is `null` or `store.opens` is `true` (§1.2); otherwise it does not `exec`, logs once per installed file (identity) `reload skipped: <path> cannot open the store: <store.refusal.message>` on the stderr of its pane and keeps running, pi untouched; a later install is checked again (contract §6.7). **A store error never ends a wrapper while its pi runs:** a failed read with a replaced cpd leads to the re-exec above; any other failed read is logged once on stderr and retried at the next poll, pi untouched. Why: wrappers that waited for the Lead's idle read the store after a newer cpd had migrated it, failed `store_too_new` and exited and six Leads were ended instead of reloaded (hs-n141, hs-n148). If pi exits on its own after an install, the wrapper `exec`s the new binary (no `--adopt`) before any store write and the existing paths run there.

**Transient store errors** (contract §6.7 "Reload on install"). The store accesses before pi starts (open, the Session's row, `sessions.file`, the port, a fork's source) and after it exits (`session state stopped`, the name for the resume prompt) are tried again while they fail with `store_busy`, `lock_timeout` (the store's setup lock), or SQLite's busy or locked as `store_failed`: 0.5 s, doubling to 5 s between tries; the pane says once `Waiting for the store (<what>): <code>: <message> Trying again.` A wrapper never ends for it. Any other error (`session_not_found`, `not_a_lead`, `wrong_pane`, a malformed row) ends it as in the table below.

**Restart for a new pi** (hs-d49). A change of pi (the identity of `<pi agent dir>/install/current-version`, else of the resolved `pi` executable) is the only reload that restarts pi and it waits for the Lead's next idle (state `idle`, last turn finished, session file quiet `fork_quiet_seconds`): the wrapper sends pi `SIGTERM`, waits for it to exit (`SIGKILL` `timeouts.pi_stop_seconds` (default 10) after `SIGTERM`) and `exec`s the same path with the same argv (no `--adopt`); the new `session run` takes step 1. A parked Lead restarts at once. The Lead in the chat slot waits until it is idle **and** parked, or idle for 10 minutes, so unsent typing is not lost. A `waiting` or `blocked` Lead is never idle. See contract §6.7 "Reload on install".

**Adapter watchdog** (hs-d141; contract §6.7 "Adapter watchdog"). While pi is alive, the wrapper checks the Session's state at every poll (2 s). When the state has been `stopped` for more than **60 s** (a constant of the wrapper, not a config key; measured from the `session-state` Event that set it, so a state the wrapper itself set after a pi exit does not count while pi is not running), it restarts pi on the session file: `SIGTERM`, wait (`SIGKILL` after `timeouts.pi_stop_seconds`, as for a reload), then step 1. In one transaction before the restart it appends one `error` Event `{source: "session run", code: "adapter_missing", message, details: {session, state_since, seconds}}` with `session` = this Session (and its `plan`, `context`), which the new adapter delivers once it follows (§15.3). It applies to every Lead and Manager, whatever the place and whatever the idle rules of the reload; a `stopped` that ends (`idle`) before 60 s is the adapter's own reload and is never touched. After the restart the 60 s start again; a broken install loops once per 60 s with one `error` Event per restart (no cap: each is a visible fact and a repaired install ends it).

The first message is the file `plan new` or `session fork` wrote (§1.4); for a Manager, `run/<context>/manager-message.md` (§3.10); none when resumed. Before it starts pi it writes the `git` wrapper `$CPD_HOME/bin/git` if it is missing or different (idempotent) and puts `$CPD_HOME/bin` first on pi's `PATH` (contract §6.5, hs-d310). It is passed as `@<path>` (its absolute path). In the same transaction it clears `switch_failed` (DEFECT 2: pi now runs the row's current Tier, so any earlier failed switch is stale). While pi runs, it watches for the session file (§6.5) and records `sessions.file` once it appears (a data write, no Event). When pi exits it runs `session state stopped` if the adapter did not, then applies the rule below. Unless that archived the Lead, it prints `pi exited. Press Enter to resume <name> here.` and resumes on Enter.

**When pi exits** (pro-d358 removed the archive on the User's quit of hs-d91 and hs-d122; pro-d361 restores it for one case, behind a marker). pi exits with status 0 on the User's `/quit` or `/q`, on Ctrl+D and Ctrl+C, and when macOS shuts down or tmux stops, which sends pi `SIGTERM` or `SIGHUP` (pi 1.2.0, `interactive-mode.js`: `shutdown()` ends in `process.exit(0)`; verified by reading it). pi's `session_shutdown` reports reason `quit` on all of them, so neither the exit status nor the reason tells `/quit` from a signal. **A Lead is archived only when pi exits 0 after the User explicitly submitted `/quit` or `/q`, marked by the quit marker: never on `SIGTERM`, `SIGHUP`, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D or a crash.** The marker is one file per Session, `run/quit/<session-id>`, at the path that `CpdHome::quit_marker` (`core/src/home.rs`, beside `run_dir`) returns. `session run` passes it to a Lead's pi as the env `CPD_QUIT_MARKER` (§6.6). The pi adapter writes it, empty, only when the User submits exactly `/quit` or `/q` (trimmed) in the editor (§15.1); nothing else writes it, and a Manager's pi gets no marker.

When pi exits, `session run` runs `session state stopped` if the adapter did not, then: if the exit status is 0, the Session's role is `lead` and the marker exists, it removes the marker (one-shot) and calls `archive_on_quit`. That archives the Lead with the full archive rule of §10.10 (`archive_blockers`, contract §2.2 "Archived"): if the Lead holds the chat slot it is parked first; a Plan's own Lead archives its Plan with its Sessions, as `plan archive` does, and its pane is closed last, once the archive has returned. `archive_on_quit` calls the archive functions in-process, not the `session archive` command, so the `agent_forbidden` guard of that command (§1.3) is not reached: it is unchanged for `context`, `plan` and `session` `archive` and `unarchive`. When the rule refuses the archive, `session run` prints the refusal on stderr and falls through to the resume prompt below. In every other case it does not archive: a nonzero exit, a missing marker or a Manager leaves the Session `stopped`.

Unless it archived the Lead, `session run` prints `pi exited. Press Enter to resume <name> here.`; on Enter it starts pi again on the session file (step 1). End of input ends `session run`. Unless archived, the Session's pane stays recorded, so after a shutdown engine E2 restarts the Lead or Manager (contract §3.7). Apart from the marker rule, a Lead or Plan is archived only by the User's `session archive`, `plan archive` or `context archive`, by E14 after the Lead has slept (contract §3.7), or by `plan cancel` (§4.12); a Manager and a Lead otherwise behave the same.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session is a `lead` or a `manager` | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| its pane's `@cpd_session` is this Session | `wrong_pane` | 3 |


Idempotent: yes; a restart resumes (§6.7 step 3).

### 10.9 `session close`

```
cpd session close <id>
```

Ends a Lead's pane (`<id>` accepts any form of §1.3): pi stops and the Session's file stays, so `session open` resumes it later (§10.4). It is the tree's `x` key (§13.2). Added by cockpit parity (amendment 14, §19).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session is a `lead` | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| its place is not `chat`: the Lead in the chat slot is never closed; `details.next` = `cpd session park` | `in_chat_slot` | 3 |

Effects:
- No live pane (`tmux_pane` null, or the pane is gone): nothing; `"already": true`. A `durable` Session (`runner` `durable`, contract §3.6) has no pane to kill and takes this branch: it succeeds with `"already": true` and writes nothing, as a `pi` Session with no pane does. It leaves the Session's host running (contract §6.19): the host is stopped when the Session sleeps (E13) or is archived (E14, §10.10), not by close.
- **tmux:** `kill-pane -t <pane>`. A parked window that held only that pane closes with it.
- **Rows**, one transaction, compare-and-swap on `tmux_pane` (when engine E2 recorded the pane as gone first, nothing is left to write: `"already": true`): `state = stopped` with **Event** `session-state` `{from, to: "stopped", label: null}` unless it already was `stopped`; `tmux_pane = NULL`; **Event** `session-moved` `{pane: null, window: null, place: "none"}`, the rows E2 writes for a pane that is gone (contract §3.6).

```json
{"ok": true, "session": "8d0e…", "pane": "%41"}
```

Idempotent: yes.

### 10.10 `session archive`

```
cpd session archive <id>
```

Archives one Session (contract §2.2 "Archived"); `<id>` accepts any form of §1.3.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the caller is not an agent: neither `CPD_SESSION` nor `CPD_ATTEMPT` is set and non-empty (checked first, before the Ledger is opened); `details` `{command, session, attempt}`, `session` and `attempt` the values of those variables or `null` | `agent_forbidden` | 3 |
| the Session exists | `session_not_found` | 4 |
| it is a `lead` (a Worker's Session is archived only by its Plan's cascade) | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| it is not its Plan's own Lead (`plans.lead_session`); `details.next` = `cpd plan archive --plan <p>` | `archive_blocked` | 3 |
| the archive rule holds for the Session alone (contract §2.2 "Archived"): (a) it is not `working`, `waiting` or `blocked` (`details.blockers` kind `session`, `Session <name> is <state>.`). The Plan clauses do not apply here, and an open Inbox item does not block it (pro-d421; E8 closes the Session's Inbox items once it is archived). The automatic sleep and archive of a Lead (E13 and E14, `LEAD_FINISHED`, §3.7) still require phase `done` and no open undismissed Inbox item | `archive_blocked` | 3 |
| it is not in the chat slot; `details.next` = `cpd session park` | `in_chat_slot` | 3 |

The engine archives on its own (E12 Worker archive, E14 Plan archive after sleep, contract §3.7); the User archives from the cockpit or the CLI.

Effects, in this order:
1. **Check** the rule above; nothing is written if it blocks.
2. **tmux:** a live pane is closed as `session close` does (§10.9). A `durable` Session (contract §3.6) has no pane: nothing is closed and `closed` is empty, and its host is stopped (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after `timeouts.pi_stop_seconds`, contract §6.19); step 3 writes `archived_at` as for any Session. The host stops within one engine tick of step 3 whichever path archived the Session (contract §6.19, the sweep).
3. **Rows**, one transaction that re-checks the rule: `sessions.archived_at` = now, `sessions.asleep_at` = null (hs-d515); **Event** `session-archived` `{archived: true}`.

```json
{"ok": true, "archived": [{"kind": "session", "id": "a41b…"}], "closed": ["%52"]}
```

Idempotent: yes; already archived: `"already": true`, nothing written, nothing closed.

### 10.11 `session unarchive`

```
cpd session unarchive <id>
```

`<id>` accepts any form of §1.3.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the caller is not an agent: neither `CPD_SESSION` nor `CPD_ATTEMPT` is set and non-empty (checked first, before the Ledger is opened); `details` `{command, session, attempt}`, `session` and `attempt` the values of those variables or `null` | `agent_forbidden` | 3 |
| the Session exists | `session_not_found` | 4 |
| it is a `lead` | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| its Plan is not archived (nor its Context); `details.next` = `cpd plan unarchive --plan <p>` or `cpd context unarchive <c>` | `archived` | 3 |

The engine archives on its own (E12 Worker archive, E14 Plan archive after sleep, contract §3.7); the User archives from the cockpit or the CLI.

Effects: **rows**, one transaction: `sessions.archived_at = NULL`, `sessions.asleep_at = NULL` (hs-d515); **Event** `session-archived` `{archived: false}`. No tmux: no pane is started; `session open` resumes the Lead (§10.4).

```json
{"ok": true, "archived": [{"kind": "session", "id": "a41b…"}], "closed": []}
```

Idempotent: yes; not archived: `"already": true`, nothing written.

### 10.12 `session history`

```
cpd session history <id>
```

`<id>` accepts any form of §1.3. Shows an archived Session's history, read-only, in the chat slot (hs-d91, hs-d122). It is the tree's click on an archived Session row (§13.2).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session exists | `session_not_found` | 4 |
| it is a `lead` | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
