| its `runner` is `pi`; a `durable` Session has no pane (contract §3.6), refused before any write or tmux call, so no Lead is parked and no history pane is made (§1.3) | `durable_session` | 3 |
| it has a session file (`sessions.file` set and readable) | `file_unreadable` | 2 |
| the cockpit's `main` window and its chat slot exist; `details.next` = `cpd tui` | `no_cockpit` | 3 |

Effects, in this order:
1. **Park:** if a Lead holds the chat slot, park it as `session park` does (§10.5): a new `park-<label>` window with a placeholder, `swap-pane`, **Event** `session-moved` `{place: "parked"}` for that Lead.
2. **tmux:** `respawn-pane -k -t <the slot's pane> -- cpd tui view history <id>` (§13.2), then `set -p -t <pane> @cpd_view history` and `set -p -t <pane> @cpd_history <id>` and `@cpd_session` unset. A placeholder or an earlier history pane is the slot's pane, so it is respawned in place.
3. **Rows:** none besides step 1's Event.

```json
{"ok": true, "session": "8d0e…", "pane": "%41", "parked": "596d007f-…"}
```

`parked` is null when no Lead held the slot. Idempotent: yes; rerunning for the same id respawns the slot's one pane, so exactly one history pane exists and no Lead is parked.

### 10.13 `session send`

```
cpd session send <id> (<text> | --file <f>) --unblocks <reason> [--origin <tui|webui>]
```

Sends one message to a Lead or a Manager Session (hs-d92, hs-d133, hs-d514). It appends an Event; the target's adapter delivers it (§15.3). The message always wakes: when the target is idle it starts a turn at once; a working, waiting or blocked target gets it after its running turn, never interrupted. It carries a required statement of what it unblocks (hs-d507, hs-d514). The command is not the User's only way to write one: the engine writes the same Event, from the User's side (`from` null), to a Context's Manager for each of its own step errors (contract §3.7, hs-d314) and for each stuck Job (contract §3.7 "A stuck Job", hs-d318) and for each repeated ask (contract section 3.7 "A repeated ask").

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | the target Session (any form of §1.3) |
| `<text>` | the message, a `Text` (1–20 000 characters) |
| `--file <f>` | the message read from a file, same limits |
| `--unblocks <reason>` | what the message unblocks, 1–200 characters, one line (hs-d514); shown in the Event's text as `Message from <who> (unblocks: <reason>): <preview>` (Effects) |
| `--origin <tui\|webui>` | the surface the message was submitted from (Plan ui-origin, air-d23): `tui` or `webui`; written as the optional `origin` of the `session-message` Event's `data` (contract §5.2). Optional; absent means no origin. Any other value is refused as `usage` (§1.5) |

Exactly one of `<text>` and `--file` (else `usage`).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session exists | `session_not_found` | 4 |
| it is a `lead` or a `manager`; a Worker is refused with "Session <id> is a worker, not a Lead or a Manager." | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| it is not archived; `details.next` = `cpd session unarchive <id>` | `archived` | 3 |
| only when the target is `stopped` with no live pane: the cockpit's tmux session exists; `details.next` = `cpd tui` | `no_cockpit` | 3 |
| only if the sender is an agent ($CPD_SESSION set; User exempt, hs-d514): the target is not a Lead of a Plan in phase `done` or `archived` (hs-d507); `details: {plan, phase}` | `plan_inactive` | 3 |
| only if the sender is an agent: the sender has not sent the exact same text (trimmed) to a different Session in the last 60 minutes (no broadcasts, hs-d507); `details: {session, at}` | `broadcast` | 3 |
| only if the sender is an agent: the sender has not sent the exact same text (trimmed) to this Session in the last 60 minutes (no duplicates, hs-d507); `details: {at}` | `duplicate` | 3 |

**A `durable` target** (`runner` `durable`, contract §3.6): the Event is appended as for any Session; the command starts no pane and no host, and raises no error for the missing pane (so `no_cockpit` does not apply); the host's follower delivers it (contract §6.13, P1.4), `started` is false and `pane` null. An asleep durable target, or one labelled `host crash loop`, is woken by the same write (Effects): the engine's hosts step starts its host at the next tick (contract §6.19). A `stopped` Lead or Manager with `runner` `pi` is accepted: this call starts it (hs-d725) as a parked `cpd session run <id>` window (hs-d726, A1) and it gets the message when its adapter starts; the chat slot never moves. A live pane of the Session means it is starting and nothing is started.

Effects:
- **Rows**, one transaction: **Event** `session-message` with `session` = the target, `context` and `plan` = the target's, `data` = `{from, text, unblocks}`; `from` is `CPD_SESSION`, else `PI_SESSION_ID`, else null (the User); with `--origin <tui|webui>` the data also carries `origin` = the given value, absent without the flag (Plan ui-origin: set only by the WebUI paths — the web pi-runner backend passes `--origin webui`, web/CONTRACT.md 11.9). For a `durable` target that is asleep (`asleep_at` set) or labelled `host crash loop`, the same transaction clears `asleep_at` and that label, as `session open` does for a durable Session (§10.4; contract §6.19).
  - **Its `text`** (what `cpd events list` shows) is `Message from <who>: <preview>`, `<preview>` the start of the message's text and `<who>` the sender: `<name> (<uuid>)` when the sender's row has a name (`sessions.name`, the agent key for a Manager, a Lead that is not a fork and a Worker), `<uuid>` alone when the row has no name, and `the User` when `from` is null. With `--unblocks <reason>` it is `Message from <who> (unblocks: <reason>): <preview>`. The text does not name the target: the Event is addressed to it (`session` = the target).
- **tmux:** when the target is `stopped` with no live pane, the mechanism of §10.4 (starting a parked window with a pane, §6.4) applies: first `kill-pane` on a dead pane of the Session, if one is still there; then `new-window -d -t =cpd: -n park-<label> | ctx-<context> -c <cwd> -e CPD_HOME=… -e CPD_SESSION=<session> -P -F '#{window_id} #{pane_id}' -- cpd session run <id>`, the pane title and `@cpd_session` set, `tmux_pane` recorded and **Event** `session-moved` `{place: "parked"}` appended, the chat slot never moving. With a live pane, nothing is started. Otherwise no tmux, and none for a `durable` target.
- **Citation marking** (best-effort, after the transaction; §3.5, the Session rule of §3.3): the text is scanned (`RecordId::scan`, contract §2.1), and each record id it cites that the sender Session read in the sender's Context (`sessions.context`; a sender with none logs nothing) gets `used` = 1. The User (`from` null) logs nothing. A failed marking never fails the command or changes its output or exit status.

```json
{"ok": true, "event": 4812, "session": "a41b…", "from": "596d007f-…", "unblocks": "PR #210 opened", "started": true, "pane": "%47"}
```

`from` is null when neither variable is set. `unblocks` echoes the reason. `started` is true when this call started a pane. `pane` is the started pane, or null when none was started. Idempotent: no; each call is one message.

### 10.14 `session retitle` (internal)

```
cpd session retitle <session> --width <cols>
```

Writes the Session's **dynamic title** (contract §2.2, hs-d257): a glance reminder of what was **last happening** in its conversation (hs-d543: the input is the last 2 turns only and the length is the chat slot's width minus 8; no word count), written by an auxiliary agent (hs-n95: cpd never calls an LLM API itself, only pi, here as a one-shot run, `pi --print`, docs: pi `cli.md`). **Internal:** engine E10 starts it (contract §3.7) for each Lead or Manager Session after its turns end, at most once every 10 minutes; anyone may run it. `<session>` accepts any form of §1.3.

`--width <cols>` (required, hs-d543) is the width in columns of the chat slot pane (contract §6.2); the title's limit is **N = cols − 8, capped at 200** (a Title's maximum). `--width` missing, not an integer, or **below 9** is `usage` (§1.5). Engine E10 reads the width from tmux and passes it (contract §3.7); a later resize truncates the shown title as the header does today.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session exists | `session_not_found` | 4 |
| it is a `lead` or a `manager`; a Worker is refused | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| it is not archived; `details.next` = `cpd session unarchive <id>` | `archived` | 3 |
| `locks/title-<session>.lock` is free (step 1; held: `details.reason` is `running`, nothing written and the other run is the one that counts) | `title_failed` | 1 |

**Steps.**
1. Take `locks/title-<session>.lock` without waiting and hold it for the run's whole life, so a Session never has two runs at once; the kernel frees it when the run dies, so a crashed run leaves no stale lock (contract §1.4).
2. **The conversation text.** Read the Session's pi session file (`sessions.file`, JSONL) and take **the last 2 turns** (hs-d543): from the **second-to-last** message of role `user` to the end of the file (the whole file when it holds fewer than two `user` messages), the text of the messages of role `user` or `assistant` in it (tool calls, tool results and other entries are not messages here), in order; if their text exceeds **8 000 characters**, cut it so the **newest** characters are kept. With no such message (no `file` yet, or none in it), **skip**: print the JSON below with `"skipped": "no_messages"`, run no pi, append no Event, write nothing and set nothing. A skip is not an error.
3. **Run pi** once, in `run/titles/` (created when missing): `pi --print --no-session --no-extensions --model <model>:off -- "<prompt>"` where `<model>` is from the policy's `[model]` table's `G` key (contract §8.3, §9) and `:off` is pi's level for no thinking: the title writer needs only the model. The prompt asks for a reminder of **what was last happening** in the conversation, answered as **one line `TITLE: <what was last happening, at most N characters>`** (N of the usage above) and nothing else. pi's environment is `PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=1` only, no `CPD_*` (contract §6.5, "Title writer", hs-d562). Its stderr is kept (its last lines are the `tail` below).
4. **Parse and check the answer** (hs-d356). The title is taken **only from an explicit, parseable answer**: **the only line that starts with `TITLE:`** (leading spaces allowed), the text after the marker, trimmed and unquoted. Lines without the marker are ignored, so a preamble before the marked line does no harm. The answer is **malformed**, never a title, when: no line has the marker, or two lines do; the marked text is empty; it is over **N characters** (N = cols − 8, at most 200; it is **never cut**: an over-long answer is not a title; there is no word cap); it reads as sentences (a `. ` inside it, or it ends in `.`, `…` or `:`); or it is not a Title (`core/src/args.rs`: 1–200 characters, no control characters). An answer that is empty or only whitespace is `empty`, not `malformed`.
5. **Write**, in one transaction: `sessions.title` and `sessions.titled_at` (now); **Event** `session-titled` `{title}` (context, plan if any, session). Then **tmux**: sets `@cpd_title` to the title on the Session's live pane, when it has one (a tmux failure does not undo the write: it is reported on stderr and the header is made right by the next start or move of the pane, which apply contract §6.1's precedence).

pi failing to start or exiting non-zero, or an answer that is empty or does not pass step 4, is a refusal `title_failed` (exit 1), with `details: {session, reason: "running" | "spawn" | "exit" | "empty" | "malformed" | "invalid", exit?, tail?}` (`tail`: the last lines of pi's stderr) and **writes nothing**: `titled_at` stays, so the Session stays due and the engine retries at the next tick, logs the failure and reports it (an `error` Event) only once that Session's titling has failed for 10 minutes in a row; a success clears it (contract §3.7 E10, hs-d356). It appends no `error` Event itself: the engine's `report` does.

```json
{"ok": true, "session": "596d007f-…", "title": "Dynamic session titles contract", "titled_at": "2026-10-20T09:12:41Z", "event": 4821, "pane": "%12"}
```

`pane` is the pane whose header was set, null when the Session has no live pane. A skip prints:

```json
{"ok": true, "session": "596d007f-…", "title": null, "skipped": "no_messages"}
```

(`"already"` is not used here: it means the same value was already stored and a retitle never compares.) Idempotent: yes: rerunning is safe and writes a new title each time (it never answers `"already"`).

### 10.15 `session first-message` (internal)

```
cpd session first-message [--session <id>]
```

`--session <id>` takes any form of §1.3. **Internal:** the pi adapter runs it at turn start for a by-user Lead or Manager Session whose `cpd-first-message` custom message has not yet been delivered (hs-d542 A3); the durable host runs it too, at startup, for a fresh non-by-user Lead or Manager whose conversation is empty, and submits the returned text as the first turn's input (hs-d812, contract §6.13 "Delivery (P1.4)" 3). Renders the first message at call time with the same functions `plan new` and `context manager` use (§4.1 step 3, §3.10), writes it to the session file's destination (`run/<plan>/lead-message.md` or `run/<context>/manager-message.md`) and prints JSON for the adapter to add the message to the run (§15).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session exists | `session_not_found` | 4 |
| it is a `lead` or a `manager`; a Worker is refused `not_a_lead` | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| the Session is a Lead of a Plan or is a Manager (not a side fork) | `not_a_lead` | 3 |

Effects:
- **Files**, one write: render the first message (contract §4.6 "Consumers", hs-d194 D6) and write it to `run/<plan>/lead-message.md` (for a Plan Lead) or `run/<context>/manager-message.md` (for a Manager), overwriting if it exists (hs-d542 A3: a by-user Session has no first message written at registration, so this is the first write).
- **Rows:** none. No database write, no Event appended.
- **tmux:** none.

Output: JSON with the rendered message text and metadata for the adapter to add it to the run.

```json
{"ok": true, "session": "596d007f-…", "role": "lead", "text": "You are the Lead of Plan …", "file": "/home/clayton/.cpd/run/pay-4521/lead-message.md", "event": 4820}
```

`role` is `lead` or `manager`. `text` is the rendered first message content. `file` is the path where it was written. `event` is the highest Event id at rendering (hs-d542 A3: for the pi adapter to track delivered messages, §15.7).

Idempotent: yes; rerunning renders the message again (the same if no Events occurred, different if the Context's records or Plans changed); the adapter tracks delivery by `details.event` and the fork-safe rule (§15.2 step 4, §15.7).

### 10.16 `session retier`

```
cpd session retier [--all | <id> [--tier <T>]]
```

Moves live Leads and Managers to the Tier the config names for them now (hs-d506: the User sets `lead_tier` and `manager_tier` and every running Session must follow, not only those registered later; pro-d139, pro-d140). With `--tier <T>` it instead moves the one Session `<id>` to `<T>` (pro-d142, below). **A Session's `tier` is not fixed at registration** (contract §2.2 Session): this command is the one that changes it. Workers are not touched: a Worker's Tier is its Job's (contract §9).

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | one Session (any form of §1.3) |
| `--all` | every Lead and Manager that is not archived |
| `--tier <T>` | with `<id>` only: the Tier the Session moves to instead of its target (below). With `--all`, or without `<id>`, it is `usage` |

Exactly one of the two: neither, or both, is `usage` (exit 2). `--tier` with `--all` is `usage` too (a clap conflict: nothing is changed) and so is `--tier` without `<id>`.

**The target.** A Session of role `lead` (a Plan's Lead and a side fork alike) moves to the config's `lead_tier`; one of role `manager` to `manager_tier` (contract §8.2; `review_lead_tier` is removed, pro-d328 to pro-d332, superseding pro-d139 and pro-d140). A later retier without `--tier` moves a Session to its target again, so a `--tier` override is reset by it.

**`--tier <T>`** (pro-d142). The one Session `<id>` moves to `<T>` instead of its target, with no config change. `<T>` is checked before anything is written, in the order of `plan new --tier` (§4.1): a bad syntax, or an effort the catalog lacks for the Tier's model (the models of the Session's Context, contract §8.3; the catalog is read only when `--tier` is given), is `tier_invalid` (exit 2); a Tier outside the lead range (a Lead) or the manager range (the Manager, from `manager_tier` up to the top valid rung; contract §9 "Roles and ranges") is `tier_not_allowed` (exit 2), with the `details` of §4.1 (`role` `lead` or `manager`, `key` `lead_tier` or `manager_tier`). A Worker is never retiered (`not_a_lead`, above). A refusal changes nothing. A Session already on `<T>` is unchanged (`already`).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session exists (`<id>`) | `session_not_found` | 4 |
| it is a `lead` or a `manager`; a Worker is refused, its Tier is its Job's | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| it is not archived; `details.next` = `cpd session unarchive <id>` | `archived` | 3 |
| `--tier` (with `<id>`): a bad syntax, or an effort the catalog lacks for the Tier's model (`details.efforts`) | `tier_invalid` | 2 |
| `--tier` is outside the lead range (a Lead, §4.1) or the manager range (the Manager); `details` `{tier, role, floor, ceiling, allowed, key}`, `key` `lead_tier` or `manager_tier` (contract §9 "Roles and ranges") | `tier_not_allowed` | 2 |

`--all` refuses nothing for a Session it passes over: archived Sessions and Workers are not part of it and are not listed.

**Effects**, one transaction for the whole command:
- **Rows:** for each selected Session whose `tier` differs from its target, `sessions.tier` = the target (the store's history trigger records the old row) and `sessions.switch_failed = NULL` (DEFECT 2: a new target is a new attempt; any earlier failed switch is stale).
- **Event** `session-retiered` `{from, to}` for each such Session, one each, addressed to it (`session` set, with its `context` and `plan` when it has one), appended in the same transaction. `from` and `to` are Tier strings (`O3`, `O2`). `text`: `Session <id> moved from O3 to O2.`
- A Session already on its target is **unchanged**: no row write, no Event. When no Session changes, nothing is written at all.
- **No tmux call and no pi restart.** A running pi switches itself (below); a Session with no pi keeps the new `tier` for its next start (§10.8).

**The adapter's switch** (contract §5.3, §6.5; commands §15.3 `session-retiered`). The Event reaches the adapter of the Session it names. **At the Session's next idle** (right away when it already is) the adapter reads `cpd session show` for the Session's `model` and `thinking` (§10.2), finds the model in pi's registry (`ctx.modelRegistry.find(<provider>, <model-id>)`, the provider being the part of `model` before its first `/`) and calls `pi.setModel(<that model>)` and `pi.setThinkingLevel(<thinking>)`, once per change and never while the Session works, waits or is blocked: no turn is interrupted and nothing is restarted and the conversation stays whole (docs: pi 1.3.0 `extensions.md`, `ExtensionAPI.setModel` "for the current session without changing the configured default"). Several Events before one idle make one switch, to what the row says at that idle. When the model is not found, `setModel` throws or answers false (DEFECT 2), the adapter runs `cpd session switch-failed --code model_unavailable --message "<text>"` in addition to its existing error report (§10.18); after `setModel` accepts and the thinking level is set it runs `cpd session switched`, so `session show` clears the failed switch record and the Lead sees success.

**A durable host's switch** (contract §6.18 "Retier"; User decision D2, pro-d430). A durable Lead's or Manager's host applies a retier only when it is idle with nothing queued. A retier whose Event finds the host busy (a run pending, or input queued) changes no model or thinking level and is not held for a later idle: the host runs `cpd session switch-failed --code host_busy --message "<text>"` (§10.18a), `<text>` naming the busy state. `host_busy` replaces `model_unavailable` for this case; `model_unavailable` stays for a model the host does not offer or that its `configure` rejects. `switch_failed` names `host_busy` until `session switched` clears it (§10.18b).

```json
{"ok": true, "retiered": [
  {"session": "596d007f-…", "role": "lead", "from": "O3", "to": "O2", "event": 48214},
  {"session": "9a41c0de-…", "role": "manager", "from": "O5", "to": "O4", "event": 48215}],
 "unchanged": ["0c77e1b2-…"]}
```

`unchanged` lists the ids of the selected Sessions already on their target. `"already": true` is added (and `retiered` is `[]`) when nothing changed. Per Session: `session` (id), `role`, `from`, `to` and `event` (the id of its Event).

Idempotent: yes; run again, nothing changes (`"already": true`). With `--tier`, a rerun is the same. A later `session retier` without `--tier` moves the Session to the config's target again: the override is not sticky.

### 10.18 `session report` (internal)

```
cpd session report --what <text> --code <code> --message <text> [--details <json>] [--session <id>]
```

Reports an adapter error to the Manager (hs-d573, M4). Its callers are: **the adapter of a Lead**, for every error it hits (not to its chat, M3), once per distinct (`what`, `code`), keyed by `host.report`'s memory in pi/lib/host.ts; **the adapter of any role** (a Manager's or a Worker's too) for `mcp_register_failed` (pro-d226; §15.1 'Errors'), for every refused registration, with `--what 'mcp attach <name>'`, and for `skills_unreadable` (pro-d260; §15.23), with `--what 'skills check'`; and **the adapter of any role** for every refusal of its guards (contract §5.2; §15.13, §15.16, §15.17, §15.27): with `--kind protocol-breach` and the breach's flags below, so the ledger holds one `protocol-breach` Event for the refusal, every protocol's breach logged with its protocol name (D14, air-d119). `mcp_register_failed` is exempt from the memory, so each refusal is one call; `skills_unreadable` is not, so it is one call per start. No other code is called by a Manager's or a Worker's adapter. A failed call is one log line, `report failed:`, never reported again (L4, §15.1 'Errors', §15.6 'Log').

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--what <text>` | what failed (1–2000 characters); `code` and `message` are from the error; combined as `cpd adapter: <what>: <code>: <message>` in the Event's `text` |
| `--code <code>` | error code (the adapter's code, not a command's exit code): `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`, else `usage` |
| `--message <text>` | error message (1–2000 characters), else `usage` |
| `--details <json>` | additional details as a JSON object, else `usage`; the report adds `what`, `session` and `plan` (null if the Lead's Plan is none) |
| `--session <id>` | the Session reporting the error, in any form of §1.3; default `CPD_SESSION` (§1.3) |
| `--kind <kind>` | the breach leg (below): `protocol-breach` only, else `usage`; without it the command is the `error` report above |
| `--protocol <name>` | with `--kind protocol-breach`: the breached protocol, one of the guarded protocol names `bug report`, `primary checkout`, `secrets`, `external approval`, `questions stay short` (contract §5.2), else `usage` |
| `--source <name>` | with `--kind protocol-breach`: the emitting guard, one of `mainguard`, `secretguard`, `externalguard`, `askguard`, else `usage` |
| `--tool <name>` | with `--kind protocol-breach`: the refused tool's name (`bash`, `edit`, `write`, `ask_user_question`), else `usage` |
| `--command <text>` | with `--kind protocol-breach`: the refused call's first line, at most 200 characters; omitted (stored null) when the refused call has no command line — an `ask_user_question` has none; over 200 characters is `usage` |

**The breach leg** (D14, air-d119; contract §5.2). With `--kind protocol-breach` the command appends one `protocol-breach` Event instead of an `error` Event: `data` `{protocol, source, role, model, tier, tool, command}` — `role`, `model` and `tier` are not flags, the command reads them from the reporting Session's row; `context`, `plan` and `session` are the reporting Session's own Context, Plan and id, not the DEFECT-1 null of the `error` leg (a breach is a ledger record, not an error echo); `text` is the guard's refusal reason, given as `--message`. The idempotence window compares `protocol`, `tool` and `command` instead of `code` and `message`. Every flag of the leg is required except `--command`, `usage` (exit 2) when a value is missing or not in its list.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session exists | `session_not_found` | 4 |

Effects: **Rows**, one transaction: `events` (one `error` Event, none when the same one is in the window (below), source `adapter`; context = the Session's Context; **session = the reporting Session, plan null** (DEFECT 1: so the Manager can identify which Session failed; the follower rule of §11.2 excludes adapter-source errors from any Session's follower, so a Lead does not see its own adapter errors); data `{source: "adapter", code, message, details}` with `details` = the given object plus `{what, session, plan}`; text `cpd adapter: <what>: <code>: <message>`). Idempotent inside the window (contract §3.7): a call whose `code` and `message` equal those of an adapter `error` Event of the same Session appended less than `watch.error_repeat_seconds` ago appends nothing and prints that Event's id; any other call appends an Event. `what` and `details` are not compared. The `mcp_register_failed` exemption above is from the adapter's own memory: each refusal is still one call, and its Event follows this window.

Output:

```json
{"ok": true, "event": "4823"}
```

`event` is the id of the Event that reports the error: the new one, or the earlier identical one of the window.

**A report of a refusal carries the `guard` kind** (contract §5.2, Plan `agent-refusals`): when the report is a refusal of the reporting Session's own tool call or command — an adapter guard refusal (a `toolResult` whose text starts with `φ: ` and whose `details` are empty) or an agent-caused CLI refusal (the `{"ok":false,"error":{…}}` envelope) — the appended Event is a `guard` Event instead of an `error` Event, with `data` `{code, role, tier, model, tool, excerpt}` (`code` the guard rule or the envelope's error code, `excerpt` the refused command line or path cut to 200 characters) and the scope columns of the reporting Session; the dedupe window above is the same, matched on `code` and `excerpt` instead of `code` and `message`. Any other report keeps the `error` kind exactly as the Effects above state.

### 10.18a `session switch-failed` (internal)

```
cpd session switch-failed --code <code> --message <text> [--session <id>]
```

Records a failed model switch (DEFECT 2): the adapter of a Lead runs this when `setModel` fails (the three `unavailable` paths), to record the failure for the Lead to see in `session show` and to help it relaunch pi. The `next` hint that `session show` derives from the record (§10.2) is a `cpd session run <id>` command and is given only to a `pi` Session; a `durable` Session has no pane, so its `switch` has no `next` key (§10.2, test `session_retier::a_durable_sessions_switch_failure_has_no_next_hint`).

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--code <code>` | error code (the adapter's code): `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`, else `usage` |
| `--message <text>` | error message (1–2000 characters), else `usage` |
| `--session <id>` | the Session whose switch failed, in any form of §1.3; default `CPD_SESSION` (§1.3) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session exists | `session_not_found` | 4 |
| it is a `lead` or a `manager`, never a Worker | `not_a_lead` | 3 |

Effects: **Rows**, one transaction: `sessions.switch_failed = {tier, code, message, at}`, where `tier` is the row's current `tier`, `code` and `message` are the given values and `at` is the current RFC 3339 UTC time. No Event. Idempotent: yes; rerunning with the same or different code/message overwrites the existing `switch_failed` (the latest failure stands).

Output:

```json
{"ok": true, "session": "596d007f-…"}
```

### 10.18b `session switched` (internal)

```
cpd session switched [--session <id>]
```

Records a successful model switch (DEFECT 2): the adapter of a Lead runs this after `setModel` accepts and the thinking level is set, to clear the failure record.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--session <id>` | the Session whose switch succeeded, in any form of §1.3; default `CPD_SESSION` (§1.3) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session exists | `session_not_found` | 4 |
| it is a `lead` or a `manager`, never a Worker | `not_a_lead` | 3 |

Effects: **Rows**, one transaction: `sessions.switch_failed = NULL`. No Event. Idempotent: yes; rerunning does nothing when `switch_failed` is already null.

Output:

```json
{"ok": true, "session": "596d007f-…"}
```


### 10.17 `session resume`

```
cpd session resume <id>
```

Resumes a Lead or a Manager Session that is blocked by the loop guard, appending an Event and delivering one message with a turn (L6 of hs-d552, hs-d571). `<id>` accepts any form of §1.3. Only the User and the engine resume: an agent is refused (pro-d374).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the caller has `CPD_SESSION` or `CPD_ATTEMPT` set and non-empty (an agent); `details` `{command: "session resume", session, attempt}`, `session` and `attempt` the values of those variables or `null`; the check and message are §1.3's `agent_forbidden`, refused before the Ledger is opened | `agent_forbidden` | 3 |
| the Session exists | `session_not_found` | 4 |
| it is a `lead` or a `manager` | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| it is not archived; `details.next` = `cpd session unarchive <id>` | `archived` | 3 |
| it is `blocked` with the label `φ: loop guard`; `details` `{state, label}` | `not_loop_guarded` | 3 |

Effects:
- **Rows**, one transaction: nothing is written to the Session.
- **Event** `session-resumed` (session = the target, context and plan = the target's), `data` `{}`, `text` `Loop guard of Session <id> resumed.`. The adapter clears the trip (L5): empties the window, closes the blocking reason, appends the pi session entry `{tripped: false}` and delivers ONE message with a turn (the Event's text, `followUp`), so one turn starts.
- **tmux:** none.

```json
{"ok": true, "event": 4816, "session": "a41b…"}
```

`event` is the id of the `session-resumed` Event. Idempotent: no; each call is one Event. A second call finds the Session no longer blocked once the adapter has acted.

### 10.19 `session tail` (P1.11)

```
cpd session tail <id>
```

The read path of a live durable Lead's or Manager's transcript (contract §6.20; the research's Q33 Decided A): it connects to the Session host's socket (§6.14, protocol 2), folds the frames onto the pi-durable `ConversationView` (its base `view` frame and its `ops` frames) and prints the transcript as plain lines, then follows the host live. It writes nothing — no row, no Event, no tmux, never the store (the host is the one owner of the store; the socket is the tail's only path). It never sends `submit`, `abort`, `detach` or `ping` to the host: read-only.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | the target Session (any form of §1.3) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session exists | `session_not_found` | 4 |
| it is a `lead` or a `manager` | `not_a_lead` | 3 |
| it is not archived; `details.next` = `cpd session unarchive <id>` (an archived Session has no host: the stop hooks of contract §6.19 stopped it) | `archived` | 3 |
| its `runner` is `durable`; a `pi` Session has no host socket, and its pane is read in tmux, not over a socket. Message: `Session <id> runs on pi: it has no host socket to tail. Open it with cpd session open.` | `no_host_socket` | 3 |
| the socket path `$CPD_HOME/run/host/<id>.sock` is at most `SOCKET_PATH_MAX` (107) bytes (contract §6.14 step 1, applied symmetrically) | `usage` (`socket_path_too_long`) | 2 |

Effects:
- **Startup:** the client (contract §6.20) connects through the `HostConn` port, sends `hello` (`protocol: 2`, `min_protocol: 2`, `client: "cpd session tail"`), attaches without a cursor, and prints the transcript of the base `view` frame: the window the host's watch starts with, the newest 50 entries (up to 100), so a long transcript shows its recent part; earlier entries are read with `cpd session history` (§10.12). One line per completed message, the grammar of contract §6.20 (`user: `, `assistant: `, `system: `, `tool <toolName>: <text>` with ` (error)` on a failed tool result; a text with newlines prints one line per source line, the prefix on the first line only; thinking stays unprinted; bookkeeping entries are silent).
- **Follow:** every live `ops` frame prints the entries it appends, as they complete. The message still streaming is not printed until its entry is appended. When the window moved past entries the tail had not printed (a gap), one line on stderr names the gap and the tail goes on.
- **Reconnect:** on `bye {reconnect: true}` (`shutdown`, `restart`, `storage_failed`, `slow_client`) or a lost socket it reconnects and attaches with the cursor, napping on the back-off of §10.4's wait (100 ms doubling to a 1 s cap, a 30 s deadline — design defaults, not measured); past the deadline the command ends `host_timeout`, exit 5, `details: {session, socket}`. A new epoch re-attaches in view mode: the fold replaces its replica, prints the entries it has not printed and writes one line on stderr (`view <epoch> seq <seq>: view replaced`), so the stream never repeats a line it printed.
- **End:** exit 0 when its stdout closes (EPIPE, as §11.2's follower ends), when it reads a `bye` with `reconnect: false` (none of the host's reasons can reach a tail that never detaches; the branch ends the stream cleanly), or on SIGINT/SIGTERM.
- **Rows / Events / tmux:** none.

Output: plain lines on stdout, one per transcript line, nothing else (§1.2's exception list gains the row; diagnostics go to stderr). Example:

```
user: run the checks
assistant: Running them now.
tool bash: all checks pass
assistant: All green. Ready for review.
```

Idempotent: reading only; the same transcript renders the same lines (the base view's rendering is deterministic); the lines a live stream prints depend on when the frames arrive.

## 10a. `board` (hs-d514)

The message board: a SQLite table whose posts name who they are for (to), read by `cpd board list` and picked up at an agent's turn start by `cpd board take`. Posts are written by `cpd board post` and never start a turn (hs-d514). Important facts stay Context records.

### 10a.1 `board post`

```
cpd board post <text> --to <ref>
```

Post a message to the board. It appends no Event and never starts a turn (hs-d514). The message is addressed to a Session (the target's context is the message's context).

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<text>` | the message, a `Text` (1–2000 characters) |
| `--to <ref>` | the target: `manager`, the alias for the live Manager of the sender's Context (else `no_manager`), or any form of §1.3 (a Plan id names that Plan's Lead Session). A Lead of a Plan in phase `done` or `archived` is refused `plan_inactive` whatever the form |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `<text>` is 1–2000 characters | `usage` | 2 |
| the target Session exists (resolved from `<ref>`); when `<ref>` is `manager` and there is no live Manager, refusal `no_manager` | `session_not_found` | 4 |
| `<ref>` resolves to a Lead of a Plan in phase `done` or `archived`, whatever the form of §1.3 (hs-d514); `details: {plan, phase}` | `plan_inactive` | 3 |

Effects:
- **Rows**, one transaction: **Row** `board_posts`: `at`, `context` (target's), `from_session` (sender's Session or null), `to_session` (target), `text`, `read_at` (null); `id` is auto-incremented.
- **Events:** none. It does not append any Event.
- **tmux:** none.

```json
{"ok": true, "session": "a41b…", "context": "inbox", "posted_at": "2026-10-21T15:30:00.000Z"}
```

Idempotent: no; each call is one post.

### 10a.2 `board list`

```
cpd board list [--session <id>] [--all]
```

List posts to a Session. By default, unread posts only (`read_at` null), oldest first (hs-d514).

Every post carries `from_name` (in `board list` and `board take`): the sender Session's current `sessions.name` (its agent key for a Manager, a Lead that is not a fork and a Worker; `contract §2.2 "Agent key"`), or null when `from_session` is null (the User). The adapter shows a post's sender by it (§15.7).

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--session <id>` | the target Session (default: `$CPD_SESSION`); accepts any form of §1.3 |
| `--all` | show all posts, including read ones (`read_at` is not null) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session exists | `session_not_found` | 4 |

Effects:
- **Rows:** none.
- **Events:** none.
- **tmux:** none.

```json
{"ok": true, "session": "a41b…", "posts": [{"id": 142, "at": "2026-10-21T15:30:00.000Z", "from_session": "596d…", "from_name": "building-cpd:cpd2", "text": "PR #207 opened", "read_at": null}, {"id": 143, "at": "2026-10-21T15:31:00.000Z", "from_session": null, "from_name": null, "text": "Inbox item closed", "read_at": null}]}
```

Idempotent: yes; the same list each run.

### 10a.3 `board take` (internal)

```
cpd board take --session <id>
```

Return and mark as read the unread posts to a Session (internal, the adapter's message picker at turn start, commands.md §15.7, hs-d514). In the same transaction, the rows' `read_at` are set to `now`.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--session <id>` | the target Session; accepts any form of §1.3 |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the Session exists | `session_not_found` | 4 |

Effects:
- **Rows**, one transaction: **update** every `board_posts` row with `to_session` = the target and `read_at` null, setting `read_at = now`.
- **Events:** none.
- **tmux:** none.

```json
{"ok": true, "session": "a41b…", "taken": [{"id": 142, "at": "2026-10-21T15:30:00.000Z", "from_session": "596d…", "from_name": "building-cpd:cpd2", "text": "PR #207 opened"}, {"id": 143, "at": "2026-10-21T15:31:00.000Z", "from_session": null, "from_name": null, "text": "Inbox item closed"}]}
```

`from_name` is as in `board list` (§10a.2).

Idempotent: yes; the second call returns an empty list and updates nothing.

## 11. `events`

§5. Selection: `--plan <id>`, `--context <id>` or `--session <id>`, at most one (`usage`), or none for every Event; `--kind <kind>` may repeat (a kind not in §5.2 is `usage`). These flags are filters: they do not fall back to `CPD_PLAN` or `CPD_SESSION`.

`--session <id>` takes any form of §1.3 and applies §5.3's rule, with "a Lead of Plan P" made precise (amendment 7, §19):
- for the Session that is its Plan's `lead_session`: Events with `plan` = its Plan; Events with `plan IS NULL AND context` = its Context; Events with `session` = itself;
- for any other Session (Workers, side forks): Events with `session` = itself;
- for a Manager (B3-A5): Events with `session` = itself only, so a Plan's Events never wake it (hs-d86). It reads them itself at turn start (§15.7). A Manager of a Lead-less Plan also receives the engine's `session-message` for each `job-merged`, `job-failed` and `escalation` Event of that Plan (contract §5.3); the Plan's own Events are still not routed to it.

The kinds `attempt-ended` and `job-blocked` and the `error` code `worker_stalled` (hs-d798, contract §5.2, §3.4) are read like any other kind: `--kind attempt-ended`, `--kind job-blocked`, `--kind error`. `attempt-ended` carries the `attempts.metrics` blob that `cpd metrics` (§14.7) aggregates.

The kind `guard` (contract §5.2) is read like any other kind too: `cpd events list --kind guard` lists every refusal, scoped by `--plan`, `--context` or `--session` (§1.3), `--since` and `--limit` as always, and `cpd events follow --kind guard` streams them. One Event per guard Event row; its `data` carries the refusal's own fields, so a ranking per guard, role, model and day is an aggregation over these rows:

```json
{"id": 48216, "at": "2026-11-08T03:10:00.000Z", "kind": "guard", "context": "building-cpd", "plan": "cpd2", "job": "ev-docs", "attempt": "ev-docs-a1", "session": "9f2e…", "text": "Worker ev-docs-a1 refused: explore network write: scout has no network: git fetch", "data": {"code": "explore network write", "role": "worker", "tier": "H3", "model": "github-copilot/gpt-5", "tool": "bash", "excerpt": "git fetch origin agent-refusals/miner"}}
```

`data.code` separates the two refusal families: a guard rule (`explore network write`, `loop guard`, `primary-checkout`, …) for an adapter guard refusal, a CLI error code (`usage`, `spec_invalid`, `shape_violation`, …) for an agent-caused CLI refusal. To rank one code across the store: `cpd events list --kind guard --context <c> | jq '[.events[] | select(.data.code == "spec_invalid")] | length'`. The repeat dedupe (contract §5.2) shapes what the rows mean: one row per refusal episode, at most one per (`session`, `code`, `excerpt`) per `watch.error_repeat_seconds` window, never one per raw refusal.

### 11.1 `events list`

```
cpd events list [--plan <id> | --context <id> | --session <id>] [--kind <kind>]… [--since <id>] [--limit <n>]
```

`--session <id>` takes any form of §1.3. `--since` is exclusive and defaults to 0; `--limit` defaults to 500 (1–5000). Effects: none.

```json
{"ok": true, "events": [{"id": 48214, "at": "…", "kind": "job-merged", "context": "building-cpd", "plan": "cpd2", "job": "contract-core", "attempt": "contract-core-a1", "session": null,
  "text": "Job contract-core merged at c0ffee1 (Tier O3). Next: cpd plan show", "data": {"sha": "c0ffee1…", "tier": "O3"}}], "next": 48214}
```

`next` is the id of the last Event returned, or `--since` when none; pass it as the next `--since`. Idempotent: read-only.

### 11.2 `events follow`

```
cpd events follow [--plan <id> | --context <id> | --session <id>] [--kind <kind>]… [--since <id>] [--until-idle]
```

`--session <id>` takes any form of §1.3. §5.4, normative: one Event per line, in id order; without `--since`, only Events committed after it starts; polling `PRAGMA data_version` every `events.poll_ms`; ends on EPIPE, on kill, or when its stdout is closed (`POLLHUP` or `POLLERR` on fd 1, checked at each poll, so an idle stream whose reader is gone still ends), with exit 0, or with `--until-idle` once it has printed everything committed when it started.

**Stale Events** (pro-d214): a `--session` follower drops a `plan-done`, `pr-feedback`, `job-failed`, `escalation`, `error` or `attempt-nudge` Event whose condition a later Event or the Workflow's stored state proves over; the table, the fail-open rule and the cursor are in contract §5.4 and `--plan`, `--context`, unscoped follows and `events list` are unchanged.

**Adapter-source error Events** (DEFECT 1): a Lead's follower (`--session` with a Lead Session) and any other Session's follower (`--session` with any non-Lead Session) skip `error` Events whose `data.source` is `adapter`, so a Session does not see its own adapter error. The Manager can read all Events (no `--session` filter applied, or `--context` filter), including adapter-source errors with their `session` field naming which Session failed.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the selected Plan, Context or Session exists | `plan_not_found`, `context_not_found`, `session_not_found` | 4 |
| `--since` is not above the highest Event id (a cursor from another database) | `cursor_ahead` | 3 |

**A migration in progress is waited out** (hs-n278; contract §4.2, §1.4): when it opens the store, or reopens it, while another cpd is migrating it, it waits, up to `MIGRATION_WAIT_CEILING` (10 minutes) and prints one line on stderr (`waiting for cpd pid <pid> to migrate the store <from> -> <to> (<command>)`), nothing on stdout; it does not fail `lock_timeout` for it, so an install never ends a follower.

**Any other store error ends it** (hs-d140; contract §5.4): `store_too_new` after an upgrade (the verdict of contract §4.5, which the follower recomputes when `PRAGMA schema_version` changes), `migration_changed`, `migration_order`, `store_busy`, `store_failed`, … is printed as the last line, as the failure envelope and the process exits with that code's exit (§1.2); it never stays alive on a store it cannot read. The pi adapter restarts a follower that ends (§15.2).

**Re-exec** (hs-d140; contract §5.4): between polls it checks its executable path with `core/src/host/exe.rs`'s `(device, inode, mtime)` check, as `session run` and `attempt run` do (hs-d55); when it changed it re-execs itself with the same argv except `--since`, set to the id of the last Event it printed (none printed: the cursor it started from), so no follower outlives an install. `cockpit serve` restarts in place the same way (§11a "Restart on a new install", pro-d450). Each line:

```json
{"id": 48215, "at": "2026-10-14T21:41:02.114Z", "kind": "escalation", "context": "building-cpd", "plan": "cpd2", "job": "contract-commands", "attempt": "contract-commands-a1", "session": null, "text": "Worker contract-commands-a1 asks: … Answer: cpd answer contract-commands-a1-q1 \"<answer>\"", "data": {"escalation": "contract-commands-a1-q1", "question": "…"}}
```

Idempotent: read-only; the same `--since` replays the same lines.

## 11a. `cockpit serve`

The WebUI backend's state and event stream (Plan `cpd-realtime-engine`; its invariants are contract §5.5). One process replaces the backend's spawns: the four list commands and `plan show` that it ran on every refresh, and the `events follow` child whose lines triggered them. A committed change reaches the stream without a spawn.

```
cpd cockpit serve
```

No flags and no arguments; any argument is `usage` (exit 2). Callers: none. The WebUI backend (`web/src/server/`) starts it once and keeps it; it is not a command an agent or the User types, and not a cockpit action (§2). It reads requests on stdin and writes frames on stdout, one JSON object per line, each with a string field `t`. stderr carries logs only. It binds no socket and no port: the frames reach the renderer over the WebUI backend's own WebSocket transport, one endpoint on loopback (contract §5.5 "The WebUI transport and the serve-stream watchdog", air-d46) — not over any channel of this command.

**Liveness as seen by the WebUI backend.** The backend keeps this command under two watchers that run whatever the stream's ready state says (contract §5.5, same section): the transport heartbeat, which sees the WebSocket socket, and the serve-stream watchdog, which sees this command's frames. The watchdog writes a `refresh` request on stdin every `STREAM_PROBE_MS` while the stream is connected, and reads the answer inside `STREAM_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`: any frame of any `t` answers it, and the answering `snapshot`'s `seq` must advance past the last `seq` seen from this process — each snapshot advances `seq` ("`seq`", below), so a `refresh` answered with a `seq` that does not advance is a process that no longer serves. A window with no frame, or a `seq` that does not advance, is a stall: the backend reports it loud, resyncs the panes by spawn, and restarts this child if it is still silent, with the restart backoff. A `hello` of the in-place restart below starts a new generation, so snapshot 1 is fresh, never read as a non-advance. The backend does not restart or probe on its own beyond this: a malformed line and a failed request keep the process serving (below), and only the watchdog turns silence into a restart.

**Lifecycle.** It opens the store as `cpd events follow` does (§11.2: it waits out a migration in progress), once, as one Env (its store, home and ports). Every snapshot pane and every `plan_show` reply is read through that same open Env: `serve` never reads `$CPD_HOME` after start and never opens another store connection per snapshot (contract §5.5). It then writes `hello`, writes snapshot 1 and sets its cursor to the highest Event id, so no Event before the start is replayed: the first snapshot carries the state. It serves until stdin reaches end of file, then exits 0. The parent's death closes stdin, so the process never outlives its parent.

**Restart on a new install** (pro-d450; hs-d140; §11.2 "Re-exec"). On each tick it checks its own executable path with the `(device, inode, mtime)` check of `core/src/host/exe.rs`, as `events follow` does between polls; the same check runs first when a request line arrives, before the line is answered. When the executable was replaced, it execs the replacement in place as `<that path> cockpit serve`, with the same pid and pipes: the new process starts a fresh serve, says `hello` and writes snapshot 1 (`seq` starts at 1 again, and no Event is replayed). It does the same on a `store_too_new` while the executable is replaced, and writes no error frame then, on three paths: the store read of a batch; a `plan_show` that fails with `store_too_new`; and a pane read in a snapshot that fails with `store_too_new` (the snapshot then carries no error: none is written). While the executable is unchanged, these keep their behaviour: a `store_too_new` from the store read of a batch still ends serve with the error frame below; a failed `plan_show` gets its `error` frame and serve goes on; a failed pane read is embedded in its snapshot as before.

### Frames out

| `t` | When | Frame |
|---|---|---|
| `hello` | first, once per process (also first in the process that restarts in place, above) | `{"t":"hello","protocol":1}` |
| `snapshot` | after `hello`; after every batch of committed changes; on `refresh` | `{"t":"snapshot","seq":<n>,"panes":{"context":V,"plan":V,"session":V,"inbox":V}}` |
| `event` | each newly committed Event, before the snapshot that follows it | `{"t":"event","event":E}` |
| `plan_show` | the answer to a `plan_show` request | `{"t":"plan_show","id":"<request id>","value":V}` |
| `error` | a malformed line, an unknown `t`, a failed request, or the store error that ends the process (below) | `{"t":"error","id":"<request id or null>","error":{"code":"<code>","message":"<text>"}}` |

- **The panes** `context`, `plan`, `session` and `inbox` are V = the JSON value that `cpd context list`, `cpd plan list`, `cpd session list` and `cpd inbox list` print (same function, same fields, `ok` included). A failure value of one of them is that pane's value, not an `error` frame. Each snapshot is full: no diffs.
- **`seq`** counts this process's snapshots from 1; a new process starts at 1 again.
- **`E`** is exactly the object one line of `cpd events follow` prints (§11.2), for every Event: the command takes no selection flags.
- **`value`** of `plan_show` is V = exactly what `cpd plan show --plan <id>` prints.

Each frame is one line, written and flushed when it is produced, in the order it is produced.

### Frames in

| `t` | Shape | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `plan_show` | `{"t":"plan_show","id":"<request id>","plan":"<plan id>"}` | a `plan_show` frame with the same `id`; or, when `cpd plan show --plan <id>` would print a failure value, an `error` frame with the same `id` and that value's code and message |
| `refresh` | `{"t":"refresh"}` | one snapshot at once, with the next `seq`, and no `event` frame |

`id` is a string the caller chooses; it is echoed unchanged. A request's fields are exactly those of its `t`: any other field is an error.

### Batches and latency

- Changes are found by polling `PRAGMA data_version` every `POLL_MS` = 10 ms. (`cpd events follow` polls at `events.poll_ms`, 200 ms by default, §11.2.)
- A change starts a batch. Every change seen within `COALESCE_MS` = 16 ms of the batch's first change joins it. The batch goes out as one `event` frame per Event with an id above the last one sent, in id order, then one snapshot.
- Commit to frame: at most `POLL_MS` + `COALESCE_MS` plus the time to read the four panes (unmeasured).

### Errors

| Trigger | `error.code` | `id` |
|---|---|---|
| a line that is not one JSON object, or whose `t` is missing or not a string | `usage` | the request's `id` when the object has a string one, else `null` |
| an unknown `t`, or a field its `t` does not take | `usage` | the request's `id` when it has a string one, else `null` |
| `plan_show` whose `id` or `plan` is missing or not a string | `usage` | `null` |
| `plan_show` for which `cpd plan show --plan <id>` would print a failure value (`plan_not_found`, exit 4; `invalid_plan_id`, exit 2; a store code) | that value's code | the request's `id` |

These keep the process serving. A **store error** that ends `cpd events follow` (§11.2: `store_too_new`, `migration_changed`, `migration_order`, `store_busy`, `store_failed`, …) ends this command too, the same way, except a `store_too_new` while the executable is replaced (restart above). `serve` does not track `PRAGMA schema_version`: each batch it flushes recomputes the store verdict (contract §4.5), so it ends at the first batch flushed after a migration it cannot read; `events follow` recomputes the verdict at its next poll after the schema changes. Its last line is `{"t":"error","id":null,"error":{"code":"<code>","message":"<text>"}}` and it exits with that code's exit. A store that cannot be opened at the start ends it before `hello`, with the same last line.

| Exit | When | Codes |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | stdin reached end of file, or stdout closed (EPIPE) | |
| `1` | a store or config failure; a failed write to stdout other than EPIPE | `config_invalid`, `store_failed`, `migration_changed`, `migration_order`, `internal` |
| `2` | an argument was given | `usage` |
| `5` | the store was busy or a lock timed out | `store_busy`, `lock_timeout` |

Other store codes exit with the exit that §1.2 gives them. A malformed or failed request does not change the exit: it is an `error` frame, and the process goes on.

**Effects:** none. It writes no row, no Event, no file under `$CPD_HOME` and takes no lock. Idempotent in the sense that a restart starts again at `seq` 1 and replays no Event.

### Example session

`in` is stdin, `out` is stdout; `…` stands for the full value.

```
out {"t":"hello","protocol":1}
out {"t":"snapshot","seq":1,"panes":{"context":{"ok": true, …},"plan":{"ok": true, …},"session":{"ok": true, …},"inbox":{"ok": true, …}}}
in  {"t":"plan_show","id":"r1","plan":"cpd-realtime-engine"}
out {"t":"plan_show","id":"r1","value":{"ok": true, …}}
    (another process commits Event 48215)
out {"t":"event","event":{"id": 48215, "at": "2026-10-14T21:41:02.114Z", "kind": "escalation", "context": "building-cpd", "plan": "cpd2", "job": "contract-commands", "attempt": "contract-commands-a1", "session": null, "text": "Worker contract-commands-a1 asks: … Answer: cpd answer contract-commands-a1-q1 \"<answer>\"", "data": {"escalation": "contract-commands-a1-q1", "question": "…"}}}
out {"t":"snapshot","seq":2,"panes":{"context":{"ok": true, …},"plan":{"ok": true, …},"session":{"ok": true, …},"inbox":{"ok": true, …}}}
in  {"t":"refresh"}
out {"t":"snapshot","seq":3,"panes":{"context":{"ok": true, …},"plan":{"ok": true, …},"session":{"ok": true, …},"inbox":{"ok": true, …}}}
in  not json
out {"t":"error","id":null,"error":{"code":"usage","message":"…"}}
in  {"t":"plan_show","id":"r2","plan":"no-such-plan"}
out {"t":"error","id":"r2","error":{"code":"plan_not_found","message":"…"}}
    (the parent closes stdin)
    exit 0
```

## 12. `watch`

```
cpd watch [--ensure | --check]
```

(and the internal `cpd watch --restart-tmux`, `cpd watch --ensure --wait` and `cpd watch --mark-restart`, below)

The engine, one per machine (§3.7, §6.6, D5).

**Without `--ensure`:** runs the `@cpd_workers` step (below), then E1–E5, E7, E20, E21 and E8–E14 (E6 is removed; E4 is the `open` Jobs since hs-d340, no longer the completion step; E7, the Workflow start, since R34; E20, the parked drafts, after E7 and before E8 (hs-d731, contract §3.7 "Parked drafts"); E21, the closed-pull-request wake, right after E20 (contract §3.7); E25, the bug protocol, right after E21 (contract §3.7, air-d105); E8, the Inbox, §21; E9, the Context curation, since hs-d194 (hs-d549, hs-d551); E10, the Session titles, since hs-d257; E11, the team review read, §21.5; E12, the Worker archive, since hs-d516; E13, the Sleep, since hs-d515; E14, archive asleep Sessions and their Plans, hs-d630, pro-d391) (E23 is retired, pro-d388, contract §3.7; no Step sends a Slack message by itself) every `tick_seconds` (a decimal, minimum 0.1; default 5) in the foreground, in `cpd-work:watch`, logging to stderr and appending the same lines to `run/watch.log`.

E5 (the PR poll) runs at its due time, `pr_poll_seconds` after the previous poll ended (5 s by default), not at the next tick: the engine sleeps until the earlier of its next tick and E5's due time (contract §3.7). The pi stop grace is `timeouts.pi_stop_seconds` (default 10; contract §8.2).

**Two new signals** (hs-d798): E3 appends one `job-blocked` Event per waiting episode when the queue walk skips a Ready Job for want of a pool slot (contract §3.7 E3, §5.2); and a `durable` Attempt whose transcript has not grown for `timeouts.stall_minutes` (default 15) is reported by its driver with one `error` Event, code `worker_stalled`, per stall episode; it opens no Inbox item and wakes the Plan's Lead only (contract §3.4, §2.2). The engine does not act on the stall: the Lead decides.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `locks/watch.lock` is free | `watch_running` | 3 |

Effects: **Events** `watch-started` and `watch-stopped` `{pid}`, one `session-message` to each Manager that is not archived when this engine follows an earlier one (how long none ran, contract §3.7) and every row and Event of E1–E5 and E7–E14 (E3 starts nothing while a tmux restart is pending and the engine starts that restart once nothing is in the way, §3.7) (§3.7; a Workflow that E7 fails to start gets its own `error` with code `workflow_start_failed` and is not tried again, §9.7; a distill run E9 starts appends its own `error` when it fails, §3.12; a retitle run E10 starts (§10.14) appends its own `session-titled` when it succeeds and when it fails E10 reports one `error` with code `title_failed` for the Session). An unexpected failure in a step appends `error` `{source: "watch", code, message, details}` for the Plan it concerns and the loop continues; the same failure for the same object is appended once until it clears. It waits out a migration in progress when it opens the store (hs-n278; contract §3.7, §4.2): it does not fail `lock_timeout` and logs the one waiting line to `run/watch.log`. It runs until SIGTERM or SIGINT, or when its store outgrows the binary and it stands down (contract §3.7 "An engine whose store outgrew its binary stands down"), then prints `{"ok": true, "stopped": true}` and exits 0.
**The `@cpd_workers` step** (contract §6.1; User, hs-d149, hs-d198; hs-d749): on each tick the engine reads, in one read, `N` (the occupancy of the `workers` pool: its tenant Jobs, a `failed` Job and a retried `queued` Job included, contract §3.4 "Tenancy"), `M` (config `concurrency`), `W` (**waiting**: the Ready Jobs, §3.2, the ones E3 would start if a slot were free) and `Q` (**queued**: every Job with status `queued`, waiting ones included) and builds the StatusBar's texts: the long form `workers Q󰞘W󰞘N/M` and the short form `Q󰞘W󰞘N/M`; The status line measures their display widths using tmux's #{w:…} format modifier, so no width is computed in the engine. The workers' pill with its two caps `` and `` (the text's width plus 2; hs-d479, contract §6.1); plain text with no style (contract §6.1); the engine still computes no width (tmux's `#{w:…}` counts styles as 0 cells). It runs `tmux -L <socket> set -g @cpd_workers '<long>' ';' set -g @cpd_workers_short '<short>'` **only when a text changed** since the last tick it set (the first tick always sets them and so does the first tick after a tmux failure or a missing server: a restarted server starts without them). No row, no Event; a tmux failure of the step is no `error` Event while a tmux restart is pending and has not failed (§13.3: the restart takes the server away under the step), it is tried again at the next tick. The indicator is therefore up to one tick (`watch.tick_seconds`) late and stale while the engine is stopped; this deviates on purpose from §17's "no tmux option carries state".

**The `@cpd_runner` feed** (contract §6.1 "The runner pill"; pro-d199): in the same tick, the workers step reads `[experimental].durable_workers` from `$CPD_HOME/config.toml` afresh (`Config::load`, through `Config::worker_runner()`; `pi` when the key is absent) and sets `@cpd_runner` to `pi` or `durable` in the same tmux invocation as the workers texts (the `;`-joined `set -g` of each value that changed). It is part of the step's remembered state: it sets the option only when the value differs from the one it last set (the first tick always sets it and so does the first tick after a tmux failure or a missing server). A config that does not parse is an error of the step, reported through `engine.fail`; the step then sets nothing: no value is substituted for the unreadable one and the option keeps whatever it held until the file parses again.

Idempotent: a second one is refused.

**E3: Linear vs parallel Attempts** (pro-d52, hs-d680, hs-d682, hs-d683; contract §3.7 E3, §7.2, §7.4, A1). When E3 schedules a Ready Job of a Workflow each pass, it derives which Attempt runs as the linear one (the Workflow's only live Attempt for its whole life, reusing the Workflow's Lead worktree on its Lead Branch) and which as parallel siblings (each with its own worktree): by the rule of contract §3.7 E3, (1) if the Workflow has a live linear Attempt, no Ready Job starts; (2) if the Workflow has only live parallel Attempts, every Ready Job is parallel; (3) if no Attempt is live, one Ready Job is linear and the rest are parallel. E3 passes this allocation to the driver starter, which takes the driver lock and enforces it atomically before starting, ensuring no two Attempts can share the Lead worktree.

**With `--ensure`:** starts the engine when it is not running and returns at once. It fails and creates nothing when `$CPD_HOME` does not exist (hs-d519 3c/5, docs/research/hygiene.md, bug 3c/5).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `$CPD_HOME` exists | `watch_start_failed` | 1 |
| the window started and its process took the lock within 10 s | `watch_start_failed` | 1 |

Effects: probe `locks/watch.lock` (open and `flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)`, released at once). Free: start the server and `cpd-work` session if needed (§6.1), set the server options and hooks again on a running server (§6.1), respawn a dead `watch` pane in its window (killing the window of any other dead one), else `new-window -d -t =cpd-work: -n watch -c $CPD_HOME -P -F '#{pane_id}' -- cpd watch`. No rows. The engine itself appends its stderr to `run/watch.log` (§1.4), so no shell is needed.

```json
{"ok": true, "started": true, "pane": "%3"}
```

Idempotent: yes; a running engine gives `"started": false` with `"already": true`.

Every `--ensure`, plain or `--wait`, takes `locks/watch-ensure.lock` before it probes the engine's lock and holds it until it has started the engine, so two calls never start two windows. A plain call waits for it 30 s at most (a supervising call holds it up to 15 s + 10 s + 2 s) and then fails with `watch_start_failed` (`details.next` = `cpd watch --ensure`); it still answers `already` when an engine runs.

**With `--check`** (hs-d463; contract §3.7 "The install's engine order"): verifies and **writes nothing**, what `--ensure` and the engine's start depend on: no row, no Event, no migration, no window, no pane, no lock taken, no tmux option set, no server started, no directory made. In this order, failing at the first, each with its own error and exit code (§1.2): (a) the config loads (`config_missing`, `config_invalid`); (b) the store opens, from the **read-only verdict** of `cpd --version` (§1.2; `store::verdict`, contract §4.5) on the database opened read-only: it reads `user_version`, `schema_migrations` and this binary's list and **never migrates or writes**; the database file, its WAL and `locks/store.lock` are not written, created or locked (no `Store::open`, which migrates). No database is no refusal; a verdict that opens, with every pending migration known to this binary, passes; a refusal is its own `store_too_new`, `store_failed`, `migration_changed` or `migration_order`. The migration happens only in the new engine's own start, after the old engine is retired, so a failed check leaves the old engine working against an unmigrated store (hs-d463); (c) `tmux -V` parses and is at least 3.6 (`tmux_failed`); (d) the tmux listing: with the server of `<socket>` running, `list-panes -a -F` with the format of the liveness call (§6.3), as a UTF-8 client (§6.1) and every line parses (`tmux_failed`); with no server it is skipped; (e) `$CPD_HOME/locks` and `run` exist or can be made (their nearest existing ancestor is a writable directory) and `locks/watch.lock`, only if it exists, opens read-write, with no `O_CREAT` and no `flock`, so nothing is created or locked (`store_failed`); a missing file passes, `--ensure` creates it. Idempotent; no bound of its own.

```json
{"ok": true, "checked": ["config", "store", "tmux", "listing", "home"], "tmux": {"version": "3.8", "server": "running"}}
```

`"server"` is `"running"` or `"none"`. `cpd install` runs it with the new binary before it stops anything (§14.4, contract §3.7).
**`--mark-restart` (internal; hs-d471).** What `cpd install` runs right before it retires the old engine (contract §3.7 "The install's engine order", step 3); not an interface of the User or an agent. It writes `run/install-restart.json`, `{"by": "install-cpd.sh", "at": <now>, "engine_pid": <pid>}` (`pid` of the latest `watch-started` Event, the engine about to be retired), by rename of a temporary file, replacing any earlier marker. No Event, no row, no lock, no tmux call. It does not need the engine to run.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the home has a `watch-started` Event | `watch_not_started` | 3 |

```json
{"ok": true, "marked": true, "engine_pid": 4242}
```

Idempotent: a second one rewrites the same marker with a new `at`. The next engine consumes the marker at its start: a restart back within 10 s (`PLANNED_RESTART_QUIET_SECS`) whose marker names the previous engine's pid is logged only (`watch-started`'s `text` and `run/watch.log`) and sends no `session-message` to the Managers; past 10 s, or with no valid marker, they hear it as before (contract §3.7 "A planned restart", hs-d471). The tests are listed there.

**`--ensure --wait` (internal; hs-d328).** What the tmux server's hooks run when the engine's pane died or its window is gone (contract §6.1, §6.6); not an interface of the User or an agent. As `--ensure`, with these differences:

- a held lock with no live pane in the `watch` window (its window is gone, its process is stopping) is waited for, 15 s at most, then the engine is started; with a live pane it answers `already` at once;
- it takes `locks/watch-ensure.lock` first, as every `--ensure` does and waits for it without a limit and holds it until it is done, so only one runs at a time; after a failed start it waits 2 s under it, so a failing engine is tried once every few seconds;
- a dead engine pane is respawned in its window (`respawn-pane -e CPD_HOME=…`), the other dead `watch` windows are killed;
- it sets the server options and hooks again on a running server (§6.1), as `cpd tui` does: **`--ensure` does it too**, so every start of the engine leaves the hooks in place;
- it appends one line `supervision: …` to `run/watch.log` with the outcome. Its own output is dropped by the hook.

The engine it starts says how long it was down to each Manager (contract §3.7).

**`--restart-tmux` (internal; hs-d294).** Started by the engine, detached, when a restart of the tmux server is pending and nothing is in the way (contract §3.7, §6.1; §13.3); it is not an interface of the User or an agent. It restarts the server onto the installed tmux as §13.3 describes and exits 0, also when it did nothing (the server needs no restart, it is not safe now, another run holds `locks/tmux-restart.lock`). It prints one JSON value, `{"ok": true, "outcome": "…"}` and logs to stderr, which the engine appends to `run/tmux-restart.log`. A failed restart exits with its failure and keeps the reason in `run/tmux-restart.pending`.

## 13. `tui`

### 13.1 `tui`

```
cpd tui [--attach] [--respawn]
```

Builds the cockpit (§6.1, §6.2) unless it exists and starts the engine.

Effects, each only when missing:
- **tmux:** the server with §6.1's options; the session `cpd` with window `main` (`new-session -d -s cpd -n main -x 215 -y 62`), split into the tree (left, 25 %), the plan view (centre top) above the chat slot (centre bottom) and the widgets (right, 25 %), with the centre column 50 %; the plan view is 25 % of its height over the chat slot's 75 % (reset-layout §13.2); each pane runs `cpd tui view <tree|plan|widgets>` with `@cpd_view` set, with no StatusBar pane (the StatusBar is the session's status line, below); the chat slot holds the placeholder (§10) or, when one exists, the Plan Lead whose latest `session-moved` Event with `place: "chat"` is the newest, moved in as `session open` does. "Plan Lead" here means any Lead with a Plan, as for `session open` (side forks included, a Context's grounded Lead never) and one that `session open` refuses stays where it is while the placeholder keeps the slot (Escalation `tui-cockpit-a1-q3`). The session `cpd-work`.
- **Layout:** right after building a new `main`, `tui` runs reset-layout once (§13.2). On an existing `main` it adds every pane of the layout that is missing (the `tree`, `plan`, `widgets` or `chat` placeholder, each running its view with `@cpd_view` set; the User killed it, or a build stopped half-way) where it goes in the layout above and then runs reset-layout, so the added panes are taken from the layout and the other panes get their sizes back (amendment 15, §19; tui-W5). A chat slot that holds a Lead is not missing, so no placeholder is added beside it; a placeholder added opens the last chat Lead as a new `main` does. On an existing `main` that still has a `statusbar` pane (a cockpit built before the StatusBar moved to the status line) it kills that pane once (`kill-pane`) and then runs reset-layout, so the other panes take the freed row and get their sizes back (amendment 15, §19). The same for a `worker` pane left by a cockpit built before the Worker pane was removed (pro-d63): `cpd tui` kills it once, then runs reset-layout and listing panes skips it quietly, as for the StatusBar.
- **tmux options:** every option, the border format, the root `MouseDown1Status` binding and the conditional `pane-died` hook of §6.1. `host` sets them at every server start, so a server started by `plan new` or `watch --ensure` has them too; `cpd tui` sets them again on a running server (rerunning is safe). It also restores tmux's default `MouseDown1Pane` binding (`select-pane -t = ; send-keys -M`), which replaces cpd's earlier override.
- **The status line:** `status on` (hs-d567; hs-d561 had `2`), `status-style default` and `status-format[0]` (the `─` line, the StatusBar, §13.2), set with `-t <cockpit session>` once the session exists, never `-g`, so `cpd-work` has no status row (contract §6.1).
- **`--respawn`:** `respawn-pane -k` on every live pane of `main` that has `@cpd_view` (the views and the chat placeholder), so each runs the installed binary again; a Lead or engine pane is never touched. `scripts/install-cpd.sh` runs `cpd tui --respawn` when a cockpit exists. (Why: `cpd tui` respawns only dead panes, so a reinstall would never reach a running view.) Bare `cpd` does it too when it finds a view on an older binary (§13.3). While a preview is on (`@cpd_preview` is set on the server, §13.2), the views keep the preview build, so `--respawn` prints one line on stderr: `a preview is on (<value>); its views keep the preview build until 'preview-tui.sh off'` (hs-n264). Nothing is printed when it is unset and the value's JSON is unchanged.
- `watch --ensure` (§12).
- **tmux version** (hs-d294): when the server runs an older tmux than the installed one, marks a restart pending (`run/tmux-restart.pending`, §13.3) and says so on stderr; it never restarts the server itself, since it may run inside it. The engine does it once nothing is in the way.
- No rows of its own; moving a Lead appends `session-moved`.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| with `--attach`: stdin and stdout are a terminal | `not_a_terminal` | 3 |

```json
{"ok": true, "built": true, "socket": "cpd", "session": "cpd", "attach": ["tmux", "-L", "cpd", "attach", "-t", "cpd"], "watch": {"started": true, "pane": "%3"}}
```

With `--respawn` the value also has `"respawned": ["%1", "%2", …]`, the panes restarted. With `--attach` it then replaces itself with `tmux -L cpd attach -t cpd` and prints nothing (§1.2); bare `cpd` is the same attach with the follow-ups of §13.3. Idempotent: yes; an existing cockpit gives `"built": false`. A pane of the layout that has died is respawned (`respawn-pane`, amendment 9, §19), never duplicated and one that is gone is added again, so a second run adds nothing; a view pane that dies while the cockpit runs is respawned at once by the `pane-died` hook (§6.1).

### 13.2 `tui view` (internal)

```
cpd tui view <tree|plan|widgets|chat|legend>
cpd tui view logs [--event <id>]
cpd tui view settings
cpd tui view merge <owner>/<repo>#<n> --client <name>
cpd tui view history <id>
cpd tui view dialog <confirm|input|text> …
```

The ratatui programs in the cockpit's panes (§6.2). They own their terminal (§1.2), make no writes of their own (two exceptions: the `plan` view's scroll offsets and the `tree` view's folds, below) and change state only by running `cpd` commands (`session open`, `plan new`, `session close`, `session park`, …) as subprocesses. What they read is §17.

A view in a pane never exits on a key: the `pane-died` hook (§6.1) starts a view again whenever its program exits, so the widgets view has no `q`. A view that fails (at start or later) prints its error, waits 3 s and then exits, so the hook does not start it again in a tight loop. Without a terminal the error is returned at once.

**Cockpit parity** (User, 2026-10-15). The cockpit matches the running cpd 1 cockpit exactly: layout, elements, text, colours, keys, mouse and behaviour. The reference was cpd 1's cockpit spike, `tui/` on branch `main` before the switch-over (`tui/src/*.rs`, `tui/README.md`; `tui/` now holds the Rust cockpit crate `cpd-tui`); the checklist of every difference is [cockpit-parity.md](archive/cockpit-parity.md). Where this section states a deviation, it is deliberate and has its reason.

| View | What it is | Keys and mouse |
|---|---|---|
| `tree` | the **Context column**: Contexts, their Plans' Lead Sessions and counters | ↑↓ and j/k move the cursor, Enter opens the Lead in the chat slot (on an Inbox row it jumps to the item's cause), `n` a new Plan, `x` closes a Lead's pane, `s` and `d` snooze and dismiss the selected Inbox item, `?` the legend; the popups of `n` and `x` are the `dialog` view's; clicks and the right-click menu as below. The tree's main loop may write a frame trace to its log (§17 "Frame trace") when `CPD_TUI_TRACE` is set. |
| `plan` | the **Plan view**: one box per Workflow of the chat slot's Plan, each holding the flowchart of its Jobs; with a Manager in the chat slot, it shows **Pulse** (one row per Plan of the Context) | ←→↑↓ and h/j/k/l select, Enter opens a Job's Worker, Esc clears the selection; the wheel scrolls (3 rows, 4 columns); clicks as below; no `q`. The view remembers each Plan's scroll offset and restores it when a Lead of that Plan comes back to the chat slot (a Plan Lead and its side forks share it), clamped to the chart, which may have changed size; the selection is not kept (reset). The offsets also survive a restart of the view: they are kept in `run/tui/plan-scroll.json` (below; User, hs-d197, hs-d254). With Pulse, a left click on a row opens that Plan's Lead and the wheel scrolls the rows (3 rows a notch). The plan view's main loop may write a frame trace to its log (§17 "Frame trace") when `CPD_TUI_TRACE` is set. |
| `widgets` | the **Dispatch column**: the machine (hostname, CPU, GPU and memory) and the Inbox (§13.2 below; pro-d130) | no keys; a left click on a `pr-ready` row of the Inbox opens its url (on the label) or its owning Plan's Lead in the chat slot (on the rest of the row); a right click opens the Inbox item's menu; the wheel over the Inbox scrolls it; mouse capture on |
| `history` | an archived Session's history, read-only: the Session's pi file drawn with the session renderer the history view owns (`tui/src/history/render.rs`); its top line is `<name> (archived, read-only)`; **its content area is one row shorter than the pane, so the pane's last row is empty** (User, hs-d567; contract §6.1 "The blank row", Q2). Started by `session history` (§10.12) in the chat slot | `q` or Esc quits to the placeholder text; ↑/k, ↓/j, PageUp, PageDown and the wheel (3 rows) scroll; End or `G` follows the end again; no other keys |
| `chat` | the chat slot's placeholder (§10) | none |
| `legend` | the key legend, in a popup | ↑↓, j/k, PgUp/PgDn and the wheel scroll it when it is taller than its popup; any other key closes it |
| `logs` | the Event log, in a popup; `--event <id>` opens it at that Event | ↑↓, j/k, PgUp/PgDn and the wheel scroll; End or `G` goes to the bottom, where it follows again; `q` or Esc closes it |
| `settings` | the **settings** popup (below): it opens on a menu of two entries, **Agent Tiers** and **Workers**; the Agent Tiers screen has the four Tier defaults, the four models of the machine and the Experimental Features' switches, the Workers screen the machine's concurrent Worker count (`concurrency`) | ↑↓ move the focus, Enter opens the focused menu entry, a value's list, the Workers count's editor, flips an Experimental row or presses a button, Esc closes a list or the editor first; Esc or `q` closes without writing; clicks and the wheel as below |

| `dialog` | the **dialog kit's** popup (below; hs-d295, hs-d297), of one kind: `confirm` (a question, two buttons), `input` (a labelled text box, contract §6.1.1), `text` (scrollable read-only text), `checklist` (tickable rows, hs-d549), `select` (radio list, a cursor row picked with Enter or [OK]; hs-d-tui-docs) or `form` (a labelled text box and a labelled radio list, pro-d114); its colours are contract §6.1.1's (title pill, body 7, the first button the blue block, the others 15, an input's refusal yellow, its border focused blue 12 and unfocused white 15, its cursor the blue block) | Enter or `y`, or a click on the first button, confirms; Esc, `n`, `q` or a click on the second cancels; `input`: Enter accepts, Esc cancels; `select` and `form`: ↑↓ and j/k move the cursor, Enter or a click on [OK] confirms, Esc or [Cancel] cancels; `checklist`, `select` and `form`: the cursor row is styled like checklist's, PgUp/PgDn and the wheel scroll; mouse capture on |
