**`plan`: the scroll offsets file** (User, hs-d254). The `plan` view keeps each Plan's scroll offset in `$CPD_HOME/run/tui/plan-scroll.json` (contract §1.4), a JSON object `{"<plan id>": [x, y]}`, so that the offsets survive a restart of the view (every install restarts the views, `cpd tui --respawn`). This is a deliberate exception to "the views make no writes of their own" (the `tree` view's folds file is the other, below): the file is the view's own state, not Ledger state, as the Worker pane is the view's own layout (§17 "Actions"). Nothing else reads it.
- **Read** once, at the view's start. A missing file is an empty map. A file that cannot be read or is not that object (invalid JSON, an id that is not a Plan id, an offset that is not two non-negative integers) is not an error: the view starts with an empty map, logs `scroll positions reset: <reason>` (no note, §17 "No notes") and replaces the file at its next write. The view never exits because of this file.
- **Written** atomically (a temporary file in the same directory, then a rename; the directory and its parents are created) whenever an offset has changed, at most once per second and again as soon as the chat slot's Plan changes. A failed write is logged (§17 "No notes") and retried at the next write; it never ends the view.
- **Not cleaned up**: archived or unknown Plans stay in the file, harmlessly. Offsets are stored as left, not clamped: clamping stays at draw.
- The selection is never stored (reset at every restart and switch, above).

**Design rule** (User, Plan tui-visuals, 2026-10-17; hs-d124; refined by the powerline look, hs-d266 and hs-d322, 2026-10-19). Top-level layout separators (the tmux pane borders) are colour 7 when unfocused (interactive: they can be dragged) and blue when focused (hs-d531, hs-d534; contract §6.1.1); separators inside a slot are colour 8. The pane headers are tmux's (contract §6.1), **with a rounded cap on each side** and, by the title rule (User, hs-d475; hs-d478): the text in **Title Case**, **no padding** inside the pill, **a read-only title pill (colour 7 inverted: text in the terminal's background colour, caps colour 7), blue on the focused pane (colour 4 inverted: text in the terminal's background colour, caps colour 4)** (hs-d534, replacing hs-d530's 8 and 7; contract §6.1.1) and the pill starting **three columns from the pane's edge**, like the in-pane titles. `` (U+E0B6, nf-ple-left_half_circle_thick, left) and `` (U+E0B4, nf-ple-right_half_circle_thick, right) are one cell each on the normal background: `━━━Context━━━━━━━━━━━━`. The `━` before the pill is part of the border line and takes the line's colour (7 unfocused, blue focused), not the pill's. This is the powerline style of the User's zsh theme (agnoster) and needs the MesloLGS Nerd Font that dotfiles installs on every machine (`font-meslo-lg-nerd-font`, `~/dotfiles/home/.chezmoidata/packages.yaml`). A section title inside a slot is §17's "Section titles" rule (hs-d475, hs-d478, hs-d480), e.g. ` ──Jobs───────────3 ` (` ╭─Inbox───…───35 ` for a collapsible widget's title): the title in Title Case as a read-only title pill (colour 7 inverted: text in the terminal's background colour, caps colour 7, `palette::pill_static()`, hs-d534) with no padding spaces, a muted line (colour 8) to the right edge, an optional count at its end as a pill too, the same colours as the title, inside the slot's one column of padding on each side (hs-d476), its left cap three columns from the edge (hs-d478). A slot's first section has no title, so no two titles stack: the pane header is the slot's title. **Pills** have the same rounded caps (the Plan view's Job pills, the legend's sample pill, the StatusBar's items): a pill is its block with a cap on each side, in the pill's background colour as their foreground (white for an interactive pill, grey for a read-only title, blue for the focused pane's title, the meaning's colour for a coloured one; hs-d534, contract §6.1.1), so the cockpit has one look, rounded.

**The chat slot's header** (hs-d257, contract §6.1). The border header of a Session's pane (a Manager's, a Lead's, a Worker's or a fork's) is tmux's, from the pane option `@cpd_title`, not a view's: it shows the Session's **dynamic title** (`sessions.title`, written by `session retitle`, §10.14, started by engine E10 after the Session's turns end, at most every 10 minutes) when it has one, else its key (`sessions.name` of a Manager, of a Lead that is not a fork and of a Worker), or the name of a fork. The Plan's title is never the header. It changes when a new title is written, not on a timer; a pane that gets no title yet shows the fallback. The text is title-cased by `Tmux::set_pane_title` (the first letter of each space-separated word upper-cased, the rest unchanged; hs-d475), which writes `@cpd_title`; the store's titles are unchanged. **The tree keeps showing ids** (hs-d101, "Labels" below): a title is never drawn in it.

**The dialog kit** (User, hs-d295, hs-d297; `tui/src/dialog/`). Every cockpit confirmation and input is a **tmux popup** running `cpd tui view dialog <confirm|input|text|checklist|select|form> …`, built on this one kit. The kit has six kinds: **confirm** (a question with two pill buttons, for example `[Archive] [Cancel]`; used only by Delete, pro-d111), **input** (a labelled text box, contract §6.1.1), **text** (scrollable read-only text), **checklist** (a scrollable list of rows the User ticks, with the pill buttons `[Approve] [Later]`; hs-d549, hs-d551), **select** (a scrollable radio list, the cursor row picked with Enter or [OK], with the pill buttons `[OK] [Cancel]`; hs-d-tui-docs) and **form** (a labelled text box and a labelled radio list, pro-d114, below).
- **The caller keeps its actions.** It opens the popup with `display-popup -E`, which returns when the popup closes, then reads the **result file** the view wrote at the path the caller named with `--out <path>` (a temporary file the caller makes and removes): *confirmed* or *cancelled* and for `input` and `form` the typed value and choice. The view runs no command and holds no caller logic; the caller runs its `cpd` commands (§17).
- **Style.** A dialog is one rounded frame and the popup is exactly that frame (hs-d578, amending hs-d569 CD1, hs-d475 to hs-d478 and hs-d298's section-title form): row 0 is `╭─`, the title as a pill, `─` up to `╮`; rows 1 to H-2 are `│`, the inside, `│`; row H-1 is `╰`, `─` × (W-2), `╯`. The title appears there and nowhere else (no tmux title, no header rows). A title wider than `W - 6` cells is cut to `W - 6` and the top row keeps at least one `─` before `╮`; with no room for a pill (`W - 6 < 1`) none is drawn. The frame's corners, walls and lines (the `─` fill of the top row included) are colour 8 (muted); the title pill is the read-only pill (text in the terminal's background colour, in colour 7, caps colour 7 on the terminal background, `palette::pill_static()`), as every title pill. The view draws the frame itself and tmux draws none (`-B`, below), so a dialog cannot be dragged by its border any more. Buttons and keys are the `merge` popup's: a click on a button, Enter or `y` confirms; Esc, `n` or `q` cancels. In `input`, Enter accepts and Esc cancels and `y`, `n` and `q` are typed text. Mouse capture is on. **Scrolling** is ↑↓, j/k, PgUp/PgDn and the **mouse wheel** and End or `G` goes to the bottom (in `input`, the keys that are text stay text). A scrolling popup draws the scroll cues right-aligned (§17, "Scroll cues").
- **Size.** The popup is opened with `display-popup -E -B -w W -h H <command>` (`popup_args` in `tui/src/dialog/mod.rs`): `-B` means tmux draws no border and there is no `-T`, so the program gets a pane of the full `W` × `H` (tmux 3.8: `stty size` 6 42 for `-w 42 -h 6`). The inside is 40 to 76 columns (`popup_size`: `(natural + 2).max(title chars + 6).clamp(40, 76)`); the popup is the inside plus 2 wide (the walls), capped at the newest client's width minus 2 (at least 1; `newest_client`, as the `logs` popup does) and `body + 5` rows tall (the top and bottom borders and the three template rows below; it was `body + 5 + 2` with tmux's border), capped at the client's height (vertical margin 0). The `confirm` natural width is unchanged (`max(widest line, accept label + 6 + 8)`).
- **The frame and its rows** (hs-d578, template hs-n437; the Box rule, contract §6.1.1 "Boxes"). A popup of `H` rows with a body of `b` rows has `H = b + 5`: row 0 the top border, row 1 blank, rows 2 to `H-4` the body (`H - 5` rows), row `H-3` blank, row `H-2` the buttons, row `H-1` the bottom border. The two blank rows are spacing between elements, not padding. **Margin and padding:** the inside is `W - 2` cells wide and its first and last cell are the padding: content starts at popup column 2 (wall at 0, padding at 1) and ends at column `W - 3` (padding at `W - 2`, wall at `W - 1`), so the content width is `W - 4`; no padding row above or below. The popup has a margin of one column on each side (at most `client width - 2` wide, at least 1, so a column of the cockpit stays on each side) and 0 vertically. **The body:** `confirm` and `text`: each row is the padding cell, the row's text (wrapped or cut at `W - 4`), blank to the padding cell. `checklist`: entries as below, at width `W - 4`. `input`: the input box (the dialog's body rect, contract §6.1.1) is the box_widget, drawn from popup column 2 to column `W - 3` (the dialog's padding cells form the input's margin; `tw = (W - 2) - 6`, starting on popup row 2), with refusal rows directly under it (up to 2, the note colour, a leading space, cut at `W - 4`), the rest blank. **The buttons row** (row `H-2`): buttons are pills, the cap U+E0B6, the label, the cap U+E0B4, so `[Archive]` is nine cells. The accepting button (`confirm` the caller's label, `input` `OK`, `checklist` `Approve`; `text` `Close`, which is alone) is flush left: its left cap is at popup column 2. The other button (`Cancel`, `Later`) is flush right: its right cap is at column `W - 3`. Nothing is drawn between them. Colours (hs-d534: interactive pill 15, selected 12): the accepting button is colour 12 inverted (text in the terminal's background colour), caps colour 12; the other is colour 15 inverted (text in the terminal's background colour), caps colour 15. The whole pill, caps included, is the hit target. **The scroll position** of a scrolling body (`1-5/20`) stays on the buttons row, colour 8, right-aligned inside the padding (its last character at popup column `W - 3`) and only when at least one blank cell lies between it and the pill on its left and, if there is a right pill, between it and that pill; else omitted.
- **Drawn.** In every drawing `[` and `]` stand for the pill's caps, U+E0B6 and U+E0B4, one cell each (so a pill is as wide as its drawing) and `█` is the cursor cell. Each drawing is a whole popup, 42 columns wide, exactly as the User sees it.

`confirm` (title `Archive`, question `Archive cpd-ui?`, accept label `Archive`; 42 × 6):
```
╭─[Archive]──────────────────────────────╮
│                                        │
│ Archive cpd-ui?                        │
│                                        │
│ [Archive]                     [Cancel] │
╰────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

`input` (title `New Plan`, prompt `Name:`, validator `plan-id`, the text `sketch` typed; 42 × 10; the two rows under the box are the reserved refusal rows, a refusal draws in them):
```
╭─[New Plan]─────────────────────────────╮
│                                        │
│ ╭─[Name]─────────────────────────────╮ │
│ │ sketch█                            │ │
│ ╰────────────────────────────────────╯ │
│                                        │
│                                        │
│                                        │
│ [OK]                          [Cancel] │
╰────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

`text` (title `session open l-ship`, body `no_cockpit: No cockpit.`; 42 × 6):
```
╭─[session open l-ship]──────────────────╮
│                                        │
│ no_cockpit: No cockpit.                │
│                                        │
│ [Close]                                │
╰────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

`checklist` (title `Retire records of cpd`, two entries `r-1` and `r-2`, the cursor on `r-1`; 42 × 10):
```
╭─[Retire records of cpd]────────────────╮
│                                        │
│ [ ] r-1 — duplicate r-0                │
│     use sqlite as the store            │
│                                        │
│ [ ] r-2 — documented docs/a.md         │
│     wire format                        │
│                                        │
│ [Approve]                      [Later] │
╰────────────────────────────────────────╯
```
- **`checklist`** (hs-d549, hs-d551; hs-d568, hs-d569): `cpd tui view dialog checklist --title <t> --items <json file> --out <file>`. `--items` is a JSON file, an array of `{"id": <record id>, "text": <full text>, "detail": <text>}` (hs-d569 CD2; `text` the record's full text; `detail`: `<reason> <target>` for a retirement; the caller builds it from `cpd context curation`, §3.15); a file that is not that shape is refused at the view's start, with the envelope of §1.2. The view draws a scrollable list of entries, one per array element, each of which is a header line `[ ] <id> — <detail>` (`[x]` when ticked) followed by the record's full `text`, wrapped to the body's width and indented by four columns; one empty row separates two entries (hs-d569 CD2). The cursor is an ENTRY: ↑↓ and j/k move one entry at a time, **Space toggles the cursor entry, a click on any line of an entry toggles that entry**, `a` toggles all entries (all ticked when any unticked, else all unticked), PgUp/PgDn and the wheel scroll the entries and after the cursor moves the window shows at least the cursor entry's header line. The buttons are `[Approve] [Later]` (hs-d569 CD3: `[Later]` decides nothing; Esc, `q` or a click on `[Later]` close with `approved: false`, every entry stays pending). Enter or a click on `[Approve]` approves (ticked entries decided). The **result file** is `{"approved": bool, "ticked": [id], "unticked": [id]}`, the ids in entry order (on `[Later]` `approved` is false and the two lists are what was on screen; the caller ignores them). Colours are contract §6.1.1's, title pill 7, frame 8, body 7, the first button the blue pill 12, the other the white pill 15. Mouse capture is on. The view runs no command: the caller does (the Inbox click table below).
- **`select`** (new): `cpd tui view dialog select --title <t> --prompt <p> --option <o> [--option <o>…] --out <path>`. `--option` is repeated, in the order shown; at least one; each one non-empty single line without control characters, distinct, at most 70 characters; otherwise `args_invalid` like an unreadable checklist file. The view draws a scrollable list of rows, one per option, `(x) <option>` for the cursor row (the choice) and `( ) <option>` for the others, styled as checklist's cursor entry. Keys: ↑↓ and j/k move the cursor one option and stop at both ends (no wrap); Enter or `y` confirms; Esc, `n` or `q` cancels. Mouse: a click on an option row moves the cursor there and does not close; a click on [OK] confirms, on [Cancel] cancels; the wheel and PgUp/PgDn scroll the body when it is taller than the popup and a cursor move scrolls so that the cursor row stays visible. The **result file** is `{"confirmed": true, "value": "<the option>"}` or `{"confirmed": false}`. Popup size: natural width = the widest of the prompt and `(x) ` + each option; body rows = the prompt's rows + one per option. The buttons are `[OK]` (first, left) and `[Cancel]` (second, right). Example, title `New Context`, prompt `Owner:`, options `clayton-duarte` and `other`, a popup of 42 × 8:
```
╭─[New Context]──────────────────────────╮
│                                        │
│ Owner:                                 │
│ (x) clayton-duarte                     │
│ ( ) other                              │
│                                        │
│ [OK]                          [Cancel] │
╰────────────────────────────────────────╯
```



- **The input box** (contract §6.1.1). The prompt is the box's label (trailing whitespace, then one trailing `:`, then trailing whitespace trimmed again; `Title: ` gives `Title`). There is no prompt row: the prompt moved into the box's top border. The box is always focused (border 12). The box starts on popup row 2 and is `W - 2` cells wide, with the refusal rows directly under it (up to 2, colour 8, a leading space, cut at `W - 4`; the frame and rows are "The frame and its rows" above) and its label pill follows the border's colour (12 here, focused). When the text needs more rows than available, the box shows consecutive rows from `start = max(0, cursor row + 1 - avail)` where `avail = max(H - 5 - 2 - REFUSAL_ROWS, 1)` and cursor row is `cursor / tw` (`tw = (W - 2) - 6`, `W` the popup's width; contract §6.1.1), the body being `H - 5` rows. The popup is sized so the box always fits the validator's longest accepted value (Plan id 24, title 200, name 80): `input_popup_size(client, title, prompt, initial, validator)` in `tui/src/dialog/mod.rs` computes the inside width and the height `body + 5` and caps both by the client (width minus 2, at least 1; height; no more `adds 2`; contract §6.1.1 has the worked sizes).
- **Validation** (`input`). The caller passes the check by name, from a closed set: `plan-id` (the Plan id of the `n` key, contract §2.1), `title` (`Title`, 1–200 characters) and `name` (`Name`, 1–80 characters). A refused value shows its reason **inside the popup**, which stays open and the User keeps typing; only an accepted value is written to the result file.

**`tree`.**
- **Top row and side margins.** The view keeps one blank row at its top and one blank column on each side; its content starts one row lower, inside the inner area (the pane minus one column left and right), so the tree never touches the pane's edges. Everything the view draws sits inside it: the cursor's blue row (contract §6.1.1), the message row at the bottom (a command's refusal or result, never an input) and the right-click menu's clamping.
- **Rows** (User, hs-d337, hs-d339; replaces hs-d309's `┌` / `└` shapes). There is **no indent** and **no in-pane `Context` title** (the pane border's CPD mark, contract §6.1, is enough; hs-d729, superseding the view-title part of hs-d671). Each Context is a collapsible block (§17, "Collapsible blocks") drawn by the one shared widget (`tui/src/fold.rs`). **Always:** the title row is `╭` + the Context's glyph + its name (bold), for example `╭󰽢 building-cpd`, with **no Plan count** (main's count of a folded Context stood for the Plans folding hid; a fold hides no live Plan, hs-d344) and each content row, one per live Lead Session, is `├─` + the row's glyph + its text, straight against the branch, for example `├─󰽢 cross-repo       3⋅1⋅0⋅0⋅92`, with the counters right-aligned. **The toggle shows and hides only the archived rows** (hs-d344): live Plans and Sessions always show, folded or expanded. **Folded:** the title row, the live rows, then the closing row `╰󰬦 expand`. **Expanded:** the title row, the live rows, the archived rows (below, colour 8), then the closing row `╰󰬬 collapse`. A Context with **nothing to fold** (no archived rows; hs-d477) has **no closing row** and no toggle: its **last row's branch is `╰─`** instead of `├─`, for example

```
╭󰽤 homeserver
├─󰽤 b2-budget …
╰─󰽧 speedtest …
```

The Context block's rows (title, `├─` rows, closing row) end at column `W - 2`, the row area's last cell (column `W - 1`, the pane's margin, stays blank; there is no right pad): the counters are right-aligned to it and the name is cut with `…` before them and before the cost (see Cost counters; the branch rows' glyph placement is unchanged). The Context tree is the one place that leaves the rail rule's `W - 4` right edge (pro-d186); contract §6.1.1 "The rail fold" keeps the rule for every other rail. A Context with archived rows keeps its closing row, `╰󰬦 expand` / `╰󰬬 collapse` and its live rows keep `├─`. A LIVE Context with **no row at all** under it ends with the clickable row ` ╰󰬪 new` — the muted `╰` and glyph and the word `new` in colour 15 (clickable text) — and a left click on that row opens the New Plan input popup for that Context (the same action as `n` and the context menu's New Plan...). An ARCHIVED Context with **no row at all** keeps the plain muted terminator ` ╰󰬪` (U+F0B2A, colour 8, no word, no toggle; hs-d574, replacing hs-d459 and the plain closing `╰─` line). Each Context block is a collapsible widget and so has **one empty row above and one below** (hs-d476; the view's blank top row is the first block's and the body has no vertical spacing). The closing row is drawn once per Context, never twice, by the shared helper (§17, "Collapsible blocks"; hs-d349), its lines colour 8 and its toggle (arrow and word) colour 7 (contract §6.1.1, hs-d534). The content rows are the Plans' Lead Sessions and every Session forked by `session fork` as siblings under the Context (B1, contract §6.8: a fork is a sibling under the Context, never nested under a Plan or under the Session it came from, whatever its `plan` or `forked_from`), ordered together at both levels by dot-urgency tier (red, yellow, magenta, cyan, shiro, then archived last), within a tier by creation (`created_at`, newest first; hs-d686, pro-d48); forks show no Job counters (the counters belong to the Plan Lead's row); then, for an expanded Context, **its archived Plans and Sessions, after the live ones, colour 8** (contract §6.1.1), with the same `├─` rows (hs-d339). There is **no archived `󰇘` row and no separate archived toggle**: the closing toggle is the archived rows' (hs-d344). Row: `├─`, glyph, one space, name (cut with `…` before the counters) and the four Job counters `planned⋅active⋅failed⋅done` right-aligned and **only the nonzero roles are drawn** (a zero role draws no number and no separator; a Plan with every role zero, for example all its Jobs cancelled, shows no counters; cancelled Jobs are not counted; no counters without a Plan; hs-d636). **planned** is `draft + queued` (all not-started work: a Plan with 3 drafts and 7 queued shows 10, not 3), colour 13 (magenta, `Meaning::Planning`) while it has any Job in `draft`—a draft appended after the lock included (hs-d173, hs-d179)—else 15 (the queued colour, `Meaning::NotStarted`). **active** is `running + merging`, colour 14 (cyan, `Meaning::InProgress`), or 11 (yellow, `Meaning::Review`) when any of it is landing (**landing** counts the Jobs whose active Attempt is checking or merging, contract §6.1.1, hs-d604). **failed** is 9 (red, `Meaning::Failed`, always). **done** is `merged`, 10 (green, `Meaning::Done`). hs-d636 replaces hs-d623's draft-takes-the-first-slot rule and the five-counter row; hs-d580 keeps the role colours and amends audit Q3, hs-d303 for the counters. On an ASLEEP Lead's row every counter is colour 8 whatever the count, its dot and name staying 7; separators `⋅` colour 8. **A row has no icon** (hs-d337, which replaced hs-d266's tree icons): the corner or branch, the dot glyph, the name. **The selected row** (User, hs-d351, 2026-10-20) is the Plan or Session row whose Session is in the chat slot, or a Context row whose Manager is in the chat slot: its **name** (the text after the dot glyph, up to the counters) is drawn in blue (`palette` blue, §17, "Blue") and blue **beats the muted colour of archived and asleep rows**; the rest of the row (the branch, the glyph, the counters) keeps its colours and the name is not bold for being selected. There is no marker in column 0. The glyph is one of `` U+E3E3 (moon_alt_new: the Session needs you, coloured by case), `` U+E3E3, U+E3C8..U+E3E2 (the 28 moon_alt phases, section 17; the Lead is working: a loader of 28 frames, one every 50 ms, on one shared clock, so every spinner turns together; red 9 while its Plan has a failed Job being worked on or an open Worker Escalation (hs-d581, pro-d200), else the Work colour of pro-d200 ("The Lead dot rule", §17): magenta 13 while the Lead plans (any draft Job, grounding, a follow-up), yellow 11 for pull-request, deploy and landing work, cyan 14 for dispatch, white 15 with no Plan (superseding the phase colours of hs-d622 and hs-d624), §6.1.1), `` U+E3D5 (moon_alt_full: idle, nothing needed) or `` U+E3D5 (pi stopped, colour 8). A Session row's glyph looks at the Session's own state first (a working Session shows the spinner) and its `󰽢` comes only from its open, visible Inbox items (§17); a Context row shows the glyph of its Manager Session (hs-d215): a `󰽢` only from the Manager's own Inbox items (hs-d217), `󰽤` (colour 8) when the Context has none. Archived rows are colour 8 on every mark; asleep rows colour 7 except their Job counters, 8 and neither animates. The cockpit needs a Nerd Font for these symbols (https://www.nerdfonts.com/cheat-sheet). The rule, the colours and the precedences are §17's (The tree's dot rule) (hs-d622, hs-d624).

**Cost counters** (decisions pro-d179 and pro-d186; contract §2.2 "Session cost"). A Context row and a Plan row draw their `cost_usd` (when it is not `None`) as `cpd_core::metrics::format_cost` text, drawn beside the name or id, never at the right: on a Plan row one space after the name, on a Context row one space after the id. The Job counters stay right-aligned and unchanged, ending at the row's last cell, column `W - 2`. The cost is always colour 8 (`palette::muted_text()`, `Color::Indexed(8)`), never bold, on every row. With `width` the row area's width, `c` the width of the Job counters text and `k` the width of the cost text (`format_cost`, never a literal): a Plan's name is cut with `…` to `width - 6 - R` cells, where `R` is the reserve to its right, `1 + k` when the cost is drawn, plus `c + 1` when the Plan has counters (drawn or too narrow to be drawn), so a cut name leaves 3 blank cells before the counters; a Context's id is cut with `…` to `width - 4 - k` cells, so `3 + id + 1 + k <= width` and the cost ends at the row's last cell when the id is cut. A Plan with no nonzero counter draws the cost after the name and nothing at the right; a Context row draws nothing at the right. With no cost the row is as before. **By default the tree draws no cost on Context and Plan rows** (pro-d189): the state is a flag of the view's process, toggled by the `$` key (the StatusBar's costs button sends it), so a restart of the view or of the cockpit turns it off and nothing is stored. With the costs off a Plan name is cut only by its counters (it takes the room of the hidden cost, `R` is `c + 1` or 0) and a Context id only by the row's end; the rules above apply while the costs are on. The Workflow box footer's cost is not affected and is always drawn (pro-d194). Examples, with `row_of` (the helper of the tree's row tests, which pads the left text so that the right text ends at the row's last cell, no `RIGHT_PAD`):

- E1: Plan `ship`, last row of its Context, counters `2⋅2⋅5`, cost 0.12, width 44: `row_of("╰─{WORKING} ship $0.120", "2⋅2⋅5", 44)`.
- E2: Plan `ship`, counter `1`, cost 1234.0, width 30: `row_of("╰─{IDLE} ship $1.23k", "1", 30)`.
- E3: Plan `ship`, no counter, cost 0.004, width 30: `╰─{IDLE} ship $0.004` (nothing after it); with cost 0.12: `╰─{IDLE} ship $0.120`.
- E4: Context `alpha`, cost 12.30, width 30: `╭{IDLE} alpha $12.30` (nothing after it).
- E5 (cut name): Plan named `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwx`, counters `2⋅2⋅5`, cost 0.12, width 30: the name keeps 30 - 6 - 7 - 6 = 11 cells (k=6), `abcdefghij…`; `row_of("╰─{IDLE} abcdefghij… $0.120", "2⋅2⋅5", 30)` (3 blank cells before the counters).
- E6 (cut id): Context whose id is 30 `a`, cost 12.30 (k=6), width 30: the id keeps 30 - 4 - 6 = 20 cells, 19 `a` and `…`; the row is `╭{IDLE} ` + 19 `a` + `… $12.30` and fills the 30 cells exactly.

**Narrow rows.** The counters are drawn when `c + 5 <= width` (`MIN_LEFT`), as before. The cost is drawn only when the Plan has no counters or its counters are drawn and the cut name keeps at least one cell: `width - 6 - (1 + k) - (c + 1 if it has counters) >= 1`; otherwise the cost is dropped and the name is cut as if it had no cost. The cost goes first and never makes the counters disappear. A Context row draws its cost when `k + 5 <= width` (the id keeps at least one cell), else not. E7: Plan `ship`, counter `1` (c=1), cost 0.12 (k=6, `$0.120`): at width 16 the name keeps 16 - 6 - 7 - 2 = 1 cell, `…` and the row is `row_of("╰─{IDLE} … $0.120", "1", 16)`; at width 15 the cost is dropped and the row is `row_of("╰─{IDLE} ship", "1", 15)`; the counters alone are drawn from width 6 (the row ends with ` 1`, no `$`) and neither is drawn at width 5. E8: a Plan `ship` with a cost and no counters draws the cost at width 14 (the name keeps 14 - 6 - 7 = 1 cell, `…`) and not at width 13; a Context with cost 0.12 draws it at width 11 (the id keeps 11 - 4 - 6 = 1 cell, `…`) and not at width 10.

**Muted rows.** An archived row keeps its cost in colour 8, as its other marks. An asleep Plan row keeps its cost in colour 8: the muted restyle skips the cost cells as it skips the counters. The selected-name blue is the name's alone and the cost is never blue; the cursor's reversed block covers the whole row. A Context row's cost is never bold, though its title is.

**Rows without a cost.** Fork, Manager, Worker and toggle rows draw no cost, though each Session node carries its own cost (`SessionNode.cost_usd`, the read model's data, not a row element). A tree whose every cost is `None` draws what it drew before, except that its rows now end at column `W - 2` (pro-d186).
- **The Standing section** (User, 2026-11-02 EST, pro-d339, amended by pro-d347, amended by pro-d351; the Permanent Contexts of pro-d338 and pro-d340). Below the project tree the pane holds a docked section `Standing` with the Permanent Contexts that exist in the store, `cpd`, `host` and `codereview` (`ContextId::permanent()`, `PermanentContext::ALL`), in that fixed order, never sorted by tier or age. A Permanent Context that does not exist yet is not drawn; with none, there is no section. *Assumption (I infer it; the User did not state it):* a Permanent Context is drawn in Standing only, never in the project tree or in the Archive section, so each row has one place. **Layout**, top to bottom: the project tree (its rows as above, its own `▲ n more` / `▼ n more` cue rows and its own wheel), then ONE blank row, then the **header** row, then ONE reserved row (the section's `▲` cue row, blank when nothing is hidden above), then the Standing rows, then ONE reserved row (its `▼` cue row, blank when nothing is hidden below) above the statusline, the bottom of the pane. The two reserved rows are kept also when the rows fit; no spacing is doubled. Two consecutive Standing Context blocks are separated by ONE blank spacer row, as two live Context blocks of the project tree are, and none follows the last. Amended by pro-d347: an open section is `4 + rows` high (the blank row above the header, the header, the two reserved rows and the `rows` Standing rows, its spacer rows included), at most half the pane's height, rounded down; its spacer rows count in `rows`, and when its rows do not fit they scroll between the two reserved rows, spacer rows with them, the two reserved rows then being the section's own cue rows (`dialog::scroll::cue`), with their own wheel. The project tree never shares that scroll, and the section never moves while the project tree scrolls. **The docked group** (pro-d348, pro-d349, amended by pro-d351): the layout now ends with the Archive section (below), so the pane, top to bottom, is the project tree (live non-permanent Contexts only: it has no `archive` row and no archived Context any more), the empty middle, then the docked group, Standing and Archive together, aligned to the bottom of the pane while the project tree's Contexts stay at the top. The group is ONE blank row, then Standing when a Permanent Context exists, then Archive when a Context is archived; an open section is its header, one reserved `▲` cue row, its list rows and one reserved `▼` cue row, a folded one its header and ONE blank row below it (pro-d351); between Standing and Archive there is exactly ONE row, Standing's reserved end row when Standing is open (the shared empty row) or Standing's own blank row below its header when Standing is folded (no separate row is added between them). The four folded cases, rows top to bottom (`H` a header row, `.` a blank row, `▲` and `▼` the reserved cue rows, `rows` the list rows, the glyph in brackets): (1) Standing folded alone: `. H(Standing, U+F0B2C) .`; (2) Standing open, Archive folded: `. H(Standing, U+F0B26) ▲ rows ▼ H(Archive, U+F0B2C) .`, the `▼` row being the one shared row above Archive's header; (3) both folded: `. H(Standing, U+F0B2C) . H(Archive, U+F0B2C) .`; (4) Standing folded, Archive open: `. H(Standing, U+F0B2C) . H(Archive, U+F0B26) ▲ rows ▼`, the same rows as before pro-d351. An absent section is 0 rows: with only Archive present the group is case (1) with `Archive`. The group is capped at half the pane's height, `B = floor(H / 2)` for a pane of `H` rows (the cap of the group, not of each section; amending the cap of pro-d347 above), and the project tree takes the rest, at least the other half. The group wants `1 + height(Standing) + height(Archive)` rows, an open section being `3 + n` high (`n` list rows, spacer rows included) and a folded one 2 (its header and the blank row below it), an absent one 0. When that fits in `B` nothing scrolls. Otherwise the fixed rows (the blank row, the headers, the reserved rows of the open sections, the blank row below each folded header) stay and `L = B - fixed` list rows are shared: Standing first, with `n_S' = min(n_S, L - a)` (`a` is 1 when Archive is open and has rows, so Archive always keeps one list row, else 0), then Archive with `n_A' = min(n_A, L - n_S')`. A section with `n' < n` scrolls on its own between its two reserved rows, which are then its own `▲ n more` / `▼ n more` cue rows (`dialog::scroll::cue`, ending at column `W - 2`), with its own scroll offset and its own wheel: a wheel over a section's list rows scrolls that section only, over the project region only the project tree. When `B` is smaller than the fixed rows, or `L` is smaller than the number of open sections, the group draws from the top what fits and cuts the rest at the bottom; with `B < 2` there is no group. The project region is `H` minus the group's height. **Rows**: each Standing Context is drawn as any Context row, with the same text, its Plans under it, the same expansion of its archived rows, the same closing row and the same dots. **Header** (pro-d347): `section::flush_title_with("Standing", Some(glyph), width)` (`tui/src/section.rs`) at the pane's width, from column 0 to the last column: the left pill `Standing` (the title, the static grey pill `palette::pill_static()`) and the right pill the fold glyph, with no count and no padding cells. The glyph is U+F0B26 (`󰬦`, `fold::DOWN`) when the section is open and U+F0B2C (`󰬬`, `fold::UP`) when it is folded: the section is docked at the bottom, so folding collapses it down toward the statusline and opening expands it up. At `W` = 30 the header is 3 (`───`) + 10 (the pill `Standing`: 8 + 2 caps) + 13 `─` + 3 (the glyph pill: 1 + 2 caps) + 1 (`─`) = 30 cells. The header row keeps no menu; a left click on it folds or opens the section (below). **The section is open by default.** A left click on the header row folds it (then the blank row above it, the header and the blank row below it remain; the rows are hidden) and a second click opens it. The folded state lives in the view's memory only. **Keys**: the cursor (`j`/`k`, Down, Up, Enter, `x`, `n`) crosses from the last project row into the first Standing row and back, and each region keeps the cursor row in view; a folded section has no rows for the cursor. **Click**: a left click on a Standing Context row runs `context manager --context=<id> --by-user`, as any live Context row. **Menu**: a right click on a Standing Context row opens `New Plan…` and `Copy id` only (no `Rename…`, no `Archive`); every other Context row keeps its menu; the header row has no menu. Standing Contexts are never in the Archive section.

**Worked example**: a pane 30 columns wide and 26 rows high (columns and rows counted from 0; colours are not shown). A dot is drawn as §17 draws it:  where the Context or Plan needs the User,  where nothing does. The project tree has 22 rows, its 18 Context and Plan rows and the 4 blank spacer rows between its 5 Context blocks, and 11 of them are shown: row 0 is its `▲` line (blank: nothing is hidden above), rows 1 to 11 its rows, up to `receipts`, and row 12 its `▼ 11 more` line. The 11 hidden rows are `export-csv`, a blank row, `garden` with its two Plans, a blank row and a fifth Context of five rows (its title and four Plans). Row 13 is the blank row and row 14 the header. Row 15 is the blank row reserved under the header (its `▲` cue row: nothing is hidden above). Rows 16 to 24 are the Standing rows: `cpd` (its Plan `perm-managers` and an archived Plan behind the `expand` toggle), a blank row, `host` (no Plan yet, so its row is the clickable ` ╰󰬪 new`), a blank row and `codereview` (one live Plan, so its last row is `╰─`). Row 25 is the blank row reserved above the statusline (its `▼` cue row: nothing is hidden below). The section is 13 rows (the blank row, the header, the two reserved rows and 9 rows: 7 Context and Plan rows and 2 spacer rows), exactly the 13 that half of 26 allows, so nothing scrolls. A folded section is its header and the ONE blank row below it (pro-d351), at the pane's bottom. Folded alone, as case (1) of "The docked group", it is rows 23 to 25: row 23 the blank row above it, row 24 the header, which then shows U+F0B2C (`󰬬`), and row 25 the blank row below it, the pane's last row. The group is then 3 rows (1 + 2, within the 13 allowed), so the project region is 23 rows, rows 0 to 22: row 0 is its `▲` line (blank), rows 1 to 21 the first 21 of its 22 rows, and row 22 its `▼ 1 more` line (the one hidden row is its last row).

**Worked example of the docked group**: a pane 30 columns wide and 30 rows high (rows counted from 0; colours are not shown; the headers are drawn as the Standing example above draws them, each 30 cells with the pills' caps). Half of 30 is 15, so the group may take 15 rows. The project tree has 2 rows (the Context `homeserver` and its Plan `b2-budget`), so rows 0 to 14 are the project region: row 0 is its `▲` line (blank), rows 1 and 2 its rows, rows 3 to 14 the empty middle. The group is rows 15 to 29. Row 15 is the blank row above the first header. Row 16 is Standing's header and row 17 its reserved `▲` row (blank). Rows 18 to 22 are the 5 Standing rows: `cpd` (its title and its one Plan `perm-managers`), a spacer row, and `host` (its title and the clickable ` ╰󰬪 new`). Row 23 is Standing's reserved `▼` row and also the empty row above Archive's header: the ONE shared row. Row 24 is Archive's header (open, so the glyph is U+F0B26) and row 25 its reserved `▲` row (blank). Rows 26 to 28 are the 3 rows of one archived Context, expanded: its title, its archived Plan and its closing row `╰󰬬 collapse`. Row 29 is Archive's reserved `▼` row (blank), above the statusline. Count: Standing is 8 rows (rows 16 to 23: the header, 2 reserved rows and 5 rows) and Archive is 6 (rows 24 to 29: the header, 2 reserved rows and 3 rows), with the blank row 15: 1 + 8 + 6 = 15, exactly the 15 that half of 30 allows, so nothing scrolls. Archive is folded by default. Folded, Archive is 2 rows (its header and the blank row below it, pro-d351), so the group is 1 + 8 + 2 = 11 rows, aligned to the bottom: rows 19 to 29. Row 19 is the blank row. Rows 20 to 27 are Standing: row 20 its header, row 21 its reserved `▲` row, rows 22 to 26 its 5 rows (`cpd` with its title and its Plan `perm-managers`, a spacer row, and `host` with its title and the clickable ` ╰󰬪 new`), and row 27 its reserved `▼` row, the ONE shared row above Archive's header. Row 28 is Archive's header (U+F0B2C) and row 29 the blank row below it, the pane's last row. The project region is then rows 0 to 18 (19 rows): row 0 its `▲` line, rows 1 and 2 its two rows, and rows 3 to 18 the empty middle. The 11 rows are within the 15 that half of 30 allows, so nothing scrolls.

- **Cursor.** Keyboard only: a click never moves or shows it. It moves between Sessions only (Context rows are not selectable) and, after the last Session row, on into the Inbox section's item rows (below; the header, the cue lines, the up-to-date row and the blank rows are skipped by the cursor and the cursor goes back up from the first item row to the last Session; there is no toggle row, pro-d147), is drawn as the blue block (colour 4 inverted: text in the terminal's background colour, contract §6.1.1) across the full row only while the pane has keyboard focus (`focus-events`, §6.1) and after an arrow key; Enter, `n` and `x` act on it only while it shows.
- **Inbox section** (hs-d165, hs-d167, hs-d168, hs-d298, hs-d337, hs-d339, hs-d345 to hs-d349, pro-d147, pro-d177; contract §2.2 "Inbox item", commands §21). The right column (the `widgets` view, below) shows, directly under the machine lines, the Inbox, the **single source of "needs you"**: the open, visible items (not snoozed, not dismissed) of **every** Context, in the order of `cpd inbox list` (red, yellow, magenta, blue, cyan, white; oldest first; `engine-down` first, when no live Manager exists). Its section header is the **flush form** of §17 (`flush_title`, pro-d147, which supersedes pro-d141 and the collapsible, rail-and-toggle Inbox of hs-d337 and hs-d476) and the Inbox is **flat and bottom-aligned**: no `│` rail, no closing row, no fold state, no 3-item limit; an item is one list row or two, by its content. **Rows**, top to bottom, of a section of `height` rows: row 0 blank (spacing above the header); row 1 the header; row 2 the ▲ cue line; rows 3 to `height - 2` the list, as many rows as the items' heights add up to (1 or 2 each, below), or with no item one muted row ` up to date, drink some water` (column 0 blank, the text from column 1); the last row, the pane's last row, the ▼ cue line. **The header** spans the full pane width from column 0: `───` (three muted `─`, columns 0 to 2), the title pill `Inbox` (caps U+E0B6 and U+E0B4, the static grey pill `palette::pill_static()`, its left cap at column 3), a muted `─` fill, the count pill `<n>` (`n` the count of visible open items; the same grey pill) and one muted `─` at column `W - 1`; no padding cell on either side. At `W` = 30 with 2 items it is 3 + 7 (the title pill) + 16 `─` + 3 (the count pill) + 1 = 30 cells. The header's column 0 `─` is the first cell of the pane, next to tmux's `┃` border cell; tmux draws its `┃` in the middle of its own cell, so half a cell lies between the vertical line and the header and the two do not join (pro-d157; docs/research/inbox-pane.md). **An item row** has one blank column on each side: it is drawn at columns 1 to `W - 2` (width `W - 2`) as ` <glyph> <label> … <age> `: the tier glyph at column 1 (the glyph in its tier's colour, bright, the row is clickable; §6.1.1; its tier glyph, or for three kinds its own, below), a space, the label cut with `…` so that it never reaches the age, the age right-aligned and ending at column `W - 2` (`42s`, `5m`, `3h`, `2d`: the largest whole unit of `age_seconds`), columns 0 and `W - 1` blank; for example ` \u{F12F4} cc-api-orc-apollo#2309 merg… 5h` over `   Add retries to the payment client` (two rows, below) and ` \u{F0362} cpd#129 merge conflict       18m` (a one-row item; the escape stands for the glyph, written here as its code point; the first glyph is yellow, the second red). An `unread` item is ` \u{F06F1} cpd replied 2m` (cyan glyph, pro-d401) over `   Variable-height Inbox rows` (its Row 2, the Plan's title); a one-row item stays one row, with no blank row under it. **An item is one row or two** (pro-d171, amended by pro-d177; contract §2.2 "Inbox item"): its height is 1 when its label has no Row 2 (no `\n`, or nothing after it) and 2 otherwise (one function, `item_height` in `tui/src/widgets/inbox.rs`). **Row 1** is the row above, unchanged: the first line of the stored `label`. **Row 2**, when it has one, is its second line, in muted colour 8 (`palette::muted_text()`): column 0 blank, columns 1 and 2 the `LEAD_WIDTH` (2) spaces, the subtitle from column 3 (under the label), cut with `…` so that it ends at most at column `W - 2`; an item with no Row 2 takes one row and no blank row follows it. The state dots and spinner glyphs stay reserved for the Context tree (hs-d483). The Inbox's order is that of `cpd inbox list`. **Hits:** the header row is `Hit::Header` (no action); both rows of a two-row item and the only row of a one-row item are `Hit::Item(i)` (a left click jumps to its cause, a right click opens its menu) and the `Link` widget covers Row 1's label only; the spare blank row of a capped list, the cue lines and the up-to-date row are no hit; there is no toggle. **The tier glyphs** (hs-d483; User, 2026-10-20; decided work, hs-d301). The urgency levels are named by their colours and rise in urgency white < cyan < blue < magenta < yellow < red (hs-d570 added the notice tier between white and magenta, pro-d16 named it cyan, and pro-d401 swaps the two: unread is cyan, the notices are white, the rank unchanged; blue means focus and selection only, amended by pro-d58 for the blue Inbox tier for external support, `review-requested`, between cyan and magenta). The glyph comes from the item's **urgency** (its tier), never from its kind and is drawn in the urgency's existing colour, **with three exceptions by kind** (pro-d98, pro-d100; User, 2026-10-27; an exception to hs-d483 for these three kinds only): `deploy` draws U+F15A9 (`\u{F15A9}`, yellow tier), `pr-ready` draws U+F12F4 (`\u{F12F4}`, yellow tier; it was U+F069A) and `review-requested` draws U+F12F2 (`\u{F12F2}`, blue tier; it was U+F0368); each is coloured by the item's tier colour as before (`palette::color_clickable(...)`, `palette::tier_span`). Every other kind keeps its tier glyph. The six tier glyphs are named once, in `tui/src/palette.rs` beside the urgency colours:

| Urgency (colour) | Glyph: code point and escape | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| white | U+F0366 (`\u{F0366}`) (pro-d401) | a cpd notice: curation, nothing blocks; also a change in the models a provider offers (hs-d570, pro-d401); also a pull request of yours in progress (updating, fixing, checks running, waiting; pro-d130, pro-d428) |
| cyan | U+F06F1 (`\u{F06F1}`) (hs-d570, pro-d16, pro-d401) | an unread reply (pro-d401); also a pull request of yours that is a draft or stacked (pro-d428) |
| blue | U+F0368 (`\u{F0368}`) (pro-d58) | external support (the blue tier's glyph; its only kind today, `review-requested`, draws its own, U+F12F2) |
| magenta | U+F173A (`\u{F173A}`) (hs-d570: back from U+F06F1) | a decision before the work runs (a Plan review, a question while the Plan is still planning) |
| yellow | U+F069A (`\u{F069A}`) | pull-request work (the yellow tier's glyph; its two kinds today, `pr-ready` and `deploy`, draw their own: `deploy` U+F15A9 in yellow; `pr-ready` U+F12F4 is drawn in the colour of its own urgency, red `Meaning::Failed`, yellow `Meaning::Review`, cyan `Meaning::Notice` or white `Meaning::NotStarted`, pro-d130) |
| red | U+F0362 (`\u{F0362}`) | a blocker only the User can clear (a dialog while the Plan runs, `engine-down`, `engine-error`, `pr-closed`) |

The header's lines are colour 8 and its two pills are read-only title pills (colour 7 inverted: text in the terminal's background colour, `palette::pill_static()`, hs-d475, hs-d480, hs-d534); the items are not (their own tier glyphs and colours; the label is 15, the age and the Row 2 subtitle 8, contract §6.1.1); the up-to-date row and the cues are colour 8. **The Inbox's size and position** (pro-d147, pro-d177 for the heights, replacing pro-d130's top placement and the share rule of hs-d307). The `widgets` column is: row 0 blank, row 1 ` <hostname>` (bold), row 2 the CPU/GPU/memory line, then `rest`, the rows below. The Inbox section sits at the **bottom** of `rest`: its first row is `rest.bottom() - height`, so it grows upward as items arrive and the rows between the usage line and the section are blank. `height` = list rows + 4, where list rows = the sum of the items' heights (1 or 2 each, below), or 1 for no item (the up-to-date row), capped at `rest.height`; when capped, list rows = `height - 4` and the items drawn are those from the scroll offset on whose heights add up to at most the list rows, stopping at the first one that does not fit; the rows left (at most 1, when the next item has two rows) stay blank above the ▼ line and an item never splits across them; fewer list rows than the next item's height show no item, only the ▼ cue. The items scroll with the mouse wheel (`WHEEL_ROWS` items a notch) over the section only; the scroll offset counts items, the ▲ and ▼ counts are items and the largest offset is the smallest one from which the heights of the remaining items add up to at most the list rows (every item when none does). Rows that do not fit are cut from the bottom of the section. The offset is view state only (starts at 0, a refresh keeps it, nothing is written) and is clamped by `Window` (§17 "Scroll cues"); the keyboard cursor on an item scrolls the list to keep it visible. **Worked examples** (a 30 x 12 column, machine `homeserver` at 23% CPU and 41% memory; rows 0 to 2 are the blank row, ` homeserver` and the usage line): **0 items**: `rest` is rows 3 to 11 (9 rows); the section is 5 rows, rows 7 to 11: row 7 blank; row 8 the header with count 0; row 9 blank (the ▲ line); row 10 ` up to date, drink some water`; row 11 blank (the ▼ line); rows 3 to 6 are blank. **2 items**, each with a Row 2: the section is 8 rows, rows 4 to 11: row 4 blank; row 5 the header (count 2); row 6 blank (▲); rows 7 and 8 item 1 (Row 1, Row 2); rows 9 and 10 item 2; row 11 blank (▼). **12 items**, each with a Row 2: the section is capped at the 9 rows of `rest`, rows 3 to 11, with 5 list rows: 2 items fit and 1 list row is blank. Scrolled to 0: row 3 blank; row 4 the header (count 12); row 5 blank (▲); rows 6 to 9 items 1 and 2; row 10 blank; row 11 `▼ 10 more` (ends at column 28). Scrolled to 3: row 5 `▲ 3 more` (ends at column 28); rows 6 to 9 items 4 and 5; row 10 blank; row 11 `▼ 7 more`. Scrolled to the maximum (10): row 5 `▲ 10 more`; rows 6 to 9 items 11 and 12; row 10 blank; row 11 blank (no ▼). **3 items** of heights 2, 1, 2 (5 list rows, the section is 9 rows, rows 3 to 11): row 3 blank; row 4 the header (count 3); row 5 blank (▲); rows 6 and 7 item 1 (Row 1, Row 2); row 8 item 2 (one row, nothing under it); rows 9 and 10 item 3; row 11 blank (▼). **6 items** of heights 1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1 (8 list rows, capped at the 5 list rows of `rest`): scrolled to 0: row 5 blank (▲); row 6 item 1; rows 7 and 8 item 2; rows 9 and 10 item 3; row 11 `▼ 3 more`. Scrolled to 1: row 5 `▲ 1 more`; rows 6 and 7 item 2; rows 8 and 9 item 3; row 10 item 4; row 11 `▼ 2 more`. Scrolled to the maximum (2): row 5 `▲ 2 more`; rows 6 and 7 item 3; row 8 item 4; row 9 item 5; row 10 item 6; row 11 blank (no ▼). **5 items** of heights 1, 1, 2, 2, 2 (7 list rows, capped at 5): scrolled to 0: row 6 item 1; row 7 item 2; rows 8 and 9 item 3; row 10 blank (item 4 has two rows and one row is left); row 11 `▼ 2 more`. **The tree's cue lines and layout.** The tree (the left pane; its header is the tmux pane title) is laid out inside the pane's one blank column on each side (width `W - 2`, from column 1): row 0, the blank row under the title, is the ▲ line; the list starts at row 1; the pane's last row, or the row above the error footer when the snapshot has an error, is the ▼ line; the error footer stays below the ▼ line. A pane with fewer than 3 rows beyond the footer has no ▼ line: the list takes the rows after row 0. `no Contexts` is the list's first row. The tree scrolls inside its list rows: the wheel over it, 3 rows a notch and the keyboard cursor (a Session row moving out of view scrolls it back; the wheel does not move the cursor), with the cue rule of §17's "Scroll cues" (hs-d348, pro-d147). Examples: a 43 x 12 pane with 11 tree rows: row 0 blank (the ▲ line); rows 1 to 10 the first 10 tree rows; row 11 `▼ 1 more` (ends at column 41). A 43 x 31 pane with 61 tree rows (a Context and 60 Plans), scrolled by one wheel notch (3 rows): row 0 `▲ 3 more`, rows 1 to 29 the 4th to the 32nd tree row, row 30 `▼ 29 more`; scrolled to the end (32 rows hidden above): row 0 `▲ 32 more`, rows 1 to 29 the last 29 tree rows, row 30 blank. **The empty Inbox** (hs-d487, amended by pro-d147): with no open, visible item the list is exactly one muted row ` up to date, drink some water` (colour 8; column 0 blank, the text from column 1), between the ▲ and ▼ cue lines, under the header with the count pill at 0 (the 0-items example above). The row is no hit: a click on it does nothing.
- **Clicks on an Inbox item** jump to its cause (the cockpit never decides; each jump runs a command or is a link):

  | Kind | A left click on the row |
  |---|---|
  | `dialog`, `unread` | `session open <the item's Session>`, then `select-pane` on the chat slot: as a click on that Session's tree row (an archived Session: `session history`, as there) |
  | `plan-review` | a `Link` widget: the label is the Link's text, the cue `󱆭` follows and a plain left click on them opens the item's `url` when present; with no `url` the label draws with no link and a plain click jumps to the Lead instead (no url, no link drawn, the row's jump rule applies). An item with no `url` still jumps; if that jump fails the failure is a `text` dialog (§17 "No notes") |  
  | `loop-guard` (pro-d372) | `session open <the item's Session>`, then `select-pane` on the chat slot: as a click on that Session's tree row (an archived Session: `session history`, as there). The Session is the one the loop guard tripped on; the trip is cleared by the User's next prompt there (L5) or by `cpd session resume` (§10.17) |
  | `refusal-alert` (Plan `agent-refusals`; contract §2.2, §3.7 E25) | `session open <the item's Session>`, then `select-pane` on the chat slot: as a click on that Session's tree row (an archived Session: `session history`, as there). The Session is the one whose refusals crossed the threshold; the rate behind the count is `cpd metrics refusals` (§14.7). No link is drawn and no dialog opens |
  | `drafts-parked` (hs-d731, hs-d733) | jumps to the Plan's Lead Session, as `plan-review` with no `url` does: no link is drawn and no command runs; the contract's rule (§2.2) gives the item its label `<plan>: <N> parked drafts` |
  | `pr-failing`, `pr-changes` (history rows only: hs-d470 dropped the kind, E8 opens none; no check or review state opens an Inbox item, hs-d470) | nothing; no jump, no click action |
  | `pr-ready` (the User's open authored pull request, in every state; the row's colour is the state, contract §2.2 "The authored pull request rule") | the glyph U+F12F4 is drawn in the item's urgency colour. The label is a `Link` widget (the label is the Link's text, the cue `󱆭` follows): a plain left click on it opens the item's `url` (the GitHub pull request page). A click on the rest of the row runs `session open <lead>`, then `select-pane` on the chat slot when a Plan owns the pull request (its Lead Session) and does nothing when none does. While that pull request's merge is running (the merge marker, below, hs-d495) the glyph cell is the yellow spinner and a click does nothing |
  | `pr-closed` (Plan closed-unmerged; contract §2.2 "Inbox item") | no link is drawn; a left click on the row runs `session open <the item's Lead Session>`, then `select-pane` on the chat slot, as a click on the rest of a `pr-ready` row does (Go to Lead); with no Lead it does nothing |
  | `review-requested` | a `Link` widget: the label is the Link's text, the cue `󱆭` follows and a plain left click on them opens the item's `url` (the GitHub pull request page); with no `url` the label draws with no link and a plain click does nothing |
  | `deploy` (pro-d100, A8) | a `Link` widget, as the link kinds: a plain left click on the label opens the item's `url`, the GitHub Actions workflow run's page, in the default browser. Its right-click menu starts with **Approve**, which runs `cpd inbox approve <id>` at once (§21.13; the menu below) |
  | `engine-down` (shown only when no live Manager exists, below) | `cpd watch --ensure` (§12; idempotent) and says nothing (the result goes to the log only, never stderr; a failure is a `text` dialog); no popup (the StatusBar's `󰧭` button still opens the logs) |
  | `engine-error` (history rows only: hs-d314 dropped the kind, E8 opens none; the engine's errors are recorded in Events, counted in the Manager's turn-start digest, hs-d514, contract §3.7) | nothing: no jump, no popup |
  | `job-stuck` (history rows only: hs-d318 dropped the kind, E8 opens none; a stuck Job goes to the Context's Manager as a message, contract §3.7 "A stuck Job") | nothing: no jump, no popup |
  | `curate-retire` (hs-d549, hs-d551; hs-d568, hs-d569 CD4; hs-d592) | Exists only for a curable Context (R6 of hs-d592). Runs `cpd context curation --context <the item's Context> --limit=10` (§3.15; hs-d569 CD4: cockpit asks for 10) and opens the `checklist` dialog (§13.2) with title `Retire records of <context>` (with suffix ` (<shown> of <total>)` when total > 10, hs-d569 CD4) and one entry per row of `retire` (hs-d569 CD2: full `text`, header line `[ ] <id> — <reason> <target>`); on **Approve** runs `cpd context retire --context <context> --approve <ticked ids> --reject <unticked ids>` (§3.17), deciding only the shown entries; on **[Later]** (hs-d569 CD3: the button says it) or Esc/q runs nothing, every entry stays pending for the next opening. With nothing pending the dialog is not opened and nothing runs. A refusal of either command is a `text` dialog (§17 "No notes"). The click decides nothing by itself; dismissing the item (`d`) decides nothing either. Only the `pending` rows are listed: a row that a model pair approved (contract §4.6 "Retirement") is not in the dialog |
  | `curate-docs` (history rows only: pro-d327 removed the documentation suggestions, E8 opens none) | nothing; no jump, no click action |
  | `models-changed` (pro-d13, pro-d16) | opens a read-only `text` dialog (§17, the dialog kit) titled `Models: <provider>` with the announced ids of the item's `changes` read from the provider's `swr_models` row (`swr-models.md` §5) (the provider and `changes.at` are in the item's subject `models:<provider>/<changes.at>`; the announced part and its filter are contract §2.2 "The models-changed rule"): a heading `New (<N>)` and one id per line, then a heading `Gone (<M>)` and one id per line, a part with no ids omitted. No command runs and nothing is decided; Esc/q/Enter closes it. A row that no longer has that `changes` (a newer change replaced it) shows `changed again; the item closes at the next tick` in the dialog. The kind has no `url`, no OSC 8 link and no target, so the simpler rule of the other kinds (copy the `url`, or nothing) is not used: the ids are the point |
  | `question` (history rows only: hs-d306 (1) dropped the kind, E8 opens none) | `session open` of the Context's Manager Session (`cpd context manager --context <c>`, then `session open <manager>`, as a click on a Context row) |

  Every jump and link open of this table runs off the view's thread, as **Inbox actions run off the view's thread** (pro-d350, the `widgets` view) says.

  The cockpit writes no OSC 8 escape sequences in the Inbox rows. The four link kinds (`plan-review`, `pr-ready`, `review-requested`, `deploy`) draw `<label> 󱆭` as a `Link` widget; a plain left click on any part of the output opens the url in the default browser (macOS `open` only, through the `Runner` port, §13.2 Links). For `plan-review` the url is always null (§ D and G of decision hs-d738); for `pr-ready` and `review-requested` the url is the pull request's GitHub page; for `deploy` it is the GitHub Actions workflow run's page (`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/actions/runs/<id>`, GitHub's `html_url`). An item with no `url` draws no link and a plain click acts according to its kind (no link, no open action).
- **A stopped engine restarts itself** (hs-d328, hs-d363, replacing hs-d318's restart by the tree; contract §3.7 "Who restarts a stopped engine"). **The supervisor restarts it** (contract §6.6: the `pane-died` and `window-unlinked` hooks, a failed start retried and logged to `run/watch.log`); **the tree runs no `cpd watch --ensure` by itself**, because the supervisor covers every case a tree running in the same tmux server could see and the tree's own restart raced it (it found the engine already running and left `engine was down: … found it running` on screen). A snapshot (§17) that reads the engine running, or a restart that `found it running`, shows nothing. The tree only **speaks** and only when the engine **stays down past the supervisor's window**: when `locks/watch.lock` has been free on **every** snapshot for **60 s** (view state: the time of the first free read, forgotten at the first held one), the view sends, once per downtime, to **the one Manager whose Session state changed most recently** (hs-d514: the live Manager that was last active; a Session with role `manager`, not archived; `session send <manager> --wake`), `The cpd engine has been down for 60 s and its supervisor has not restarted it; see run/watch.log, start it with cpd watch --ensure.`: the view has no `CPD_SESSION`, so `from` is null (the User's side) and `--wake` wakes the Manager (hs-d514); with no live Manager nothing is sent. It shows no note (hs-d469, replacing hs-d364 (2)'s "short note"): the message to the Manager is the whole of it and the view logs it. **The `engine-down` item shows in the Inbox section only when no live Manager exists** (with one, the message handles it: no red for what an agent handles, hs-d303); its click, the User's own explicit action (`Action::EnsureWatch`), is the one of the table above and its reply goes to the log only, never to stderr (§17: a view never writes to its terminal outside its frame).
- **Clicks.** A click on a live Session opens it in the chat slot and focuses the chat (`session open`, then `select-pane`); a click on an **archived Session** row (a Plan row's Lead or a fork) runs `session history <id>` (§10.12), then focuses the chat; a Context is a collapsible block (§17, "Collapsible blocks"; hs-d337) whose title row is the Context row: a click on the closing toggle row (`╰󰬦 expand` / `╰󰬬 collapse`) shows or hides its archived rows and a click on the title row, elsewhere on a live Context row, runs `cpd context manager --context <c> --by-user` (hs-d542 A1), then `session open <manager>`, then `select-pane` on the chat slot (B3-A6). For a by-user Session the Manager starts with no first message and waits for the User's first prompt to deliver it (hs-d540, hs-d542 A2, §15.7a). Clicks are ignored while a dialog popup is open.
- **Folds** (User, hs-d260). The folds survive a restart of the view: which Contexts have their archived rows hidden and which archived Contexts are expanded (the toggle shows and hides only archived rows, hs-d344; live Contexts start expanded and archived ones folded, hs-d339; the cursor and the scroll position are not kept). They are kept in `$CPD_HOME/run/tui/tree-folds.json` (contract §1.4), a JSON object `{"collapsed": ["<context id>", …], "expanded": ["<context id>", …], "archived": true}`: a Context in `collapsed` has its archived rows hidden (its closing row reads `╰󰬦 expand`) and one in `expanded` has them shown (`╰󰬬 collapse`); the `archived` key is the Archive section's fold (absent or false = folded, true = open), starts folded; a live Context's own rows always show and a Context with no archived rows has no toggle. It is under the same exception as the Plan view's offsets file (above): the view's own state, not Ledger state, written and failing as that file is. **Read** once, at the view's start: a Context in `collapsed` has its archived rows hidden and one in `expanded` has them shown, both counting as known; the `archived` key is the Archive section's fold; ids that match no Context are harmless and a missing key is treated as false. A missing file is today's defaults. A file that cannot be read or is not that object is not an error: the view starts with the defaults, logs `fold state reset: <reason>` (no note, §17 "No notes") and replaces the file at its next write. **Written** atomically (temporary file, rename, parents created) whenever the folds have changed, at most once per second; only Contexts that exist and differ from their start are written, so unknown ids are dropped at the next write. A failed write is logged (`fold state not saved: …`) and retried; it never ends the view.
- **`n`** asks for the new Plan's id in an **`input`** popup (the dialog kit above; validation `plan-id`; its question and texts are the former inline prompt's, `Fork <label> into a new Plan, name:`; Enter starts, Esc cancels, an empty or invalid id is refused inside the popup) and runs `plan new` (§4.1) in the selected Session's Context: the Plan forks the Context's grounded Lead (R15), the one deviation from cpd 1's `n`, which forked the selected session. On a Context row it says `pick the session to fork`.
- **`x`** closes the selected Session's pane after a **`confirm`** popup (the dialog kit above) asking `Close <label>? pi stops; the session file stays`, preceded by `<label> is working.` when its state is `working`, with `[Close]` and `[Cancel]`; only Enter, `y` or a click on `[Close]` closes. It runs `cpd session close <id>` (§10.9). The Session in the chat slot is refused with `switch to another session first`, also when it moved there while the popup was open. On a Context row it does nothing. `<label>` is the Session's name.
- **`s` and `d`** act on the Inbox item under the cursor (they do nothing on a Session row): `d` runs `inbox dismiss <id>` at once; `s` opens the snooze choices, the menu's three `Snooze …` entries (↑↓ and Enter pick one, Esc closes), then runs `inbox snooze <id> <15m|1h|tomorrow>`. Enter on an item row acts as a plain click does (above). A refusal is a `text` dialog with the failure (§17 "No notes"); `item_closed` cannot happen for these keys any more: a closed item is the no-op of §21's intro (air-d26), which answers ok and opens no dialog. The item leaves the section when the Inbox-* Event reaches the view (§17).
- **`$`** toggles the cost counters of the Context and Plan rows (pro-d189, pro-d196; see Cost counters). It needs no cursor (like `?`), never shows or hides the cursor, works while the pane is not focused and an open menu takes it like every key.
- **`?`** opens the legend popup. The view has no other key that opens the menu or acts on it; what a key used to do is still a command.
- **Labels** (contract §2.2: ids are unique, immutable and need not be readable; the title is the visible label). A Context row shows the Context's **id**, a Plan Lead row the Plan's **id** and a fork row (a side Session) `<plan id>·<first 4 characters of its Session id>` (for example `cross-repo·7f3a`); a fork with no Plan keeps the fallback, the first 8 characters of its Session id. Archived rows follow the same rule. Titles and names no longer show in the tree (User, hs-d101; this supersedes the titles rule, hs-d63).
- **The Archive section** (User, 2026-11-02 EST, pro-d348 and pro-d349, extending pro-d347, amended by pro-d351; amends hs-d698 and hs-d707). The archived Contexts are not a row of the project tree: the tree has **no `archive` row** (no `󰬦 archive` row, no archived Context at its root). They live in a docked collapsible section `Archive` **below** the Standing section, in the docked group ("The Standing section" above). **Header**: `section::flush_title_with("Archive", Some(glyph), width)` (`tui/src/section.rs`), the same style and position as Standing's: `───Archive────…<glyph>─` from column 0 to the last column, the left pill `Archive` and the right pill the fold glyph, both static grey pills (`palette::pill_static()`), no count. The glyph is U+F0B26 (`󰬦`, `fold::DOWN`) when the section is open and U+F0B2C (`󰬬`, `fold::UP`) when it is folded, the same bottom-docked direction as Standing's. **The section is FOLDED by default**, and is drawn only when at least one Context is archived (a Permanent Context is never archived); with none there is no Archive section. **Spacing** when open: one empty row above the header, one empty row (the reserved `▲` row) between the header and the first archived Context, one empty spacer row between two archived Context blocks, one empty row (the reserved `▼` row) between the last archived Context and the statusline. When Standing is above Archive and open, the empty row below Standing and the empty row above Archive's header are ONE shared empty row; when Standing is folded, Standing's own blank row below its header separates them (pro-d351). A folded Archive is its header with one empty row above it and ONE empty row below it (pro-d351); at the bottom of the pane that row below is the pane's last row, which is blank. **List**: the archived Contexts in the order the tree's items list them, each as a muted block exactly as the project tree draws an archived Context (colour 8 on every mark, hs-d534): the title row, then its archived Plans, forks and Manager rows when its own closing toggle has them expanded, then its closing row; one spacer row between two blocks and none after the last; the spacer rows count as list rows and scroll with them. When the group does not fit, the rule of "The docked group" above applies: Standing first, Archive keeps at least one list row, and the section scrolls on its own. **Fold**: a left click on the header folds or opens the section (one hit, no right-click menu, never a cursor stop); its fold is persisted in `tree-folds.json` under the `archived` key (the file format is unchanged: absent or false = folded, true = open; old files without the key still load). The reserved, cue and blank rows are no hit. **Clicks and menu**: the archived Contexts' rows keep every click and menu they had and are never cursor stops: a click on an archived Context's title row unarchives it and opens its Manager, a click on its closing toggle row (`╰󰬦 expand` / `╰󰬬 collapse`) shows or hides its archived rows, a right click opens the archived menu (Rename…, Copy id, Unarchive, Delete), and a click on an archived Session row runs `session history <id>` (above). Every row of an archived object carries `archived_at` from the read model (§17). History: hs-d698, hs-d707, amended by pro-d348 and pro-d351 (pro-d351: a folded docked section is its header plus one blank row below it; the group's rows, the four folded cases and both worked examples are recomputed).
- **Right-click menu** (**every item is a `cpd` command**: the tree only runs commands). A right click on an Inbox item row opens the menu with its four entries (table below); a right click elsewhere opens the menu of its row. A right click opens a menu, drawn by the view (ratatui) over the tree at the click and clamped inside the pane. ↑↓ and Enter pick an item, Esc closes it; a click picks an item; a click outside closes it. There is **no key** that opens the menu: `n`, `x` and `?` stay as above. The tree has **no inline prompt row** (hs-d295, hs-d297): the `…` items (**New Context…**, **New Plan…**, **New session…**, **Rename…**, **Fork…**) type their text in an **`input`** popup of the dialog kit, with the questions, starting values and texts of the former prompt kept verbatim (`Title: ` for a Context's or Plan's title, `Name: ` for a Session's name); **Rename…** starts with the current text; validation is `title` for Contexts and Plans, `name` for Sessions. **Close** asks in a **`confirm`** popup first, as `x` does. **Archive** asks in a **`confirm`** popup, `Archive <label>?` with `[Archive]` and `[Cancel]` (hs-d297; this supersedes hs-d90's "Archive runs at once, with no `y/N`"; the rest of hs-d90 stands). The commands each item runs and the opening of the new Lead below, are unchanged. The items by row:

  | Row | Items | Command each runs |
  |---|---|---|
  | Inbox item | Snooze 15 min, Snooze 1 h, Snooze until tomorrow 09:00, Dismiss | `inbox snooze <id> 15m`, `inbox snooze <id> 1h`, `inbox snooze <id> tomorrow`, `inbox dismiss <id>` (§21.3, §21.4) |
  | Context | New Plan…, Rename…, Copy id, Archive, Delete | `plan new` (§4.1), `context rename` (§3.7), `context archive` (§3.8), `context delete` (§3.14) |
  | Plan | New session…, Rename…, Copy id, Archive, Delete | `session fork <the Plan's Lead>` (§10.3), `plan rename` (§4.9), `plan archive` (§4.10), `plan delete` (§4.14) |
  | Fork (side Session) | Open, Rename…, Fork…, Copy id, Close, Archive | `session open` (§10.4), `session rename` (§10.7, `--session <id>`), `session fork` (§10.3), `session close` (§10.9), `session archive` (§10.10) |
  | empty tree area | New Context… | `context new` (§3.1) |
  | any archived row | Rename…, Copy id, Unarchive and Delete on a Plan or Context row (hs-d527; also on a live Plan row whose Lead is asleep and a live Context row whose Plans are all asleep or archived, which then have Delete last) | `context rename` (§3.7), `plan rename` (§4.9) or `session rename` (§10.7), `Copy id` (no cpd command; below) and `context unarchive` (§3.9), `plan unarchive` (§4.11) or `session unarchive` (§10.11); the rename commands accept archived objects (F4) |

  **Copy id** (hs-d102) is offered on every row that has an id: Context, Plan, fork and archived rows. It copies the row's shown id (see Labels) to the User's clipboard with `tmux -L <socket> set-buffer -w -- <id>`; tmux sends it to the outer terminal by OSC 52, which works over ssh when the terminal allows it (tmux's default `terminal-features` give `xterm*` the `clipboard` feature). Whether it reaches the User's Ghostty on the Mac is **unverified** until the User tries it. It says nothing. It is the one item that runs no `cpd` command: it changes no Ledger state.

  **Opening the new Lead** (hs-d103). After **New Plan…**, **Fork…** or **New session…** succeeds, the tree runs `session open <the new Session id>` (from the command's JSON: `plan new`'s `lead.session`, `session fork`'s Session id), then focuses the chat slot, as Open does. The commands themselves never move the chat slot.

  **Archive of the chat slot's Lead** (F3, hs-d90). Archive on a Session row (a Plan row's Lead, or a fork) whose Lead holds the chat slot, or a Context row whose Manager holds the chat slot, cannot go straight to the archive command, which refuses with `in_chat_slot` (§10.10, unchanged). The tree first frees the slot, then archives: it opens the next live Session in tree order, excluding every Session the archive cascade archives (`session open`, then focuses the chat); if none follows, the previous one; if there is none at all, it runs `session park`, so the placeholder holds the slot. Then it runs the archive command. Only the tree does this two-step; the CLI keeps its refusal.

  A refusal (`archive_blocked`, `in_chat_slot`, `archived`, …) is a `text` dialog with the failure (§17 "No notes").
- **New Plan… and New Context…** ask a title in an `input` popup (validation `title`); the tree derives the id. The id is a lowercase ASCII slug of the title: each run of other characters becomes `-`, leading non-letters are dropped and it is cut to fit the id pattern (Plan `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,23}$`, Context: contract §2.1); `-2`, `-3`, … are appended while the id is taken in the tree's snapshot. New Plan… runs `plan new <id> --context=<c> --title=<title> --by-user` (hs-d542 A1): no repo, a Plan has none (R34, A12; its Workflows are added with `workflow add`). For a by-user Session, pi starts with no first message and waits for the User's first prompt to deliver it (hs-d540, hs-d542 A2, §15.7a). **New Context… is ONE dialog** (pro-d114, superseding hs-d297): a `form` dialog (§13.2, the dialog kit) titled `New Context`, with title input (label `Title:`) and owner selection (label `Owner:`, options the policy files' stems sorted, the first selected at start, the owner list as the tree derives it). Enter or [OK] confirms (only when the title passes validation) and runs `context new <id> --title=<title> --owner=<chosen>`; Esc or [Cancel] cancels and nothing runs. The cockpit takes no "Another owner" choice (pro-d114); the login box and confirm are gone. With no policy file the refusal is a `text` dialog `No owner policy: add $CPD_HOME/policy/<owner>/owner.toml`, running nothing. A title no id can be made of is refused in a `text` dialog after [OK], nothing runs.
- **Right button.** The view relies on tmux 3.4's default root `MouseDown3Pane` binding: believed to pass the click to a pane whose app captures the mouse (`mouse_any_flag`) and to show tmux's own menu otherwise (**unverified**). cpd adds no binding for it (§6.1, §13.1 unchanged).

**`plan`.**
- **No top row, no tabs** (User, hs-d102). The ` explore Jobs ` box, when the Plan has one, starts at the top of the pane, inside the margin below, with the Workflow boxes in the rows under it; the view draws no Context id, no tab and no separator line. Switching Leads is the tree's (Enter or a click). With no Lead in the chat slot, the message row reads ` no Lead session in the centre` (colour 8). With a Manager in the chat slot, the pane shows Pulse (one row per Plan of the Context), not the Plan view. With the placeholder or a history pane in the slot, the message shows.
- **Chart:** the Plan's Jobs in a flowchart of boxes (reference `flow.rs`, ported), laid out when a snapshot arrives or the pane width changes, and at no other time; at a frame change only spinner glyph cells change, never the layout. Each Workflow box is a `BoxWidget<Full>` (the box widget, `tui/src/box_widget.rs`), a full box with rounded corners (`Borders::ROUNDED`, hs-d474), whose body is the flow chart of that Workflow's Jobs; the box's title row is drawn by the widget and reads ` ╭─ <key> · <repo name> 󱦰 <base> · <pull request> ` (one `─` after the corner, then the key, B5), and its body contains the chart; the chart has no padding of its own (the widget's one column of padding is the only one). Inside a blank margin of 1 column and 1 row (`CHART_MARGIN`; the Box rule, contract §6.1.1 "Boxes": one blank column each side, one blank row above the first box and below the last, the canvas) that belongs to the chart's canvas, not to the scroll window (which is the whole body, so scrolled content reaches the pane's edges; at scroll (0, 0) nothing touches them; this is the one place where the pane clips a box); the layout test asserts the margin of the container at scroll (0, 0) only and the walls of the boxes the pane shows whole. A Workflow with no Jobs shows an empty box (` no Jobs `, colour 8). Cancelled Jobs shown as a colour 8 pill (hs-d518, hs-d534). Pulse's `MARGIN` (2 columns, the **Row layout** and **Buckets** bullets) is unchanged, as are the chart's message row's: Pulse rows and that row are not boxes.
