Each Job is a pill: `` (U+E0B6), the compact body `<icon> <key>[│#<n>]│<tier>` (hs-d474: no padding inside the caps and none before the `│`; pro-d62: `#<n>` is the Job's Attempt count n, shown only from the second Attempt on, between the key and the tier, so the tier is always the last cell of the pill; e.g. `󰗠 titles-docs-2│S3` and, from the second Attempt, `󰗠 titles-docs-2│#2│S3`; the label is `#<n>`, while Attempt ids in commands, logs and the store stay `aN`; the keys of a column are padded so the right edges align). The `<tier>` is the Tier a Job is shown at, derived by contract §3.4a: the Tier of its active Attempt, or its `retry_tier` while queued at that Tier after a `job retry`, or the Tier of its latest Attempt, or its stored `tier`. After a `job retry --tier <T>`, a Job shows `<T>` until an Attempt starts at that Tier. The `│` (U+2502) in the pill's style (User, Plan tui-visuals), then `` (U+E0B4). The two caps are one cell each, so the pill is two cells wider than its text, and the layout's widths follow from the text; they are drawn as a **coloured pill** (hs-d534, contract §6.1.1: the status colour's base colour as the background (a pill that is not clickable takes the base index, contract §6.1.1 rule (3); pro-d63), text in the terminal's background colour (inverted), the icon included, caps the same colour as `fg`: draft 5, queued 7, running 6, landing 3, merged 2, failed 1, cancelled 8; from `palette::pill(…)`) on the normal background, so the pill has rounded ends (hs-d266; mockup: `✓ header-reverse│S2`, the `✓` standing for the status icon). A `running` Job's icon spins `` (the 28 moon_alt phases, one frame every 50 ms on the shared clock, as listed in §17 section 17 "The tree's dot rule"); every other status, landing `󱑤` included, stays static; the `queued` icon stays `󰝦` U+F0766 (nf-md-circle_outline, hs-d235; the Lead's assumption in hs-d579: it is not a dot of the tree). A `cancelled` Job's pill is colour 8; colours and icons are unchanged (User, hs-d567). A pill's colour shows the status again (hs-d534, which replaces hs-d530's single interactive colour; the icon shows it too) and the Job pills take the base colours and the tree's counters the bright pairs (they sit in clickable rows), the tree's failed counter staying always red (hs-d580, §13.2). A `failed` Job's pill is **red in every case** (hs-d586 refined by pro-d88): with the static glyph U+F0159 while the Job is not being worked on, and the moon loader (the 28 frames of §17 section 17, one frame per 50 ms on the shared clock `palette::frame`) while it is, each failed pill by its own Job (hs-d586 refined by pro-d88). A `cancelled` Job's pill is colour 8 with the static U+F0159. A Job pill is read-only (pro-d63): a click on it and every key do nothing, no pill is selected and no pane opens. **Job connector lines** (R1, R5): a Job's connector line leaves from the right cap of its own pill (the cell right after the pill's last cell, where the left arm of a `─` or `┤` points) and enters the Job it feeds at the cell just left of that pill's left cap (where the right arm of a `─` or `├` points), with an arm pointing toward the cap. Pill widths do not change: a `cancelled` Job's pill is as wide as itself and never widens a live pill; a live pill is as wide as the widest live pill of its column. A card of several stacked Jobs with the same needs is held by a bracket on each side: the left bracket (one cell left of the pills' left caps) and the right bracket (one cell right of the pills' right caps) touch every pill of the card. **Every connector cell touches what it joins** (R5): in the drawn view, scrolled or not, every connector cell's arms lead to another connector cell, to a pill's cap (Job lines) or to a `┬` / `┴` on a box border; no line ends in a blank cell, in the title's text or on a plain `─`. The glyphs and their arms: `─` left,right; `│` up,down; `╭` down,right; `╮` down,left; `╰` up,right; `╯` up,left; `├` up,down,right; `┤` up,down,left; `┬` left,right,down; `┴` left,right,up; `┼` all four. Messages are one row at the bottom of the pane: `no Plan yet`, `loading… (first fetch)`, or the note.
- **Workflow boxes** (R34, A15; contract §2.5). The chart is split into **one box per Workflow** that is not `cancelled`, each a bordered block (`Borders::ALL`, colour 8, with rounded corners `╭ ╮ ╰ ╯` instead of `┌ ┐ └ ┘`, hs-d474; every other line and junction, `─`, `│`, the `┬` and `┴` where the needs links join a box, stays) holding the cards and Dependency connectors of that Workflow's Jobs, laid out inside it as the single chart was. A Workflow with a base Workflow or a need of another Plan carries one more line under its title, `on <plan>/<key>` (the base Workflow, a reference printed bare for this Plan's own) and `needs <plan>/<key>` for each need of another Plan, colour 8; a same-Plan base Workflow is also an arrow, dashed, and orders the boxes as a need does; a reference to another Plan has no box and no arrow (contract §2.5, hs-d324). The box's title, on its top border, reads ` <key> · <repo name> 󱦰 <base> · <pull request> `: the Workflow key in bold (colour 7, the title's read-only text; contract §6.1.1); the repo's directory name (the last component of `workflows.repo`); its base; then `#<number> <state>` once the Workflow has a pull request, where `<state>` is `open`, `merged`, or `closed` while the pull request is closed without a merge (`pull_request.state` is `closed`, A11), in the palette's pull request state colours (contract §6.1.1, hs-d534; the box title is a hit target, so they are the bright pairs: `open` is 15, and 11 only when its pull request is ready to merge, `merged` 10; reference `pr_state`; `closed` is cyan (`Meaning::Waiting`'s colour) while the Lead handles it, and **red only when the Plan's Lead has an open, visible `dialog` item**, it asks the User about it; a closed pull request no Plan owns is red, but no box draws one; audit Q4, hs-d303); `<state>` reads, instead of `open`, when the pull request is `open` and its `mergeable` is `conflicting` (`unknown` is not a conflict; `merged` and `closed` never read either word), **the conflict rule** (hs-d532, written once here; the legend refers to it): `updating` while the Workflow has an update Job (`jobs.kind = 'update'`, key `up-<pr>`, hs-d490, hs-d340) that is not ended (`status` `queued` or `running`), in cyan, whether that Job is `running` or `queued` (both are the Lead's agent activity, hs-d534: the two colours of hs-d532 are one); `conflict`, in cyan too (not red: every box is a pull request a Plan owns, so its Lead fixes the conflict, hs-d302, hs-d303), only when no such update Job exists. For example ` api · api-repo 󱦰 main · #12 updating 󱆭 ` and ` api · api-repo 󱦰 main · #12 conflict 󱆭 ` (the state word cyan). The update Job comes from `tui/src/read/flow.rs`'s `Pull`; the colours only from `tui/src/palette.rs`. Else the Workflow's status (`waiting`, `dispatch`) colour 8. **The Lead's dot** (contract §3.6, "The Lead's Workflow", the display rule; hs-d335, pro-d217, pro-d219, pro-d259): the box of the Workflow that the Plan's Lead is working on (`sessions.working_pr`) draws the Lead's working dot while the Lead is `working` and the Workflow is neither `merged` nor `cancelled`, **whether or not the Workflow has a pull request**: with one, the dot follows the state word, a space between: `#<number> <state> <dot>`; without one, it follows the status word: `dispatch <dot>`. The dot is the tree's spinner (``, the 28 frames of §17 section 17, one frame per 50 ms on the shared clock, `palette::frame`), in the Lead's Work colour of pro-d200 ("The Lead dot rule", §17), or red when that Workflow has a failed Job or an open Escalation of one of its Attempts (§17). No other box draws the dot or the red loader, and a Plan whose Lead names no Workflow draws none. The view reads the dot from `PrNode::lead_dot` (`tui/src/read/flow.rs`), which is `Some` exactly when the box draws it. Once the Workflow has a pull request, the title ends with the `Link` widget (Links, below; pro-d60), which draws `#<number> <state>` (and the dot, which is not part of the link) as underlined text, then one space, then the cue `󱆭`: the whole `#<number> <state> <dot> 󱆭` appears as the underlined state and cue, the whole output clickable, and a plain left click opens `pull_requests.url` in the default browser (pro-d60). The Workflow key, the repo, the base and the spaces around the link are not linked; a `cancelled` Workflow (hs-d518) shows `cancelled`, and a Workflow that is `waiting` (display status only, hs-d523) is drawn colour 8 (User, hs-d567). The boxes are laid out **top to bottom** in the order of the needs graph, one row per level: a box sits below every box it needs; boxes of the same level sit side by side in that row, by key (hs-d115). A merged Workflow's level is 0 with no needs, else one more than the highest level among its needs. A Workflow that is not merged (any status but `merged`) is at the level max(1 + the highest level among its needs, M + 1), where M is the highest level of any merged Workflow (no floor when none is merged): **every box that is not merged is drawn below every merged box**, so the work in progress sits together, close below the finished work, instead of sharing a wide row with it (User, 2026-10-18). Each need is a plain box-drawing line from the needed box's bottom border to the needing box's top border: a `┬` on the bottom border, a line with `╭╮` corners, and a `┴` reaching the top border ON the needing box's top border; there is no arrowhead, the direction being implicit (the needed box sits above; hs-d638), and the ┬ exit is unchanged while the bottom-border text does not cover the box's middle column (pro-d175, pro-d179; see the counter and the cost below). The landing `┴` is on the box's middle column, or when the title covers that column, on the first `─` after the title. Inside a box the Jobs still flow left to right, and a box is as wide as the largest of its own chart, its title plus 4 cells and, when it shows one, its bottom-border text (the counter, and the cost after it when there is one) plus 4 cells: `╭`, `─`, the title with its own leading and trailing space, at least one `─`, `╮`. **The active-time counter** (User, Context records pro-d175 and pro-d182, 2026-10-29 EDT; Plan workflow-counter, PR counter; the code still calls a Workflow a PR): the bottom border of each box reads ` <duration> ` (a space before and after), in `palette::muted_text()` (the border's style), written on the bottom border row from column box.x + 2, right after `╰─`: `╰─ 1h·2m·3s ───────╯`. The duration omits leading zero units and joins them with `·` (U+00B7, one cell wide): under 60 s `<S>s` (`0s`, `42s`); 60 s to 3599 s `<M>m·<S>s` (`1m·0s`, `2m·3s`, `12m·0s`); 3600 s and more `<H>h·<M>m·<S>s` (`1h·0m·0s`, `1h·2m·3s`). Hours are never rolled into days: 90061 s is `25h·1m·1s`. The counter is hidden, a plain `╰──────╯` bottom border, before the first Attempt of the Workflow starts (`elapsed_seconds` is `None`). The box is at least as wide as the counter text with its two spaces, plus 4 (`╰`, `─`, ` <duration> `, at least one `─`, `╯`). A need line that leaves a box (the `┬` on its bottom border) lands on the box's middle column, or, when the bottom-border text covers that column, on the first `─` after the text, as a need line lands on the top border on the first `─` after the title (`land`). The active time (`PrNode.elapsed_seconds`, `tui/src/read/flow.rs`; `None` until a Job of the Workflow has an Attempt) is the length of the union of the Attempt intervals of every Job of the Workflow (every Job with `job.workflow == workflow.key`, of any kind: work, docs, test, impl, open, update; follow-up Jobs after the pull request opened included), except explore Jobs, whose Attempts count in no Workflow's cost and no Workflow's active time, each interval being [`started_at`, `ended_at`, or now when the Attempt has not ended], MINUS the union of the Plan's Lead's `blocked` intervals, in whole seconds rounded down. The Lead's `blocked` intervals come from the `session-state` Events of `plans.lead_session` (`json_extract(data, '$.to')`, in id order): a transition to `blocked` opens one that lasts until the next transition to another state, or until now when there is none. `waiting` is never subtracted, and every Workflow of the Plan loses the same Lead `blocked` time. A queued Job that waits for a resource slot or a dependency has no Attempt, so that wait is excluded by itself. `plan_boxes_at(store, plan, now_ms)` (`now_ms` Unix milliseconds) reads it with the snapshot's own clock; `plan_boxes(store, plan)` keeps its signature and uses the store's clock; the plan view's snapshot (`snapshot_timed`, `tui/src/plan/mod.rs`) passes its own `now_ms`, so a running Attempt counts up to the snapshot's `now`. The counter is static between reads (pro-d182): the view has no timer, no per-second redraw and no per-second re-read, so it is the time as of the last snapshot. The view also re-reads its snapshot when a `pull_requests` row changed (see Rates), with the Event-driven coalescing as before: a conflict clears with no Event (`mergeable` changes silently; only becoming `conflicting` appends `pr-feedback`), so without that a box would keep `conflict`; a change of the update Job's status (`job-started`, `job-merged`, `job-failed`, `job-cancelled`, `job-added`; Events with `plan = p`) re-reads it too, which moves `updating` to `conflict` or back. It reads on no timer: the counter is the time as of the last read (pro-d182). **The cost** (User, Context record pro-d179 item 3, 2026-10-29 EDT; Plan workflow-cost-box, PR cost-box): when the Workflow has cost data, the bottom-border text is ` <duration> · <cost> `, the counter and the cost joined by ` · ` (a space, U+00B7, a space) inside the one pair of outer spaces; `<cost>` is `cpd_core::metrics::format_cost` of `PrNode.cost_usd` (contract §2.2 "Session cost", "Formatting": `$0.450`, `$4.500`, `$0.004`, `$1.23k`: always 5 cells after the `$`, contract §2.2), for example `╰─ 1h·2m·3s · $0.450 ───╯`. `footer_text` in `tui/src/plan/boxes.rs` is still the only place that builds the text, and it drives the box's width, the exit `┬` and the drawing: the whole text is written in `palette::muted_text()` from column box.x + 2, the box is at least as wide as the whole text plus 4, and a need line leaves on the middle column or, when the whole text covers it, on the first `─` after the whole text (in a box 26 cells wide the middle column is 12: ` 5s ` leaves the exit on column 12, and ` 5s · $0.450 ` covers it and moves the exit to column 15). A segment with no value is left out: with no cost data the text is ` <duration> ` exactly as before (no ` · `, and never `$0.000` for a missing cost), and with neither the border is plain; a cost of exactly zero (`Some(0.0)`) is drawn `$0.000`. `PrNode.cost_usd` (`tui/src/read/flow.rs`; `None` until some Attempt of the Workflow has cost data) is the Workflow's cost of contract §2.2 "Totals": the total of the costs of every Attempt of every Job of the Workflow, except explore Jobs, whose Attempts count in no Workflow's cost and no Workflow's active time, each by the rule of contract §2.2 "An Attempt's cost" (the stored `attempts.metrics` `$.cost_usd`, else the own cost of the Attempt's Worker Session file, the two never added); the Lead's and its side forks' own costs are in the Plan row's cost only. It is read by `plan_boxes_at` with the rest of the snapshot, so it is static between reads like the active time (pro-d182): no timer and no per-second re-read, and a running Worker's cost is its cost as of the last read.

  ```
  ╭ schema · api 󱦰 main · #31 open ────╮
  │  󰗠 types│S1 ── 󰗠 gql│S2         │
  ╰────────────────┬─────────────────╯
          ╭───────┴───────╮
          │               │
  ╭ web · web 󱦰 main ┴─╮ ╭ docs · api 󱦰 main ┴─╮
  │  󰽧 page│S1        │ │  󰝦 readme│H2     │
  ╰───────────────────╯ ╰─────────────────────╯
  ```

  A Workflow with no Jobs shows an empty box (` no Jobs `, colour 8). A Plan with one Workflow shows one box; a Plan with no Workflow yet shows the message `no Workflow yet: cpd workflow add` (colour 8), unless it has a reviewed PR (contract §2.2 Plan `reviewed_pr`): then it draws the Review PR box instead (contract §2.6), and the message is not drawn. The wheel and the scroll offsets apply to the whole canvas.

- **The explore Jobs box** (Plan `explore-roles`; Plan `explore-view` moved and retitled it; display only, no schema change). A Plan with at least one explore Job (§5.1) has **one Plan-level box titled ` explore Jobs ` (the leading and trailing space are part of the title; no state word, no pull request, no footer)** in its own row **above the Workflow boxes**. A Plan with no explore Job has no such box, and an explore-only Plan (no Workflows) still renders it. Its body is the same flow chart a Workflow box draws of its Jobs, with the same pills (the key, the kind, the Tier each Job is displayed at (contract §3.4a), the status, the live spinner of a running Attempt and the Attempts) and the connector lines of needs among the explore Jobs as for a Workflow. There is **no need line between the box and a Workflow box**: an explore Job never shares a need with a Workflow Job. It has no `open` Job row and no pull-request or branch footer, and it draws **no cost counter and no active-time counter**: the cost and the active time of an explore Attempt are in the Plan's cost only (contract §2.2 "Session cost", decision pro-d237, unchanged by the visibility). The same Jobs are in `plan render`'s `## Explore` section (§4.5).
- **Pulse** (User, hs-d229, hs-d232): with a Manager in the chat slot, the pane shows Pulse instead of the Plan view: one row per Plan of the Manager's Context, with a sparkline of the Plan's activity, so a stalled Plan stands out. It draws no icon: no dot, no `󰗠` (User, hs-d327). Reads only what the store holds; no write.
  - **When.** The newest `session-moved` Event with `data.place = 'chat'` (over all Sessions) belongs to a Session with role `manager`. With a Lead or a side fork in the slot the Plan view is unchanged; so it is with the placeholder or a history pane (message ` no Lead session in the centre`). The pane's tmux header stays ` Plan `.
  - **Rows.** The Plans of that Context that are not archived and either not done, or done (`plans.done_at`) inside the window (the n buckets shown, see Buckets). In tree order, a Plan row as the tree's Plan row: by tier (its Lead's dot, the Plan row's tier of the tree's rule in §17), then `plans.created_at` newest first (hs-d686, pro-d48).
  - **Row layout,** inside the Plan view's margin (MARGIN: 2 columns left/right, 1 row top; kept at 2 because Pulse rows are not boxes): `<plan id padded to the longest id>  <sparkline>  <age right-aligned in 9>`. The id is plain text. No icon: no dot before the id, no `󰗠`, no merge-count column (User, hs-d327); the sparkline takes the width they freed. The row is 13 + id_width + n columns.
  - **Buckets.** 5 minutes each, aligned to wall-clock multiples of 5 min since the Unix epoch; the last one is the current, partial bucket. The window is n buckets ending now, n = max(12, pane width - 2*2 (margin) - (13 + id_width)). If n < 12, 12 is used and the line is cut at the pane's edge.
  - **Activity** (what a bucket counts). The Events of the Plan (`events.plan`) of kinds plan-phase, plan-review, plan-outlined, plan-done, job-added, job-edited, job-merged, job-failed, job-retried, job-cancel-requested, job-cancelled, attempt-started, attempt-status, attempt-retry, attempt-nudge, all-merged, pr-feedback, workflow-added, workflow-edited, workflow-cancelled, workflow-started, pr-opened, pr-merged, escalation, escalation-answered, escalation-expired, error; plus Lead turns: `session-state` Events with `data.to = 'working'` whose Session has role `lead` (the Plan's Lead and its side forks). Not counted: session-moved, session-registered, session-renamed, session-archived, session-message, inbox-*, context-*, plan-created, plan-renamed, plan-archived, watch-*.
  - **Kinds** (User, hs-d327). Each counted Event has a kind of activity, by its Event kind; the kinds are what the bars are coloured by:

    | Kind | Colour (bright pairs: the row is clickable; contract §6.1.1, hs-d534) | Events |
    |---|---|---|
    | error | red (9) | `error`, `job-failed` |
    | plan / ask | magenta (13) | `plan-phase`, `plan-review`, `plan-done` |
    | PR opened | cyan (14) | `pr-opened` |
    | escalation | cyan (14) | `escalation`, `escalation-answered`, `escalation-expired` |
    | merged | green (10) | `job-merged`, `pr-merged` |
    | other | cyan (14) | every other counted Event, Lead turns included |

    A bucket holding several kinds takes the first in this order: **error, plan / ask, PR opened, escalation, merged, other** (the precedence the colours had, red, magenta, yellow, blue, green, white; the Manager's assumption, accepted with hs-d327, unchanged: only the colours of three kinds moved with hs-d534, so the kind decides, not the colour).
  - **Bars.** A bucket with activity: a bar `▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█` of level ceil(count * 8 / max) (1..8), where max is the largest bucket count over ALL rows (one scale, so rows compare; counts and scale as before hs-d327), in the colour of the bucket's kind (Kinds above): red, magenta, cyan or green, each the bright pair (`Color::LightRed`, `LightMagenta`, `LightCyan`, `LightGreen`). A bucket with no activity: a `▁` in colour 8, so the line never breaks. A row with fewer buckets than the line's n is blank on the left. No `󰗠` and no distinction for a running Attempt.
  - **Age.** Minutes since the Plan's latest activity Event (any time, not only the window); `0m` while one of its Attempts is not ended (status starting, running or merging). The age text follows the tree's rule below (with minutes converted to seconds). Colour 8. Blank when the Plan has no activity Event at all.
  - **Quiet.** A Plan is quiet when all four hold: it has queued or running Jobs (drafts do not count); no Attempt of it is not ended; its latest activity is 30 min old or more (no activity at all also counts); its Lead's dot is not a needs-you dot (`Dot::needs_you()` false). The age cell then reads `quiet <age>` (e.g. `quiet 41m`) in colour 8, like the age (hs-d534: it was the Review colour). The 30 minutes are a constant, not a config key.
  - **Clicks and wheel.** A left click on a row runs the Plan view's `Actions::open_lead(<the Plan's lead_session>)` (session open, then focus the chat slot); a failure is a `text` dialog (§17 "No notes"). The wheel scrolls the rows (3 rows a notch, clamped). No keys, no selection.
  - **Re-read.** A new Pulse snapshot on any Event of the Manager's Context (`events.context`) and on `session-moved`, coalesced as other views; also every 60 s (the window moves and ages tick; a running Attempt is not an Event) and on pane resize (the bucket count changes). Between reads the rows do not change: a row has no spinner.
  - **Escalation bar.** Cyan, agent activity (hs-d534 replaces hs-d352's blue: blue is focus and selection only, contract §6.1.1).
  - **Empty.** A Manager whose Context has no row shows ` no Plans yet` (colour 8) in the message row.

    Example, a 60-column pane, id_width 10, so n = 60 - 4 - 23 = 33 buckets (colours by kind, as above; a `▁` in colour 8 is an empty bucket):

    ```
      cross-repo  █▃▁▁▄▁▁▁▁▁▁▂▁▂▁▁▄▁▁▃▁▁▁▂▁▁▁▁▅▁▁▂▇         4m
      manager     ▁▁▁▁▁▃▁▁▁▁▅▁█▄▁▁▃▁▇▅▃▁▂▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁         3m
      quality     ▁▄▃▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▄▄▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁  quiet 41m
    ```

**`widgets`** (reference `dispatch`), top to bottom: the **Dispatch column** is the machine and the Inbox (pro-d130, placed by pro-d147). Rows: row 0 blank, row 1 ` <hostname>` (bold), row 2 the CPU/GPU/memory line, then `rest`, the rows below, whose bottom holds the Inbox section (§13.2 "Inbox section"; its first row, empty, is `rest.bottom() - height`, its header the next row and its last row is the pane's last row); the Inbox is bottom-aligned and grows upward and the rows between the usage line and the section are blank. There is no git and no Jira section (hs-d257). The pane has no title (contract §6.1, hs-d729).
1. the machine (no header): its hostname in bold (` <hostname>`; the row is colour 7), then ` <cpu icon> N%  <gpu icon> A% B%  <mem icon> M%` (hs-d257, hs-d333), for example `  23%   61% 0%   41%` under ` homeserver`, with the CPU icon `nf-oct-cpu` (U+F4BC), the GPU icon (U+E266) and the memory icon (U+EFC5). The GPU part has one utilization % per GPU, in the order the tool lists them, one space between a GPU's numbers and two spaces between the parts; a GPU that reports no number is `–%` in its place. When no GPU is found (neither tool is available, or its output has no GPU) there is no GPU part at all and the row is `  N%   M%`; a missing tool is an empty list, never an error. All numbers are integers, drawn in colour 7 (read-only text, contract §6.1.1; no thresholds); the load average is not shown. CPU % is the share of non-idle time across all CPUs over the last 2 seconds, so the view keeps its previous CPU sample and shows `–%` until a second sample exists; a number that cannot be read is `–%` too, which is no error of the view (as the hostname, tui-W10). Memory % is used / total. GPU % is the GPU's utilization. All are re-read every 2 seconds. On Linux the CPU comes from two reads of the `cpu` line of `/proc/stat` (idle = idle + iowait) and the memory from `/proc/meminfo` (`MemTotal - MemAvailable`, over `MemTotal`); both files are read (a file read, never a process) through the sampler's reader, which tests script and what a test does not script is unreadable (`–%`). On macOS the CPU is the sum of `ps -A -o %cpu=` divided by `sysctl -n hw.ncpu`, capped at 100 (a point-in-time figure, so it needs no earlier sample) and the memory is `vm_stat`'s pages active + wired down + occupied by compressor, times the page size `vm_stat` prints, over `sysctl -n hw.memsize`. The GPUs come, on Linux, from `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits -lms 2000`, one long-running process for the view's life (one integer per line, one GPU per line; a line that is no integer is `–`) and on macOS from `ioreg -r -d 1 -w 0 -c IOAccelerator` (each accelerator's `"PerformanceStatistics"` dictionary has `"Device Utilization %"=N`; an accelerator without that key is `–`). The macOS parse is unverified on hardware: it is tested on a captured sample only;



**A merge in progress** (User, hs-d495, hs-d550 B4–B5; the marker design is the Lead's, the User may correct it). From the confirm until the background request ends (`cpd tui action merge`, below), **every place that shows that pull request's merge button shows the cockpit's spinner (`palette::SPINNER`, framed by the shared clock as for a running Job) instead and it cannot be clicked**: the Inbox's `pr-ready` row (its glyph cell shows the yellow spinner, a click does nothing) and the right-click menu's **Merge** entry (shown as `Merging`, not selectable). On success the merge's `cpd pr poll` clears the pull request from the lists; on failure the indicator goes and the failure dialog opens (hs-d469 `dialog::show_error`). **One marker is the source every view reads:** `$CPD_HOME/run/tui/merging/<owner>__<repo>__<n>.json` (contract §1.4), one file per pull request. The views (the cockpit's Inbox and the tree's) read the markers on each snapshot and a restarted view reads the same files, so all views and restarts agree. **B5** A pull request is merging (spinner shown) when its marker's pid is alive, or when its marker has `"merged": true` and its pull request's `pull_requests` row is `open`; a marker with `merged: true` whose row is not open and a marker without it whose pid is dead, are ignored.

The menu is drawn as a rounded box (the Box rule, contract §6.1.1 "Boxes", by `tui/src/menu.rs` using box_widget), at the click, clamped inside the pane less one blank column on each side, as the tree's menu is; ↑↓ and Enter pick, Esc closes; a click picks an item; a click outside closes it. The generic menu drawing is shared between the tree's right-click menu and the Inbox's (`tui/src/menu.rs`, shared with `tui/src/tree/menu.rs`, hs-d9: reused, not copied). There is no key that opens it.

**The Inbox's right-click menu** (Dispatch column). Claim is the first entry on `review-requested` rows only and runs `inbox claim <id>` (§21.7, review-requested items only), which creates the review Plan and starts its Lead; the other entries are the Snooze and Dismiss entries. **Approve** is the first entry on `deploy` rows only (pro-d167), then the Snooze and Dismiss entries (no Claim): it runs `cpd inbox approve <id>` (§21.13) at once through the cockpit's command runner, with no confirm popup (pro-d111); a refusal or failure opens the failure dialog titled with the command words, exactly as a refused `Claim` does (`dialog::report`). No other kind has Approve. A `dialog` row whose Session's Plan has a `reviewed_pr` (contract §2.2 Plan) has **Open Link** (opens its `url` in the default browser, as the TUI's links do) and **Copy Link** (copies `url`) first, then the Snooze and Dismiss entries, and no other entry; its click stays Go to Lead (`docs/architecture/attention-inbox.md`, "The reviewed PR of a review Plan"). **A `pr-ready` row's menu** (pro-d130), in this order, each entry only when it applies: **Merge** (status `ready to merge`, so never on an `updating` row, contract §2.2 STATUS row 3; shown busy as **Merging** while the pull request's merge marker is live and then not selectable) runs `cpd tui action merge <owner>/<repo>#<n> --client <name>` at once, no confirm popup (pro-d111); **Post** (status `ready for user review`) runs `cpd pr post --workflow <key> --plan <plan>` (§9.8b) at once, no confirm popup, through the cockpit's command runner, where `<key>` is the key of the `workflows` row of the item's Plan that points to the pull request, read from the store when the entry is picked (the view does not wait for the Slack call: the menu is closed and the view draws on, it shows no spinner, and a failure opens the error dialog titled `Post Pull Request`; a failed post writes nothing and Post is offered again; a post whose outcome is unknown, or one the User made by hand, is recorded by the engine's Slack poll when it finds the message (§9.8b, §21.5), and then the item reads `waiting for peer review` and Post is not offered again); **RePost** (the label's Row 1 tail is `review overdue`, `cpd_core::inbox::pr::is_overdue(item)`; it follows Post and precedes Go to Lead, and Post and RePost never both show: a row that is overdue is posted) runs `cpd pr repost --workflow <key> --plan <plan>` (§9.8b2) at once, no confirm popup, through the cockpit's command runner, with `<key>` and `<plan>` read exactly as Post reads them (the argv is `["repost", "--workflow", &key, "--plan", plan.as_str()]` behind `PROGRAM` and `"pr"`, `tui/src/widgets/mod.rs`; a failure opens the error dialog titled `RePost Pull Request`); the TUI types are `Entry::RePost` in `tui/src/widgets/inbox.rs` (label `RePost`) and `InboxEntry::RePost` dispatched to `Opener::repost(&self, item: &Item)` beside `post`; **Go to Lead** (a Plan owns the pull request) runs `cpd session open <lead>`, then `select-pane` on the chat slot; **Copy Link** (the item has a `url`) runs `tmux set-buffer -w -- <url>` (no `cpd` command); then **Snooze 15 min**, **Snooze 1 h**, **Snooze until tomorrow 09:00** and **Dismiss**. The status is the label's tail, parsed by `cpd_core::inbox::pr::Status::of_item`; the cockpit never re-derives a state from the pull request row. **A `pr-closed` row's menu** (Plan closed-unmerged) has **Go to Lead**, **Copy Link** (its `url`) and the Snooze and Dismiss entries, and no Merge, Post, RePost or Claim. Every other kind's menu is unchanged.

**Inbox actions run off the view's thread** (User, pro-d350, 2026-11-02 EST; tui-W7). (a) Every pick of the `widgets` view's Inbox menu (Approve, Claim, Snooze 15 min, Snooze 1 h, Snooze until tomorrow 09:00, Dismiss, Merge, Post, Go to Lead, Copy Link), every left click on an Inbox item (its jump) and every left click on a link (its `link::open_url`) closes the menu, when one is open, and the view draws the next frame without it BEFORE the command runs to its end, never after. (b) The command runs on the view's `Background` (`tui/src/background.rs`, the one the tree and the Plan view use), one job at a time and in the order the picks and clicks were made, so two clicks never race, while the view goes on drawing and reading input. (c) When a job ends, the view reads the Inbox again at once (a forced read, with no wait for the next commit or safety poll) and redraws; the pick itself only closes the menu and redraws (Accepted assumption A3). (d) A refusal or failure opens the same failure dialog, with the same title as before (`dialog::report` or `dialog::report_why`, as the Plan view's actions do), from that job; the view never waits for the dialog to close. (e) A popup that a jump opens and waits for (the `curate-retire` checklist, a failure dialog) holds the later jobs until it closes: a tmux popup is modal on the client, so no later click can reach the view meanwhile (Accepted assumption A1). (f) **The optimistic hide of a `pr-ready` row** (User, 2026-11-05 EST; refines pro-d350, whose (a) to (e) stand). When the pick is **Post** or **Merge** on a `pr-ready` row, the menu closes at once and the command runs as in (b), and the row is hidden while the command runs: the view leaves it out of the Inbox it draws and out of its clicks and menus, keyed by the pull request. The hide is client-only: it lives in the cockpit's memory, **writes nothing to the database** and sets no snooze, dismissal or closed marker; the command itself writes as it does today. It is lost when the cockpit restarts mid-command (accepted). On **success** the view drops its cached Inbox read, so the next engine tick or poll shows the real new state (a posted pull request reads white `waiting for peer review`); the hidden entry goes once a read no longer shows that row yellow or red. On **failure** the hidden entry goes at once, so the row comes back with the state the database still holds (the database is unchanged), and the failure dialog opens as (d) says and `widgets.log` is written exactly as today. Cyan waiting rows stay listed; this rule filters nothing by urgency.

The column has no engine line, no slots, no Escalations, no Events and no footer hint. The Event log is the `logs` view (R36, below).

**Links** (User, pro-d60; hs-d187, hs-d191). The cockpit links a page through the `Link` widget (pro-d60, 2026-10-26: cpd's cockpit links are one reusable ratatui widget, never OSC 8 terminal escape sequences). the Plan view's Workflow box title draws the pull request's state `#<number> <state>` (and the Lead's working dot when the Lead works on it) as underlined text, then one space, then the cue, the whole output clickable. The Inbox's link-kind rows (the four kinds `plan-review`, `pr-ready`, `review-requested` and `deploy`, §13.2 Clicks on an Inbox item) draw the item's label as the link's text. A click on any other cell does what it did before. The click rule: a plain left click (any modifiers) on a link's cell calls `link::open_url(&*ports.runner, url)`, which opens the url in the default browser; in the `widgets` view that call runs off the view's thread, as **Inbox actions run off the view's thread** (pro-d350) says, and other views are unchanged. The widget API: `Link` takes a url and optional text; `Link::new(url)` draws the cue only (one cell); `Link::text(line)` sets the text (drawn with `Modifier::UNDERLINED` added to each span's style, its colours kept) and outputs `<text> 󱆭` (the space unlined, the cue in `palette::clickable_text()`, not underlined); `Link::width()` returns the output's width in cells (1, or text's width + 2). `Links` holds the (Rect, url) of every link drawn on the frame; `Links::draw(link, area, buf)` renders into `area` and records the rect it drew with the url; `Links::at(pos)` returns the url at that cell or None. The widget never holds an escape character; output is ordinary cells. `open_url` refuses with an `Err` a url that does not start with `http://` or `https://` or holds a byte outside 0x21..=0x7e; otherwise it runs `open` with the url as its one argument through the `Runner` and reports a non-zero exit or a runner failure as an `Err` whose message names `open`, the url and what `open` said on stderr, using the `ErrorCode` of `tree/actions.rs`.

**The StatusBar** (R36, User decision; moved to tmux's status line by the User, Plan tui-visuals, hs-d149, hs-d179) is **not a view and has no pane**: it is the one row of tmux's status line on the cockpit session (contract §6.1), as **one dark grey (colour 8) `─` line across the full width** at the bottom of the client, drawn by tmux from `status-format[0]` (one status row; hs-d567: the chat slot's last row, the one above the line, is empty by its occupant, so the chat's content never touches the line; contract §6.1 "The blank row" has the rules Q1-Q4, the evidence and the 20-row mock-up). There is no `statusbar` view, no `@cpd_view statusbar` and no process behind it; it takes no keyboard focus (a click on it is not a click on a pane) and draws no border title. **Its left side holds action buttons only; its right side holds read-only information.**
- **Left, in order** (hs-d479): the line starts with one `─`, then five buttons, `󰨝` (U+F0A1D md-view_dashboard_outline, reset layout), `󰨁` (U+F0A01 md-map_legend, legend), `󰧭` (U+F09ED md-text_box_outline, logs) and `` (U+EEC1 nf-fa-comment_dollar, costs; Context records pro-d189, pro-d195) and `` (U+F013 nf-fa-gear, settings; pro-d296, pro-d332), Material Design (hs-d235) and Font Awesome, **joined by a single `─`**; the leading `─` and the joins are **outside the click ranges** (a range also owns the cell after it, so each join is the cell the button before it owns; a space inside a button lies inside that button's own range and moves no join or other range; the click columns with the runner unset, the check that the space shifts no click, are reset 1-4 (owns 5), legend 6-9 (owns 10), logs 11-14 (owns 15), costs 16-19 (owns 20, a join), settings 21-24 (owns 25), hs-d730, pro-d296, pro-d332). Each is a **pill** (hs-d266): the left cap `` (U+E0B6), the glyph followed by one space on a white block, no other padding (the space is inside the block: the terminal draws a Nerd Font glyph full size only with an empty cell after it, hs-d730, pro-d296) (interactive, hs-d534; all five buttons share the one base colour 7, drawn bright 15 as a clickable pill, pro-d195, so the five look alike and the costs button looks the same whether costs show or not: `#[fg=colour15]#[reverse]`, `#[noreverse]#[default]`, no `reverse`), the right cap `` (U+E0B4), the caps in `fg=colour15` on the normal background (contract §6.1.1 has the exact format); a button is 4 cells wide (the two caps, the glyph and its space), the left group 25 cells (the leading `─`, five buttons of 4 cells and 4 joins). Each is its own `#[range=user|…]` (`reset`, `legend`, `logs`, `costs`, `settings`) wrapping the whole pill, caps included and a click runs `cpd tui action <range> --client <name>` (below). Tooltips are not built (the User dropped them, hs-d179). Mockup: `─󰨝 ─󰨁 ─󰧭 ─ ───…───inbox 8─workers 6·0·4/6─`.
- **Runner pill** (pro-d199), right after the settings button (the fifth, after the costs button), while the tmux server option `@cpd_runner` is set (the engine sets it from `[experimental].durable_workers`, §12; `RUNNER_OPTION` in `core/src/host/tmux.rs`): a single `━` join and then a **clickable pill with text only**, the option's value `pi` or `durable` between the caps, with no icon and no padding; it is drawn like a button (base 7 drawn 15, inverted, caps 15; contract §6.1.1). Its `#[range=user|runner]` wraps the whole pill and a click runs `cpd tui action runner --client <name>` (below). Nothing is drawn while the option is unset. The left group is then 25 cells plus `#{n:@cpd_runner}` + 3.
- **Preview marker** (hs-n264, hs-d479), right after the buttons and the runner pill: while the tmux server option `@cpd_preview` is set (`scripts/preview-tui.sh on` sets it to `<worktree basename> <short sha>`, `off` unsets it), a single `─` join and then a **non-interactive pill** (yellow, hs-d534: colour 3 inverted: text in the terminal's background colour, caps colour 3; it was grey from hs-d530 to hs-d534) with no padding: the left cap ``, `preview: <value>`, the right cap ``, so a preview never passes for the installed cpd; nothing when it is unset. The group is then `─󰨝 ─󰨁 ─󰧭 ─preview: <value>───…` and the fill is shorter by the pill's width (`#{n:@cpd_preview}` + 12).
- **The fill** (User, hs-d479): a `─` (U+2500) in **dark grey, colour 8** (no `reverse`) fills the **free width** between the left group and the right group, across the whole row, so the row has no blank gap; the line ends with one closing `─`. Its width is `#{client_width}` minus the left group (25 cells, plus the preview's) minus the right group (`#{w:@cpd_workers}` or `#{w:@cpd_workers_short}`, the form drawn, plus 1 for the closing `─`).
- **Right**, in order: the workers pill, a single `─` join, the version pill, then the closing `─`, **each item its own pill** with no padding (hs-d479; the joins and the closing `─` are outside the click ranges). There is no Inbox pill (hs-d541, the User's decision: the Inbox is the tree's section only). The workers and version pills use the tmux `pill!` shape: `#[fg=colour8]U+E0B6#[reverse]<text>#[noreverse]U+E0B4#[default]`, where the text is inverted (text in the terminal's background colour) and the caps are colour 8 (non-interactive; hs-d561 supersedes hs-d534's 7 for the workers and version pills, contract §6.1.1); the pill has one text colour: the text carries none. The workers text (User, hs-d198, hs-d749) is `workers Q󰞘W󰞘N/M`, where `Q` is the number of `queued` Jobs, `W` is the number of Ready Jobs (a `queued` Job whose Dependencies are all `merged` and whose Workflow has started, §3.2), `N` is the number of Attempts not `ended`, and `M` is config `concurrency`. The text is plain with no colours. **The form is chosen per client**: the long form when the fill would still be at least 1 cell with it (`#{client_width}` at least the left group's 25 cells (plus the preview's) + `#{w:@cpd_workers}` + 1 for the closing `─` + 1 for the fill; the constant without the text is 25 + 1 + 1 = 27, so 44 columns with the example's 17-cell text and 89 with the 33-cell preview), else the short form `Q󰞘W󰞘N/M`, same plain text; the status line draws the pill of the form it chooses per client with `#{?#{e|>=:#{client_width},<20 + preview + #{w:@cpd_workers} + 2>},#{@cpd_workers},#{@cpd_workers_short}}`; the fill's width uses `#{w:@cpd_workers}` or `#{w:@cpd_workers_short}` the same way. Both texts are fed by the engine (§12), not computed by the status line: up to one tick late and stale while the engine is stopped (the deviation in §17). The old failure note is gone: a failed click reports with `display-message -c <client>` (below).

**`cpd tui action merge <owner>/<repo>#<n> --client <name>`** (internal; hs-d473, hs-d495): what the `merge` popup's confirm starts, with `run-shell -b`, after the popup has closed. It runs `cpd pr merge <owner>/<repo>#<n>` (§9.10), then `cpd pr poll`, in the background. The merge marker (Lead's design, User may correct it; contract §1.4):
- **File:** `$CPD_HOME/run/tui/merging/<owner>__<repo>__<n>.json`, `{"pid": <the action's pid>, "at": <RFC 3339 time>, "merged": <true when the merge succeeded, absent otherwise>}`, written atomically (temporary file, then rename).
- **Writer and remover:** only this action (**B4**). It writes the marker first (the initial `{"pid", "at"}`), before `cpd pr merge`; on success rewrites it atomically with `"merged": true` after the merge and then runs `cpd pr poll`; then removes it when the pull request's `pull_requests` row is not `open` (merged, closed, or no row); removes it before opening the failure dialog on failure; and removes it on any error path, so no exit leaves it behind. **B5**: a marker with `merged: true` whose pull request's row is not open and a marker without it whose pid is not alive, are ignored; a second `cpd tui action merge` for a pull request that is merging (`merged` field true or pid alive) does nothing and logs `merge already running`.
- **Readers:** the views, on each snapshot (above); a marker whose pid is not alive is stale and ignored.

**`cpd tui action <reset|legend|logs|costs|settings|runner|host|incident> --client <name>`** (internal) is what a click on a StatusBar button runs (the `MouseDown1Status` binding, contract §6.1); **`cpd tui action merge <owner>/<repo>#<n> --client <name>`** is what the `merge` popup's confirm starts (hs-d473, below). Not a view, it owns no terminal; it runs the action **on the client named** (`#{client_name}` of the clicking client), so a popup opens on that client only, whatever other clients are attached.
- `reset` runs reset-layout (below); `legend` opens the legend popup, `logs` the logs popup, `settings` the settings popup (the settings menu, below), each `display-popup -c <name> …` sized to that client, `host` opens the host Manager (as the host action, §9.12, the same park/swap as the incident action below) and `incident` opens the incident's Lead (the same park/swap as the host action, no message sent; a failure is reported on the client).
- `costs` sends the literal key `$` to the tree pane, the pane of `cpd:main` whose `@cpd_view` is `tree` (`send-keys -t <pane> -l $`): **`cpd tui action costs --client <name>`** prints nothing and exits 0; with no live tree pane it fails like every other action (the error is shown on the client with `display-message -c`).
- `runner` flips the Worker runner (contract §6.1 "The runner pill", §8.1, §8.2): **`cpd tui action runner --client <name>`** reads `$CPD_HOME/config.toml` and calls `cpd_core::config::toggle`, which takes the effective Worker runner (`Config::worker_runner()` of `[experimental].durable_workers`, `pi` when the key is absent), flips it (`pi` ↔ `durable`), rewrites ONLY the `durable_workers` key of `[experimental]` atomically (the setter of `cpd config experimental`, §14.2b: a temporary file in the same directory, then a rename) and returns the new value. The action then runs `set -g @cpd_runner` to that value and `refresh-client -S -c <name>`. It prints nothing and exits 0. It opens no store, touches no Attempt and sends no signal: a started Attempt keeps its runner and only Attempts created after the click follow it (contract §3.4). A config that does not parse is refused by `toggle` (`config_invalid`); the file is left untouched and the failure is shown on the client with `display-message -l -c <name>`.
- **It prints nothing, on stdout or stderr**: tmux's `run-shell -b` puts the active pane into view mode when its command fails (research `statusbar-no-row.md` 2c) and shows any output of it in view mode (tmux(1), `run-shell`). On a failure (an unknown action, whose message lists `costs` among the actions, a client that has gone, a tmux error) it shows the message with `display-message -c <name> '<message>'` and exits 0; the binding also appends `2>/dev/null`.

**`legend`** is what every colour and icon of the cockpit means, from the palette (contract §6.1.1, hs-d534: each swatch and sample is drawn by the same palette call as the element it shows, so the legend shows the colours the views show; its title is a read-only title pill, its section titles and words colour 7, its column header and scroll position colour 8). It opens in a tmux popup (`display-popup -E -T ' legend ' -w <w> -h <h>`, sized to the legend and at most the client's size) from the tree's `?` key or the StatusBar's legend button (`cpd tui action legend`), because the columns are narrower than the legend; its title is drawn in the pill section-title style, the plain form (§17, the dialog kit's, hs-d297, hs-d475, hs-d478): ` ──Legend: …───`; when it is taller than its popup, ↑↓, j/k, PgUp/PgDn and the **mouse wheel** scroll it (mouse capture on; the kit's scrolling); any other key closes it. It has no `@cpd_view` pane of its own. The Job states it lists include **landing** (the sample is the Job pill's, the base yellow 3, drawn by the same palette call; the counter beside it is the bright 11; a Job is landing from its first check to the end of its merge, contract §6.1.1). Its section titles are `Jobs: Plan Pills And Context Counters`, `Session Dots`, `Inbox` and `Pulse` (Title Case, hs-d475; the popup's own tmux title ` legend ` is tmux's and unchanged); the Job statuses it lists are those the chart draws, so `cancelled` is not among them, The Job statuses it lists are those the chart draws, so `cancelled` is not among them and `running` is listed with the spinner frames `` (the 28 frames of §17 section 17). `Session Dots` lists each glyph (`` U+E3E3, `` U+E3E3, U+E3C8..U+E3E2 in each of the four Work colours of pro-d200 (magenta 13, cyan 14, yellow 11, white 15; the phase colours of hs-d622 and hs-d624 are superseded), then `` U+E3E3, U+E3C8..U+E3E2 in red 9 (a Plan's failed Job is being worked on or a Worker Escalation is open, one frame every 50 ms, hs-d581, pro-d200), `󱡓` U+F1853, `` U+E3D5, `` U+E3D5) and each `` colour (red, yellow, magenta, cyan, white) with its meaning: red 9 `the Lead is fixing a failed Job or answering a Worker's question`, yellow 11 `the Lead is working on a pull request (open, conflict, deploy, landing)`, magenta 13 `the Lead is planning (grounding, drafts, a follow-up)`, cyan 14 `the Lead is working alongside running Jobs`, white 15 `a working Session with no Plan`, as §17's dot rule gives them (the same colours mark the Inbox's items; the Inbox's items draw their own tier glyphs and three kinds their own glyphs, below; the legend says so in one line), then the precedence line `red > yellow > magenta > cyan > white >  > 󱡓 >  > `, drawn with the real glyphs and colours. `Inbox` (hs-d483; between `Session Dots` and `Pulse`) lists the six tiers, one line each, in the order red, yellow, magenta, blue, cyan, white and the three kind lines below them: the tier's glyph in its colour, then its meaning: `\u{F0362}` (U+F0362, red) `a blocker only you can clear`, `\u{F069A}` (U+F069A, yellow) `pull-request work`, `\u{F173A}` (U+F173A, magenta) `a decision before the work runs` (hs-d546, hs-d547), `\u{F0368}` (U+F0368, blue, pro-d58) `external support: a review asked of you`, `\u{F06F1}` (U+F06F1, cyan) `an unread reply` (pro-d401), `\u{F0366}` (U+F0366, white) `a cpd notice: curation, models changed; nothing blocks` (pro-d401); then **three more lines, one per exception kind** (pro-d98, pro-d100), each with the kind's glyph in its tier colour and its meaning: `\u{F15A9}` (U+F15A9, yellow, `deploy`) `a deploy waits for your approval`, `\u{F12F4}` (U+F12F4, yellow, `pr-ready`) `a pull request of yours, coloured by its state`, `\u{F12F2}` (U+F12F2, blue, `review-requested`) `a review asked of you`; the Inbox rows draw no state dot. Its lines say what needs the User and what only waits for an agent (hs-d303): `red: a dialog in dispatch or deploy, a stuck Job, an engine error, your own broken pull request that nobody is fixing` (an Escalation is no Inbox item, so it is never red; a pull request a cpd Plan owns is not red, hs-d302); `yellow: ready to post, ready to merge, review requested`; `magenta: a Plan review decision, a dialog question while planning` (hs-d570 changed meaning); `blue: review requested` (pro-d58); `cyan: an unread reply (pro-d401)`; `waiting: an agent waits for another agent (a Worker for its Lead), not for you` (the `waiting` dot, between `working` and `idle`). The `Meanings → colour` table lists `waiting on an agent` in `Meaning::Waiting`'s colour, cyan (`Color::Cyan`: not blue, which means focus only, §17 "Blue"; neither the red of a failure nor the yellow of attention; the User's decision of 2026-10-20, which resolves hs-d303 against hs-d352 and cyan is agent activity in hs-d534). Its Jobs list shows one failed pill row: red loader: a failed Job being worked on (the same pill with the moon frames, one frame every 50 ms, hs-d586); no stuck row, as E8 opens no `job-stuck` item (hs-d318). Its counters row lists the four roles in the tree's order `planned⋅active⋅failed⋅done`, with a sample of one of each (planned 1 magenta 13, active 1 cyan 14, failed 1 red 9, done 1 green 10); the tree draws only nonzero roles and a failed counter is always red (hs-d580, hs-d636). Its cost row lists the cost counters of the Context and Plan rows (decision pro-d179): the plain text `cost`, the sample `format_cost(0.12)` (`$0.120`) in colour 8 (`palette::muted_text()`) and in colour 8 the words `$0.004 ⋅ $1.23k ⋅ omitted when unknown`. Its pull request states list is `open`, `merged`, `closed` (waiting: `its Lead handles it`), `closed` (red: `its Lead asks you`) `updating` (cyan, both: `its update Job is fixing the conflict`, `its update Job is queued`; the rule of §17 Workflow boxes, hs-d532) and `conflict` (red: the one of a pull request no Plan owns; an owned one with no update Job is drawn cyan, as the plan view's box titles do). Its sample pill has the same form, `` + `<icon> key│S1` + ``, drawn as the Job pill is (hs-d534, pro-d63: the status colour's base colour, text in the terminal's background colour (inverted), caps the same; one sample per status); the legend's titles are read-only title pills (colour 7 inverted: text in the terminal's background colour). Pulse section (hs-d327): `▂▄▆` = `activity per 5 min, first colour wins` (a slot takes the first colour below); then one `▄` per kind in the precedence, red `an error, or a Job failed`, magenta `a Plan or ask Event`, cyan `a PR opened`, cyan `an escalation`, green `a Job or a PR merged`, cyan `any other activity` (the colours are the bars', §13.2 Pulse); a `▁` in colour 8 = `no activity`; `quiet 41m` (colour 8) = queued or running work with no activity for 30 min. Three entries a row (the popup is at most 80 % of the client tall).

**`merge`**: there is no confirm popup and no merge icon (pro-d111, pro-d130); the action is started from the Inbox's `pr-ready` menu (**Merge**) only, with tmux `run-shell -b`. **The `merge` action** (hs-d473, hs-d312) is the background run, in its own process, owned by the tmux server, with none of the popup's. It prints nothing, on stdout or stderr and exits 0 whatever happens, as every `cpd tui action` does (`run-shell -b` puts the active pane into view mode on a failure or any output, above):
- It runs `cpd pr merge <owner>/<repo>#<n>` (§9.10), which records the merge in the store immediately (hs-d526), then `cpd pr poll` (§9.2) to refresh (the poll's result window is unchanged: no second merge by the poll itself, just refresh of the stored merge). A failed merge runs no poll. **Nothing shows on success**: the Inbox shows the merge after the poll, which is already stored.
- **A failed merge** is the cockpit's one failure rule (§17 "No notes (a)"): a `text` dialog of the dialog kit (§13.2), the same one every failure opens, never a second dialog, opens on that client (`<name>`) with `merge <owner>/<repo>#<n>: <code>: <message>`, the `<code>` and `<message>` those of the failed command's error (for example `merge_not_clean`) and a line with the same text goes to the merge's log, `$CPD_HOME/run/tui/merge.log` (hs-d364: the log of the `merge` view that started the action).
- **A poll that fails after a merge** is **a log line only**, in the same file, `pr poll after merge <owner>/<repo>#<n>: <code>: <message>` and no dialog: the pull request did merge and the next periodic poll refreshes the column (hs-d473's first reading, a dialog for it, is replaced by §17 "No notes").
- **When the dialog cannot open** (the client has gone, tmux fails), the error does not vanish: the log line is written **first**, before the dialog is tried, so it is always there; then the dialog is tried; if that fails, the action shows the message with `display-message -c <name> '<message>'`, as every `tui action` does for its own failures and if that fails too the log line is what is left. Why the log first: it needs no client and no tmux, so it is the one place that cannot fail for the reasons the other two can.
- **A second confirm while a merge runs** (the icon shows while the stored `merge_state` is still `'clean'`, until the poll after the merge): the second action runs `cpd pr merge`, which reads GitHub fresh (§9.10 step 1). Either the first merge is done and it is refused `merge_not_clean` (`details.state` `MERGED`), or `gh` is still merging and GitHub accepts one of the two and refuses the other. One pull request is merged once; the refused run's error opens the failure dialog. Acceptable, not harmful: the User asked twice and the dialog says why the second did nothing.

**`logs`** (R36) is the **Event log**: every Event (§5), one line each: its local time of day (`HH:MM:SS`, colour 8, bare with no zone per §1.3 pro-d42), then its `text`, or its kind when the `text` is empty, an `error` Event in the failed colour (red 1; the dialog is read-only), except one **addressed to a Lead**, in `Meaning::Waiting`'s colour (cyan 6): the Lead handles it (audit Q5, hs-d303). An `error` is addressed to a Lead when it names a Plan (`plan` set) and its `data.source` is not the engine's own `watch`, or its `data.code` is `workflow_start_failed` or `push_failed` (the engine reports those for a Lead, with source `watch`); the engine's own step errors (`source` `watch`, contract §5.2) and any `error` that names no Plan stay red. It opens in a tmux popup (`display-popup -E -T ' logs '`, at most 80 % of the client's width and height) from the StatusBar's `󰧭` button (`cpd tui action logs`, on the clicking client; no Inbox click opens it: `engine-down` starts the engine and the engine's errors go to the Manager, hs-d314) and has no `@cpd_view` pane of its own. With `--event <id>` (an Event id of §5) the view opens **at that Event**: its line is selected (the blue block, colour 4 inverted: text in the terminal's background colour, contract §6.1.1) and scrolled into view and it does not follow until the User scrolls to the bottom; an id outside the latest 500 Events is read on its own too. Without it, it opens at the bottom. The newest Event is last; the view follows live while it shows the bottom and stops following when the User scrolls up (it follows again at the bottom). Its title is drawn in the section-title style, the plain form (§17; hs-d297, hs-d475, hs-d478): ` ──Logs───…`. ↑↓, j/k, PgUp/PgDn and the **mouse wheel** scroll and End or `G` goes to the bottom, where it follows again (mouse capture on; the kit's scrolling, hs-d297), with the live follow and `--event` behaviour above unchanged; `q` or Esc closes it. **Margin** (the Box rule, contract §6.1.1 "Boxes"; the popup's contents are a widget in the space inside tmux's border): every row has 1 blank column on each side, so the text starts at column 1 of the popup's inside and ends at column `W - 2`.

**`settings`** is the **settings** popup (User decisions pro-d296, pro-d332, pro-d333; the two-entry menu User decision D3, assumption A4 of Plan `settings-workers`; contract §6.1): the settings view, `cpd tui view settings`, opened by the StatusBar's gear button (U+F013) through `cpd tui action settings` in a tmux popup on the clicking client (`display-popup -E -w 66 -h 26`, capped at 90 % of the client; the inside is 64 × 24 inside tmux's border). The popup is **two-level**: it opens on a **menu** of two entries, `Agent Tiers` and `Workers`, and picking an entry opens that screen in the popup's place. **Agent Tiers** is today's view, unchanged: a scrolling body of sections, **Agent Tiers**, then **Experimental**; other settings and per-Context settings are not in it. **Workers** is the screen below. The popup is left by Esc or `q` from the menu or from either screen, without writing, as by `[ Cancel ]` on a screen; the menu is shown again only the next time the popup opens. It owns its terminal (§1.2), has no `@cpd_view` pane and writes no file of its own: it reads and writes only through `cpd` commands, run on the `RunCommand` the view is given (the views change state only through commands, §13.2 above).

- **Reads.** At the start, and again after a model pick (below):
  - `cpd config`: the four Tier keys (`context_distill_tier`, `worker_tier`, `lead_tier`, `manager_tier`), `presets`, each name's four refs `O`, `S`, `H` and `G`, the four switches of `[experimental]` (`durable_workers`, `write_curation`, `failure_triage`, `turn_question_guard`), and `concurrency`, the machine's concurrent Worker count (the command's JSON already carries the key, §14.2; the Workers screen reads it from this same read, no second command);
  - `cpd tiers --model O=<ref> --model S=<ref> --model H=<ref> --model G=<ref>` with the four refs of the rows (at the start, the configured ones): each letter's `model` and `efforts`, and `pi_version`. The view builds a `cpd_core::config::Catalog` from that JSON and takes its rungs from `Catalog::ladder` and each role's range from `Catalog::range` (with `RoleTiers` and `Role`); the rungs' order is `Tier`'s `Ord`. Nothing re-implements either;
  - `cpd models show`: `providers[].provider` is the Provider list and `providers[].ids` the models of each provider. Built-in providers are not cached, so they are not offered.
- **Writes**, in this order, only the steps that have something to write:
  1. `cpd preset set --O <ref> --S <ref> --H <ref> --G <ref>` when a model changed (each ref `<provider>/<model-id>`);
  2. `cpd config tiers set --auxiliar <T> --worker <T> --lead <T> --manager <T>` when a tier changed (all four flags);
  3. `cpd config concurrency set <n>` when the Workers count changed, `<n>` the committed count (§14.2c);
  4. `cpd config experimental <feature> <on|off>`, once for each Experimental row whose value changed, in the order of the rows (§14.2b);
  5. `cpd session retier --all` once the writes have succeeded and a model or Tier write changed something (an Experimental switch and the Workers count change no Tier, so neither runs a `retier`).

  A successful step becomes the baseline. Save stops at the first refusal: the footer shows its error code and message in red, the view stays open, and a retry runs only the steps that have not succeeded yet. A refused `retier` leaves the files written, and the footer says so. When every step has succeeded the view closes. Nothing changed: Save just closes. The menu's two screens share the one model and the one baseline: a Save on either screen runs every changed step in the order above, whichever screen the change was made on.
- **Keys.** On the menu: ↑ and ↓ move the focus between the two entries, Enter opens the focused one. On a screen: ↑ and ↓ move the focus between rows; Enter opens the focused value's list, opens the Workers count's editor, flips the focused Experimental row or presses the focused button. Esc or `q` closes the popup without writing when no list or editor is open, as does `[ Cancel ]` — from the menu, from the Agent Tiers screen and from the Workers screen alike. With a list open: ↑ and ↓ move its cursor, Enter picks, Esc closes the list only, and typing narrows its entries by substring (its first row is `filter: <text>`); Backspace deletes one character of the filter. With the Workers count's editor open: a digit appends at the end, Backspace deletes the last digit, Enter commits the digits as the new value (an empty editor commits nothing: the editor closes and the value is unchanged), Esc discards the edit and closes the editor.
- **Mouse.** On the menu, a click on an entry opens it. On a screen, a click on a value opens its list, on the Workers count's value opens its editor (the digits, Backspace, Enter and Esc then edit it as the keys above say), on an entry picks it, on an Experimental row flips it, on `[ Load ]`, `[ Save ]` or `[ Cancel ]` presses it; the wheel scrolls the body (the dialog kit's `Scroll`, `tui/src/dialog/scroll.rs`). Mouse capture is on.
- **Layout.** Every level's title is a section header (`SectionTitle`: a blank row, the title row, a blank row), drawn as the legend's section titles are: the menu's ` ──Settings`, the Agent Tiers screen's ` ──Agent Tiers`, the Workers screen's ` ──Workers`, each fill a `─` to the right edge. The body has a left margin of 1. The focused row has `▸` in column 3. A value with a list shows `▾`, and `▴` while its list is open; the Workers count's row offers no list, so its value has neither. The Workers count's value ends with the block cursor `▌` (U+258C) while its editor is open. A value changed since the baseline ends with `*`. An invalid value (a default that is no longer a rung of its model, or an unset model) is drawn red and ends with `!`; it blocks Save, and the footer names the row and why; the Workers count has no invalid state of its own (its range is the command's, under **Workers** below). The footer row, below the buttons, shows the last refusal in red, or nothing. A model row shows the model id as its provider lists it; the Provider row names the provider. The screens below are the machine of the example: models `bifrost`, GX H3 S4 O3, the ladder of `cpd tiers` (H efforts 0-4, S 0-4, O 0 2 3 4, G none) and `concurrency` 3.
- **Models.** One provider per machine: the four refs must share one provider. `[ Load ]` fills the Provider and the four model rows from the preset selected in the Preset row; it writes nothing, and it re-reads the rungs as a pick does. Changing the Provider keeps a letter's model only when the new provider's `ids` offers that id; otherwise the letter is unset (invalid, blocks Save). After a model is picked the view runs `cpd tiers --model …` with the four candidates to re-read the rungs. A failure shows its reason in the footer and blocks the Tiers section: its rows offer no list, and Save is refused until a later read succeeds.
- **Tiers.** The default of each role; the range column shows its range under the current defaults: `default only` for the auxiliar, `<floor>..<ceiling>` (`Catalog::range`) for the others. A role with no range is invalid. A Tier row offers only the rungs strictly above the next-lower role's current default and strictly below the next-higher role's: the worker's rungs lie between the auxiliar's and the lead's defaults, the lead's between the worker's and the manager's, the manager's are everything above the lead's, and the auxiliar's everything below the worker's (`GX` only). So an invalid order cannot be picked.
- **Experimental.** A section below the Tier rows and above the buttons, after a blank line: the header `Experimental` (no subtitle), then one row per Experimental Feature, in the order of §14.2b. The label is the feature's key and the value is `on` or `off`; the labels are padded to the longest key, so the values line up two spaces after it. A boolean row offers no list, so it has no `▾` or `▴`. A click on the row, or Enter on it, flips the value, and a value changed since the baseline ends with `*` as a Tier value does. Save runs `cpd config experimental` for each changed row, and Cancel discards the flips. The section adds six lines to the Tier body (the blank line, the header, four rows): the body is then 21 lines against the 20 rows of the 64 × 24 popup (by count, not run), so the buttons scroll and the focus brings the section into view. The rows as drawn, with the focus on `write_curation`, which a click has turned off:

```
 Experimental
     durable_workers      off
   ▸ write_curation       off*
     failure_triage       on
     turn_question_guard  on
```

- **Workers.** A screen of the menu, not a section of the Agent Tiers body. It holds the machine's concurrent Worker count, config `concurrency` (§14.2, §14.2c): the count of Attempts not ended the machine runs at once (contract §3.4 "The built-in resource `workers`"). The screen has the Agent Tiers view's chrome with one section: the header `Workers  the Attempts the machine runs at once`, then the row `concurrency`, its value the count as `cpd config` carried it at the start, then the `[ Save ]` and `[ Cancel ]` buttons and the footer, laid out as the Agent Tiers body is (the labels are padded so the values line up two spaces after the section's longest label; the section's only row is `concurrency`, so its value starts two spaces after it). Enter on the focused row, or a click on its value, opens the value's editor as **Keys** and **Mouse** above say; the row shows the digits typed so far and ends with the cursor `▌` while the editor is open. A committed value changed since the baseline ends with `*`, as every value. The accepted range is 1 to 16 inclusive, and it is the command's, not the view's: the view adds no range check, no red and no `!` of its own — Save runs `cpd config concurrency set <n>` in process, like every write of this popup (§14.2c), and a value outside the range is refused loudly there: `config_invalid: concurrency must be between 1 and 16, got <n>.` (exit 1, air-d70). The refusal shows in the footer in red, the screen stays open, and a retry runs only the writes that have not succeeded (above). Saving the count with nothing else changed runs that one command and closes the popup when it succeeds; the count equal to the current one writes nothing (`already`, §14.2c). A lowered count stops nothing — it gates new starts only, and the running tenants keep their slots to the end (air-d71, contract §3.7 E3). The screens below show it with the count 3.

**Refusals.** The view runs these commands and shows their refusal in the footer (the code and the message, in red); none of them is retried by the view.

| Command | Refusals (code, exit) |
|---|---|
| `cpd config` (read) | `config_missing` (1), `config_invalid` (1) |
| `cpd tiers --model …` (read, and after a pick) | `pi_not_found` (1), `catalog_failed` (1), `tier_model_unknown` (1), `lock_timeout` (5) |
| `cpd models show` (read) | none: a row it cannot parse is `store_failed` (§14.5); `warnings` stays `[]` |
| `cpd preset set --O … --S … --H … --G …` | `usage` (2), `policy_invalid` (1), `pi_not_found` (1), `spawn_failed` (1), `tool_timeout` (5), `models_helper_failed` (1), `preset_provider_unconfigured` (3), `preset_model_unoffered` (3) (§14.6a) |
| `cpd config tiers set --auxiliar … --worker … --lead … --manager …` | `config_missing` (1), `tier_invalid` (2), `config_invalid` (1), `policy_invalid` (1), `lock_timeout` (5), `pi_not_found` (1), `catalog_failed` (1), `tier_model_unknown` (1) (§14.2a) |
| `cpd config concurrency set <n>` | `usage` (2), `config_missing` (1), `config_invalid` (1; `details.key` `concurrency` when `<n>` is outside 1 to 16), `internal` (1) (§14.2c) |
| `cpd config experimental <feature> <on|off>` | `usage` (2), `config_invalid` (1), `config_missing` (1) (§14.2b) |
| `cpd session retier --all` | none for a Session it passes over (§10.16); a refusal of the command itself is shown as it is |

**The screens.** The inside of the popup at its 64 columns; the title row is drawn in its pill's text, and the footer row is the last row. Colours are not shown: the footer row is red when it holds a refusal; the cursor of an open list is not drawn; the Workers count's editor cursor `▌` is drawn.

**Reset-layout** is not a CLI command. `cpd tui action reset` and `cpd tui` run it. It runs `resize-pane` on the panes of `<cockpit>:main` found by `@cpd_view`, in this order:

| # | `@cpd_view` | Size |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tree` | `-x 20%` |
| 2 | `widgets` | `-x 30%` |
| 3 | `plan` | `-y 30%` |

The chat slot is never resized; it takes what is left. **The chat slot's last row (hs-d567; contract §6.1 "The blank row", Q1-Q4):** the status line is one row (`status on`), so the window is as tall as before hs-d561. The layout divides the window into columns: tree 20%, middle 50%, widgets 30%. The middle column's rows divide as: Plan view 30%, chat slot 70%. The `resize-pane` calls and these sizes are fractions of the window. The last row of the chat slot's pane is empty **by its occupant**, not by tmux: a Lead's or Manager's pi (the adapter, §15.1), the history view (§13.2); the placeholder draws one line at the top and needs nothing. In a 20-row client: row 1 the pane borders, rows 2-19 the panes (row 19, the chat slot's last row, empty), row 20 the `─` line; the tree, the Plan view and the widgets reach row 19. Code and tests: `core/src/host/tmux.rs` and `tui/src/cockpit.rs`, with the tests that pin the status options or a pane's height. The StatusBar's 󰨝 click runs it through `cpd tui action reset`; `cpd tui` runs it once, right after building a new `main` and after killing a leftover `statusbar` pane of an existing one (§13.1).

Refusal before drawing: an unknown view or Attempt is `usage` or `attempt_not_found`. Idempotent: they only read.

### 13.3 `cpd` with no arguments

```
cpd
```

User decision hs-d259 (2026-10-19), Plan pi-pin, PR `bare`. **Bare `cpd` opens the cockpit.** In a terminal it attaches that terminal to the cockpit (`tmux -L <socket> attach -t <cockpit_session>`, the `attach` of §13.1) after doing every follow-up an update needs, so the User needs no other command after an install. It owns its terminal (§1.2): nothing on success.

**Follow-ups**, in this order:

1. **Engine:** `cpd watch --ensure` (§12).
2. **Cockpit:** what `cpd tui` does (§13.1): build it when missing, respawn a dead pane of its layout, remove an older cpd's StatusBar pane or `worker` pane (pro-d63) and set the server options and the status line. One implementation, shared with `cpd tui`: bare `cpd` calls it, never a copy.
3. **Views on an old binary:** when the panes of the views run an older cpd than the installed one, `cpd tui --respawn` (§13.1).
4. **tmux version:** when the cockpit's tmux server runs an older tmux than the installed client (`tmux -L <socket> display -p '#{version}'` against `tmux -V`; hs-d166), restart the server onto the installed tmux **when it is safe**, reopen every Lead and Manager Session that had a pane (same pi session file, same place: the chat slot, its parked window, a Context's window), then attach. When it is not safe, **hold, drain, restart** (User, hs-d294):
   - **Safe** means: no Attempt `starting`, `running` or `merging` and no Lead or Manager Session mid-turn (state `working`; a `blocked` Session has a dialog open, so it is also not safe). Restarting stops every pi in the server; Leads and Managers resume from their session files.
   - **Safe now:** bare `cpd` restarts the server itself, in its own process (it runs in a terminal outside the server): it records every Lead and Manager Session with a live pane and its place (`chat`, or parked: its `park-<label>` window, or a Manager's `ctx-<context>` window); `kill-server`; `cpd tui` (the cockpit on the installed tmux, which also runs `watch --ensure`; the last chat Lead is back in the chat slot); then each Session in the same place: the one of the chat slot as `session open` does, the others in a new window running `cpd session run <id>`, which resumes the Session's pi file, each with `session-moved`. It then attaches with the installed tmux and says in one line how many Sessions it reopened.
   - **Not safe:** it **marks a restart pending** (the file `$CPD_HOME/run/tmux-restart.pending`, JSON `{"at", "server", "installed", "failed"}`; no store change), attaches at once with the **server's own tmux binary** (its path from the server pid: on Linux `/proc/<pid>/exe`, on macOS read with `libproc`), because a newer client cannot attach to an older server (`open terminal failed: not a terminal`, hs-n224) and prints one line saying so and that the restart happens once nothing is in the way. `cpd tui` does the same marking when it finds the server older (it never restarts the server itself, since it may run inside it) and `tui --attach` attaches with the server's own binary then as well.
   - **While a restart is pending, the engine starts no new Attempt** (E3's hold, contract §3.7); running Attempts finish normally. It is a planned hold, not an error: `cpd doctor` shows it as the `tmux_restart` check ("tmux restart pending", §14.1). Once none runs (no Attempt `starting`, `running` or `merging`) and no Lead or Manager Session is `working` or `blocked`, the engine starts the restart **detached** (`cpd watch --restart-tmux`, internal; `setsid`, its log `run/tmux-restart.log`), because the restart kills the server the engine itself runs in. The detached process takes `locks/tmux-restart.lock`, checks again that it is safe, does what "safe now" does, clears the pending file and logs the result. Then the engine, started again by `cpd tui`, schedules as usual. The User reconnects with bare `cpd`.
   - **A failed restart** keeps the pending file with `failed` (`at`, `code`, `reason`) and the engine that runs again appends one `error` Event (`source: "watch"`, `code` of the failure, `details: {at, server, installed, log}`); a failed restart holds nothing. The next bare `cpd` finding the server still older tries again (a failed file is marked afresh); finding it as new as the installed tmux, it says the failure in one line and removes the file. Never from inside the cockpit's own server.

Rerunning is safe: a restart already pending keeps its time and a server that is not older is left alone. Internal command: `cpd watch --restart-tmux` (not an interface of the User or an agent; it conflicts with `--ensure`).

`scripts/restart-tmux.sh` (PR `tmux`) is gone: its checks (the refusal while an Attempt runs, the attach hint with the server's binary) are the binary's own.

**Assumptions, confirmed by the User in the Plan review:**

- **A1** Without a terminal on stdin and stdout, bare `cpd` keeps today's behaviour: the JSON usage error `usage`, exit 2. It does no follow-up.
- **A2** Inside the cockpit's own server (`$TMUX` names its socket), bare `cpd` does not nest an attach: it does the follow-ups that are safe from inside, never the tmux restart nor the marking of one (it would kill the pane it runs in) and prints one line saying how to reach the cockpit.
- **A3** Each follow-up's failure is printed in one line on stderr and the attach still happens when the cockpit exists. When the cockpit does not exist and could not be built, bare `cpd` prints the failure value and exits with its code.
- **A4** Nothing new in the store: no table, column or Event kind.

## 14. `doctor`, `config`, `tiers`, `models`, `preset`, `metrics`

### 14.1 `doctor`

```
cpd doctor
```

Checks the machine (cpd 1 §11 `doctor`, kept in shape). Each check has `name`, `ok`, `severity` (`error` or `warn`) and when relevant `found`, `expected` and `message`. Any failing `error` check makes the result `doctor_failed` (exit 1) with every check in `details.checks`; `warn` checks never fail it.

**Minimum versions.** Each minimum is the version verified on this machine (the homeserver, 2026-10-14), because the contract's tmux, git, gh and pi behaviour was verified on exactly these (contract.md, evidence labels). Older versions may work; that is unverified, so doctor refuses them.

| Tool | Command run | Output found on 2026-10-14 | Minimum | Parsed as | What cpd needs from it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
