| git | `git --version` | `git version 2.43.0` | `2.43.0` | the first `x.y.z` | `worktree add`, `update-ref` with an old value, `merge-base --is-ancestor`, `merge-tree --write-tree --name-only` (git 2.38 or later, docs), `read-tree -m -u` (§7) |
| tmux | `tmux -V` | `tmux 3.4` | `3.6` | `x.y`, ignoring a letter suffix (`3.4a`); `next-…` builds pass | `new-window`/`split-window -e`, argv commands after `--`, `swap-pane`, `pane-border-lines`, `extended-keys`, `#{pane_dead_status}` (§6); **3.6 because** older tmux can lose a pane's `SIGCHLD`, so `pane-died` never respawns a cockpit view (contract §6.1; fixed in tmux 3.6, tmux/tmux#4559) |
| pi | `pi --version` | `1.2.0` | `>= 1.2.0 < 2.0.0` | `x.y.z` | `--fork`, `--session-id`, `-n`, `--exclude-tools`, `--no-skills`, `--approve`, `--no-mcp`, `--tools +name`; the catalog of §9 (cpd 1 §11: pi updates itself, so a range) |
| gh | `gh --version` | `gh version 2.45.0 (2025-07-18 Ubuntu 2.45.0-1ubuntu0.3)` | `2.45.0` | the first `x.y.z` | `pr create`, `pr list --json`, `pr view --json …statusCheckRollup…`, `api` (§7.6) |
| pi's Node | `<pi node> --version`, the binary §9 chooses | `v22.23.2` (`/usr/local/bin/node`; this machine has no `pi-node` directory) | none: it must run | | runs the catalog module of §9 |

**Deadline.** Each probe `doctor` runs (the five commands of the table, `<pi node> --version`, the catalog module of §9 and `gh auth status`) has a deadline of 10 s. A probe that runs past it is a failed check whose `message` names the tool, its argv and the deadline (contract §1.2 `tool_timeout`); `doctor` goes on with the next check and still reports every check.

Checks, in order:

| Name | Severity | Passes when |
|---|---|---|
| `config` | error | `config.toml` exists and is valid (§8) |
| `store` | error | the store verdict (§1.2 `--version`, contract §4.5) says the database opens and it migrates and passes the schema check (§4.3); otherwise `found` is the verdict's refusal (`code`, `message`). Unknown additive migrations (`store.unknown`) are not a failure and have no check of their own: `--version` reports them (hs-d178 D1) |
| `tamper` | error | the tamper report (§4.3) is empty; `found` lists it |
| `git`, `tmux`, `pi`, `gh` | error | found on `PATH` at or above the minimum above |
| `gh_auth` | warn | `gh auth status` exits 0 (needed only by `pr` commands; verified on 2026-10-14: logged in through `GH_TOKEN`) |
| `pi_node` | error | pi's Node runs |
| `tiers` | error | each model in the policy's `[model]` table is in pi's catalog (contract §8.3, §9); `lead_tier`, `manager_tier`, `context_distill_tier` and `worker_tier` are Tiers in the syntax of §5, each a valid rung of its model (contract §9 "Roles and ranges"), and they strictly ascend (`context_distill_tier` < `worker_tier` < `lead_tier` < `manager_tier`). It also fails when a role default is not a rung of the catalog, or when a role's span (its floor to its ceiling, contract §9 "Roles and ranges") holds no valid rung; the error names the key. These replace the fixed ranges of hs-d562, pro-d82, hs-d554 and hs-d506 (pro-d328 to pro-d332). `review_lead_tier` is no longer checked: it is removed |
| `pi_adapter` | error | the `pi_adapter` directory has a `package.json` |
| `worker_runner` (the check's name) | error | while `[experimental].durable_workers` is off (`pi`), passes without looking at anything; when it is on (`durable`), passes when `<pi_adapter>/durable-worker/main.ts` exists and pi's Node is at least 22.19.0 (the `engines.node` of the runner's package, contract §6.12): `found` is the Node version, `expected` is `>= 22.19.0` (contract §3.4 "The Worker runner and its seam") |
| `host_runner` | error | when `lead_runner` and `manager_runner` are both `pi`, `experimental.durable_leads` is off and the store has no live durable Session (a `lead` or `manager` row with `runner = 'durable'` and `archived_at` null), passes without looking at anything; when either key is `durable`, `durable_leads` is on or such a live durable Session exists, passes when `<pi_adapter>/durable-host/main.ts` exists and pi's Node is at least 22.19.0 (contract §6.19): `found` is the Node version, `expected` is `>= 22.19.0` |
| `lead_packages` | warn | reports, for each `lead_pi_packages` entry and the adapter, whether a Lead gets it by `-e` or from which settings file (§6.5); warns when an entry is neither declared nor resolvable |
| `watch` | warn | the engine runs when any Plan is in `dispatch` or `deploy` |
| `tmux_restart` | warn | present only while `run/tmux-restart.pending` exists: it passes (`message` "tmux restart pending", `found` the times and versions) while the restart waits, a planned hold of E3 (contract §3.7) and not a failure; it fails, with the reason, when the restart failed (§13.3) |

```json
{"ok": true, "checks": [
  {"name": "git", "ok": true, "severity": "error", "found": "2.43.0", "expected": ">= 2.43.0"},
  {"name": "tmux", "ok": true, "severity": "error", "found": "3.4", "expected": ">= 3.4"},
  {"name": "pi", "ok": true, "severity": "error", "found": "1.2.0", "expected": ">= 1.2.0 < 2.0.0"},
  {"name": "gh", "ok": true, "severity": "error", "found": "2.45.0", "expected": ">= 2.45.0"}]}
```

Change from cpd 1: no `node`, `bd`, `wt` or `herdr` checks (§1.1); `gh` now has a minimum. Idempotent: yes; it writes nothing except a migration on first open.

### 14.2 `config`

```
cpd config [--migrate]
cpd config tiers set --auxiliar <T> --worker <T> --lead <T> --manager <T>
cpd config experimental [<feature> <on|off>]
cpd config concurrency set <n>
```

Without `--migrate`, prints the effective configuration: defaults merged with `config.toml` (§8), each value with its source. Refusals: `config_missing`, `config_invalid` (exit 1, `details.key` = the key path), among them the Tier checks of contract §8.2 and §9 (pro-d328 to pro-d332): a `lead_tier`, `manager_tier`, `context_distill_tier` or `worker_tier` outside the Tier syntax (effort 5 included), the role defaults out of ascending order, `lead_runner` or `manager_runner` other than `"pi"` or `"durable"`, and an unknown key or a non-bool value in `[experimental]` (contract §8.2: each key is validated and printed, with its source like every key; `lead_runner` and `manager_runner` default to `pi` and are independent, contract §6.19). Defaults: `context_distill_tier` `GX` (the auxiliar role's default: the Tier every distill run uses, one step only, no ladder, hs-d560), `worker_tier` `H3` (the worker role's default: the Tier of the `open` and `update` Jobs), `lead_tier` `O2`, `manager_tier` `O4` (pro-d328 to pro-d332; contract §9 "Roles and ranges"), `context_curation_min_records` `25` (hs-d592: a Context is curable when it holds at least this many records; an integer >= 1), `loop_guard_turns` `20` (hs-d552, hs-d571: an integer >= 1; the window size for the loop guard's turn counter). `timeouts.explore_minutes` `20` (Plan `explore-roles`: the active-time limit of an explore Attempt, `scout` or `research`, used instead of `timeouts.attempt_minutes`; an integer >= 1, else `config_invalid` with `details.key`). It reads only the config files and never opens the store, so it never waits on the setup lock (hs-n278; `config tiers set`, §14.2a, opens it); `cpd tiers` and every command that opens the store wait out a migration in progress (contract §4.2). No effects.

`config tiers set` (§14.2a) writes the four Tier keys; `config experimental` (§14.2b) prints and sets the Experimental Features; `config concurrency set` (§14.2c) writes the machine-wide Attempt limit (`concurrency`, contract §8.2).

With `--migrate`, reads `$CPD_HOME/config.toml`, applies the ordered, additive migrations (contract §8.1 "Config migrations", hs-d722: `distill-tier-gx`, `drop-test-concurrency`, `drop-plannotator-ports`, `open-tier-worker-tier` and `drop-review-lead-tier`, in that order, then `drop-inbox-review-context` (pro-d338: the `review_context` line of the `[inbox]` table is removed, other keys and comments survive), then `worker-runner-to-experimental` (Plan `experimental-config`: the top-level `worker_runner = "durable"` becomes `durable_workers = true` in `[experimental]`, and `worker_runner = "pi"` is only dropped)), validates the result (the same checks as plain `config` above) and writes the file only when it changed and only when the result is valid. The file is untouched on any refusal. Refusals: `config_missing` (exit 1) when the file is missing; `config_invalid` (exit 1, `details.key`) when the migrated file is still invalid after the migrations; any other code the migrations may return. It prints `{"ok":true,"path":"<path>","migrated":["<name>",...]}` with an empty array when nothing changed. Used only by `cpd install` before replacing the binary (contract §3.7 "The config migration and validation", commands.md §14.4 step 3).

```json
{"ok": true, "path": "/home/clayton/.cpd/config.toml",
 "config": {"version": 1, "machine": "hs", "concurrency": 3, "retry_cap": 2, "lead_tier": "O2", "timeouts": {"attempt_minutes": 30, "...": "..."}, "watch": {"tick_seconds": 5, "...": "..."}, "events": {"poll_ms": 200}, "tmux": {"socket": "cpd", "cockpit_session": "cpd", "work_session": "cpd-work"}, "experimental": {"durable_workers": false, "durable_leads": false, "write_curation": true, "failure_triage": true, "turn_question_guard": true}},
 "sources": {"version": "file", "machine": "file", "host": "default", "concurrency": "default"}}
```

`sources` has one entry per leaf key. Idempotent: read-only.

### 14.2a `config tiers set`

```
cpd config tiers set --auxiliar <T> --worker <T> --lead <T> --manager <T>
```

Sets the four Tier keys of `$CPD_HOME/config.toml` (contract §8.2): `--auxiliar` is `context_distill_tier`, `--worker` is `worker_tier`, `--lead` is `lead_tier` and `--manager` is `manager_tier`. All four flags are required (a missing one is `usage`, exit 2); each value is a Tier of the syntax of contract §9. Callers: none, the User at a shell (§2); cockpit: yes (§2).

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--auxiliar <T>` | the auxiliar role's default, `context_distill_tier` (§9 "Roles and ranges") |
| `--worker <T>` | the worker role's default, `worker_tier` |
| `--lead <T>` | the lead role's default, `lead_tier` |
| `--manager <T>` | the manager role's default, `manager_tier` |

**Validation.** The checks run in the order of the table below, and every one of them runs before any write. The catalog they need is read from the models of `host.toml`'s `[model]` table as they are when the command runs (the built-in default of contract §8.3 when the file has no `[model]` table, as `cpd tiers` reads them), so `config tiers set` opens the store (the catalog cache) like `cpd tiers` does (§14.3), and it is not a plain `config` read: it waits out a migration in progress (hs-n278; contract §4.2). Writing the catalog cache is not an Event.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `config.toml` exists (it is read first) | `config_missing` | 1 |
| each of the four values is a Tier of the syntax of §9, effort 5 included; `details.key` is the config key | `tier_invalid` | 2 |
| the new text parses as a Config: each key's own rules hold, and the four defaults strictly ascend, `context_distill_tier` < `worker_tier` < `lead_tier` < `manager_tier` (§9 "Roles and ranges"); `details.key` is the key that breaks the order, or the key whose value is refused | `config_invalid` | 1 |
| `host.toml` exists and parses, or is absent (the built-in default applies); a file that does not parse is `policy_invalid` (`details.file`) | `policy_invalid` | 1 |
| the store cannot be opened for the catalog, or the migration wait ends (as `cpd tiers`) | `lock_timeout` | 5 |
| pi is found as §9 says | `pi_not_found` | 1 |
| the catalog module ran and printed valid JSON | `catalog_failed` | 1 |
| each model read for the catalog (the `[model]` refs of `host.toml`) is in the catalog | `tier_model_unknown` | 1 |
| each value is a valid rung of its letter's model: a digit only for an effort the model offers, `X` for every model (§9 "Valid efforts per model", air-d16, air-d17, air-d21); `details.key` and `details.efforts` (the model's valid efforts) | `tier_invalid` | 2 |
| each role's span holds a valid rung: the floor (the lowest valid rung at or above the role's new value) is at or below its ceiling (the highest valid rung strictly below the next role's new value; the top valid rung for the manager; the value itself for the auxiliar), §9 "Roles and ranges"; `details.key` is the role's key | `config_invalid` | 1 |

**Effects.** Only a key whose effective value changes is written; an absent key has its default as its value. The rewrite keeps every other byte of the file:
- a changed key's line is replaced whole by `<key> = "<T>" # set by the Agent Tiers dialog, <YYYY-MM-DD>`, the date from cpd's ports clock;
- an absent key is inserted after the last top-level `key = value` line before the first `[table]` header, at the end when there is no table (contract §8.2);
- a key whose value is unchanged is not touched, its line and its comment stay.

The file is written atomically (a temporary file in the same directory, then a rename: contract §8.1 "Every write is atomic"). No row, no Event. **No running Session moves**: a live Lead or Manager keeps its Tier until `cpd session retier --all` (§10.16) moves it to the new `lead_tier` or `manager_tier`. A Worker's Tier is its Job's: `worker_tier` applies to the Jobs cpd adds after the write, and a started Attempt keeps its Tier (§9 "Attempt Tier").

```json
{"ok": true, "changed": ["worker_tier", "lead_tier"], "already": false,
 "config": {"version": 1, "machine": "hs", "context_distill_tier": "GX", "worker_tier": "H3", "lead_tier": "S4", "manager_tier": "O3", "...": "..."}}
```

`changed` lists the keys whose effective value changed, in the order `context_distill_tier`, `worker_tier`, `lead_tier`, `manager_tier`. When no value changes, `changed` is `[]` and `already` is `true`, and nothing is written (the file is not touched and its comment dates stay). `config` is the effective configuration after the write, as plain `cpd config` prints it (§14.2). Idempotence: yes, a rerun with the same four values writes nothing (`already`).

### 14.2b `config experimental`

```
cpd config experimental
cpd config experimental <feature> <on|off>
```

The Experimental Features (CONTEXT.md) are the five switches of the `[experimental]` table of `$CPD_HOME/config.toml` (contract §8.2): `durable_workers` (the Worker runner: `off` is `pi`, `on` is `durable`), `durable_leads` (the Lead runner: `on` makes each new Lead `durable`, `off` leaves it to `lead_runner`; contract §6.19 "The config keys"), `write_curation`, `failure_triage` and `turn_question_guard`. Each feature's config lives only in that table (contract §8.1).

`cpd config experimental` prints the five switches, read from the file as it is now (the defaults of contract §8.2 for an absent key: `durable_workers` and `durable_leads` `off`, the other three `on`). `cpd config experimental <feature> <on|off>` sets one of them: it writes the key in `[experimental]` atomically (a temporary file in the same directory, then a rename: contract §8.1 "Every write is atomic"), keeps the comments and every other key, and prints the same object. The file is parsed before and after the change, and it is written only when the result parses. Setting a key that is already in the file to its current value rewrites the same bytes. A change to `durable_workers` affects the Attempts started afterwards: a started Attempt keeps its runner (contract §3.4 "The Worker runner and its seam"). A change to `durable_leads` affects the Leads created afterwards (contract §6.19). The Settings popup's Experimental section (§13.2) runs this command once per changed row.

| Refusal | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| a feature that is not one of the five keys, a state that is not `on` or `off`, or a wrong number of arguments | `usage` | 2 |
| `config.toml` does not parse, before or after the change; `details.key` names the key that breaks it | `config_invalid` | 1 |
| `config.toml` is missing | `config_missing` | 1 |

```json
{"ok":true,"experimental":{"durable_workers":false,"durable_leads":false,"write_curation":true,"failure_triage":true,"turn_question_guard":true}}
```

Idempotence: yes, a rerun with the same feature and state leaves the file as it is. Callers: none, the User at a shell (§2); cockpit: yes (§2, the Settings popup, §13.2).

### 14.2c `config concurrency set`

```
cpd config concurrency set <n>
```

Sets the machine-wide `concurrency` key of `$CPD_HOME/config.toml` (contract §8.2): the count of Attempts not ended the machine runs at once (contract §3.4 "The built-in resource `workers`"). `<n>` is required and is the only argument. Callers: none, the User at a shell (§2); cockpit: no (§2).

**Validation.** The checks run in the order of the table below, and every one of them runs before any write. The file is read first and parsed (the typed key walk of contract §8.1), the key's line is then rewritten, and the new text is parsed again: the file is written only when the result parses. The rewrite keeps every other byte of the file (comments, formatting, every other key):

- a changed key's line is replaced whole by `concurrency = <n>`;
- an absent key is inserted after the last top-level `key = value` line before the first `[table]` header, as `config tiers set` inserts (§14.2a);
- setting the key to its current value rewrites the same bytes.

The file is written atomically (a temporary file in the same directory, then a rename: contract §8.1 "Every write is atomic"). It opens no store and never waits on the setup lock (hs-n278; contract §4.2), as plain `cpd config` and `config experimental` (§14.2b) do not.

| Refusal | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| a missing or extra argument, or an `<n>` that is not an integer | `usage` | 2 |
| `<n>` outside the accepted range 1 to 16 inclusive; `details.key` is `concurrency` | `config_invalid` | 1 |
| `config.toml` does not parse, before or after the change; `details.key` names the key that breaks it | `config_invalid` | 1 |
| `config.toml` is missing (it is read first) | `config_missing` | 1 |
| the write of the file fails | `internal` | 1 |

The bound is the whole rule: a value outside 1 to 16 is refused loudly, no clamp and no silent default (air-d70); a hand-edited `config.toml` is no exception — a value outside the range is `config_invalid` (`details.key` `concurrency`) when the file is loaded, by plain `cpd config` as by the engine (contract §8.2).

**Effects.** Only the `concurrency` line is written; no row, no Event. The engine reads the count from the config file on each tick (contract §8.2), so the set takes effect without a restart; a lowered count stops nothing — it gates new starts only, and the running tenants keep their slots to the end (air-d71, contract §3.7 E3). The next Attempt started is gated by the new count, and an urgent Job may still take the one slot beyond `concurrency` (contract §3.7 E3).

```json
{"ok": true, "changed": ["concurrency"], "already": false,
 "config": {"version": 1, "machine": "hs", "concurrency": 8, "...": "..."}}
```

`changed` is `["concurrency"]` when the effective value changes and `[]` when `<n>` equals the current value, in which case `already` is `true` and nothing is written (the file is not touched). `config` is the effective configuration after the write, as plain `cpd config` prints it (§14.2). Idempotence: yes, a rerun with the same value writes nothing (`already`).

### 14.3 `tiers`

```
cpd tiers [--model <L>=<ref>]...
```

Kept from cpd 1 §7 and §11; output of §9.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| pi is found as §9 says | `pi_not_found` | 1 |
| the catalog module ran and printed valid JSON | `catalog_failed` | 1 |
| each model read is in the catalog: the configured one of each letter, or the `--model` candidate that replaces it | `tier_model_unknown` | 1 |
| `--model` is `<L>=<ref>` with `L` one of `O`, `S`, `H`, `G`, `<ref>` a model ref of §8.3 (`<provider>/<model-id>`), and no letter is given twice | `usage` | 2 |

**`--model <L>=<ref>`** (repeatable) names a candidate model for the letter `L`, for this call only. The catalog is read for the candidate instead of the configured model of `L`, and the output's `tiers.<L>.model` and `efforts` are the candidate's. Nothing is written to `host.toml` or `config.toml`; the candidate's catalog rows are cached like any model's (a cache, no Event). The output shape is unchanged, and `tiers.<L>.model` shows the candidate:

```json
{"ok": true, "pi_version": "1.2.0", "tiers": {"O": {"model": "github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5", "efforts": [0, 2, 3, 4]}, "S": {"model": "github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5.5", "efforts": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]}, "H": {"model": "github-copilot/claude-sonnet-4.5", "efforts": [0, 2, 3, 4]}, "G": {"model": "github-copilot/gemini-3.8-flash", "efforts": []}}}
```

The example is `cpd tiers --model H=github-copilot/claude-sonnet-4.5` (an illustration, not a verified model): `H` is the candidate, and `O`, `S` and `G` are as the host file gives them. Idempotent: yes; read-only for every file but the catalog cache.

It opens the store (the catalog cache), so it waits out a migration in progress (hs-n278; contract §4.2): one line on stderr, the one JSON value at the end and `lock_timeout` only past `MIGRATION_WAIT_CEILING`.

Effects: the cache is keyed by `install/current-version` and the fingerprint of `<agentDir>/models.json` (`models_sha`: lowercase hex SHA-256 of its bytes, `""` when the file does not exist; any other read error is `catalog_failed` with the path in `details`), so the key is `(pi_version, models_sha, letter, model)` (pro-d26, Plan bifrost, PR catfp; contract §4.4, §9). When either differs from the cached rows, one transaction inserting `tier_catalog` rows (append-only; old rows stay) (a cache: no Event). The rows of every letter are cached, `G` included (contract §4.4, §9). No tmux, no git.

```json
{"ok": true, "pi_version": "1.2.0", "tiers": {"O": {"model": "github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5", "efforts": [0, 2, 3, 4]}, "S": {"model": "github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5.5", "efforts": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]}, "H": {"model": "github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5", "efforts": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]}, "G": {"model": "github-copilot/gemini-3.8-flash", "efforts": []}}}
```

The `efforts` above are an illustration, not verified values. `G` reads like the other letters (pro-d328 to pro-d332): its model here has only `off`, so its `efforts` are `[]` and `GX` is its one valid Tier; a model with an effort level gives `G` efforts like any letter. Efforts are 0–4 (`minimal` and `max` are dropped, §9). Idempotent: yes.

### 14.4 `install`

```
cpd install --root <checkout> [--no-follow-up]
```

Installs the cpd built from `<checkout>`: the binary and the pi adapter, then restarts what runs the old binary, then builds the checkout's Electron app and signals the running one (step 7a). With `--no-follow-up`, step 7 is skipped: no follow-up runs (steps 7a and 8 are unchanged), so the binary and the adapter are installed and nothing that runs them is disturbed. The Electron app uses it to install at once while attempts run, and runs the follow-ups later by a second install without the flag, when no attempt runs (web/ELECTRON.md, "Auto-update and CLI bootstrap"). The User's command at a shell, run by `scripts/install-cpd.sh` and, through it, by dotfiles' install and sync; no agent runs it and no cockpit action does (callers none, cockpit no, internal no: §2). `scripts/install-cpd.sh` is the bootstrap: `CPD_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) scripts/cargo.sh build --release --locked -p cpd`, then `exec target/release/cpd install --root <checkout>`. `--root` is the checkout (a git worktree with `pi/`, `scripts/` and `core/src/store/migrations/`); the release binary is `<target>/release/cpd` (`$CARGO_TARGET_DIR` or `<root>/target`). The home is `$CPD_HOME` (default `~/.cpd`), the destination `~/.local/bin/cpd` and the adapter `~/.local/share/cpd/pi`.

Steps, in order (implementing.md "`cpd install`" has each with its message; contract §3.7 "The adapter swap" and "The install's engine order" fix the rules):

1. **Preflight.** `~/.local/share/cpd/pi` is absent, a symlink or a directory; else refused.
2. **The migration check.** `git fetch --quiet origin main` (a failed fetch refuses); every file of `core/src/store/migrations/` must be on `origin/main` with the same content; else refused, listing the names.
3. **The verdict of the built binary.** `<target>/release/cpd --version` must succeed, carry a `store` field and not say `store.opens` false; else refused with the refusal's message and the fix of its code. Nothing migrates.
4. **The config migration and validation.** `<target>/release/cpd config --migrate` reads `$CPD_HOME/config.toml`, applies the migrations (contract §8.1 "Config migrations", hs-d722; the migrations include `distill-tier-gx` and `drop-test-concurrency` (hs-d722, hs-d679), a third migration (hs-d738) and `drop-inbox-review-context` (pro-d338: the `review_context` line of the `[inbox]` table is removed, other keys and comments survive)), validates the result and writes the file only when it changed and only when the result is valid. The file is untouched on any refusal. Prints `{"ok":true,"path":"<path>","migrated":["<name>",...]}` and each applied migration as a stderr line `cpd install: config.toml migrated: <name>`. Refusals: `config_missing` (the file is absent), `config_invalid` (the migrated file is still invalid, `details.key` names it). The migration happens before the binary is replaced, so that if it fails, the config is not mutated.
4a. **The adapter packages.** Runs after step 4 and before step 5, so a failure leaves the binary, the adapter link and the config as they are. It reads `<root>/package.json`. When the file is absent, or has no `dependencies` key or an empty one, it does nothing and runs no pnpm. Otherwise `<root>/pnpm-lock.yaml` must exist; else refused: `cpd install refused: package.json has dependencies but the checkout has no pnpm-lock.yaml`. It creates `~/.local/share/cpd` if needed, copies `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` and, when present, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` there byte for byte; when `<root>/patches` is a directory, it replaces `<share>/patches` with a copy of it (the whole tree, so a patch removed from the checkout is removed from the share) before pnpm runs; when the checkout has no `patches` directory, nothing is copied and an existing `<share>/patches` is left alone. Then it runs `pnpm install --prod --frozen-lockfile` with that directory as working directory, bounded at 10 minutes, output captured. Result: `~/.local/share/cpd/node_modules` holds the production packages only (no devDependencies), so every package a non-test file under `pi/` imports must be a `dependencies` entry (contract §3.7 "The dependency rule", pinned by `pi/test/adapter-deps.test.ts` and by `pi/test/gate.test.ts`; `typebox` and `@earendil-works/pi-tui` are); the adapter's `pi.<id>` finds them (implementing.md "The adapter swap"). A non-zero exit, a timeout, or a pnpm that cannot start (not installed) refuses the install (the refusals table below). Idempotent: the same package.json and lockfile give the same result.
5. **The binary.** Copied to `~/.local/bin/.cpd.tmp.<pid>`, `chmod 755`, `rename`d over `~/.local/bin/cpd` (atomic, also while it runs).
6. **The adapter swap.** `pi/` minus `test/` is built as `pi.tmp.<pid>`, renamed to `pi.<id>`, linked as `pi.link.<pid>` (a relative symlink) and `rename`d over `pi` in one `rename(2)`; a real `pi/` directory is first renamed to `pi.legacy` (the one non-atomic moment, restored if the swap fails); `pi/package.json` must exist; then `pi.<id>` and `pi.legacy` that are neither current nor displaced, are not protected by a live pin (`pi.pin.<pid>` of a live pid, whose target is a version name; contract §3.7 "The pin") and are older than 60 minutes and `pi.tmp.<pid>` and `pi.link.<pid>` of dead pids and the pins of dead or unparseable pids, are removed (a failure only warns); the cleanup never touches `<share>/node_modules`, `<share>/package.json`, `<share>/pnpm-lock.yaml`, `<share>/pnpm-workspace.yaml` or `<share>/patches`. Prints `installed <bin> and <link>` on stderr.
7. **The follow-ups, on the new binary:** `cpd config`; `cpd watch --check` (§12); `cpd tui --respawn` (§13.1) when the cockpit has its `main` window; when the work session has its `watch` window, `cpd watch --mark-restart` (§12), `tmux kill-window -t =<work>:watch`, the wait for `locks/watch.lock` to be free (0.25 s steps, `CPD_INSTALL_LOCK_WAIT_SECS`, default 60), `cpd watch --ensure` and the check that the lock is held. A failure of `config` or `watch --check` leaves the engine and the views alone and skips the rest; any other failure prints and goes on. Each failure is one line `cpd install follow-up failed: <text>` on stderr (texts: contract §3.7).
7a. **The Electron step** (Plan cpd-app-launch, decision pro-d431; `cpd desktop`, §14.4a). It runs after the follow-ups and before the tag, with `<root>` the checkout, in this order. Each pnpm run is bounded at 10 minutes and captured, like step 4a. When `<root>/web/package.json` does not exist the step does nothing and prints `no web client in the checkout: electron step skipped` on stderr.
   - a. `pnpm --dir <root> install --frozen-lockfile`.
   - b. `pnpm --dir <root> --filter cpd-web-client run build:electron`, always, so that the bundle is the new code. Then the ensure steps of `cpd desktop` (§14.4a, step 1): when the Electron binary is missing (web/node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app or path.txt absent), run `node web/node_modules/electron/install.js` through the Runner; if it fails, stop before plutil; when the binary is present, no extra install command runs. Then always `chmod +x` on `<root>/web/node_modules/node-pty/prebuilds/*/spawn-helper`, and on macOS `plutil -replace` of `CFBundleName` and `CFBundleDisplayName` to `CPD` in `<root>/web/node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/Info.plist`.
   - c. `<home>/.local/share/cpd/app-root` (`<home>` = `$HOME`) is written with `<root>` as its one line, the absolute path, after b succeeded (a temporary file, then a rename).
   - d. When `<preview_dir>/web-state` exists (`<preview_dir>` = `$CPD_PREVIEW_DIR`, else `~/.cache/cpd-preview`), a web preview is on: Electron is left alone and stderr says `cpd install: web preview is on; Electron was not signalled`. Otherwise SIGUSR1 goes to the pid in `<cpd_home>/run/preview-health.json` (field `pid`) when that pid is alive. With no live Electron, nothing is signalled and nothing is started.

   A failed step a, b, c or d prints one line `cpd install follow-up failed: electron <a|b|c|d>: <text>` on stderr, skips the steps after it, and the install goes on to the tag. The binary and the adapter are installed already, and the install exits 1 at the end (step 10 above).
8. **The tag.** `scripts/tag-version.sh` (docs/versioning.md): a failure warns with `tag-version:` and does not change the exit.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--root` is given | `usage` | 2 |
| Step 4a: `<root>/package.json` has `dependencies` and `<root>/pnpm-lock.yaml` is absent: `cpd install refused: package.json has dependencies but the checkout has no pnpm-lock.yaml` | `install_failed` | 1 |
| Step 4a: `pnpm install --prod --frozen-lockfile` exits non-zero, times out (10 minutes) or cannot start (pnpm not installed): `cpd install refused: pnpm install --prod --frozen-lockfile failed in <share>:`, then its captured stdout and stderr, trimmed (for a pnpm that cannot start, the error) | `install_failed` | 1 |

Every refusal (steps 1 to 4a, nothing replaced), failure (steps 5 and 6) and failed follow-up (steps 7 and 7a) is a message on stderr as above and **exit 1**; the exit is 1 at the end when any follow-up line was printed.

Output: the install's progress and every message above go to stderr as human text, as the script's did (a Lead's commit hooks and dotfiles read the exit code and the text, not JSON); the one JSON value on stdout is `{"ok": true, "binary": "<path>", "adapter": "<path>", "version": "<cpd --version of the built binary>"}` on success and the error value (§1.2) with exit 1 otherwise (the messages are the script's own; every refusal, failure and failed follow-up is `install_failed`, exit 1). Effects: writes only `~/.local/bin`, `~/.local/share/cpd` (the adapter, `app-root`), the checkout's `web/node_modules` and `web/dist-electron` (step 7a) and what the follow-ups write (`run/install-restart.json`, the engine's own files); no row, no Event. Idempotent: yes, safe to rerun, also by two installs at once (contract §3.7 "The adapter swap"). The command-tree test `cli/tests/tooling/interface.rs` lists it (callers none, cockpit no, internal no); `docs/interface.md` is regenerated from the tree.

### 14.4a `desktop`

```
cpd desktop
cpd desktop --preview [<worktree>]
cpd desktop --reload [<worktree>]
cpd desktop --off
cpd desktop --status
```

The Electron app of the installed checkout and the web preview, from the User's shell. Plain `cpd desktop` launches the Electron app (`web/`, `web/ELECTRON.md`), or reloads the one that runs. The four flags run the web preview of `scripts/preview-web.sh` (docs/ui-preview.md, "Previewing the web UI"). The User's command: no agent runs it and no cockpit action does (callers none, cockpit no, internal no: §2). The flags are mutually exclusive (clap: `usage`, exit 2). `--preview` and `--reload` take an optional `<worktree>`; `--off` and `--status` take none.

**The checkout.** Every form reads `<home>/.local/share/cpd/app-root` (`<home>` = `$HOME`): one line, the absolute path of the checkout that `cpd install --root <checkout>` built (§14.4, step 7a). A missing file is `desktop_not_installed`. Nothing else is read: `~/.local/share/cpd/web` is not used.

**Plain `cpd desktop`.** Ensure, then reload or launch:
1. **Ensure** (idempotent). `pnpm --dir <root> --filter cpd-web-client run build:electron` runs only when `<root>/web/dist-electron/main.js` is missing (install always builds, §14.4 step 7a). Then, always: when the Electron binary is missing (web/node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app or path.txt absent), run `node web/node_modules/electron/install.js` through the Runner; if it fails, stop before the remaining steps; when the binary is present, no extra install command runs. Always `chmod +x` on `<root>/web/node_modules/node-pty/prebuilds/*/spawn-helper`, and on macOS `plutil -replace` of `CFBundleName` and `CFBundleDisplayName` to `CPD` in `<root>/web/node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/Info.plist`. These are the steps of the `electron` script of `web/package.json`. The build is bounded at 10 minutes.
2. **Reload or launch.** The running Electron is the pid in `<cpd_home>/run/preview-health.json` (`<cpd_home>` = `$CPD_HOME`, else `~/.cpd`; field `pid`; every Electron launch writes it), when that pid is alive. Alive: SIGUSR1 to it, action `reloaded`. Otherwise: spawn `<root>/web/node_modules/.bin/electron .` with cwd `<root>/web`, in its own session (`setsid`), stdout and stderr to `<cpd_home>/run/app.log`, without waiting; action `launched`. The spawned Electron inherits the environment of `cpd desktop` minus the five per-session cpd variables — `CPD_SESSION`, `CPD_PLAN`, `CPD_ATTEMPT`, `CPD_QUIT_MARKER` and `CPD_JOB_KIND`, the one canonical per-session list of contract §6.6 — which are removed from the child; `CPD_HOME`, `PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK` and every other variable are kept (so a run from inside an agent Session hands no agent identity to the app). The app strips the same five again at its own boot (web/ELECTRON.md, "Boot order").

Output: `{"ok": true, "action": "launched" | "reloaded", "pid": <N>}`, where `pid` is the new process or the signalled one.

**`--preview [<worktree>]`, `--reload [<worktree>]`, `--off`, `--status`.** Each runs `sh <root>/scripts/preview-web.sh on [<worktree>]`, `reload [<worktree>]`, `off` or `status` through the Runner, with a 15-minute deadline, and returns its stdout and stderr text in `output`. `--preview` starts no Electron: the script prints the command that does (docs/ui-preview.md). `--reload` builds and signals as the script does (docs/ui-preview.md, `reload`).

Output:
- `--preview`: `{"ok": true, "action": "preview_on", "output": "<text>"}`.
- `--reload`: `{"ok": true, "action": "reloaded_preview", "output": "<text>"}`.
- `--off`: `{"ok": true, "action": "preview_off", "output": "<text>"}`.
- `--status`: `{"ok": true, "action": "status", "output": "<text>", "electron": {"pid": <N>, "running": <bool>} | null}`. `electron` is `null` when the health file is missing or has no `pid`; `running` is `false` when that pid is not alive. `--status` does not ensure.

| Error | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | 2 | clap: two of the four flags at once, a `<worktree>` after `--off` or `--status`, an unknown flag |
| `desktop_not_installed` | 1 | `app-root` is missing (every form); the message says to run `scripts/install-cpd.sh` |
| `spawn_failed` | 1 | a child could not be started or exited non-zero: `pnpm` or `plutil` (ensure), `sh preview-web.sh` (the preview forms), the Electron launch; `details` is `{argv, exit, stdout, stderr}` as in §21.6, `exit` `null` when it did not start. A refused SIGUSR1: `details` is `{pid, error}` |
| `tool_timeout` | 5 | the ensure's build passes 10 minutes, or a preview script passes 15 minutes; `details.argv` names the child |

A failed ensure or a failed script exits with its error and runs nothing after it.

Effects: plain `cpd desktop` writes `<root>/web/dist-electron` when it is missing, sets the mode bits and `Info.plist` of `<root>/web/node_modules` (ensure), then launches an Electron process, writing its output to `<cpd_home>/run/app.log`, or sends SIGUSR1 to the running one. The preview forms write what `preview-web.sh` writes (docs/ui-preview.md). No row, no Event.

Idempotence: yes for each form. Ensure builds only a missing bundle; a second plain run signals the running Electron again; `--preview` respawns the dev server and rewrites `web-state`; `--off` with no preview on succeeds (docs/ui-preview.md, `off`).

### 14.5 `models`

```
cpd models refresh
cpd models show [--provider <provider>]
```

The model lists of the providers pi can use (contract §3.7 E15, Context decisions pro-d13, pro-d17, pro-d20). **cpd has no provider list and names no key**: the providers come from pi, through the helper `pi/lib/models-list.ts` and `--provider` only names one of the providers already cached. Callers: Manager, Lead, or the User at a shell (§2). Both commands open the store (the `swr_models` rows, contract §4.4, `swr-models.md`); `refresh` writes rows and appends no Event.

**`models refresh`** reads the lists now, whatever their age. It runs the helper exactly as E15 does (no argument, under pi's Node, its own process group, a deadline of 120 s, the engine's environment inherited; contract §3.7 E15 for the answer, its validation, the error codes and the file), then computes each provider's diff and writes its `swr_models` row in one store transaction (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`), by the same code as the engine, so a refresh and the engine never interleave (no lock file). A provider whose list is empty or failed keeps its row: `last_error` is set and nothing else moves. A first run, or a run after a change of `auth`, reports no change.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| pi is found as §9 says | `pi_not_found` | 1 |
| the helper starts | `spawn_failed` | 1 |
| the helper answers within 120 s | `tool_timeout` | 5 |
| the answer is the JSON of contract §3.7 E15 | `models_helper_failed` | 1 |
| pi can use a provider the contract lists | `models_no_provider` | 1 |
| the helper's whole run did not fail | the helper's code (`models_refresh_failed`, …) | 1 |
| every provider listed has a good, non-empty list | the provider's code (`models_key_unset`, `models_unauthorized`, `models_unreachable`, `models_tls`, `models_timeout`, `models_unparseable`, `models_empty`, `models_refresh_failed`) | 1 |
| the store's write lock is free within `store_busy_ms` | `store_busy` | 5 |

When one provider fails and others do not, **the good ones are written first and the command then fails** with the failing provider's code (the first, in the helper's order) and `details.providers`: the same array as `ok`'s, a failed entry being `{provider, error: {code, message, details}}`. Nothing is hidden and nothing good is lost. No key is ever in an output, a message or `details`.

Effects: the `swr_models` row written for each provider that has a good list; the helper's own effect on pi (`models-store.json`'s `checkedAt` for `github-copilot`). No Event, no tmux, no git. The engine's next E15 is not due for `watch.models_discovery_seconds` after the newest row's `polled_at`.

```json
{"ok": true, "pi_version": "1.3.0", "providers": [
  {"provider": "bifrost", "polled_at": "2026-11-02T09:00:00Z", "count": 41, "changes": {"at": "2026-11-02T09:00:00Z", "appeared": ["acme/new-model"], "went_away": []}},
  {"provider": "github-copilot", "polled_at": "2026-11-02T09:00:01Z", "count": 11, "changes": null}]}
```

`changes` is the diff of this run when it is not empty, else `null` (a list that did not change, a first run and a change of `auth` all print `null`). The ids above are an illustration, not verified values. Idempotent: yes (the same lists write the same ids and move `polled_at`).

**`models show`** prints the cached lists from the `swr_models` rows and runs nothing (no helper, no network, no write). `--provider <provider>` prints only that provider's row. A home with no row is an empty `providers` array, not an error. A row it cannot parse is a store fault: the command fails with `store_failed` (exit 1), it is not skipped. `warnings` stays in the output as `[]`.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--provider` is a file-name-safe token (`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`) | `usage` | 2 |

```json
{"ok": true, "providers": [
  {"provider": "bifrost", "polled_at": "2026-11-02T09:00:00Z", "age_seconds": 3600, "pi_version": "1.3.0", "auth": "custom", "count": 41, "ids": ["…"], "changes": {"at": "2026-11-02T09:00:00Z", "appeared": ["acme/new-model"], "went_away": []}}],
 "warnings": []}
```

`ids` is the file's sorted list, `count` its length, `auth` the file's `source.auth`, `changes` the file's last `changes` (`null` when it has none), `age_seconds` the time since `polled_at`, at the call. The providers are in name order. Idempotent: yes, read-only.

### 14.6 `preset`

```
cpd preset list
cpd preset show <name>
cpd preset apply <name>
cpd preset set --O <ref> --S <ref> --H <ref> --G <ref>
```

The tier-preset switch (D1–D5 of Plan `tier-presets`): a named set of four model refs — the `O`, `S`, `H` and `G` keys of a `[presets.<name>]` table of `$CPD_HOME/config.toml` (contract §8.1, §8.2) — applied to the machine by rewriting the `[model]` table of its host policy. `list` and `show` are read-only and their callers are `[Manager, Lead]`; `apply` and `set` write and their caller is `[Manager]` (§2). `set` takes the four refs as flags, with no name (§14.6a). None of the four writes `config.toml`: presets are the User's, managed by dotfiles. A provider is the text before the first `/` of a ref. `apply` writes a single-provider table (step 4), as contract §8.3 "One provider per table" holds of any written model table.

**`preset list`** prints every preset with the provider of its `O` ref. No precondition, no effect (one read of `config.toml`, no store):

```json
{"ok": true, "presets": [
  {"name": "fast", "provider": "github-copilot"}]}
```

`presets` is sorted by name, `[]` when the config has none. Idempotent: read-only.

**`preset show <name>`** prints the preset's four refs and the current host `[model]`:

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `<name>` is a `[presets.<name>]` table of `config.toml` | `preset_unknown` | 4 |

```json
{"ok": true, "name": "fast",
 "O": "github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5", "S": "github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5.5",
 "H": "github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5", "G": "github-copilot/gemini-3.8-flash",
 "host": {"O": "github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5", "S": "github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5.5",
          "H": "github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5", "G": "github-copilot/gemini-3.8-flash"}}
```

`host` is the machine scope's `[model]` refs read from `$CPD_HOME/policy/host.toml`, or the built-in default of contract §8.3 when the file has no `[model]` table. No registry is read and nothing is validated: `show` reports, it never checks. Idempotent: read-only.

**`preset apply <name>`** validates the preset and, when it differs from the current host `[model]`, rewrites the `[model]` table of `$CPD_HOME/policy/host.toml`, then records the live Sessions whose model changed. Steps, in order; **every refusal happens before any write: nothing is written and no Event is appended**:

1. **The name.** `<name>` must be a `[presets.<name>]` table of `config.toml`, else `preset_unknown` (exit 4).
2. **The host file.** `$CPD_HOME/policy/host.toml` must exist and hold a `[model]` table, else `policy_invalid` (exit 1, `details.file`, `details.key` `model`): there is nothing to rewrite.
3. **Equality.** When the preset's four refs equal the current host `[model]` refs of step 2, `apply` is a no-op: no write, no Event, `"already": true` (idempotent).
4. **The one-provider invariant.** The preset's four refs must have one provider, the invariant contract §8.3 holds of a written model table; else `policy_invalid` (exit 1, `details.file`, `details.key` `model`), before anything external runs.
5. **The registry** (D3). The command lists pi's **full** registry on this machine — every provider pi can use, the built-in providers included, each with its offered model ids — by running the model-discovery helper (`pi/lib/models-list.ts`, the helper §14.5's `models refresh` and the engine's E15 run with no argument) in its `--all` mode, through the host runner, under pi's Node, in its own process group, with the deadline of `models refresh`'s (120 s). **The cached `run/models-<provider>.json` files are never the source**: they exclude the built-in providers, so the registry is always listed at apply time. The registry listing's own failures are the helper's codes (`pi_not_found`, `spawn_failed`, `tool_timeout` exit 5, `models_helper_failed`, …), writing nothing. Then:
   - a ref whose provider is not in the registry refuses `preset_provider_unconfigured` (exit 3);
   - a ref that is not among its provider's offered ids refuses `preset_model_unoffered` (exit 3).
6. **The write** (D4). The `[model]` table of `host.toml` is rewritten: the section header `[model]` and its `O`/`S`/`H`/`G` lines are replaced by the preset's four refs, in that order, and every other byte of the file is unchanged. The write is atomic: a temporary file in the same directory, then a rename over `host.toml` (`write_atomic`). `host.toml` stays the **only** place `[model]` is written (pro-d25): no owner or repo policy file and no dotfiles template.
7. **The live Sessions** (D5). After the write, the command recomputes the model each live (not archived) Lead and Manager Session resolves at its tier's letter — the `model` of `cpd session show` (§10.2), i.e. the ref contract §8.3's resolution gives the letter of the Session's stored tier, so a letter whose effective ref an owner or repo file overrides is unchanged. For every Session whose model differs under the pre-write and the post-write host `[model]`, ONE `session-model-changed` Event is appended, scoped to it (`context` and `plan` when it has them; `data` `{from, to}` = the resolved refs under the pre-write and the post-write `host.toml`), all in one store transaction, in the same style as `session-retiered` (contract §5.2, §5.3). A Session whose letter's model is unchanged gets none. Nothing else is written for Sessions.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `<name>` is a `[presets.<name>]` table of `config.toml` (step 1) | `preset_unknown` | 4 |
| `host.toml` exists and holds a `[model]` table; `details.file`, `details.key` `model` (step 2) | `policy_invalid` | 1 |
| the preset's four refs are one provider — the invariant of contract §8.3 for the written table; `details.file`, `details.key` `model` (step 4) | `policy_invalid` | 1 |
| the registry can be listed: pi is found as §9 says | `pi_not_found` | 1 |
| the registry can be listed: the helper starts | `spawn_failed` | 1 |
| the registry can be listed: the helper answers within 120 s | `tool_timeout` | 5 |
| the registry can be listed: the answer is the JSON of contract §3.7 E15, in `--all` mode | `models_helper_failed` | 1 |
| the preset's provider is in the registry (step 5a) | `preset_provider_unconfigured` | 3 |
| every ref is among its provider's offered ids (step 5b) | `preset_model_unoffered` | 3 |

`apply` opens the store (it appends the Events of step 7; the no-op of step 3 opens nothing and writes nothing), so the write path waits out a migration in progress as every store-opening command does (contract §4.2). The file write of step 6 is not a store write: only the Events of step 7 write rows, each with the usual `txns` and `history` rows of a transaction.

```json
{"ok": true, "preset": "fast", "host": "/home/clayton/.cpd/policy/host.toml",
 "already": false,
 "changed": [
   {"session": "596d007f-…", "role": "lead", "from": "github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5", "to": "github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5.5", "event": 48220}]}
```

`host` is the path of the rewritten file; `changed` lists one entry per Session whose model changed, with the Session's id and role and its Event's `from`, `to` and `event` (the Event's id). When step 3 finds the host already on the preset, the output is `{"ok": true, "preset": "fast", "already": true, "changed": []}`. Idempotent: yes — a rerun whose preset already equals the host `[model]` is the no-op above.

### 14.6a `preset set`

```
cpd preset set --O <ref> --S <ref> --H <ref> --G <ref>
```

The switch of `preset apply` with the four refs given as flags instead of a `[presets.<name>]` table: steps 2 to 7 of `preset apply` below are shared, and `set` replaces its step 1 (the name lookup) with the flags. Each ref is `<provider>/<model-id>` (contract §8.3, 1 to 200 characters, no NUL). All four flags are required; a missing one is `usage`. Callers: `[Manager]`, as `apply` (§2); cockpit: yes (§2). It needs no `[presets]` table in `config.toml`, and it writes nothing to `config.toml`.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--O <ref>` | the model ref of the `O` letter |
| `--S <ref>` | the model ref of the `S` letter |
| `--H <ref>` | the model ref of the `H` letter |
| `--G <ref>` | the model ref of the `G` letter |

**Steps, in order.** Every refusal happens before any write: nothing is written and no Event is appended.

1. **The refs.** Each `--O`, `--S`, `--H` and `--G` parses as a model ref (`usage` otherwise), before anything is read.
2. **The host file, equality, one provider, registry.** Exactly `preset apply`'s steps 2 to 5 with the flags' four refs as the preset's: the host file must hold a `[model]` table; when the four refs equal the host's, the command is a no-op (`already`, no registry run, no store opened); the four refs must be one provider; the registry (pi's full list, §14.6 `apply` step 5) must hold each provider and each model id, `preset_provider_unconfigured` and `preset_model_unoffered` otherwise.
3. **The write and the live Sessions.** Exactly `preset apply`'s steps 6 and 7: the `[model]` table of `host.toml` is rewritten atomically, and one `session-model-changed` Event is appended for each live Lead and Manager whose model changed, in one store transaction.

**Effects.** The `[model]` rewrite of `host.toml` and the Events of step 3, and nothing else: no `config.toml` write, no other row, and no write at all on a refusal or on the no-op of step 2.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| a ref does not parse as a model ref of §8.3, or a flag is missing (step 1) | `usage` | 2 |
| `host.toml` exists and holds a `[model]` table; `details.file`, `details.key` `model` (step 2) | `policy_invalid` | 1 |
| the four refs are one provider; `details.file`, `details.key` `model` (step 2) | `policy_invalid` | 1 |
| the registry can be listed: pi is found as §9 says | `pi_not_found` | 1 |
| the registry can be listed: the helper starts | `spawn_failed` | 1 |
| the registry can be listed: the helper answers within 120 s | `tool_timeout` | 5 |
| the registry can be listed: the answer is the JSON of contract §3.7 E15, in `--all` mode | `models_helper_failed` | 1 |
| the ref's provider is in the registry | `preset_provider_unconfigured` | 3 |
| every ref is among its provider's offered ids | `preset_model_unoffered` | 3 |

It opens the store only to append the Events of step 3, so it waits out a migration in progress as `preset apply` does (contract §4.2). A rerun whose refs equal the host `[model]` is the no-op of step 2 and writes nothing.

```json
{"ok": true, "preset": null, "host": "/home/clayton/.cpd/policy/host.toml",
 "already": false,
 "changed": [
   {"session": "596d007f-…", "role": "lead", "from": "github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5", "to": "github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5.5", "event": 48221}]}
```

The output is `apply`'s, with `preset` `null` (there is no name). When the refs equal the host `[model]`, the output is `{"ok": true, "preset": null, "already": true, "changed": []}`, as `apply`'s no-op. Idempotence: yes; a rerun with the same four refs is the no-op above.

### 14.7 `metrics`

```
cpd metrics [--format json|prometheus]
```

The read-only aggregate of the machine's Ledger (hs-d798). Callers `[Manager, Lead]` (§2). It opens the store read-only, reads the `attempts.metrics` blobs the `attempt-ended` Events carry (contract §5.2) and the queue Events, and prints one aggregate value; it writes nothing, appends nothing and touches nothing but the store file it reads. **Fail-open (hs-d798, quoted): `cpd metrics` reads the local store and `cpd` never depends on the LGTM exporter, Prometheus or the homeserver being up.** Nothing in cpd may depend on the exporter, Prometheus or the homeserver: a dead collector costs a metric, never a Workflow.

**The default (`--format json`) is one JSON value** with the keys `store`, `per_tier`, `per_model`, `retries`, `plans`, `queue`:

- `per_tier` and `per_model`: per-Tier and per-model counts — attempts, merged, failed by cause, average and median duration, average cost, total cost.
- `retries`: the retry-cause histogram (the `cause` of every `attempt-retry`, contract §5.2).
- `plans`: per Plan, the cost in `$` per merged pull request.
- `queue`: the queue-wait decomposition — the `job-added` → `attempt-started` wait (average and max, seconds) and the count of `job-blocked` episodes (contract §5.2).
- `store`: the store the value was read from (its path), so a value can always be traced to what it was read from.

**Refusals are their own metric** (Plan `agent-refusals`; air-d85): the causes above cover Jobs' Attempts, not an agent's refusals. Every guard refusal and agent-caused CLI refusal is appended as a guard Event (contract §5.2), and `cpd metrics refusals` aggregates those Events into the refusal rate per guard, role, model and day (below).

**`cpd metrics refusals`** is the one aggregate of the refusals this machine's agents suffered: the rate over the guard Events, per guard, role, model and day. Read-only, as its parent is: it opens the store read-only, reads the `guard` Events, prints one JSON value and writes nothing. Callers `[Manager, Lead]` (§2).

```
cpd metrics refusals [--since <date>] [--until <date>] [--limit <n>]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--since <date>` | the window's start, **inclusive**; an RFC 3339 timestamp or a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` date (`YYYY-MM-DD` is `00:00:00Z` of that day). Default: 7 days before `--until` |
| `--until <date>` | the window's end, **exclusive**, in the same two forms. Default: now, on the reading process's clock |
| `--limit <n>` | at most this many rows of each table, `0` for every row. Default `20` |

**The window and what it counts.** One guard Event is counted when its `at` is at or after `--since` and before `--until`: every refusal the adapter guards and the agent-caused CLI refusals appended (contract §5.2 "The guard Event"), of every role and every Plan. The window is echoed in the value as `{since, until, days}`, `days` its length in days (`until − since` in seconds, divided by 86400), the divisor of every rate.

**The value**, one JSON object:

- `store`: the store the value was read from (its path), so a value can always be traced to what it was read from.
- `window`: `{since, until, days}` as above, `since` and `until` in RFC 3339 UTC.
- `total`: the count of the counted guard Events.
- `per_guard`, `per_role`, `per_model`: the same Events in the three other dimensions — one row per `data.code` for `per_guard` (the guard rule, or the CLI envelope's code, contract §5.2), per `data.role` for `per_role` (`manager`, `lead`, `worker`) and per `data.model` for `per_model` (the model ref) — each row `{guard|role|model, count, per_day}`, highest `count` first, a tie by name ascending.
- `per_day`: the same Events by day, oldest day first, as `{day, count, per_guard}`, `per_guard` an object of `code` → count for that day; only days with at least one counted Event appear.

**The rate** is `per_day` on every row: its `count` divided by the window's `days`, rounded to two decimals, so 70 refusals over a 7-day window is `10.0` and 1 refusal over the same is `0.14`. The `day` of `per_day` is the **UTC calendar day** of the Event's `at` (the store keeps `at` in UTC, contract §5.2): the metric is machine-wide and applies no local zone, so the same store read in any zone gives the same tables.

```json
{"ok": true, "store": "/home/clayton/.cpd/cpd.db",
 "window": {"since": "2026-11-01T00:00:00Z", "until": "2026-11-08T00:00:00Z", "days": 7.0},
 "total": 34,
 "per_guard": [{"guard": "usage", "count": 21, "per_day": 3.0},
               {"guard": "explore timeout", "count": 7, "per_day": 1.0}],
 "per_role": [{"role": "worker", "count": 26, "per_day": 3.71},
              {"role": "lead", "count": 8, "per_day": 1.14}],
 "per_model": [{"model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4", "count": 19, "per_day": 2.71},
               {"model": "github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5.5", "count": 15, "per_day": 2.14}],
 "per_day": [{"day": "2026-11-06", "count": 12, "per_guard": {"usage": 7, "explore timeout": 5}},
             {"day": "2026-11-07", "count": 22, "per_guard": {"usage": 14, "explore timeout": 2, "test": 6}}]}
```

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--since` or `--until` is neither an RFC 3339 timestamp nor a `YYYY-MM-DD` date | `usage` | 2 |
| `--until` is not after `--since` | `usage` | 2 |
| `--limit` is not a non-negative integer | `usage` | 2 |

Idempotent: read-only, so a rerun over an unchanged store prints the same value. **There is no `--format` on it:** `--format prometheus` (below) exposes the Attempts' aggregates and nothing else, because a refusal rate feeds no exporter. The surface is the CLI only.

**The threshold alert is the engine's, not this command's** (Plan `agent-refusals`; air-d85, air-d105, air-d64; contract §3.7 E25). Engine step E25 counts the `guard` Events of each Session over a sliding window at every tick, and at or above the configured threshold it (1) appends one structured `error` Event with the code `refusal_threshold`, (2) messages the Context's Manager with a waking `session-message`, the air-d64 pattern so that the Manager acts at once instead of finding the crossing in the Inbox, and (3) leaves a red `refusal-alert` Inbox item for the User, which E8 opens and closes with the count. `cpd metrics refusals` takes no part in the alert: it reads the same Events and reports them, and it is where a Manager sees whether the crossing was real. Its only reader is a command line — no daemon, no scrape, no exported metric.

**`--format prometheus` prints the same aggregates in the Prometheus text exposition format, output only**: no scrape server, no daemon, no push in cpd; the caller collects the text. The scheme is stable, all gauges, namespace `cpd_`:

| Metric | Labels |
|---|---|
| `cpd_attempts` | `tier`, `model` |
| `cpd_attempts_merged` | `tier` |
| `cpd_attempts_failed` | `tier`, `cause` |
| `cpd_attempt_duration_seconds` | `tier`, `stat="avg\|median"` |
| `cpd_attempt_cost_usd_total` | `tier` |
| `cpd_attempt_cost_usd_avg` | `tier` |
| `cpd_model_attempts` | `model` |
| `cpd_model_cost_usd_total` | `model` |
| `cpd_attempt_retries` | `cause` |
| `cpd_plan_cost_usd_per_merged_pr` | `plan` |
| `cpd_queue_wait_seconds` | `phase="added_to_started"`, `stat="avg\|max"` |
| `cpd_job_blocked_episodes` | (none) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--format` is `json` or `prometheus` | `usage` | 2 |

Idempotent: read-only. `job-blocked` episodes are counted from the Events (one per waiting episode, contract §3.7 E3), so a rerun gives the same numbers while the store is unchanged.

## 15. The pi adapter's protocol

The pi adapter is the TypeScript package `pi/` (decisions: "the pi adapter stays TypeScript"), loaded in every pi session cpd starts (§6.5). It is the only pi-specific code: it turns Events into messages (§5.3), reports agent states (§3.6) and runs the Plan review in the Lead's chat (§15.5). It calls only `cpd` commands; it never reads the database and never types into a pane (cpd 1 §15, kept).

### 15.1 Package and activation

- **Package:** `pi/package.json` with `"keywords": ["pi-package"]` and `"pi": {"extensions": ["./extension.ts"], "skills": ["./skills"]}`; host packages are `peerDependencies: "*"` (cpd 1 §15, kept). The skill `cpd-lead` is the cpd 2 skill.
- **Location:** `pi/`, installed to `~/.local/share/cpd/pi` by `cpd install` (§14.4). (History: before the switch-over it lived beside cpd 1's `pi/`, in a second directory.)
- **Activation:** at pi's `session_start`, only when `ctx.mode` is `tui` and `CPD_SESSION` is set. Change from cpd 1: cpd 1 activated in any herdr or tmux pane (`HERDR_ENV`, `TMUX_PANE`); now cpd marks its own panes with `CPD_SESSION` (§6.5), so a pi the User starts by hand is left alone.
- **The empty last row** (User, hs-d567; contract §6.1 "The blank row", Q2-Q3): in its `session_start` handler (`pi/lib/adapter.ts`), the adapter calls `ctx.ui.setStatus("cpd-pad", "")` (`ctx.mode` `tui`; it knows nothing of the chat slot, so a parked pane has the extra empty row too). pi's footer draws one more line, empty, when its extension statuses are not empty, so pi's last row is empty; a `/reload` runs `session_start` again and sets it again and a resize needs nothing (verified in real pi, contract §6.1 evidence). The key `cpd-pad` is ours; another extension's status text would share the line.
- **Footer and status text** (`rg -n "setStatus|statusbar|footer|setWidget" pi/lib pi/durable-host`, Plan `agent-keys-surfaces`): the adapter sets one status key, `cpd-pad`, to the empty string, and one widget that renders nothing (`pi/lib/pad.ts`). No footer or status text names the Session, so none shows its key. The notices that name a Session are the fork's rename notice (§15.3) and the key notice (§15.4), which states the key.
- **The quit marker** (pro-d361; §10.8, §6.6). At `session_start`, in `tui` mode, `pi/lib/adapter.ts` calls `installQuitMarker` (`pi/lib/quit.ts`), which installs an editor wrapper with `ctx.ui.setEditorComponent`. The path comes from `host.env` (`CPD_QUIT_MARKER`, set by `session run`); the adapter computes no path. When the User submits exactly `/quit` or `/q` (trimmed), the wrapper writes the marker, an empty file, synchronously and creates its directory if missing; then pi quits as for `/quit`. `/q` is an alias of `/quit` (pro-d406): in the tmux pi TUI it behaves exactly like `/quit`, and the marker is written for both. It writes nothing for any other input, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D or a signal. The marker is one-shot: `session run` removes it (§10.8), and nothing else in the adapter reads it. Unverified: that the replaced editor keeps pi's Ctrl+D and Escape handlers; a spike must confirm it before this lands. The wrapper's editor is built with `embedWorkingStatus: true` (pro-d389), so pi embeds the working-status pill in the editor's top border (with compact-tools-editor) rather than mounting it above the input box.
- **Identity:** `CPD_SESSION` must equal `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()`. If not, the adapter delivers one error message (below) and stays inactive: it would otherwise report another Session's state.
- **Calls:** one-shot commands through `pi.exec("cpd", args)`, whose stdout is parsed as the JSON envelope at the boundary (a non-JSON stdout, or `ok: false`, is an error with the code). Each call passes a timeout of 30 s and the abort signal of the adapter's run (aborted at `session_shutdown`); a call that times out or is aborted is reported like a failed call (the error delivery below, code `tool_timeout` for a timeout). The follower is a child process (`node:child_process` `spawn`, argv, stdin `/dev/null`) read line by line. Every argv the adapter builds is one cpd's own grammar accepts (the clap tree of `cli/src/cli.rs`, as `cpd <command> --help` shows it): a flag where the command takes a flag, a positional only where it takes one. A `usage` refusal of an argv the adapter built is an adapter defect, never a condition: it is reported like any adapter error (the error delivery below), and a read that fails with it never renders a polite line in a message (§15.7 (4)). The guard is `docs/implementing.md` "The fake cpd refuses what cpd refuses".
- **Errors** (hs-d552; the adapter-only codes `protocol_mismatch`, `mcp_register_failed` and `skills_unreadable` are delivered by this rule, contract §1.2; `mcp_register_failed` and `skills_unreadable` are also reported, below) for a **Manager** or **Worker**: delivered to the Session as `pi.sendMessage({customType: "cpd", content: "cpd adapter: <what>: <code>: <message>", display: true, details: {kind: "error", code, …}}, {triggerTurn: false, deliverAs: "followUp"})`: no turn started, shown as a follow-up. An error identical to the last one shown in this Session (same `what` and `code`) is not shown again until a different error has been shown; one memory per Session, cleared at reload. For a **Lead** (hs-d573 cause A): one line appended to the adapter log `$CPD_HOME/run/adapter/<session>.log` (15.6 'Log'): `<time> error: <what>: <code>: <message>`, and reported to the Manager with `cpd session report` (§10.18), once per (`what`, `code`) by memory (`host.report`): the same error again is neither logged again nor reported again until a different one has been. The Manager's error Event carries `session` = the reporting Session (DEFECT 1: so the Manager can see which Session failed), and `plan` = null, so the Lead does not receive its own error back (§11.2). A failed report is one log line, as L4 below says. The adapter never throws into pi.
- **A refused MCP registration** (pro-d226; `mcp_register_failed`, §5.3, §15.3), for **every role**. **L1:** it is reported with `cpd session report --what 'mcp attach <name>' --code mcp_register_failed --message <pi's message> --details {"name","message"} --session <id>`, one `error` Event; a Manager or a Worker also gets the chat message above, and a Lead gets its log line (above) and no chat. **L2:** `what` is `mcp attach <name>`, which names the server. A refused registration is **never deduplicated**: `mcp_register_failed` bypasses `host.report`'s memory (`lastError`) in both its deliveries, the chat message and the report (and a Lead's log line), and it neither sets nor clears that memory, so the dedupe of every other error is unchanged. The same server refused twice in a row is two reports, and so are two servers refused in a row. Each report is tied to one Event id (handled at most once per run) or to one start, so it cannot flood. **L3:** the registrations of the replay at start (§15.2 step 5a) are reported the same way, one report per refused server. **L4:** a failed `session report` call is one log line, `report failed: <code>: <message>` (§15.6 'Log'), never delivered and never reported again, for every role (no recursion); the next refusal tries again. **L5:** only `mcp_register_failed` skips the memory. `skills_unreadable` (pro-d260, §15.23) is the second code reported to the ledger for every role, and, unlike `mcp_register_failed`, it is not exempt from the memory. Every other adapter error keeps its role's delivery and its memory exactly as above.

### 15.2 Start-up and the cursor

At `session_start`, in this order:
0. **Protocol check** (hs-a4): `cpd --version`, whose `protocol` (§1.2) is compared with the number the adapter was built for (`PROTOCOL` in `pi/lib/event.ts`; 23 today, contract §5.2). Equal: nothing is said. Different: one message to the Session, `cpd adapter: protocol mismatch: protocol_mismatch: cpd speaks protocol N, this adapter M; reload pi (/reload)`, with `details: {kind: "error", code: "protocol_mismatch", cpd: N, adapter: M}`, delivered like the other errors (§15.1), once per installed cpd binary (the identity of the file `cpd` resolves to), not once per follower restart. The adapter keeps following Events either way; it never types into a pane. A `--version` that fails or lacks `protocol` is an ordinary error with its code, once per error code.
1. `cpd session show <id>`: role, Plan, Context, `plan_lead`, `registered_event`, name and `key`. The `key` field must be present, a string or null (§10.2); a `session show` without it is refused as `bad_output` (§15.1 'Errors') and is retried like a failed call. The adapter keeps `key` for §15.4. A failure is delivered as an error message once per error code and the call is retried with the follower's back-off (1 s, doubling to at most 30 s) until it succeeds; the adapter does nothing else until then and `session_shutdown` ends the retries. A refusal that cannot pass (`usage`, `session_required`, `invalid_session_id`, `session_ambiguous`, `session_not_found`, `plan_not_found`, `context_not_found`, `cursor_ahead`) is delivered once and not retried: the adapter stays inactive.
2. `cpd session state idle --session <id>` (`stopped → idle`, §3.6); then `working` if `ctx.isIdle()` is false.
3. **Name:** if pi's session name differs from the Session's `name`, `pi.setSessionName(name)`: a `session-renamed` missed while pi was down still applies.
4. **Cursor** (§5.3 "No loss, no duplicates"): the greater of `registered_event` and the **highest** `details.id` of the `cpd` custom messages in the session's entries whose `details.delivered_to` is this Session's id (not the last: delivery is not in id order, `pr-feedback` is steered and the rest are follow-ups). The adapter puts `delivered_to` into every message it delivers (amendment 5, §19). Why: a fork's file starts with its source's messages, whose Event ids belong to the source's stream; counting them could skip Events addressed to the fork.
5. **Blocking reasons** (Plan Lead only; a Manager has none): one per `open` Escalation of its Plan (`cpd plan show`), and one for the Plan's **latest** Plan review when it is pending and this session opened it (its `cpd-plan-review` entries of either surface, §15.5; a pending chat entry also reopens its dialog, §15.5 "Recovery"): the latest is the one `cpd plan show` reports (`review.id`), and an undecided older review never opens a reason (hs-d224).
5a. **MCP replay** (pro-d226). pi keeps a registration only in memory, so the adapter registers the Session's attached servers again at every start. It makes ONE call, `cpd events list --session <id> --kind mcp-attached --limit 5000` (an existing command with existing flags: `protocol` is unchanged). The read is the full history: the staleness filter of pro-d214 applies only to `events follow`, never to this read, and the read does not depend on the cursor. It keeps the Events whose `session` is its own id; for each distinct `data.name` it keeps the Event with the highest id; and it registers those with `attachServer` (contract §6.11) in ascending id order, using the entry exactly as the Event holds it (a later edit of the machine policy applies at the next `cpd mcp attach`, never at replay). It runs at every `session_start` (startup, resume, new, fork, reload). A fork has none, because its Events name the source Session. A failed read (`events list` fails, or its output is not a list of valid `mcp-attached` Events) is one adapter error (§15.1) with what `events list (mcp-attached)` and the code of the failure: start-up goes on with no replay and no retry, and the next start reads again. A page of exactly 5000 Events is the adapter error `mcp_replay_truncated`: it registers nothing and counts as a failed read, because a page is the oldest 5000 and its latest Event per name could be missing. A server pi refuses during replay is reported as §15.1 'Errors' and §15.3 say for a live Event (L3, pro-d226): one `mcp_register_failed` error Event per refused server, for every role, never deduplicated, and the other servers still register.
5b. **Skill check** (pro-d260; a Lead or a Manager only): the adapter compares its skill's text with the Session's baseline and, when it changed, tells the Session at its next turn, as §15.23 says.
6. **Follow:** spawn `cpd events follow --session <id> --since <cursor>`.

The cursor in memory advances after each line is handled, delivered or not. Only delivered messages persist it. The Run also remembers the Event ids it has delivered and skips a repeated one. Step 5a (pro-d226) adds every own `mcp-attached` Event that its read returned to that memory: each counts as handled for this Run, whether it registered or was superseded by a later Event of the same name, so the follower's later delivery of the same Event id (it restarts from a cursor that delivered messages keep below the attach Event) registers nothing. An Event id the replay did not read registers as today, including a re-attach of a name already registered (pi replaces the same name, and pi's MCP extension reconnects a replaced server), so `cpd mcp attach` again stays the recovery for a server that is missing. After a restart the Events handled without a message (`escalation-answered`, `escalation-expired`, `session-renamed`, `plan-review`) are seen again; every handler below is idempotent for that reason.

**The follower ends** (EOF, exit, or a failure line): the adapter restarts it with `--since <in-memory cursor>` after 1 s, then backing off to at most 30 s. A failure line or a non-zero exit is delivered as an error message once per error code, until a line is read again. A failure line whose code is one of the refusals of step 1 is permanent: it is delivered once and the follower is **not** restarted (every other code, for example `store_busy` or `store_too_new`, is retried without end). A well-formed Event (§5.2 fields) of a kind the adapter does not know is skipped silently: no message and the cursor moves past it (an adapter that does not know a kind cannot need it, so an install that adds a kind does not flood older adapters). A malformed line (not JSON, or §5.2 fields missing or of the wrong type) is delivered as an error message and skipped and the cursor moves past it, so one bad line cannot stop delivery. Before it spawns the follower again, the adapter repeats the protocol check of step 0; the message is sent only when the installed binary is a different one from the last that mismatched.

**store_too_new when the installed cpd is newer** (hs-d7): at each follower run start, the adapter records the identity of the file `cpd` resolves to (the installed cpd identity, from `installedIdentity()` in pi/lib/cpd.ts). A failure line whose code is `store_too_new` is **not delivered** if the installed cpd identity differs from the identity recorded at this follower's start: the follower was running the old cpd binary when it was started and a newer cpd is now installed. In that case, the follower is restarted as usual (which runs the new cpd from PATH) and the restart delay resets to 1 s. When the installed cpd identity is the same as the one recorded at the follower's start (no install has happened since), `store_too_new` is delivered as today: once per error code, until a line is read again (the code is retried without end, as per the second sentence).

At `session_shutdown` the follower is killed.

### 15.3 What each Event does

Events arrive in id order; the follower already applied §11's `--session` rule and dropped the Events whose condition no longer held (§11.2) and an id already delivered in this activation is never delivered twice, so a Lead receives its Plan's Events and a Worker or side fork only those addressed to it. Delivery is `pi.sendMessage({customType: "cpd", content: event.text, display: true, details: {...event, delivered_to: <id>}}, {triggerTurn, deliverAs})` (§5.3), where `deliverAs` is `"steer"` for the **urgent kinds** and `"followUp"` for every other message (below).

| Kind | Plan Lead | Worker, side fork |
|---|---|---|
| `job-merged`, `job-failed`, `error` | message, **turn**, `followUp`. The `job-merged` of an `open` Job is the Lead's word that its pull request is open (`data.number`, `data.url`, hs-d340) | |
| `plan-done` | message, **turn**, `followUp`, except an Event whose `data.turn` is `false` (written by `review submit --event APPROVE` for a `codereview` Plan, §31.1, and by the team lookup's finish, contract §2.2 "The Plan finish"): no message and no turn (contract §5.3) | |
| `all-merged` | ignored: no longer appended (hs-d340, contract §3.7 E4); the adapter still knows the kind, because an old Event may be read | |
| `error` with code `workflow_start_failed` | the Lead answers with `cpd workflow start <key>` once the cause is fixed | |
| `pr-feedback` (every `reason`: checks failed, changes requested, closed) | message, **turn**, **`steer`**. Carries the Workflow's key in `data.workflow` | |
| `attempt-retry`, `job-cancelled` | message, no turn, `followUp` | |
| `workflow-started`, `pr-merged` | message, no turn, `followUp` (R34: a started Workflow's Jobs are now scheduled; a merged Workflow may start the Workflows that need it, §5.3) | |
| `workflow-base-changed` | message, no turn, `followUp` (informational, hs-d325: the Workflow's `base` followed the pull request's base on GitHub, as after the Workflow it is based on merged; no Gate is needed and the Workflow stays ready, hs-d326). `data` is in contract §5.2. Raises `protocol` to 5 | |
| `escalation` | message, **turn**, **`steer`**; opens the blocking reason `escalation:<id>` labelled `φ: Worker question` | |
| `escalation-answered`, `escalation-expired` | closes `escalation:<id>`; no message | |
| `plan-review` with `status: pending` | opens it in the Lead's chat (§15.5): the summary as a `cpd-plan-summary` message (no turn) and the dialog; no `cpd` message for the Event itself. A review with a higher id than another pending review of this session **closes** that one's `plan-review:<review>` reason: only the latest review of a Plan blocks the Lead (§15.5 "Latest only") | |
| `plan-review` with `status: approved` or `rejected`, for a pending entry of this session | a decision made outside this adapter (§15.5 "Deciding elsewhere"): closes `plan-review:<review>` and an open dialog of it; message `cpd-plan-decision`, **turn**, `followUp` (own custom type, not `cpd`). For any other review: ignored | |
