The file is consumed when the first matching command of that Session runs within 10 minutes of `at` (contract §8.4).

Output:

```json
{"ok": true, "action": "get", "vault": "vault-name", "item": "secret-item", "field": "secret-field", "expires_at": "2026-10-22T21:10:00.000Z"}
```

Idempotent: no; every call writes a new file.


## 23. `incident`

Incident mode (hs-d643, user decision hs-d643; supersedes hs-d634): Plan-scoped hold on scheduling. One Manager-only command to start and end, one any caller may read. A Manager starts with one or more Plans (no machine-wide mode).

### 23.1 `incident start`

```
cpd incident start --plan <id> [--plan <id>...] [--reason <text>] [--until-workflow <plan>/<key>]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--plan <id>` | required, repeatable at least once; names an existing Plan in this Context |
| `--reason <text>` | optional; 1 or more characters, explanation of the incident; required only on a fresh start |
| `--until-workflow <plan>/<key>` | optional; Workflow key in format `<plan>/<key>` of one of the named Plans; incident ends when this Workflow's pull request merges |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `CPD_SESSION` is set, valid and a Manager Session (role `manager`, not archived) | `manager_only` | 3 |
| at least one `--plan` is present | `usage` | 2 |
| when incident is off, `--reason` is present and at least 1 character | `usage` | 2 |
| no `--plan` argument, or every one names an existing Plan in the store | `plan_not_found` | 4 |
| `--until-workflow` is absent, or its value is a Workflow of one of the named Plans and exists | `workflow_not_found` | 4 |
| `--until-workflow` is absent, or its value's Plan is one of the named Plans | `until_workflow_not_incident` | 3 |
| `--until-workflow` is valid JSON and `<plan>/<key>` format, or not present | `usage` | 2 |

**Effects:** one transaction. **Fresh start** (when incident is off): insert one row in `incident` table (`id = 1`, `started_at` now, `started_by` the Manager's Session id, `reason` the text, `started_txn` the transaction id, `lead` the `lead_session` of the first `--plan` argument's Plan, `until_plan` and `until_workflow` as specified or null); insert one row per named Plan in `incident_plans` table (plan, started_txn); for every running Attempt in the same transaction, if `stop_request` is null set it to `'cancelled'`; append `incident-started` Event with `data` including `plans` array; return `changed: true`. **Update on a live incident** (when incident is on): replace `incident_plans` with exactly the named Plans; when the set changed, recompute `lead` from the new first Plan's `lead_session`; when the set or `until_workflow` changed, update `until_plan`, `until_workflow` and `lead` and append `incident-plans` Event with the new `plans` array; when all are unchanged, append no Event; return `changed: true` when the Event is appended, `changed: false` when unchanged; run no stop-request sweep. The `started_at`, `started_by` and stored `reason` stay unchanged on an update. When `--until-workflow` is absent and the stored `until_plan` is not in the new set, clear both `until_plan` and `until_workflow`. The incident and incident_plans tables are registered in `history_tables` (no_delete 0).

**Output examples:**

Fresh start:
```json
{"ok": true, "changed": true, "incident": {"started_at": "2026-10-14T21:10:00.000Z", "by": "3c9a…", "reason": "database migration in progress", "plans": ["plan-a", "plan-b"], "until_workflow": null}}
```

Update with changed set:
```json
{"ok": true, "changed": true, "incident": {"started_at": "2026-10-14T21:10:00.000Z", "by": "3c9a…", "reason": "database migration in progress", "plans": ["plan-c"], "until_workflow": null}}
```

Update with unchanged set and until_workflow:
```json
{"ok": true, "changed": false, "incident": {"started_at": "2026-10-14T21:10:00.000Z", "by": "3c9a…", "reason": "database migration in progress", "plans": ["plan-a", "plan-b"], "until_workflow": null}}
```

Fresh start with auto-end:
```json
{"ok": true, "changed": true, "incident": {"started_at": "2026-10-14T21:10:00.000Z", "by": "3c9a…", "reason": "fixing PR ci", "plans": ["plan-a"], "until_workflow": "plan-a/workflow-1"}}
```

**Idempotent:** yes; when the set and `until_workflow` are already as named, returns `changed: false` with the existing incident.

### 23.2 `incident end`

```
cpd incident end
```

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `CPD_SESSION` is set, valid and a Manager Session (role `manager`, not archived) | `manager_only` | 3 |

Effects: one transaction; delete the `incident` row and every row in `incident_plans`; append `incident-ended` Event with `data` including `cause: "manual"` and `by` the Manager Session id.

Output:

```json
{"ok": true, "changed": true, "incident": null}
```

Idempotent: yes; incident mode already off returns `"changed": false` with `incident: null`.

### 23.3 `incident status`

```
cpd incident status
```

No flags, no preconditions. Any caller may read.

Effects: none (one read transaction).

Output when off:

```json
{"ok": true, "on": false, "incident": null}
```

Output when on:

```json
{"ok": true, "on": true, "incident": {"started_at": "2026-10-14T21:10:00.000Z", "by": "3c9a…", "reason": "database migration in progress", "plans": ["plan-a", "plan-b"], "until_workflow": null}}
```

Output when on with auto-end:

```json
{"ok": true, "on": true, "incident": {"started_at": "2026-10-14T21:10:00.000Z", "by": "3c9a…", "reason": "fixing PR ci", "plans": ["plan-a"], "until_workflow": "plan-a/workflow-1"}}
```

Idempotent: yes; read-only.

## 23. `gate`

The Gate's leak check (hs-d519, docs/research/hygiene.md "The Gate leak check", Plan tests-mock pro-d35). Area `core/src/gate/` and `cli/`.

### 23.1 `gate finish`

```
cpd gate finish --run <id> --status <n>
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--run <id>` | the run id (`GATE_RUN`, 6 characters). Required |
| `--status <n>` | the exit status of the run's command. Required |

Run by `scripts/gate-run.sh` after its command, with `TMPDIR` the run's directory. It lists what the run left: the processes that have `GATE_RUN=<id>` or `TMPDIR=<run dir>` in their environment (`Spawn::with_env`, both keys, counted once; the match on `TMPDIR` is exact equality, so the machine-wide sccache server, whose `TMPDIR` is the parent directory and another run's directory are not leftovers; pro-d155), the tmux sockets named with the id (`/tmp/tmux-<uid>` and `$TMUX_TMPDIR/tmux-<uid>`), the paths under `$TMPDIR` and the lines of `$TMPDIR/tripwire.log`. A clean run prints nothing, removes the empty directory and exits with `--status`. Otherwise it prints `gate-run: FAIL: …` on stderr, `SIGKILL`s only the listed pids, removes only the listed sockets and the run's directory and exits with `--status` when that is not 0, else 64. Another run's id never matches. Not covered (pro-d155): a process whose cwd is inside the run's directory (the Spawn port has no cwd reader), a process whose `TMPDIR` is a directory inside the run's directory but not the run's directory itself and a process that cleared both `GATE_RUN` and `TMPDIR`. Like `slot`, it prints no JSON of its own; a usage error is the envelope on stderr. Idempotent: yes.

## 23. `prune`

```
cpd prune [--apply] [--drop <lead-branch>]... <repo>...
```

The successor of `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` (hs-d138, hs-d143, hs-d144): the clean-up of leftover worktrees whose work reached `origin/main`, which the Manager runs by hand after a Plan. The script shrinks to `exec cpd prune "$@"`. A User's command at a shell: no callers, not cockpit, not internal.

Flags and arguments:
- `--apply`: do the removals. Without it nothing changes (apart from `git fetch origin`) and the command prints what it would do.
- `--drop <lead-branch>`: repeatable. A worktree whose Lead Branch is one of the values is removed whether or not it is merged (rule `remove dropped`), unless it is protected.
- `<repo>...`: one or more repos, at least one. A missing repo argument or an unknown flag is a usage error, exit 2.

**Protected set.** Before anything else the command reads the store (no `cpd` child, no `jq`): for every Plan that is not done, the `lead_branch` of each Workflow whose status is not merged and `cpd/<plan>--<attempt id>` for each Attempt of a Job of such a Workflow. If the store cannot be read the command exits 2 before touching anything. `git` and `gh` (authenticated) go through the `Runner`.

**Rules.** Per worktree (the main one is skipped), the first rule that holds wins:

```
keep   active       the branch is protected (also with --drop)
keep   dirty        `git status --porcelain` is not empty (untracked files included)
remove dropped      the Lead Branch L is one of the --drop values (merged or not)
remove              HEAD is an ancestor of origin/main
remove              a merged PR P has a head branch equal to L, starting with `L/`, or,
                    for an Attempt branch of Plan `<plan>`, starting with `<plan>/` (A6);
                    HEAD is an ancestor of P's head commit and P reached main (its base
                    is main, or the base is the head of a merged PR that reached main,
                    at most 5 levels)
keep   not merged   otherwise
```

L is the branch itself, except an Attempt branch `cpd/<plan>--<attempt>` (it starts with `cpd/` and its remaining text has no `/`), whose L is `cpd/<plan>` (the text before the first `--`), so a key containing `--` is never cut. A detached HEAD has no L. Removal deletes the worktree and its local branch, never a remote branch.

Effects per repo: `git fetch origin`, `gh pr list --state merged --limit 500` of the repo's `origin` slug, `git worktree list --porcelain`; with `--apply`, for each removal `git worktree remove --force`, `git branch -D` (only when no other worktree has the branch) and finally `git worktree prune`.

Output: one line per worktree, `keep <path> (<branch|detached>): <reason>`, `remove <path> (<branch|detached>)` or `remove <path> (<branch>): dropped`, `failed <path>: <error>`, then `<repo>: <n> remove, <m> keep`.

Exit codes: 0 unless a command failed; a failure is printed and the run goes on, exit 1 at the end. 2: usage, or the protected set could not be read.

Tests: in-process on `Fakes` (`FakeRunner` git and gh routes, a temp store), the names of the old `cli/tests/tooling/prune_script.rs` kept: `a_failed_command_is_reported_and_exits_non_zero`, `keeps_what_cpd_still_runs`, `matches_a_legacy_lead_branch_renamed_locally`, `drop_removes_clean_unmerged_worktrees_of_the_named_lead_branch` and `a_failing_cpd_exits_2_and_removes_nothing` (now: an unreadable store); new test names: `prune_matches_a_parallel_attempt_to_a_merged_plan_slash_key_pr` and `prune_keeps_a_key_with_a_double_dash_whole`. The command is listed in `cli/tests/tooling/interface.rs`.
## 23. `tag` and `version`

The release plumbing of docs/versioning.md, in Rust over `Ports` (`Runner` for git, std `fs` for files). `scripts/tag-version.sh` and `scripts/sync-version.sh` are thin: each is `exec cpd tag` / `exec cpd version sync "$@"` and keeps only what must exist before cpd does. Their old exec tests are replaced by in-process tests on `Fakes` (a `FakeRunner` git route; a temp dir for the files) and `scripts/check-portable.sh` still guards the two scripts.

### 23.1 `cpd tag`

`cpd tag` takes no arguments. It tags the commit of `origin/main` that last changed the workspace version of `Cargo.toml` with the annotated tag `v<version>` and pushes it. It is idempotent: a rerun does nothing or finishes the push.

Steps, each a git call through the `Runner`: `fetch --quiet origin main`; `show origin/main:Cargo.toml` (the first `version = "` under `[workspace.package]` is `<version>`); `ls-remote --tags origin refs/tags/v<version>` (output means the tag exists: exit 0, nothing more); `log -1 --first-parent -G'^version = ' --format=%H origin/main -- Cargo.toml` (the commit `<sha>`, whose `Cargo.toml` must carry `<version>`); then, when the local tag is absent, `tag -a v<version> <sha> -m v<version>` (a local tag that exists must point at `<sha>`); then `push --quiet origin refs/tags/v<version>`. A failed push is accepted only when `ls-remote --tags origin refs/tags/v<version>^{}` already answers `<sha>`.

Output (stderr, one line each; the stream the script used):

| Case | Line | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| tagged | `tag-version: tagged v<version> on <sha>` | 0 |
| the remote has the tag | `tag-version: v<version> exists; nothing to do` | 0 |
| fetch fails | `tag-version: cannot fetch origin/main` | 1 |
| no `Cargo.toml` on origin/main | `tag-version: cannot read Cargo.toml on origin/main` | 1 |
| no workspace version | `tag-version: no workspace version in Cargo.toml on origin/main` | 1 |
| `ls-remote` fails | `tag-version: cannot list the tags of origin` | 1 |
| `log` fails | `tag-version: cannot find the commit that set v<version>` | 1 |
| `log` is empty | `tag-version: no commit on origin/main changed the version` | 1 |
| the commit has another version | `tag-version: commit <sha> has version '<at>', not <version>` | 1 |
| the local tag points elsewhere | `tag-version: local tag v<version> points at <have>, not <sha>` | 1 |
| `tag -a` fails | `tag-version: cannot create v<version>` | 1 |
| the push fails and the remote lacks `<sha>` | `tag-version: push of v<version> failed` | 1 |

Every failure is a `tag-version:` line; there is no JSON. `scripts/install-cpd.sh` runs it last and only warns on a failure (docs/implementing.md "Releases"). Callers: Lead (§2).

### 23.2 `cpd version sync [--print]`

cpd's version is `0.<PROTOCOL>.<migrations>`: `PROTOCOL` is the `pub const PROTOCOL: u32 = <n>;` of `core/src/events/kind.rs`, `<migrations>` the count of `.sql` files in `core/src/store/migrations/`.

- `cpd version sync --print` prints the version (for example `0.13.45`) on stdout and writes nothing. Exit 0.
- `cpd version sync` rewrites the first `version = "` under `[workspace.package]` of `Cargo.toml` and the `version` of the four workspace crates (`cpd`, `cpd-core`, `cpd-engine`, `cpd-tui`; never a package with a `source`) in `Cargo.lock`, then prints `sync-version: <version>`. Rerunning changes nothing.
- Any other argument is a usage error: `usage: cpd version sync [--print]`, exit 2.
- Failures print a `sync-version:` line on stderr and exit 1, writing nothing: `sync-version: no 'pub const PROTOCOL: u32 = <n>;' line in <kind.rs>.`, `sync-version: no .sql file in <dir>.`, `sync-version: no [workspace.package] in <Cargo.toml>.`, `sync-version: no version line under [workspace.package] in <Cargo.toml>.`

The test that fails when `Cargo.toml` differs from the derived version (docs/implementing.md "The version string") stays; `cpd version sync` is what fixes it.

## 23. `test`

The logic behind `scripts/test-changed` and `scripts/tests.sh`, which become thin (`exec cpd test …`). The selection and the name classification are pure over `git diff` and `cargo metadata` output, read through the `Runner`; the commands start `cargo` through `scripts/cargo.sh` (the bootstrap that builds cpd). Callers: Manager, Lead, Worker; not cockpit, not internal. The command tree is pinned by `cli/tests/tooling/interface.rs` and [docs/interface.md](interface.md) is regenerated.

### 23.1 `test changed`

```
cpd test changed [--dry-run] [<base>]
```

Runs the Rust tests the changed files can reach: exactly the selection of docs/implementing.md "The scoped loop" (changed files from the merge base of `<base>`, default `origin/main`, to the working tree and untracked files; crate and reverse dependencies as `-p`; `cli/tests/<area>/<module>.rs` as `--test <area> -E 'test(/^<module>::/)'`; root-level inputs as `--workspace`; docs, `pi/`, `web/` and other scripts select nothing). `--dry-run` prints the one command on stdout and runs nothing, exit 0. Nothing selected: `test-changed: nothing to run` on stderr, exit 0. Otherwise the exit status is nextest's. `scripts/test-changed [--dry-run] [<base>]` stays as `exec cpd test changed "$@"`.

### 23.2 `test run`

```
cpd test run <name>...
```

Runs the named tests and exits non-zero when any failed or did not run. A name is a pi name, `pi/test/<file>.test.ts::<title>` (the file's path, `::`, the exact `node:test` title; run with `node --test --test-name-pattern=<title> <file>` and refused when the title is in no `test(` or `it(` call of the file), a web name, `web/<file>.test.ts(x)::<title>` (the file's path, `::`, the exact vitest title; run through the web package's vitest, `pnpm --filter cpd-web-client exec vitest run --testNamePattern <title> <file>`), or a Rust name as nextest filters it (run with `nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast`). All run filtered, so none takes a test slot. Runs from the repo root, whatever the cwd. No name is a `usage` error.

### 23.3 `test list` and `test build`

```
cpd test list <name>
cpd test build
```

`list` exits 0 only when that one test exists: a pi name when its title is in a `test(` or `it(` call of its file (nothing is started), a web name when the web package's vitest answers it from collection mode (`pnpm --filter cpd-web-client exec vitest list <file> --json`: an existing test lists as found whether it passes or fails, and only an absent title or a file that does not collect is refused), a Rust name when `nextest list --workspace --message-format oneline <name>` prints a test. `build` runs `nextest run --workspace --no-run`, then `pnpm run typecheck` and, when `web/package.json` exists, typechecks the web client (it skips the web client when the file does not exist), and stops at the first failure; its status is that of the step that failed. Both run from the repo root, whatever the cwd.
`list` exits 0 only when that one test exists: a pi name when its title is in a `test(` or `it(` call of its file (nothing is started), a web name when the web package's vitest answers it (the same runner as `run`, `pnpm --filter cpd-web-client exec vitest run --testNamePattern <title> <file>`), a Rust name when `nextest list --workspace --message-format oneline <name>` prints a test. `build` runs `nextest run --workspace --no-run`, then `pnpm run typecheck` and, when `web/package.json` exists, typechecks the web client (it skips the web client when the file does not exist), and stops at the first failure; its status is that of the step that failed. Both run from the repo root, whatever the cwd.

### 23.4 The `scripts/tests.sh` contract

`.config/cpd.toml` `[tests]` keeps calling `scripts/tests.sh build`, `scripts/tests.sh list <test>` and `scripts/tests.sh run <tests>` (contract §7.7); that argument contract does not change. The script is only the bootstrap: it builds cpd with `scripts/cargo.sh build -p cpd` (a no-op when cpd is current, so a stale cpd never answers), takes the newest `target/*/cpd` and runs `exec cpd test <command> "$@"`; `scripts/test-changed` does the same for `cpd test changed`. A process's output reaches the caller when that process ends, not line by line: the runner returns it whole.

## 24. `mcp`

Attaches an MCP server to a Session (contract §6.11; pro-d2, pro-d8). The servers a machine may use are listed in the `[mcp]` table of its machine file, `$CPD_HOME/policy/host.toml` (contract §8.3 "MCP servers of the machine scope"; `cpd policy show`, §22.1). Dotfiles render that file per machine: its `[model]` table first, then the machine's `cpd.policy` text, which holds the `[mcp.servers.*]`. Area `core/` and `cli/`.

### 24.1 `mcp attach`

```
cpd mcp attach <name>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<name>` | a server of this machine's policy; it matches the server-name rule of contract §8.3 |

The caller's Session is selected as §1.3 says (`--session <id>`, else `CPD_SESSION`). Any role may run it.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `<name>` is given and matches the server-name rule (contract §8.3) | `usage` | 2 |
| a Session is selected | `session_required` | 2 |
| the Session exists | `session_not_found` | 4 |
| the machine file, `$CPD_HOME/policy/host.toml`, is valid TOML and its `[mcp]` table has known keys and types (contract §8.3 "MCP servers of the machine scope"; the file's other domains are the policy scope's and an invalid one is `policy_invalid` too); `details.file`, `details.key`; nothing is appended | `policy_invalid` | 1 |
| the machine file's `[mcp]` lists `<name>`; `details` `{name, machine, available}` (`machine` is the config key `machine`), `available` the sorted server names (an empty array when none); the message names the machine and lists what is available, or says none | `mcp_unknown` | 4 |

**Effects**, one transaction:
- **Event** `mcp-attached` (contract §5.2) addressed to the caller's Session (`session` set, with its `context` and `plan` when it has one), `data` `{name, server}`: `server` is the entry exactly as the machine policy gives it (pi's key names; a key left out is absent). `text`: `Server <name> attached to Session <id>.`
- Nothing else: no row, no file, no tmux call.

**The adapter** of that Session registers the server with pi (§15.3 `mcp-attached`, contract §5.3). The attach is for that Session only: never for another Session and never for a later one, and never done by default (pro-d2). cpd saves nothing of its own: the `mcp-attached` Events are the record (pro-d226). The adapter registers the Session's attached servers again at every start (§15.2 step 5a), so a reload or a restart keeps them. There is still no list and no detach command (pro-d8): `cpd policy show` lists what the machine allows. An attachment lasts as long as the Session (pro-d226): an archived Session runs no adapter, so it registers nothing, and when it runs again (`session unarchive`, then `session open` or `session resume`) its adapter replays; `session retier` changes the model, not the registrations; a fork has none, because its Events name the source Session. The server's `direct` tools appear in that Session as `mcp__<name>__<tool>` on a later model call of the same turn, not the call right after the attach (the adapter registers the server when it delivers the Event, then pi connects), and `tool_search` never finds the `direct` tools of a `hidden` server.

```json
{"ok": true, "attached": {"name": "slack", "session": "596d007f-…", "event": 48301}}
```

Idempotent in effect: running it again appends another Event and the adapter registers the same name again, which pi accepts as a replacement.

#### Signing in

A server that uses OAuth needs the User to sign in once on the machine (pro-d10): in that Session's pi with `/mcp login <name>`, or from a shell with `pi mcp login <name>`. The shell form works while the user-level `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` has an entry with the same name and URL, because pi keys the credential by server name and URL. Tokens live in pi's own `mcp-auth.json`; cpd never reads or writes one (hs-d107, pro-d4). A running Session uses new credentials on its next turn (pi's rule) and an attached server that needs a sign-in shows pi's own "requires sign-in" report.

## 29. `janitor`

```
cpd janitor
```

Removes the worktrees and branches of merged and cancelled Workflows (pro-d70, pro-d71) and of the ended Attempts of merged Jobs on live Workflows (contract §7.2). It also prunes (pro-d378) the `target` directory of the Lead of each idle Workflow in status `open`, `merged` or `cancelled`, and the `durable` directory of each archived or deleted Plan whose Attempts are all ended (§4a). One pass, then exits. It runs once every `watch.janitor_minutes` minutes (config key, default 60) via engine step E16 (§3.7) and may be run by hand. The User calls it, not Leads or Workers (§2).

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| (none) | `cpd janitor` takes no flags |

| Precondition or failure | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the store can be read (as `prune`, §27) | see §27 for store errors | 2 or 1 |

**Effects** (pro-d70, pro-d71, pro-d72; contract §7.1, §7.2):

The pass scans every Workflow of every Plan (archived included) whose status is `merged` or `cancelled` that still has on disk an Attempt worktree, its Lead worktree, or its aside leftover (a directory `<path>.removing` from a failed removal, §4 below). It also scans the Workflows whose status is `dispatch` or `open` for the ended Attempts that contract §7.2 'Ended Attempts of merged Jobs on a live Workflow' sweeps. It does not start a pass when another is running: the lock `locks/janitor.lock` (exclusive, non-blocking) is held by another; it prints `{"ok":true,"skipped":"running"}`, exits 0 and touches nothing.

For each such Workflow (a **Workflow to clean**), in this order:

1. **Idle check**: every Attempt of the Workflow's Jobs is `ended` and its driver lock is free (probed without creating the file, as `merged_workflows_to_clean` does today, contract §7.2). For a swept Attempt of a `dispatch` or `open` Workflow (contract §7.2 'Ended Attempts of merged Jobs on a live Workflow') the check is that Attempt's (`ended`, lock free), not the Workflow's. If not, the outcome is `pending`, nothing is touched, no Event for this Workflow in this pass.
2. **Kill Attempt windows**: `tmux kill-pane` on every pane of this machine's Attempt windows of the Workflow's Jobs (as today, `core/src/pr/poll.rs` `clean_up`).
3. **Discard parallel Attempt worktrees**: per Attempt of the Workflow's Jobs whose worktree exists on disk (a linear Attempt runs in the Lead worktree): removed as contract §7.2 'Removal' says, forced: rename aside, prune, branch -D, delete the aside; an Attempt's leftover `<path>.removing` counts as on disk.
4. **Rule S** on the Lead worktree (contract §7.4: fetch, merge base): its local branch stays up to date for the dirty and unpushed check (§4 below).
5. **Remove the Lead worktree** (§4 below).

**§4. Removal of a Lead worktree** (pro-d72; refusals keep it whole or mark it for retry):

When the Lead worktree is dirty (output of `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain` not empty, untracked files included) or unpushed (`git rev-list --no-merges HEAD --not --remotes=origin` not empty, **unless** `HEAD` is the pull request's recorded head commit or an ancestor of it, as the poll checks today with `headRefOid`; a squash-merged PR whose branch GitHub deleted is cleaned up; contract §7.2 "The recorded head and the unpushed rule"), the outcome is `kept` with the reason and nothing is touched. Otherwise, in this order, each step idempotent (a stop at any point leaves the worktree whole or marked for retry):

(a) **Rename**: `<path>` to `<path>.removing` (atomic rename, a sibling in the same directory; Workflow keys have no dot, so no collision; a failing rename is `kept` with the error as reason).
(b) **Prune**: `git worktree prune` (the registered directory is gone, so git drops it).
(c) **Delete branch**: `git branch -D <lead branch>` when it exists.
(d) **Delete directory**: `std::fs::remove_dir_all(<path>.removing)`.

A stop (kill, crash, failing call) at (a) leaves the worktree whole and untouched. A stop at (b), (c) or (d) leaves the worktree gone (`<path>` absent) with `<path>.removing` as the marker (the directory is present from the rename, empty of tracked files). A pass that finds `<path>` absent and `<path>.removing` present retries (b), (c), (d) again; every step is idempotent. A failure in (b), (c) or (d) is outcome `failed`: the path is gone and later passes retry (a contract violation: the marker stays; the worktree can never be recovered). Renamed but uncleaned paths show in the log (§5).

**§4a. Prune of `target` and `durable`** (pro-d378; contract §3.7 E16 "Prune"). It runs first in the pass, before the Workflow clean-up of §3, so a Lead's `target` is reported even when that clean-up then removes the whole Lead. Both steps remove a whole directory and are idempotent: a missing directory is no entry. Neither step raises an Event.

- **(T) Lead `target`**: for each Workflow of any Plan (archived included) in status `open`, `merged` or `cancelled` that has no Job of its Plan with `workflow` equal to its key in status `queued` or `running`, and no Attempt of those Jobs in status `starting`, `running` or `merging`: remove `<lead_worktree>/target` if it exists. `<lead_worktree>` is the Workflow's `lead_worktree`, or for a `cancelled` Workflow (column null) the path `workflow_lead_worktree_path` derives. The entry's `workflow` is the key. The Lead worktree, its Lead Branch, its sources and every Attempt worktree stay. A `cancelled` Workflow whose stored pull request is `open` (A8) is included: pro-d378 supersedes A8 for `target` only.
- **(D) `durable`**: for each Plan with `archived_at` or `deleted_at` not null and no Attempt in a status other than `ended`: remove `run/<plan>/durable` (`CpdHome::durable_dir`) if it exists. The entry's `workflow` is `null`. Nothing else under `run/<plan>` is removed.

A Job in any other status (`draft`, `merged`, `failed`, `cancelled`) and an `ended` Attempt do not block a removal. A removal that fails is outcome `failed`; the pass goes on with the next entry.

**§5. Output and Log**:

One JSON value: `{"ok":true,"outcomes":[...],"pruned":[...]}` or `{"ok":false,"error":{...}}` (store unreadable only). `pruned` (§4a) has one entry per Prune removal that found its directory, in the order the steps ran, and is `[]` when nothing was pruned. Each `pruned` entry is `{"plan", "workflow", "path", "outcome", "reason"}`: `path` is the absolute path; `workflow` is the key for (T) and `null` for (D); `outcome` is `pruned` (the directory was removed whole) or `failed` (it was not; the next pass tries again); `reason` is present only for `failed`. The output `{"ok":true,"skipped":"running"}` has no `pruned` key. `outcomes` is one entry per pending Workflow path scanned (paths of Attempt worktrees, Lead worktrees and aside leftovers), in the order they were found. Each entry:

```json
{"plan": "pay-4521", "workflow": "api", "status": "cancelled", "path": "/home/clayton/projects/pay.pay-4521.api", "outcome": "removed", "reason": null}
```

or, when not removed:

```json
{"plan": "pay-4521", "workflow": "api", "status": "merged", "path": "/home/clayton/projects/pay.api", "outcome": "kept", "reason": "unpushed"}
```

or:

```json
{"plan": "pay-4521", "workflow": "api", "status": "merged", "path": "/home/clayton/projects/pay.api.removing", "outcome": "failed", "reason": "permission denied"}
```

and, for the Prune (§4a):

```json
{"plan": "pay-4521", "workflow": "api", "path": "/home/clayton/projects/pay.api/target", "outcome": "pruned"}
{"plan": "pay-4521", "workflow": null, "path": "/home/clayton/.cpd/run/pay-4521/durable", "outcome": "failed", "reason": "permission denied"}
```

`status` is `cancelled`, `merged`, `dispatch` or `open` (the last two for an Attempt swept under contract §7.2 'Ended Attempts of merged Jobs on a live Workflow'), read from the Workflow's status in the store. `outcome` is one of: `removed` (the path was deleted whole), `kept` (the path remains untouched, worktree dirty or unpushed), `pending` (the Workflow is not idle yet), or `failed` (the path was renamed but not fully deleted; the next pass retries). `reason` is present only for `kept` and `failed` (the dirty/unpushed rule, git's stderr tail, or a file error message); it is a short string suitable for an Event.

The pass writes a log to `run/janitor.log`, appended (new lines only, one per pass, format `<timestamp> <pass id> <status>` where `<status>` is `ok`, `locked`, or an error; the file is not parsed, so its format may change). Each `pruned` entry adds one line in the same format, before the pass's own line, where `<pass id>` is the process id and `<status>` is `prune pruned plan=<plan> workflow=<key or -> path=<path>`, or `prune failed plan=<plan> workflow=<key or -> path=<path> reason=<reason>` for `failed`. The engine's watch.log reads events from that file (§12 "The watch loop").

**§6. Events**:

One `error` Event `cleanup_failed` per `kept` or `failed` path, only from the first pass that sees it with no `cleanup_failed` Event of that Workflow yet (later passes retry silently, as `fresh` does today for a cancelled Workflow; a merged Workflow now works the same way). Never for `pending` or `removed` paths. Prune (§4a) raises no Event, `failed` included. **Text** (pro-d72):

- `kept`: `The clean-up of the <status> Workflow <workflow> of Plan <plan> kept <path> untouched: <reason>`
- `failed` (after rename at step (a) in §4): `The clean-up of the <status> Workflow <workflow> of Plan <plan> removed <path>, but not everything: <reason>. The next janitor pass retries.`
- `failed` (Attempt worktree discard at step 3 in Effects): `The clean-up of the <status> Workflow <workflow> of Plan <plan> did not remove <path>: <reason>. The next janitor pass retries.`

Each Event also has `details`: `{plan, workflow, status, outcome, path, reason}`.

**§7. Exit codes**:

- `0` on success (outcomes list may be empty or contain `pending`, `kept`, `failed` and `removed`; a `failed` `pruned` entry does not change it).
- `2` when the store cannot be read (as `prune`, §27: `store_too_new`, `migration_failed`, `migration_changed`, `migration_order`).
- `1` for other store errors (as `prune`, §27: `store_failed`, `store_tampered`).
- `1` when a git or tmux call fails unexpectedly (details `{argv, exit, stderr}`); the pass continues for the next Workflow.

**Tests**: `janitor_pass_removes_cancelled_and_merged_pr_worktrees_and_branches`, `janitor_pass_finishes_what_a_killed_pass_left`, `janitor_command_is_in_the_help_tree`, `janitor_pass_prunes_idle_lead_targets`, `janitor_pass_keeps_busy_lead_targets`, `janitor_pass_prunes_durable_of_archived_and_deleted_plans`, `janitor_pass_keeps_durable_while_an_attempt_is_not_ended`, `janitor_pass_reports_a_failed_prune_and_goes_on`, `janitor_pass_prune_is_idempotent_and_logs_each_entry`.

Idempotent: yes; rerunning with nothing to clean prints `ok` with an empty outcomes list and an empty `pruned` list, and writes nothing (a Prune whose directory is gone is no entry, §4a); rerunning after a `kept` or `failed` path retries (may succeed on rerun if the worktree was cleaned by hand; `kept` paths remain `kept`, as they are not idle yet or always dirty).

## 30. `resource`

Resources with slots, declared at host, owner or repo level (contract §8.3 "The `resources` domain", §1.4 "The resource locks and the holder record", §3.4 "Resources of a Job" and "Tenancy"; Plan `repo-lock`). Both commands derive the repo from the **current directory**: the git worktree that contains it, its `origin` keyed as `workflow add` does (`repo_unkeyed`, exit 1, when it cannot), then that repo's policy (whose visible resources are the union of contract §8.3) (the owner and policy refusals of any resolve: `owner_unconfirmed`, `policy_invalid`). A directory outside a git worktree is `usage` (exit 2). The files are in contract §1.4; no command releases another tenant's slot.

### 30.1 `resource list`

```
cpd resource list
```

Effects: none. Output: `repo` (`<owner>/<name>`) and `resources`, one entry per visible resource sorted by name (`[]` when none is declared): `name`; `scope` (`host`, `owner` or `repo`, the declaring level, contract §8.3); `slots`; `free`, the free slots of the pool (contract §1.4: `slots` minus the Job tenants minus the held command slots, never below 0); and `holders`, an array of the holders only, free slots have no entry: first one `{slot, holder}` per held command slot in slot order, `holder` the `command` record of contract §1.4 (each slot read with the shared try-lock probe; a stale slot, a `command` record whose pid is dead under contract §1.4, is free, has no entry, and its file is removed by the probe), then one `{slot: null, holder}` per Job tenant by `jobs.seq`, `holder` the derived shape `{by:"attempt", plan, job, attempt, at}` of the Job's latest Attempt, a Job holder having no slot number. The list includes the built-in `workers` (contract §8.3): `scope` `host`, `slots` = `concurrency` and `holders` one `{slot: null, holder}` per tenant Job (a `failed` Job included and more than `slots` while an urgent Job holds the slot beyond).

```json
{"ok": true, "repo": "clayton-duarte/card-dashboard", "resources": [
  {"name": "e2e-port", "scope": "repo", "slots": 1, "free": 0, "holders": [{"slot": 1, "holder": {"by": "command", "pid": 4242, "command": "npm run dev", "session": "9f1c…", "attempt": null, "at": "2026-10-26T21:40:00.000Z"}}]},
  {"name": "shared-port", "scope": "host", "slots": 2, "free": 1, "holders": [{"slot": null, "holder": {"by": "attempt", "plan": "card-dash", "job": "e2e-1", "attempt": "e2e-1-a1", "at": "2026-10-26T21:41:00.000Z"}}]}]}
```

Idempotent: yes; it only reads.

### 30.2 `resource run`

```
cpd resource run <name> [--wait <minutes>] -- <command> [<arg>...]
```

Takes a slot of the resource, then runs the command holding it. It decides the pool's free slots under the pool's guard, the same count the starter uses (contract §1.4 "The free slots of a pool"), so a command and a Job's start cannot both take the last slot. The resource is the one a human takes (the User, or a Lead running a command the User asked for, §15.20).

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<name>` | a resource visible to the repo: declared by the host, owner or repo policy; `workers` is reserved and refused `usage` (exit 2) |
| `--wait <minutes>` | a positive integer; absent means 0. Tries again every second until the minutes have passed, by the Ports' clock (so tests never sleep) |
| `-- <command> [<arg>...]` | the command and its arguments, run from the current directory with the current environment, never through a shell |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| a command follows `--`; `--wait` is a positive integer | `usage` | 2 |
| the directory is in a git worktree whose `origin` can be keyed | `repo_unkeyed` | 1 |
| the repo's policy resolves | `owner_unconfirmed`, `policy_invalid`, … | 1 |
| `<name>` is declared; `details` `{resource, repo, declared, file}` | `resource_undeclared` | 3 |
| the pool has a free slot (contract §1.4: `slots` minus the Job tenants minus the held command slots), taking under the guard the lowest free slot file by a non-blocking exclusive try-lock (a stale slot file, contract §1.4, is removed and taken afresh in its place), tried again every second for `--wait` minutes; `details` `{resource, repo, holders, waited_minutes}` (`holders` the holders of the pool, as in `resource list`; `waited_minutes` the minutes given, 0 when absent). The command never starts | `resource_busy` | 3 |
| the command can be executed (after the lock is held; the process and the lock are gone together) | `spawn_failed` | 1 |

Effects: after it holds a slot it writes the command holder record (contract §1.4: `pid` its own process id, `command` the argv joined by single spaces, `session` from `CPD_SESSION` and `attempt` from `CPD_ATTEMPT`, null when unset), then **replaces itself with the command** (`exec`):

- the command keeps the process id (the record's `pid`), the stdio and the signals;
- it inherits the slot file's lock descriptor, so the slot stays held for as long as the command or any descendant that keeps the descriptor lives, which is what a dev server on a port needs;
- a signal to the process or to its group (`kill -TERM -- -<pgid>`) stops both the command and the hold;
- the command's output is the output: `run` prints no JSON value once it has exec-ed (a command that owns its terminal, contract §1.2) and the exit status is the command's;
- if the exec fails, `spawn_failed` (exit 1) and the lock goes with the process.

**Re-entrant for an Attempt whose Job is a tenant of the pool.** When `CPD_ATTEMPT` is set and the Job of that Attempt is a tenant of the pool (contract §3.4 "Tenancy"), `run` takes nothing more and execs the command at once: the Job already holds a slot and must not wait on itself or take a second.

**Hooks.** A repo may write `cpd resource run <name> --` in a hook command (contract §7.3); hooks run without `CPD_*` variables, so `CPD_HOME` is the default. The Gate and the hooks take no resource by themselves.

Idempotent: no. A run while every slot is held is `resource_busy`.

## 31. `review`

Reviews on GitHub, posted by cpd commands (§2.2; pro-d107, pro-d108, pro-d110, pro-d169).

### 31.1 `review submit`

```
cpd review submit --pr <url | owner/repo#n> --head <sha> --event APPROVE|REQUEST_CHANGES --input <review.json> [--slack <channel>/<ts>]
```

Posts a GitHub review and, with `--slack`, queues a reaction to a Slack message (the same mechanism as `pr merge`, §21.9); and, with `--event APPROVE`, when `CPD_PLAN` names a `codereview` Plan that is not done, finishes that Plan; with `--event REQUEST_CHANGES` it sets `changes_requested_at` on a `grounding` one and leaves it open (below; FR10, pro-d416). **Callers:** the Lead, the Manager; not the cockpit or other agent roles. It takes a pull request URL or PullRef form, like `pr merge` (§9.10).

Steps:

1. Validate arguments: `--head <sha>` is required (a missing flag is `usage`, exit 2) and must be exactly 40 ASCII hex digits, either case: not 39 or 41, not empty, no `0x` prefix, no whitespace, no branch name, no abbreviated sha. cpd lowercases it once here; every later use (the head check, the POST's `commit_id`, `details.expected`, `review.commit_id`) is that lowercase value. `--event` must be exactly `APPROVE` or `REQUEST_CHANGES`. `--input` is a file holding the review body as a JSON object (GitHub's REST `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/reviews` body), containing `body` (optional string) and `comments[]` (optional array of `{path, line, side, body}`); it has no `commit_id` key, the head is `--head`. When a file is unreadable, not JSON, carries its own `event` key or its own `commit_id` key, or is not an object, refuse `usage` (exit 2). With `--slack`, `<channel>/<ts>` must match the pattern `^C[A-Z0-9]{8,}$/^[0-9]{10}\.[0-9]{6}$` or refuse `usage` (exit 2). Every refusal of this step happens before any `gh` call, with nothing queued.
2. Read the pull request's current head with one `gh` call, a GET: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>` (argv exactly `api` and `repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>`: no `--method`, no `--jq`, no stdin; `<owner>/<repo>` and `<n>` come from `--pr`, so a URL and `owner/repo#n` name the same call). Its stdout is the pull request's JSON object; its `head.sha` string is the current head, lowercased. A non-zero exit, a signal, a timeout, stdout that is not JSON, or an object without a string `head.sha` is `gh_failed` (exit 1). If the current head is not `--head`, refuse `head_moved` (exit 3) with `details` `{pr, expected, actual}` (`pr` is `<owner>/<repo>#<n>` even when `--pr` was a URL; `expected` is `--head` and `actual` the current head, both lowercase) and a message that names both SHAs. Both refusals post nothing and queue nothing; the GET is the only `gh` call made.
3. Post the review to GitHub: `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>/reviews --input -`, with the review JSON on stdin: the input object, with `"event"` added from `--event` and `"commit_id"` set to the lowercase `--head`, so GitHub pins the review to that commit even when a push lands after step 2. GitHub's failures are relayed as `gh_failed` (exit 1, `details.stderr` the tail). cpd checks no content: no refusal for failed checks, out-of-diff comments, or empty body (GitHub enforces). An answer without `id` or `html_url` is `gh_failed` with message "review may have been posted; check the pull request".
4. On success, one store transaction, opened when `--slack` is given or when `CPD_PLAN` parses as a Plan id (nothing else opens it). In it: with `--slack`, it calls `cpd_core::pr::reactions::queue(tx, channel, ts, emoji)` with emoji `github-check-mark` for APPROVE, `github-changes-requested` for REQUEST_CHANGES; and it finishes the caller's Plan when the rule below says so. A store failure after GitHub accepted is that error with `details.review` added: the review stands.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--head` is present and is exactly 40 hex digits, either case | `usage` | 2 |
| `--event` is exactly `APPROVE` or `REQUEST_CHANGES` | `usage` | 2 |
| `--input` file is readable, is JSON, is an object and has neither an `event` key nor a `commit_id` key | `usage` | 2 |
| `--slack`, if present, matches `^C[A-Z0-9]{8,}$/^[0-9]{10}\.[0-9]{6}$` | `usage` | 2 |
| the pull request's current head can be read (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>`, a GET; its `head.sha` is a string) | `gh_failed` | 1 |
| the current head is `--head` (`details` `{pr, expected, actual}`) | `head_moved` | 3 |
| the review is posted; `details` has `stderr`, the `id` and `html_url` on success | `gh_failed` | 1 |

Effects:

- Posts a GitHub review on the pull request with the given event, body and `commit_id`. The review is pinned to `commit_id`, so a push after the head read still leaves the review on the reviewed commit.
- If `--slack` is provided, queues a reaction to the Slack message in the store after the review is posted (§21.9).
- The review verdict does not remove the Claim's :eyes: (A5).

**The caller's Plan** (FR10, C2; contract §3.1 `grounding → done`). The review Lead runs `review submit` in its pane, where `CPD_PLAN` names its Plan (§6.5). With `--event APPROVE`, when `CPD_PLAN` parses as a Plan id and that Plan exists with `context` `codereview`, `deleted_at` null and `phase` other than `done`, the transaction of step 4 finishes it: `phase` = `done`, `locked_at` = `done_at` = the transaction's time, and one **Event** `plan-done` (Plan `<id>`, Context `codereview`) with `text` `Plan <id> is done: review submitted.` and `data` `{"workflows": [], "turn": false}`. The adapter delivers that Event as no message and no turn (contract §5.3), so the review Lead is not woken after it has submitted. Only a `grounding` Plan takes this transition: the trigger `plans_phase` refuses every other phase (contract §4.4), so a `codereview` Plan in another phase is not finished, and the refusal is a store failure after GitHub accepted: the review stands (`details.review`, step 4). Nothing is written for the Plan when `CPD_PLAN` is unset or does not parse, names no Plan, names a Plan of another Context, a deleted Plan, or a Plan that is already `done`; the review still succeeds.

**REQUEST_CHANGES** (pro-d416; codereview pro-d8 D1 and D2). With `--event REQUEST_CHANGES`, the same transaction, when `CPD_PLAN` parses as a Plan id and names a `codereview` Plan with `deleted_at` null and `phase` `grounding`, sets that Plan's `changes_requested_at` to the transaction's time. Nothing else is written for the Plan: it stays in `grounding`, with `locked_at` and `done_at` as they were, and no `plan-done` Event is written, so its Lead is not finished. Its idle Lead is put to sleep once the quiet time has passed (contract §3.7 E13). For any other phase, another Context, a deleted Plan or a `CPD_PLAN` that does not parse, nothing is written; the review still succeeds. The next claim of the item reuses this Plan and clears `changes_requested_at` (§21.7).

A refused submit (`usage`, `gh_failed`, `head_moved`) writes nothing, so the Plan stays as it was. The done guard of contract §3.1 does not apply to this transition: a `codereview` Plan has no Workflow, its explore Jobs do not hold it, and `pr/review.rs` `finish_plan` is left unchanged.

Output:

```json
{"ok": true, "review": {"id": 123456, "url": "https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>#pullrequestreview-123456", "state": "APPROVED", "commit_id": "<head>"}, "reaction": null}
```

With `--slack`:

```json
{"ok": true, "review": {"id": 123456, "url": "https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>#pullrequestreview-123456", "state": "APPROVED", "commit_id": "<head>"}, "reaction": {"channel": "C123ABC45", "ts": "1234567890.123456", "emoji": "github-check-mark", "already": false}}
```

**Not idempotent** (A4): a rerun posts a second review. The queue row (with `--slack`) is unique per `channel+ts+emoji`, so the same reaction is queued once and placed once by the engine's slack-react step (§21.9).

**What it does not do** (pro-d108, pro-d169): cpd checks one thing about the pull request, its head (pro-d169), no key of the Plan, the Context or a Workflow (FR10), and no content of the review. No refusal for failed or pending checks, comments outside the diff, an empty body, or any other condition. GitHub's own refusal is relayed. Review skill rules (FR4) and COMMENT reviews are out of scope.

See §21.9 for the queue and the reaction step.

## 32. `swr`

The SWR cache and outbox (`docs/architecture/swr.md`; contract §4.4 "The SWR tables", §4.7). Every command prints one JSON value. The commands read the `swr_*` tables and never reach upstream (`swr.md` §13): a read returns what SWR holds, and `invalidate` asks the engine to fetch. The classifier's badge and health commands (§32.7 to §32.9; `docs/architecture/swr-classifier.md`) write cache rows, not upstream. Times are the stored text. Every command is read-only except `invalidate`, `badge put` and `health record`.

### 32.1 `swr list`

```
cpd swr list [--system <system>]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--system <system>` | only the queries of this datasource: `github`, `slack`, `jira`, `models` or `classifier`. Absent means every system |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--system`, when given, is one of the five names above | `usage` | 2 |

Effects: none. Output: `queries`, one entry per row of `swr_queries` in key order, each `{key, system, status, fetched_at, stale_after, invalidated, error_count, last_error, inactive_at, age_seconds}`. `age_seconds` is the time since `fetched_at` in whole seconds, by the command's clock, and `null` when `fetched_at` is null. `invalidated` is a boolean. An empty store prints `queries: []`.

```json
{"ok": true, "queries": [
  {"key": "github:pr:owner/repo#12", "system": "github", "status": "success", "fetched_at": "2026-11-06T15:50:00.000Z", "stale_after": "2026-11-06T15:50:05.000Z", "invalidated": false, "error_count": 0, "last_error": null, "inactive_at": null, "age_seconds": 42}
]}
```

Idempotent: yes; it only reads.

### 32.2 `swr show`

```
cpd swr show <key>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<key>` | a query key, `<system>:<kind>:<id>` (swr.md §4) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `<key>` has the form `<system>:<kind>:<id>` (three non-empty parts) | `usage` | 2 |
| a row of `swr_queries` has the key; `details` `{key}` | `query_not_found` | 4 |

Effects: none. Output: `query`, the row as `list` shows it (§32.1 fields), and `mutations`, the active mutations of the key in `submitted_at` order (the overlay's input, swr.md §9), each `{id, op_kind, status, patch}` with `patch` the parsed `patch_json` or `null`.

```json
{"ok": true, "query": {"key": "github:pr:owner/repo#12", "system": "github", "status": "success", "fetched_at": "2026-11-06T15:50:00.000Z", "stale_after": null, "invalidated": false, "error_count": 0, "last_error": null, "inactive_at": null, "age_seconds": 42}, "mutations": [
  {"id": 7, "op_kind": "merge", "status": "revalidating", "patch": {"state": "merged"}}
]}
```

Idempotent: yes; it only reads.

### 32.3 `swr invalidate`

```
cpd swr invalidate <key>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<key>` | a query key, as `show` (§32.2) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `<key>` has the form `<system>:<kind>:<id>` | `usage` | 2 |
| a row of `swr_queries` has the key; `details` `{key}` | `query_not_found` | 4 |
| the write transaction opens within `store_busy_ms` | `store_busy` | 5 |

Effects: one write transaction sets `swr_queries.invalidated` to 1 for the key (`cache::invalidate`, swr.md §6). No row of any other table changes and no Event is appended. After the transaction the engine is woken (`engine/src/watch/wake.rs`), so E24 fetches the key at once instead of at its next tick (swr.md §12). The command does not fetch and does not wait for the fetch.

Output:

```json
{"ok": true, "key": "github:pr:owner/repo#12", "invalidated": true, "already": false}
```

`already` is true when the flag was already 1. Idempotent: yes; a rerun writes nothing and reports `already` true.

### 32.4 `swr endpoints`

```
cpd swr endpoints
```

Effects: none. Output: `endpoints`, one entry per endpoint in the order `github`, `slack`, `jira`, `ollama.lab`, `bifrost`, each `{endpoint, status, fetch_status, paused_until, failing_since, reported_at, last_error, error_count, last_ok_at, rate_remaining, rate_reset_at}` (the columns of `swr_endpoints`, swr.md §3.2). An endpoint with no row yet reports the column defaults: `status` `pending`, `fetch_status` `idle`, `error_count` 0 and every other field `null`.

```json
{"ok": true, "endpoints": [
  {"endpoint": "github", "status": "success", "fetch_status": "paused", "paused_until": "2026-11-06T16:00:00.000Z", "failing_since": null, "reported_at": null, "last_error": null, "error_count": 0, "last_ok_at": "2026-11-06T15:50:00.000Z", "rate_remaining": 0, "rate_reset_at": "2026-11-06T16:00:00.000Z"},
  {"endpoint": "slack", "status": "pending", "fetch_status": "idle", "paused_until": null, "failing_since": null, "reported_at": null, "last_error": null, "error_count": 0, "last_ok_at": null, "rate_remaining": null, "rate_reset_at": null}
]}
```

Idempotent: yes; it only reads.

### 32.5 `swr mutation show`

```
cpd swr mutation show <id>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | a mutation id, a positive integer (the `mutation_id` a write returns) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `<id>` is a positive integer | `usage` | 2 |
| a row of `swr_mutations` has the id; `details` `{id}` | `mutation_not_found` | 4 |

Effects: none. Output: `mutation`, the row with `vars` and `patch` parsed from `vars_json` and `patch_json` (`patch` `null` when the column is NULL) and `context` parsed from `context_json` (`null` when NULL): `{id, system, target_key, op_kind, status, vars, patch, context, submitted_at, started_at, completed_at, next_attempt_at, attempt_count, error}`.

```json
{"ok": true, "mutation": {"id": 7, "system": "github", "target_key": "github:pr:owner/repo#12", "op_kind": "merge", "status": "revalidating", "vars": {"method": "squash"}, "patch": {"state": "merged"}, "context": {"plan": "p1", "workflow": "w1"}, "submitted_at": "2026-11-06T15:48:00.000Z", "started_at": "2026-11-06T15:48:02.000Z", "completed_at": "2026-11-06T15:48:09.000Z", "next_attempt_at": null, "attempt_count": 1, "error": null}}
```

Idempotent: yes; it only reads.

### 32.6 `swr mutation list`

```
cpd swr mutation list [--status <status>]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--status <status>` | only the mutations in this status: `pending`, `in_flight`, `revalidating`, `done`, `failed` or `superseded` |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--status`, when given, is one of the six names above | `usage` | 2 |

Effects: none. Output: `mutations`, every row of `swr_mutations` (of the status, if given) in `id` order, each in the shape of `mutation show` (§32.5). `done` and `superseded` rows are listed too: no command deletes a mutation. An empty result prints `mutations: []`.

Idempotent: yes; it only reads.

### 32.7 `swr badge get`

```
cpd swr badge get <session_id>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<session_id>` | the Session whose Lead completion badge is read (a non-empty text) |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `<session_id>` is non-empty | `usage` | 2 |

Effects: none. A Session with no row is not an error. Output: `badge`, `null` when the Session has no row, otherwise `{session_id, entry_id, label, score, text, tone, others, synced_at}`. `others` is present only when the row has it (`swr-classifier.md` §2.3), so the shape matches the optional `others?` of the web's `Completion`.

```json
{"ok": true, "badge": {"session_id": "s-1", "entry_id": "e-41", "label": "open_work", "score": 62, "text": "Open work · 62%", "tone": "decision", "others": [{"label": "unanswered_ask", "score": 20}], "synced_at": "2026-11-06T15:50:00.000Z"}}
```

Idempotent: yes; it only reads.

### 32.8 `swr badge put`

```
cpd swr badge put <session_id> --entry <id> --label <label> --score <n> --text <text> --tone <tone> [--others <json>]
```

| Argument or flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<session_id>` | the Session the badge is about (a non-empty text) |
| `--entry <id>` | the Session's last transcript item id at classify time (non-empty text); the freshness key |
| `--label <label>` | one of `safe_to_archive`, `unanswered_ask`, `open_work`, `unrecorded_decision`, `unescalated_issue` |
| `--score <n>` | an integer from 0 to 100 |
| `--text <text>` | the badge's text (non-empty), as the web shows it |
| `--tone <tone>` | `done`, `decision` or `blocked` |
| `--others <json>` | optional: a non-empty JSON array of `{"label", "score"}` (labels as `--label`, scores as `--score`); absent when the completion has no other scores |

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| every required flag is given, and each value is of its form above | `usage` | 2 |
| `--others`, when given, is not `[]` | `usage` | 2 |
| the write transaction, when one is needed, opens within `store_busy_ms` | `store_busy` | 5 |

Effects: the values are compared with the row of `<session_id>`. When they are equal (`entry_id`, `label`, `score`, `text`, `tone` and `others_json`, the canonical JSON of `--others` or NULL), no write transaction opens and the stored `synced_at` stays. When they differ, one write transaction replaces the row, sets `synced_at` to the command's time and `inactive_at` to NULL. No Event is appended, and no outbox row is written. Output: `{session_id, entry_id, changed, synced_at}`, `changed` true when a write was made.

```json
{"ok": true, "session_id": "s-1", "entry_id": "e-41", "changed": true, "synced_at": "2026-11-06T15:50:00.000Z"}
```

Idempotent: yes; a rerun with the same values writes nothing and reports `changed` false.

### 32.9 `swr health record`

```
cpd swr health record <system> <endpoint> <ok|error> [--text <text>]
```

| Argument or flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<system>` | the datasource the call is for: `github`, `slack`, `jira` or `classifier` |
| `<endpoint>` | the endpoint, one of the pairs below |
| `ok` | the endpoint answered (any answer, an answer, or an HTTP refusal) |
| `error` | the endpoint could not be reached (connect, DNS, timeout, deadline) |
| `--text <text>` | the failure text: required with `error` (non-empty), refused with `ok` |

The accepted pairs are `github` with `github`, `slack` with `slack`, `jira` with `jira`, and `classifier` with `ollama.lab` or `bifrost` (`swr-classifier.md` §5).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `<system>`, `<endpoint>` form an accepted pair | `usage` | 2 |
| `ok` or `error` is given; `--text` is given with `error` and not with `ok` | `usage` | 2 |
| the write transaction opens within `store_busy_ms` | `store_busy` | 5 |

Effects: one write transaction on the row of `<endpoint>` in `swr_endpoints`. `ok` clears the outage (`failing_since`, `reported_at`, `last_error`), sets `error_count` to 0, `last_ok_at` to the command's time and `status` to `success`; on a row already in that state it writes nothing. `error` records one failure: the first one of an outage sets `failing_since`, every one adds 1 to `error_count` and sets `last_error`. No Event is appended by this command: the outage's `error` Event is raised by the engine after 10 minutes (E24, contract §4.7). Output: `{system, endpoint, status, error_count, failing_since}`.

```json
{"ok": true, "system": "classifier", "endpoint": "ollama.lab", "status": "error", "error_count": 3, "failing_since": "2026-11-06T15:44:00.000Z"}
```

Idempotent: `ok` yes; `error` no, each call counts one failure.

## 33. `protocol`

The bug record (air-d104; contract §2.2 "Bug record"): the bug report protocol (pro-d204) as commands, not prose. One row per bug in the `bug_records` table. The commands append no Event and add no Event kind: the engine tick's breach check (contract §3.7 E25) owns the protocol's events — the owner wake, the `protocol-breach` Event (contract §5.2; its `protocol` is `bug report`, its `source` `E25`) and the User's Inbox item (contract §2.2 "Inbox item", kind `bug`) — the adapter ignores the kind (§15.3), and the kind raises the protocol number to 26 (contract §5.2: the guards' Ledger leg runs `session report` with new flags, §10.18). **Callers:** `report`, `mitigate` and `close` are the Lead's and the Manager's; a Worker that finds or is handed a bug reports it to its Lead, and the commands refuse it `not_a_lead` (exit 3, nothing written) when `CPD_ATTEMPT` is set and non-empty, as `job addendum` is. `list` and `show` are every agent's, read-only. **'Mitigation'** (air-d103): an agent-applied stopgap that removes or contains the User's symptom now; handing the User manual steps is not a mitigation unless the User chooses it. **Ownership** (air-d104): the Manager owns a cross-Plan bug (`plan` null), a Plan's Lead owns a bug of its Plan. The bug id is `b<k>`, the highest `<k>` in the table plus one, starting at 1, never reused.

### 33.1 `protocol bug report`

```
cpd protocol bug report --title <text> --symptom <text> [--cause <text>] [--plan <id>]
```

Records a bug and opens its protocol state. `--title` is the one-line name (1 to 200 characters with no NUL), `--symptom` what was seen (1 to 20000 characters with no NUL), `--cause` the diagnosed cause when it is known at report time, `--plan` the Plan the bug belongs to; without `--plan` the bug is cross-Plan and the Manager owns it. Every text flag is required to be non-empty (`usage`, exit 2); `--plan` must name a Plan that exists and is not deleted (`plan_not_found`, exit 4).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--title` and `--symptom` present, 1 to 200 and 1 to 20000 characters, no NUL; `--cause`, if present, 1 to 20000 characters, no NUL | `usage` | 2 |
| `--plan`, if present, names a Plan that exists and is not deleted | `plan_not_found` | 4 |
| the caller is not a Worker (`CPD_ATTEMPT` unset or empty) | `not_a_lead` | 3 |

**Effects:** one transaction, one insert into `bug_records` (contract §2.2 "Bug record"): `id` the next `b<k>`, `status` `open`, `reported_by` the caller's Session id (`CPD_SESSION`; null when unset), `reported_at` the transaction's time, `cause` from `--cause`, every other field null. **No Event is appended.** **The wake** (air-n120; contract §3.7 E25, §2.2 "Bug record", "The wake and the breach check"): at the first tick that sees the new record the engine wakes its owner — the bug's `bug` Inbox item (contract §2.2 "Inbox item") and one waking `session-message` to the owner (the Plan's Lead when `--plan` names one, else the live Manager of Context `cpd`), with a session resume when the owner is asleep or idle — so the 15-minute bound (air-d105) can be met; the command itself writes nothing beyond the row.

**Output:**

```json
{"ok": true, "bug": {"id": "b7", "plan": "protocol-enforce", "title": "pr merge refused on a clean stacked PR", "symptom": "...", "cause": null, "mitigation": null, "mitigated_by": null, "mitigated_at": null, "root_fix": null, "regression_test": null, "status": "open", "reported_by": "<session-id>", "reported_at": "2026-11-08T05:30:00Z", "closed_at": null, "closed_by": null}}
```

**Not idempotent:** every call reports a new bug.

### 33.2 `protocol bug mitigate`

```
cpd protocol bug mitigate <id> --mitigation <text> [--cause <text>]
```

Records the mitigation applied to an open bug (air-d103): `<id>` is a bug id (`b<k>`), `--mitigation` the stopgap that removes or contains the User's symptom now (1 to 20000 characters with no NUL), `--cause` the diagnosed cause when it is first known here. `<id>` that no row holds is `bug_not_found` (exit 4); a bug whose `status` is `closed` takes no mitigation (`illegal_transition`, exit 3, nothing written).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--mitigation` present, 1 to 20000 characters, no NUL; `--cause`, if present, 1 to 20000 characters, no NUL | `usage` | 2 |
| `<id>` names a `bug_records` row | `bug_not_found` | 4 |
| the bug's `status` is `open` | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| the caller is not a Worker (`CPD_ATTEMPT` unset or empty) | `not_a_lead` | 3 |

**Effects:** one transaction, the row's `mitigation` set from the flag, `mitigated_by` the caller's Session id (`CPD_SESSION`; null when unset), `mitigated_at` the transaction's time, and `cause` set from `--cause` when it is given; without `--cause` a recorded `cause` stands. A second `mitigate` of an open bug replaces the first (the applied stopgap stands); the same values again write nothing. **No Event is appended.**

**Output:** the `bug` object of §33.1, with the new values.

**Idempotent:** the same `--mitigation` (and `--cause`) on an open bug whose stored values already equal them is `{"ok": true, "already": true}` with the `bug` object, nothing written.

### 33.3 `protocol bug close`

```
cpd protocol bug close <id> --root-fix <ref> --regression-test <text>
```

Closes a bug whose root fix is in and its regression test recorded (air-d107). `--root-fix` is the root-fix Work as a reference: a Plan id, a Workflow `<plan>/<key>` ("A Workflow reference", contract §2.2) or a Job `<plan>/<workflow>/<key>`; cpd stores it and does not resolve it. `--regression-test` names the test that pins the fix, as the repo names its tests (a test function, file or filter). Both flags are required and non-empty: a missing or empty one is refused `root_fix_required` (exit 3, nothing written, `details` `{"missing": ["root-fix" | "regression-test"]}`), the refusal air-d107 names — a close without a root-fix link and a regression test does not happen. Malformed text (over 200 characters, a NUL) is `usage` (exit 2).

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--root-fix` and `--regression-test` present, 1 to 200 characters each, no NUL (`details` `{"missing": [...]}`) | `root_fix_required` | 3 |
| `<id>` names a `bug_records` row | `bug_not_found` | 4 |
| the bug's `status` is `open` | `illegal_transition` | 3 |
| the caller is not a Worker (`CPD_ATTEMPT` unset or empty) | `not_a_lead` | 3 |

**Effects:** one transaction: `root_fix` and `regression_test` set from the flags, `status` `closed`, `closed_at` the transaction's time, `closed_by` the caller's Session id (`CPD_SESSION`; null when unset). **No Event is appended.** Nothing else changes: the root-fix Job or Workflow is queued and merged by the Plan's own machinery, never by this command.

**Output:** the `bug` object of §33.1, `status` `closed`.

**Idempotent:** a close of a bug whose `status` is already `closed` is `{"ok": true, "already": true}` with the `bug` object, nothing written, whatever the flags say.

### 33.4 `protocol bug list`

```
cpd protocol bug list [--plan <id>] [--status open|closed] [--mitigated yes|no]
```

Lists bug records, `id` ascending (b1, b2, …). The filters combine: `--plan <id>` the bugs of one Plan (`--plan` is validated as §33.1 validates it, `plan_not_found` exit 4, and then filters: a Plan no bug names lists the empty array), `--status` open or closed bugs, `--mitigated yes` the bugs with a mitigation recorded, `--mitigated no` the bugs with **mitigation applied: no** (air-d104: the state is queryable). Read-only; no Worker check.

| Precondition | Code | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--status`, if present, is `open` or `closed`; `--mitigated`, if present, is `yes` or `no` | `usage` | 2 |
| `--plan`, if present, names a Plan that exists and is not deleted | `plan_not_found` | 4 |

**Output:**

```json
{"ok": true, "bugs": [{"id": "b3", "plan": null, "title": "...", "symptom": "...", "cause": "...", "mitigation": null, "mitigated_by": null, "mitigated_at": null, "root_fix": null, "regression_test": null, "status": "open", "reported_by": "<session-id>", "reported_at": "2026-11-08T05:00:00Z", "closed_at": null, "closed_by": null}]}
```

**Idempotent:** a read; the same store gives the same list.

### 33.5 `protocol bug show`

```
cpd protocol bug show <id>
```

One bug record, every field (contract §2.2 "Bug record"), so **mitigation applied: no** is visible (`mitigation`, `mitigated_by` and `mitigated_at` null). `<id>` that no row holds is `bug_not_found` (exit 4). Read-only; no Worker check.

**Output:** the `bug` object of §33.1.

**Idempotent:** a read.
